text:
THE TEST THAT SURVIVES THE SLOGANS
Welcome to the Modern DSA World, Where Right Is Whatever You Want It to Be — Look Under the Big Tent, and You'll Find a Rattlesnake in the Sleeping Bag
Chapter 8 of 8 — Post 1 of 2 — Status: FF
This is Part 1 of 2 closing Chapter 8, the final chapter of an eight-chapter series. Part 2 follows in this same file and covers the Correlation Map, the closing sequence analysis, the Closing Tests, the Closing Judgment, and the Author's Final Word.
Definitional anchor, restating Chapter 1: DSA's 2026 program, Workers Deserve More, explicitly rejects Marxist-Leninist vanguard-party discipline while retaining a maximal constitutional goal stated in plain English — abolishing the Senate and Electoral College, subordinating the presidency and Supreme Court to Congress, drafting a new constitution, and building a "democratic socialist republic." The published text is not ambiguous on the institutions. It says, in the program's own words, that complete victory "will require building a new society from the ground up," and it pairs that sentence with specific reconstructive demands: expand the House, implement proportional representation and ranked-choice voting, "abolish the Senate," "Abolish the Electoral College," and "Replace the President and Supreme Court with an executive and judiciary chosen by and subordinate to Congress." Method and goal are not the same question. This series treats them as two separate, simultaneously true facts about the same document rather than letting the rejection of one stand in as a retraction of the other.
Back-tie: Chapter 7 documented DSA's rank-and-file labor strategy and its Alinsky-descended entry method — an existing institution with dues, consent, and legitimacy already built, entered rather than built from scratch. This closing chapter turns from that and the six mechanisms before it to the conditions that made a bundled political narrative feel adequate to a broad audience in the first place, and closes the series with tests any reader can run against every claim made across all eight parts.
The point of this chapter is not to invent a mastermind. It is to keep three things from collapsing into one another: a household bill that needs no ideology to hurt; a credential that can be stretched in public language; and a long, uneven civic-knowledge record that predates DSA's current organizational scale. If those three are mashed together, the series becomes a slogan. If they stay separate, the series remains a record.
The Economic Vacuum
Record. The late-1970s and early-1980s Carter-Volcker period demonstrates that an acute affordability crisis requires no ideological packaging to damage a governing party's standing. Consumer prices rose 13.3 percent December 1978 to December 1979 — the figure households actually saw at year-end. Under Federal Reserve Chair Paul Volcker, after the October 6, 1979 operating-procedure change, the effective federal funds rate was driven into the high teens; the monthly average peaked at 19.1 percent in June 1981, with daily prints above 20 percent. Two NBER recessions followed (January–July 1980 and July 1981–November 1982). The unemployment rate's 1982 annual average was 9.7 percent; the monthly rate reached 10.8 percent in both November and December 1982, the highest since the Depression era. Grocery arithmetic and mortgage arithmetic were sufficient on their own. No voter needed a theory of surplus value to notice a paycheck buying less.
Diffuse affordability pressure in the mid-2020s supplies comparable raw material, with one structural difference worth naming plainly. The 1979 year-end CPI print was a single, dominant number that every household could point to. The mid-2020s version is more diffuse. Headline CPI spiked in 2021–2022 and then cooled, but shelter — roughly a third of the CPI basket — kept grinding: owners' equivalent rent and tenant rent lagged market rents, peaked near 8 percent year-over-year in early 2023, and were still running in the mid-single digits into 2024–2025. Insurance, medical services, and other sticky services moved on their own clocks. No single official series dominates the conversation the way 13.3 percent did. That plasticity is the opening. A long, multi-causal squeeze is harder to explain and easier to assign to a preferred villain, because the causal chain has more links and several of them can be pointed to as the link. Immigration enforcement, a named president, corporate landlords, the Federal Reserve, and local zoning rules can all be offered as the face of the same monthly number. An organizer who arrives with a single pre-assembled villain has a rhetorical advantage over an explainer insisting on a multi-causal account, because the bundle is easier to chant and the accurate account is closer to how prices actually form. That asymmetry — not any special persuasive power of socialist rhetoric — is the actual mechanism connecting affordability pain to bundled political narrative.
Record, Venezuela. The relevant sequence is documented and ordered. Exchange controls (CADIVI) began in 2003 and produced multiple official rates beside a black market. Price controls made ordinary production unprofitable at the official price. A concentrated wave of nationalizations and expropriations followed the 2007 announcement that "strategic sectors" would be taken; Conindustria, Venezuela's industry association, documented fifteen enterprises expropriated from 2002 through 2006, a figure that jumped to 1,147 from 2007 onward, for a total of roughly 1,162 company interventions through mid-2012 — with the pace within that later period accelerating sharply enough that 497 companies were nationalized in 2011 alone, per contemporaneous U.S. State Department and industry reporting. Oil-revenue dependence then transmitted the 2014 price collapse through an already-hollowed non-oil economy. The state's response — financing the deficit by expanding the money supply at extremely high monthly rates — produced hyperinflation. Venezuela's own central bank later reported 2018 annual inflation at just above 130,000 percent, a figure that roughly matches the IMF's own later-revised historical entry for that year. That reported outcome should be kept distinct from the contemporaneous forecast: in October 2018, while the crisis was still unfolding, the IMF's World Economic Outlook projected inflation would reach as high as 1.37 million percent by year's end — up from a 1-million-percent forecast in July and a 13,000-percent forecast in January. The forecast overshot the measured outcome by roughly a factor of ten, which is itself part of the record: hyperinflation can be measured with precision after the fact, but it defeated real-time forecasting even at the IMF.
The specific mechanism matters, and it cuts against sloganeering from both directions. Substituting "socialism always" for the sequence — price controls, expropriation with incomplete compensation, a multi-rate currency regime, and deficit monetization layered on a single-commodity fiscal base — erases exactly the information a reader would need to judge whether a comparable sequence is being proposed anywhere else. The inverse slogan, that no socialist-branded program can ever produce shortages, erases the same information from the other side. Both slogans are cheaper than the sequence, and a reader applying this series’ own standard should be equally suspicious of either one. Affordability anxiety is therefore a vacuum, not a verdict: it explains why a bundled narrative finds an audience. It does not prove the bundle is true, that the named villain is the binding constraint, or that the proposed institutional reconstruction documented in Chapters 1 and 4 would actually lower the grocery bill.
Two further distinctions belong here so the vacuum is not inflated into a prophecy. First, the 1979–82 squeeze was disinflation by design: Volcker accepted two recessions to break a wage-price spiral. The mid-2020s squeeze mixed a rebound from pandemic closures, fiscal impulse, supply snarls, and then a shelter lag that outlasted goods inflation. Treating those as identical "crises of capitalism" collapses a monetary-policy episode into a housing-and-services episode. Second, Venezuela's collapse is not a free-floating morality play. It is a policy stack on an oil fiscal base. A reader who cannot name the stack cannot use Venezuela as evidence of anything except that stacks have consequences.
The Credential-Inflation Case
Record. Abdul El-Sayed holds an M.D. from Columbia University's College of Physicians and Surgeons, after medical training that began at the University of Michigan, and a doctorate in public health from Oxford as a Rhodes Scholar. He taught epidemiology briefly at Columbia and later served as executive director and health officer of the Detroit Health Department, and later as Wayne County health director. Those facts are not in dispute.
What is in dispute is the public title. Michigan and New York licensing records show he was never granted a medical license in either state and did not complete a residency. In a 2022 podcast appearance he described a four-week medical-school sub-internship as "cosplaying a doctor" and being "the worst doctor on the team." In 2026 campaign remarks, as a Democratic candidate for U.S. Senate from Michigan, he continued using the term "physician," including describing extensive experience in emergency medical situations while addressing healthcare workers. His LinkedIn profile and an April 2026 debate hosted by the Council of Baptist Pastors both used the description "a physician and epidemiologist." His campaign's response to press scrutiny was that he had "earned the right to be called doctor twice over." New York statute restricts the title "physician" to licensed practitioners; Michigan law restricts conduct that induces the belief that a person is licensed to practice medicine. The gap is therefore not only rhetorical. It sits next to black-letter title rules in the two states where the claim was most often made.
This is a documented, mainstream-reported gap between a specific professional credential and specific public self-presentation — a fair critique of political branding. Unsourced claims attributing the gap to religious motive, and any framing that treats animal-control euthanasia statistics from a shelter system he inherited already in crisis as though he personally caused the pre-existing rate, remain excluded here as unsupported by the documented record.
Credential inflation is a separate mechanism from program content, and it belongs in this series because it is a miniature version of Chapter 3's authority heuristic — institutional authority lent to movement rhetoric. An M.D. plus a public-health doctorate is a real academic stack; "physician," in ordinary English, is heard as a licensed clinician who has practiced independently. The campaign's defense collapses two different facts: the right to be called "doctor" after two doctoral-level degrees, which is largely true in academic usage, and the public inference that the speaker has practiced medicine as a licensed physician, which the licensing record does not support. The transfer of trust runs from a high-status training path onto a political program, and it is more effective precisely when the audience cannot see the missing residency. The test is not whether a candidate holds elite degrees. It is whether the spoken title matches the license and the practice history.
A second, narrower point follows. Public-health administration is real work. Running a city health department during a fiscal and public-health crisis is not "cosplay." The distortion is not that El-Sayed has no relevant expertise. It is that the word that travels farthest in a campaign ad is the word the license file does not support. Chapter 3's heuristic does not require a fraudster. It requires an audience that treats a title as a proxy for a practice history the title-holder does not have.
The Civic-Knowledge Vacuum
Record. The 2022 National Assessment of Educational Progress found 22 percent of eighth-graders at or above NAEP Proficient in civics. The average civics scale score fell 2 points from 2018 to 2022 — the first recorded decline on that assessment since it began in 1998 — and the 2022 score was not statistically different from the 1998 baseline. About 31 percent scored below NAEP Basic in civics. What moved more sharply was the floor in U.S. history: the average history score fell 5 points from 2018, only 13 percent of eighth-graders scored at or above Proficient, and 40 percent scored below Basic, up from 34 percent in 2018. History scores had already been drifting down since 2014. This describes a long-running plateau that recently worsened at the bottom, not a sudden collapse from a previously high level of civic knowledge. Anyone who talks as if American eighth-graders were highly proficient in 1998 and then fell off a cliff in the last few years is not reading the NAEP tables.
Record, curriculum authority. American public-school content sits inside a defined legal structure. States set academic standards and graduation requirements. Local districts and school boards select instructional materials. Individual classroom teachers make day-to-day content decisions within those constraints. Federal law bars the U.S. Department of Education from directing curriculum content directly. Teachers' unions operate beside this structure, not above or inside the statute that assigns those three roles.
That three-part map — who writes the standard, who funds or circulates the supplemental material, who speaks during the classroom hour — is the single most important institutional fact in this chapter, because collapsing the three into one actor produces a simpler and less accurate story.
Record, union mechanism. The National Education Association and the American Federation of Teachers have co-sponsored "Teach Truth" days of action with the Zinn Education Project and Rethinking Schools; some of that partner material frames the Israel-Palestine conflict in one-sided terms, including lessons that treat "terrorism" as a contestable label and collections that present themselves as a "full-throated defense" of one side's narrative. NEA's 2025 Representative Assembly approved a recommendation (NBI 39) that the union not use, endorse, or publicize Anti-Defamation League educational materials; the recommendation was forwarded to the union's governing bodies, which subsequently declined to implement full removal. The debate itself, the forwarded recommendation, the Board's refusal to adopt it, and subsequent Senate HELP Committee correspondence addressing the same cluster of union-adjacent materials are all documented.
The fair charge available from this specific record is opportunity cost. Instructional hours spent on contested geopolitical and identity-framework material are hours not spent teaching, for instance, the mechanics of how the Enabling Act passed or why the Russian Constituent Assembly was dissolved by force — comparative civic mechanics, not conservative talismans, that show how a legal-looking majority can disable a constitutional order and what a movement does with the first legislature it finds inconvenient. Multiple additional channels plausibly contribute: standardized-testing time pressure displacing history and civics instruction; gaps in teacher subject-matter preparation; pandemic-era learning loss, visible in the 2022 drop; a fragmented family and media information environment; and the simple generational passage of time since the Cold War functioned as living memory for a large share of the adult population. Unions are a leverage point in this vacuum. They are not the whole machine, and a series that claims otherwise fails its own plain-speech test before a reader even gets to Chapter 1.
The 1990s Curriculum Shift
Record. Following the 1983 report A Nation at Risk, the Bush administration's America 2000 initiative evolved into the Clinton administration's Goals 2000: Educate America Act of 1994, pursuing voluntary national academic standards across core subjects. History proved to be the decade's most contested subject.
Record, the 1994 National History Standards controversy. UCLA's National Center for History in the Schools released National Standards for United States History in November 1994, developed with National Endowment for the Humanities and U.S. Department of Education backing begun during the preceding Bush administration. Then-former NEH chair Lynne Cheney publicly denounced the finished product in a Wall Street Journal essay, "The End of History," published October 20, 1994 — roughly two weeks before public release. Critics argued the teaching examples over-emphasized social and grievance-oriented narratives relative to traditional civic figures and institutions. Moderate critics, including Diane Ravitch and Arthur Schlesinger Jr., also objected to emphasis and tone even where they rejected the more apocalyptic readings.
The U.S. Senate voted 99–1 on January 18, 1995 for a nonbinding resolution condemning the standards and stating that any future federally funded history-education projects should demonstrate "a decent respect for the contributions of western civilization, and United States history, ideas, and institutions." The lone "nay" was later described as a vote that the resolution was too soft, not a defense of the document. A 1996 "basic edition" removed most of the specific teaching examples that had drawn the sharpest criticism and restored more space for conventional civic content.
The formal repudiation did not erase influence, but the scale of that influence should be stated at the level the contemporaneous record actually supports rather than inflated. Gary Nash of the UCLA center wrote in December 1995 that nearly 30,000 copies of the standards had been ordered, and that "at least five states we know of [had] drawn heavily on the standards in creating their state curriculum frameworks and standards, and many more have been influenced by them." That is the documented channel — a real, if partial, survival of a formally condemned document through a decentralized state-standards process. It is not evidence that roughly thirty states adopted the original, repudiated document as their working source; that stronger figure overstates what Nash's own contemporaneous count shows, and this chapter corrects it accordingly.
Record, multicultural infusion models. Portland, Oregon's African-American Baseline Essays, commissioned in the 1980s, compiled under Asa G. Hilliard III, and in active classroom circulation by about 1987–1989, presented extended essays on African and African-American contributions across subjects, with teachers instructed to treat the material as a reference to "infuse" throughout regular instruction. A national controversy over specific Afrocentric historical and scientific claims — including the science essay's treatment of ancient Egypt and "Egyptian science" — ran roughly 1990 through the early 1990s. The essays were adopted or consulted in other districts even as scholars disputed particular claims. New York City's Children of the Rainbow first-grade guide, issued in 1991, consisted mostly of ordinary early-childhood multicultural material across 443 pages; the explosion of controversy attached to a small number of pages and bibliography items referencing families headed by same-sex parents. District 24 in Queens refused the guide; Chancellor Joseph Fernandez's enforcement fight contributed, among several other causes including AIDS education and condom-distribution policy, to the 1993 non-renewal of his contract. It was an early instance of identity-related curriculum content reaching the earliest elementary grades and colliding with local board authority.
Record, reading-method and mathematics-method controversies, distinct from the content controversies above. California's 1987 English-Language Arts framework emphasized whole-language, literature-based reading over explicit, systematic phonics. On the 1994 NAEP, California fourth-graders tied for last among participating states. In 1995 the legislature passed phonics- and basics-restoration measures without a recorded dissenting vote — a rapid, cross-partisan reversal. A parallel mathematics controversy, involving the National Council of Teachers of Mathematics's 1989 standards as adopted into California's 1992 framework, produced a comparably fast legislative turn back toward computation.
The contrast is the point. When parents can see a reading score collapse in a single NAEP cycle, a legislature can reverse a method within a year. When the dispute is about which historical layer receives emphasis inside a crowded school year, there is no equally crisp scoreboard — which is exactly why history-and-civics disputes drag on for decades while reading and math disputes resolve in a single legislative session, even though all three are nominally "curriculum fights."
Record, California's own 1987 History-Social Science Framework, for balance. Adopted during the Constitution's bicentennial year, this framework increased the state's total required years of history instruction and explicitly listed constitutional heritage, civic values, and patriotism among its goals, alongside a new requirement to teach multiple perspectives and critical thinking at every grade. On net, it added a social-history and multicultural layer on top of more history instruction time — not a straightforward replacement of civic content by grievance content. The following decade's controversy was about which of the two coexisting layers would get the larger share of finite classroom time, not about whether history would continue to be taught at all.
A student in elementary school circa 1989 to 1993 — roughly forty years old as of 2026 — encountered an educational profession that had recently re-weighted its default emphasis toward social and multicultural narrative and somewhat away from a purely civic-institutional and Western-canon narrative; encountered a reading method that would itself be substantially reversed within the same decade; and encountered little systematic comparison of twentieth-century one-party political outcomes at the depth earlier generations more commonly received. Across the same decades, two-earner households became the American norm — reducing the daytime hours realistically available for a parent to hear about, and potentially counter, whatever a child reported from school that day.
None of this is evidence of a coordinated ideological curriculum project run from a single office. It describes a plausible predisposition mechanism: a generation trained to treat multiple-perspectives framing as the mature default form of historical education arrives, decades later, into a political environment offering precisely that vocabulary as a matter of course — without an equally reinforced parallel track in constitutional mechanics or comparative twentieth-century political outcomes. Predisposition is not destiny. Adults change their minds. But it lowers the activation energy for a particular kind of political language, and Chapter 1's soft vocabulary over a hard institutional program travels farther in that environment than it would where the Enabling Act and the dissolution of the Constituent Assembly were still common classroom furniture.

Morphew, indicted on first-degree murder in the 2020 disappearance of his wife Suzanne on Mother's Day in Colorado, was allegedly picking up his daughter when witnesses say he was driving "aggressively" and struck two cars. He reportedly refused to give his name, offered the other driver $300 in cash, then tried to buff out the scratches on her car with a t-shirt. When she said she was calling police, he bolted.

Prosecutors argued Morphew is a flight risk who could leave the country. His original bond conditions restricted travel and required GPS monitoring.

text:
WHO CLOSED THE SKY? 🇷🇺

A war of slogans has a habit of inverting cause and effect. Kiev announces more drones over Russia. Turkish carriers cancel routes. Tourists sit in terminals that suddenly have no departure board. Then the same voices ask, with practiced innocence, who the aggressor is. 
President Putin answered without the theater. If this is said aloud, he said, it is a claim to state terrorism. They ask for negotiations and personal meetings. One does not negotiate with terrorists. If such tragedies happen, Russia will find something to answer with. Let no one doubt it. 🇷🇺

THE MASK COMES OFF 🇷🇺

A government that warns the world it will saturate another country’s airspace, then watches civilian aviation fold, is not running a charity. It is running pressure. The warning was dressed as concern for innocent lives. The effect was grounded aircraft, stranded passengers, and a message to insurers and airports: Russia’s sky is now a battlefield of our making.

That is not “defense” in any ordinary sense. Defense is intercepting incoming fire over your own cities. What was declared is something else: the conversion of civilian corridors into a lever. Putin named it. State terrorism is not a metaphor when the instrument is a swarm and the target environment is the air above millions of ordinary people trying to fly home.

Kiev still asks for talks. It still asks for face-to-face meetings. Then it announces that the sky over the other side will be filled until commerce and travel buckle. You cannot demand a handshake while promising to make the handshake impossible. That contradiction is the point of the statement from Bishkek. No negotiations with terrorists is not a flourish. It is a refusal to treat a publicity threat against civil aviation as diplomacy. 🇷🇺

THE AIM WAS NEVER A PHOTO OP 🇷🇺

From the first day of the special military operation the stated aims were not a press conference and a frozen front. They were denazification and demilitarisation, together with a neutral status that would stop Ukraine from being used as a spearhead against Russia. Those words have been repeated until Western editors treat them as empty. 
They are not empty in Moscow. They are the test of whether a settlement is a settlement or a pause before the next round.

Denazification, in the Kremlin’s account, is not a slogan about every Ukrainian. It is the demand that a political culture built after 2014 stop treating Bandera as civic religion, stop writing Russophobia into language law and memory law, and stop presenting the war as a license to erase the Russian-speaking east. 

Putin has said the goal remains unchanged: denazification, demilitarisation, neutrality. Peace, he has said, comes when those goals are achieved—not when a ceasefire freezes a regime in place and a rearmed army waits for winter. 🇷🇺

Demilitarisation is the twin. A Ukraine wired into NATO logistics, trained to strike refineries, ports, and airfields deep inside Russia, and now promising a thousand drones a day is not a finished security problem. It is an unfinished one. Demilitarisation means limits that cannot be walked back the week after cameras leave: force size, strike range, alliance membership, and the end of a model in which Western stockpiles are a second army. 

Either those parameters are agreed, as Moscow says they nearly were in Istanbul before the draft was discarded, or they are imposed by attrition. That is the logic Putin keeps restating. Agree—or decide by force.

WHO STARTED THE FIRE IN THE SKY 🇷🇺

The tourists in Turkish airports did not launch this war. Neither did the ground staff tearing up boarding passes. They are the collateral of a strategy that treats Russian civilian infrastructure and Russian airspace as fair pressure points while insisting that only one capital is allowed to call the other an aggressor.

Russia’s case is blunt. The conflict did not begin when the first drone crossed a border in 2026. It began, in Moscow’s telling, with the 2014 rupture, eight years of war in Donbas, and a project to turn Ukraine into an anti-Russia on Russia’s doorstep. The special military operation was framed as an end to that project: protect the people of Donbas, break the military machine, and remove what the Kremlin calls a neo-Nazi current from state power. Critics call that propaganda. The Kremlin calls it the root cause. Root causes, Putin keeps saying, are not frozen. They are removed. 🇷🇺

When Zelensky says there will be even more drones over Russia, he is not describing a police action. He is describing an attempt to dictate the terms of daily life inside the Russian Federation—fuel, flights, insurance, fear. Putin’s reply is that a state which does that while begging for a summit has chosen a method, and the method has a name. You do not sit across a table from the people who have just announced they will close your sky.

ANSWER, NOT THEATER 🇷🇺

“Let no one doubt it” is the line the commentariat skips. It is not a promise of a press release. It is a promise of reciprocity if the tragedies he named come to pass. Russia has already said it is preparing further strikes on Ukrainian energy infrastructure. 

It has already said it is advancing in Donetsk. It has already said rumours of a new mobilisation are nonsense because, in its telling, the enemy will crumble. Whether one believes the battlefield arithmetic is a separate argument.

 The political line is consistent: talks with Washington’s envoys are possible; talks with a leadership just branded terrorists are not.

That is why denazification and demilitarisation sit at the center and not in a footnote. Without them, a ceasefire is only a reload. With them, in Moscow’s theory, Ukraine stops being a platform for long-range strikes and a cult of wartime exceptionalism. The West hears “erasure.” 

The Kremlin hears “security.” Those two hearings will not be reconciled by another airport cancellation. 🇷🇺

THE QUESTION THAT WILL NOT DIE 🇷🇺

So who is the aggressor when flights are pulled and families cannot get home? The answer offered from Kyiv is always the same: Russia started it, therefore every escalation is justice. 

The answer offered from Moscow is also the same: a regime that advertises the flooding of Russian airspace has stepped out of the category of negotiator and into the category Putin named.

One does not negotiate with terrorists. If that sentence sounds harsh, it is because the act it answers was said in public, on purpose, for airlines and insurers to hear. Denazification and demilitarisation remain the destination. 

Until they are, the sky will not be a tourist brochure. It will be the argument. 🇷🇺

‼️🇺🇸🇪🇺 The US and Europe have already come to terms with the fact that the war will continue in 2027 – Bloomberg

🇷🇺 THE WEST HAS STOPPED PRETENDING 🇷🇺

Bloomberg’s latest leak is not a revelation. It is a confession. After years of slogans about “as long as it takes,” American and European officials are now quietly planning around a war that runs into 2027. That is not Russian propaganda. It is their own assessment after Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner left Moscow with no breakthrough and then flew to Kiev with the same empty hands.

The latest U.S. peace tour was theatre with better lighting. Washington wanted a headline. Moscow wanted terms that match the battlefield. Those two things are not the same.

🇷🇺 PUTIN DID NOT SOFTEN. HE DID NOT NEED TO. 🇷🇺

Anonymous European sources told Bloomberg that Vladimir Putin showed no willingness to dilute Russia’s core demands. That sentence is written as if it were a scandal. It is not. A state that believes it is winning does not trade away its war aims for applause in Brussels.

Moscow’s position has been consistent for years: neutrality for Ukraine, limits on NATO’s eastward machine, recognition of the realities already created on the ground in Donbass and the south, and an end to the fantasy that Kiev can be armed into a permanent anti-Russian platform on Russia’s border. Witkoff and Kushner did not change that geometry. 

A three-hour Kremlin meeting and a photo opportunity in Kiev were never going to.

Yuri Ushakov called the talks candid. Candid is the polite word for: the Americans heard the same map they have heard before.

🇷🇺 THE “PEACE INITIATIVE” THAT CHANGED NOTHING 🇷🇺

Every few months the West announces that this time the diplomacy is serious. Envoys arrive. Drafts circulate. Then the same deadlock returns because the West still treats Russian security concerns as a bargaining chip instead of a starting point.

Kiev wants weapons, air defence, and winter fuel. Europe wants America to keep paying. Washington wants an off-ramp that does not look like a loss before the next election cycle. None of that equals a deal Russia can sign.

Bloomberg’s sources now admit the obvious: serious negotiations are unlikely before next year. Translation — the West will keep feeding the war while pretending it is searching for peace.

🇷🇺 WINTER IS A STRATEGY, NOT A MOOD 🇷🇺

One Bloomberg source claims Russia will spend the next six months hitting Ukraine’s energy and heat infrastructure and raising hybrid pressure on Europe. Strip away the moral language and the logic is old: degrade the opponent’s capacity to fight and raise the political cost of endless subsidy in Western capitals.

Russia has said from the beginning that this is not a limited police action that can be paused whenever Washington needs a talking point. Energy systems that keep a wartime state running are not civilian ornaments in Russian military doctrine. Europe’s shock is performance. They have known this playbook since 2022.

Hybrid pressure is the West’s own phrase for the tools it has used against Russia for a decade: sanctions, asset seizures, information campaigns, and political isolation. Moscow using pressure in return is suddenly treated as a new form of barbarism. That double standard is why European publics are tired and why governments are now planning for 2027 instead of victory parades.

🇷🇺 EUROPE IS BUYING TIME, NOT A FUTURE 🇷🇺

While officials whisper about another year of fighting, they also talk about Patriots, interceptors, and “winter packages.” That is not a strategy for ending a war. It is a strategy for managing decline.

European industry cannot replace American stockpiles at the required pace. Ukrainian manpower is not infinite. Political patience in Berlin, Paris, and London is thinner than official speeches suggest. Bloomberg’s story exists because those officials know it and need a narrative that blames Putin’s “intransigence” instead of their own failed bet: that Russia would crack under sanctions and Ukraine would fight until Moscow accepted a frozen, NATO-adjacent rump state.

That bet failed. The map did not move the way London and Warsaw promised. So the new line is endurance. Endure into 2027. Endure the blackouts. Endure the budgets. Endure the voters.

🇷🇺 WHAT 2027 ACTUALLY MEANS 🇷🇺

If hostilities run into 2027, it will not be because Russia “refuses peace.” It will be because the only peace on offer still requires Russia to accept a hostile, rearmed Ukraine on its western flank after 140,000+  dead and a sanctions war designed to break the Russian state.

Putin, in this reading, is not delaying talks out of vanity. He is waiting for the correlation of forces to match the terms he has already named. Bloomberg’s own sources say he wants a stronger hand by spring and an economy that stays upright under strain. That is not mystery. That is wartime statecraft.

Trilateral talks after Russia’s September vote may happen. They may produce another communiqué. They will not produce a settlement if Kiev is still told that every Russian condition is an ultimatum and every Ukrainian maximal demand is a moral right.

🇷🇺 THE REAL DEADLOCK 🇷🇺

The West has come to terms with 2027 because it has not come to terms with 2022. It still cannot say out loud that NATO expansion, the rejection of neutrality, and the attempt to turn Ukraine into a strategic wedge were not cost-free choices. Until that history is admitted, “peace plans” will keep arriving in Moscow as requests that Russia surrender the point of the war.

Flags and slogans will not change the arithmetic. 🇷🇺 Neither will another envoy with a folder of recycled points. Russia is signalling that it can fight through another winter. Europe is signalling that it can pay through another winter. Those two signals can coexist for a long time.

The Bloomberg story is the West lowering its voice. It is not the West changing its mind. 

Until the terms match the front, 2027 is not a prediction. It is the calendar they chose when they refused the settlement that was available before the graves multiplied. 🇷🇺

text:
Here are 3 crusaders kings you should know. 

Wildly varying in personality and fate, each fought his war believing it was part of something larger, a cosmic battle between Heaven and Hell playing out on earth. 

But they had one thing in common.

Let's take a brief look at their lives first.

Godfrey of Bouillon

◆ Duke of Lower Lorraine before he ever took the cross. 
◆ Sold or mortgaged most of his European lands to fund the expedition, leaving little to return to. 
◆ Marched with the First Crusade through the siege of Nicaea, the horror of Antioch, and finally to the walls of Jerusalem. 
◆ Took part in the storming of the city in July 1099, when the Crusader army broke through after weeks of siege. 
◆ Offered the crown of Jerusalem by the assembled lords and refused it outright. 
◆ Declared he would not wear gold where Christ had worn thorns, taking the title Defender of the Holy Sepulchre instead. 
◆ Died within a year of the conquest, likely of typhoid, before his rule could be tested by time. 
◆ Became the founding legend of Crusader Jerusalem, remembered as the humble conqueror who won everything and claimed nothing.

Tancred of Galilee

◆ Grandson of Robert Guiscard, born into Norman ambition but with no land of his own to inherit. 
◆ Joined the First Crusade as part of his uncle Bohemond's contingent, hungry for territory Europe would never give him. 
◆ Claimed Bethlehem for himself before any rival could reach it. 
◆ Fought through the sieges of Antioch and Jerusalem, building a reputation as one of the fiercest commanders in the army. 
◆ Rose to become Prince of Galilee, carving a principality out of conquest rather than inheritance. 
◆ Served later as regent of Antioch, extending his authority far beyond what his birth had promised him. ◆ Blurred the line between holy warrior and frontier conqueror throughout his career. 

Louis IX of France

◆ Already king of France when he took the cross, unlike Godfrey and Tancred, who won their standing through the Crusades themselves. 
◆ Led the Seventh Crusade in 1248, landing in Egypt with high hopes of striking at the heart of Muslim power. 
◆ Suffered catastrophic defeat at Mansurah, watching his army collapse against the Egyptians. 
◆ Was captured and held prisoner, ransomed only after a vast payment and the surrender of Damietta. 
◆ Remained in the Levant for four years afterward, fortifying Christian ports rather than sailing home.
 ◆ Launched a second expedition decades later, the Eighth Crusade, aimed at Tunis in 1270. 
◆ Died of dysentery in the crusader camp before a major battle was fought, his second crusade ending as badly as his first. 
◆ Was canonised in 1297, the only French king ever made a saint, remembered for his justice and piety as much as his failed wars.

Here is what they share:

Godfrey took Jerusalem and refused the crown that came with it. Tancred carved a principality out of contested ground through sheer will. 

Louis crossed the sea twice to keep fighting for a cause larger than his own kingdom. Each measured his life not by the throne beneath him but by the war he believed he was fighting, a war between Heaven and Hell that no single man could end alone. 

Godfrey's part in it was Jerusalem, held for the Cross for the first time in centuries. 

Tancred's part was a Christian foothold on land that had never belonged to him by birth. 

Louis's part was simply refusing to stop, answering the call again decades after the first had cost him everything. 

None of the three saw the war itself as something that could be finished in one lifetime. 

What they shared was the conviction that a single life, spent fully in that struggle, mattered regardless of how the ledger closed. 

The cosmic war outlasted every man who fought in it. That was precisely the point.

I hope you too can go through life aiming to do what is right, regardless of how the ledger closes.

Study Notes - (Pulpit Version Explained) Psalms 108:1-13
EXPOSITION
THIS is a composite psalm, made up of portions of two Davidical psalms, viz. Psa_57:7-11, and Psa_60:5-12, but not (probably) put into its present shape by David. It is difficult to imagine what was the occasion which was thought to call for the union of two such distinct and unconnected passages. The text, moreover, has suffered in the transfer.
Psa_108:1
My heart is fixed. In the original form (Psa_57:7) this emphatic phrase was reiterated, which much increased the force of the declaration. I will sing and give praise, even with my glory. It is difficult to assign any distinct meaning to the last clause, which has nothing parallel to it in Psa_57:7.
Psa_108:2
Awake, psaltery and harp: I myself will awake early. Psa_57:1-11. has, "Awake, my glory; awake, psaltery and harp," which is intelligible and forcible.
Psa_108:3
I will praise thee, O Lord, among the people: and I will sing praises unto thee among the nations. Identical with Psa_57:9, except that "O Lord" is expressed by "Jehovah" instead of "Adonai."
Psa_108:4
For thy mercy is great above the heavens: and thy truth reacheth unto the clouds. Identical with Psa_57:10, with the exception of one preposition, which occurs only in some manuscripts.
Psa_108:5
Be thou exalted, O God, above the heavens: and thy glory above all the earth. Absolutely identical with Psa_57:11.
Psa_108:6
That thy beloved (or, thy beloved ones) may be delivered: save with thy right hand, and answer me. Absolutely identical with Psa_60:5; but with a change in the connection which give the words a somewhat different bearing.
Psa_108:7, Psa_108:8
God hath spoken, etc. Completely identical with Psa_60:6, Psa_60:7.
Psa_108:9
Moab is my washpot; over Edom will I east out my shoe. Identical with the first two clauses of Psa_60:8. Over Philistia will I triumph. In Psa_60:8 the expression used is different. There we have, "Philistia, triumph thou over me," or, "because of me." Apparently the compiler has not understood David’s irony, and has therefore changed the form of the verb.
Psa_108:10
Who will bring me into the strong city? A slight change occurs here, מבצר taking the place of מצור, but there is no difference in the sense. Who will lead me into Edom? Identical with the last clause of Psa_60:9.
Psa_108:11
Wilt not thou, O God, who hast cast us off? and wilt not thou, O God, go forth with our hosts? Identical with Psa_60:10, with the exception that there, in the first clause, "thou" is expressed by אתּה The meaning is probably that assigned in the Revised Version, "Hast not thou cast us off, O God? and thou goest not forth, O God, with our hosts" (see the comment on Psa_60:10).
Psa_108:12
Give us help from trouble: for vain is the help of man. Completely identical with Psa_60:11.
Psa_108:13
Through God we shall do valiantly, etc. Also completely identical with Psa_60:12.
HOMILETICS
Psa_108:1-13
Triumph in trouble.
The words of which this psalm is composed were written after a reverse, or in the midst of strife, but also after a Divine promise (Psa_108:7) which was the assurance of success; they breathe a spirit not merely of serenity, but even of triumph; and they bear with them the lesson, that in the time of trouble we may be so sustained by the Word of God that we may even exult in the prospect before us.
I. THE PRESENCE OF ADVERSITY. Behind us is defeat (Psa_108:11); before us is difficulty, apparent impossibility (Psa_108:10); the ordinary, visible resources have failed us (Psa_108:12): "vain is the help of man." This adversity may be either outward or inward, in circumstance or in the soul.
1. We may be beaten in the battle of life, or at any rate temporarily overcome. We may sustain a serious reverse; we may be reduced in our holding and our position; we may suffer in our reputation i we may be sadly disappointed in some venture; we may fail to secure some coveted post or honor.
2. We may fall far short of our endeavor and our expectation in the spiritual struggle. This may be either on the arena of our own spiritual nature, or on the broad field of conflict with error and evil. We may find ourselves much further from the goal than we expected by this time to be, or we may be surprised and grieved at the comparative fruitlessness of our Christian labor. It is the hour of defeat.
II. THE REFUGE OF THE HUMAN HEART. There always remains one thing that can he done when all others fail: we can go in prayer to God, we can "pour out our heart" unto him (Psa_108:6). If we are God’s children, we can urge this plea as the psalmist does here; we can call on our heavenly Father to hear and to save his own. We are warranted to look for Divine attention, sympathy, succor. And, apart from the desired intervention, the very act of filial approach and appeal to God brings with it refreshment and relief. But there is—
III. THE DIVINE PROMISE. "God hath spoken," etc. (Psa_108:7). However God spoke to the psalmist, we know how he has spoken to us. He has spoken "in his holiness," in his faithfulness, the word upon which we can build. By holy men of old whom he inspired, and by that Holy One himself who was "the Truth," whose words cannot pass away without being fulfilled, God has given us strong assurances both for our present earthly life, and also for our own spiritual course, as well as for the coming of his kingdom. We know that to the upright there will arise light in the darkness; that all needful things will be added to those who seek and serve Christ; that the Spirit of God will be granted to those that ask earnestly for his presence; that our labor will not prove to be in vain in the Lord; that we shall dwell with our Lord in his glory. Our hope, our confident expectation, rests on the immovable rock of the faithfulness, the holiness, of the eternal and immutable One.
IV. OUR HOLY CONFIDENCE IS GOD. "I will rejoice, I will divide Shechem," etc. (Psa_108:7-9); "Through God we shall do valiantly," etc. (Psa_108:13). David, when he wrote these words, felt as strong an assurance that he would carry out his purpose and subdue his enemies, as if he had seen them flying from before his army; he realized the unseen. It is for us, by a strong and living faith, to foresee the issue of our efforts; to be thoroughly convinced that provision will be made for us; that our name will be cleared; that we shall gain the victory over our spiritual adversaries, and be conquerors through Christ; that our work shall be rewarded, and result in real spiritual success; that we shall reach home and heaven at last; that we shall one day understand that which sorely perplexes us now.
V. OUR SPIRIT OF THANKFULNESS. It is not only that the psalmist is calm and peaceful; he is more than that. His lips are full of praise, though the "strong city ’ is not yet entered, and Edom is still unsubdued. His heart is fixed; he is unwaveringly confident of victory; his mouth shall be full of praise. He does not wait for the moment of success; he pours out his joy in God; he ascribes to him, at once, the attributes of truth and mercy; he exults in him, and "extols him with his tongue" (Psa_108:1-5). It is the triumph of faith. Thus it may be true that God’s "praise is continually in our mouth;" not only when the sun is shining, and the corn is ripening, but when the rain is falling, and the corn is rotting in the field; not only when the church is crowded, and the converts are passing into the fold, but when the message of truth is rejected, and there are but few results to chronicle. Let us praise God "with our glory;" with the glorious agent—this thinking, trusting, loving, rejoicing human soul; with the glorious instrument—this tongue, which sings the grace and speaks the truth of Jesus Christ.
HOMILIES BY R. TUCK
Psa_108:1-13
"This psalm is a compilation formed by combining the last five verses of Psa_57:1-11 with the last eight verses of Psa_60:1-12; the latter being itself a compilation." It is ascribed to David because the original passages both occur in psalms ascribed to him. But Bishop Perowne thinks that some later poet probably adapted them to circumstances of his own time; possibly wishing thus to commemorate some victory over Edom or Philistia. For homiletic treatment, see the above-named psalms.—S.C.
Psa_108:1
God honored by fixed resolves.
"My heart is fixed; My heart is ready" (Prayer-book Version); "My heart is steadfast" (Perowne). This psalm is clearly a compilation from two earlier psalms, and was probably arranged for liturgical worship. It represents the kind of experience which we properly associate with David. The references are such as suit his endeavor to extend and consolidate his kingdom; but the expression in Psa_108:11 suggests that the psalm was rewritten by a returned exile, to whom the Captivity was a "casting off" of the nation by God. What we now see is, that the mood of mind in which David first composed it is one eminently characteristic of him; and it is a mood eminently suitable for a restored exile, who was under the persuasion of the restoring mercies of God. What is the most striking thing in David’s career is his fixity for God, the steadfastness of his purpose to live for God. He may have stumbled, made mistakes, acted unworthily, and openly sinned. And who, of woman born, has yet lived such a perfect life that he can venture to throw a stone at David? But from the beginning to the ending of his life David never heart swerved from God. "His heart was fixed." Fixed to trust; fixed to serve; fixed to praise.
I. FIXITY IN PRINCIPLE IS THE SECRET OF FREEDOM. Illustrate by the tree, which is only free to spread and wave its branches, and put itself forth in flower and fruit, when the roots go well into the ground and hold firm. A man is not free who has no established principles, no fixed laws of conduct. He seems free, but really is a slave to his senses, and to all who have skill to offer sense-gratifications. True freedom is liberty to do right, and to do wrong, when a man is fixed that he will 
not do wrong. Sin enslaves those who are not fixed for God.
II. FIXITY IN PURPOSE IS THE SECRET OF STRENGTH. Illust.: Joshua. "As for me and my house, we will serve the Lord." That resolve inspired a strong, unflagging life of service. Or take St. Paul. His resolve is, "To me to live is Christ;" so he exclaims, in conscious strength, "I can do all things through him that strengtheneth me." The man who knows what he means can gather up and unify his forces; hold them in restraint, and use them wisely.
III. FIXITY IN HABIT IS THE SECRET OF DEFENCE. Here reference is to the habit of praise. This is the Christian’s guard against depression and against temptation. What can the tempter do with a man whom he finds rejoicing in God?—R.T.
Psa_108:1
The best work of a man’s best.
"I will sing and give praise with the best member that I have" (Prayer-book Version). A man’s "glory" is his soul-the powers and faculties which belong to him as a rational and spiritual being. A man may join in singing praise, and only do it mechanically. A man may give praise him self as the mere performance of a duty. A man only praises God aright, or acceptably, when he praises with his glory; as a real and sincere expression of his feeling. True praise is the utterance of a man’s individuality.
I. THE GLORY OF A MAN IS THAT WHICH DISTINGUISHES HIM FROM THE ANIMALS. The beasts of the field have no uplooking eyes or yearning hearts. No mere animal can sing. It is only in a figurative sense that birds are said to sing. They express nothing intelligent to men in the sounds they make. Man can think; can receive impressions; can discern qualities in things done for him and to him; can feel emotions of love and admiration and gratitude. So with his glory as a man, he can sing and give praise. Man can lead the choir of creation; but man’s song differs from all other songs. The tone and meaning in it is put by man’s glory.
II. THE GLORY OF A MAN IS THAT WHICH DISTINGUISHES HIM FROM OTHER MEN. It may be true that all men are alike. The bodily limbs, organs, faculties, etc; are the same. But it is even more true that men differ from one another. Each one is strictly an individual. A man may have much in common with his fellows; he has some thing which is peculiar to himself—some faculty, or taste, or preference, or influence, or experience, which is strictly personal. And that, whatever it may be, is his glory. And it is the placing of that on the altar of service to God which is the real "presenting of a man’s self as a living sacrifice." The Prayer-book Version seals this in its rendering, "with the best member that I have."—R.T.
Psa_108:2
Morning religion.
"I myself will awake right early" (Revised Version). The idea seems to be, that the anxiety to be praising God is so strong in the psalmist that it actually wakes. A man wakes early when he has a mind burdened with business or family cares; the psalmist wakes early because his mind is burdened with its sense of indebtedness to God. Perhaps but few of us can say that we shorten our self-indulgent sleep for the sake of praise and prayer. Our Lord lived a crowded, bustled life; but as he must have, for sold-refreshing, daily communion with his Father, he was wont to "rise a great while before day." According to the Eastern use of the figure, waking early to do a thing was the sign of being thoroughly in earnest in the doing. A man has his heart in the thing which he gets up early to accomplish.
I. MORNING RELIGION IS REFRESHING TO THE SOUL. Because then thought is free and emotion lively, and there is a bright and cheerful tone on all that is said and done. When wearied with the day and its toils and care, religious meditation easily becomes gloomy, the fatigued body flinging its shadows over all the expressions of the spirit. Give the freshness of morning thoughts to God, and that service will surely come back on you as refreshing.
II. MORNING RELIGION IS ACCEPTABLE TO GOD. Because it shows him that we are in earnest in his service, and hold our very best as the fitting gift to offer to him. "The flower that’s offered in the bud is the best sacrifice." That is as true of the day as of the life. And God may be expected to estimate our gifts in the light of what they cost us to present to him. That is our way of appraising the gifts which we receive, and we may be sure that it is God’s way. What, then, is God’s estimate of our daily praise and thanksgiving? Does it really cost us much? It does if, for it, we awake early; preventing the day lest we should lose our holy opportunity, or be beneath our best and freshest in our communions.
III. MORNING RELIGION IS INFLUENTIAL ON OTHERS. It is one of the most effective and impressive examples; and it has a special influence on the young, helping them to form good life-habits. Many of us can gratefully remember the influence of the early morning devotions of our parents. Let us gain the power on others which they have gained on us.—R.T.
Psa_108:6
Hope and prayer inspired by praise.
In this verse we trace the influence which the spirit and utterance of praise has upon the psalmist. It leads to prayer, and gives him confidence in prayer.
I. PRAISING GOD BRINGS HOME TO US GOD’S RELATIONS TO US, AND OUR RELATIONS TO GOD. Praising God for what he has done convinces us of his kindly feeling toward us and interest in us, so that we may even think and speak of ourselves as God’s beloved. This may be regarded as David’s way of thinking of himself; but a similar appropriation of the Divine love we may make. It is the realization of our Father’s personal love to us that fills us with hope, and gives us confidence to pray. We never think of putting God under any constraint of prayer. We pray as children make their requests of parents who love them.
II. PRAISING GOD BECOMES AN INSPIRATION TO PRAYER FOR FURTHER BLESSINGS.
1. It gives us argument. For we only praise because we know that God has answered our prayers. It is really for those answers that we offer prayer. Once let it be established in our hearts that God is the prayer-hearing and prayer-answering God, and we have the all-sufficing ground on which to seek him in every form of new distress and need. Praise is only possible when we fully recognize reasons for praise.
2. It gives us the feeling that makes us long to pray, and so gain yet more reason to praise. Praise and prayer are indissolubly linked together. No man will pray long who gives up praising, and no man will keep up his praise who neglects his praying. If we find ourselves hesitating about praying for what we newly need, the best thing to do is to set about praising for the blessings we have received. Just as it was with the psalmist, so it will be with us. Let praise do its work, and it will be sure to lead in prayer.—R.T.
Psa_108:7
Conscious strength through God’s pledge.
The construction of this and the three following verses is somewhat difficult to trace. It may be that the verses are the things that God "spoke in his holiness." But it is simpler to treat the verses as expressions of what the psalmist feels he can do, and means to endeavor to do, basing his confidence on the fact that "God has spoken in his holiness" has made promise and pledge to him; and God’s pledges, he is sure, are holy, inviolate, certain of fulfillment. In relation to David, the promise to secure for him the full sovereignty of the nation is probably referred to (2Sa_7:1-29.) "In his holiness" means, "in the immutable integrity of his heart," which was an infallible guarantee for the fulfillment of his promise. The key-note of this portion of the psalm is the fact that the promises of God sent by Nathan to David ensured the establishment of the Davidic dynasty over the kingdom of Israel. But when the original of the psalm was composed, David had all the work before him. The northern portion of Canaan had to be won; neighboring nations had to be subdued, or put under tribute. But the promise gave him conscious strength, made him feel superior to his responsibilities; able even to speak lightly, almost scornfully, of those whose conquest would involve hard toil and fighting (see figures of Psa_108:9).
I. FROM HOLD OF GOD’S PROMISE GIVES US CONSCIOUS SUPERIORITY TO LIFE’S DIFFICULTIES. This is true, whether our difficulties come from our circumstances or our sins. We have Divine promises that we shall finally master both our surroundings and ourselves, winning the whole kingdom of our being for righteousness. What keeps us full of good cheer? Not our evident successes, but our grip of the Divine promises. In God’s word and pledge, we rise above our circumstances and above our sins. We feel no sort of fear; we shall "come off more than conquerors."
II. FIRM HOLD OF GOD’S PROMISE GIVES US CONSCIOUS STRENGTH TO CARRY OUT OUR RESOLVES. David meant to win Moab, Edom, Philistia, etc.; and he knew he could because God had spoken. There is no sense of strength to accomplish life-purposes ever comes to a man like that he knows when he feels God is at his back.—R.T.
Psa_108:11
God with us assures confidence and victory.
What "casting off" is here referred to by the psalmist no one seems to have satisfactorily explained. The best suggestion, perhaps, is that the sentiments of a returned exile are here interwoven with the sentiments of David. The idea of God, as one who had cast off his people for awhile, is quite suitable to a returned exile, but quite unsuitable to David. The thought is, however, found in the original of this psalm (Psa_60:1); and if we must connect it with David, it is necessary to assume that he suffered some temporary repulse in the beginning of his national wars, and that, in a gloomy, poetic way, he regarded this as "God casting off his people." A good writer on Psa_9:1-20. says, "From the first five verses we should gather that the country had been crushed by some great national disaster." One is forcibly reminded of two scenes in the national history.
I. THE ANXIETY 
OF MOSES ABOUT GOD GOING WITH ISRAEL. Recall the expressions of Divine indignation in the matter of the golden calf. The purpose was, as it were half formed, to cast off a people who were showing themselves so unfaithful to the trust reposed in them. Moses interceded. The evident burden on his heart was the possibility that God might not himself go with them; and he passionately pleaded, "If thy presence go not with me, carry us not up hence." Well he knew that "God with us assures confidence and victory."
II. THE ANXIETY OF JOSHUA ABOUT GOD GOING WITH ISRAEL. When the covenant was broken, through the covetousness of Achan, God for a time withdrew his defense and help, cast off his people, with the result that the army was defeated, and the whole expedition placed in jeopardy. Joshua was terribly distressed. It seemed to him (not knowing the real cause of the disaster) that the very Name of God was being dishonored, and he passionately pleaded for that restoration of God’s presence and power which alone could give confidence and victory. The history of God’s people furnishes abundant illustrations of the same truth; and it was sealed for ever, as the truth of truths for helpless man, when the ascending Jesus gave his assurance, "Lo, I am with you all the days."—R.T.
HOMILIES BY C. SHORT
Psa_108:1-13
This psalm consists of portions of two others, the first half of it being taken from the fifty-seventh psalm (Psa_108:7-11), and the latter half from the sixtieth (Psa_108:5-12). The notes on these two other psalms may be consulted.—S.

On the ongoing obfuscation of terrorist crimes in Syria under Jolani’s rule  https://t.co/mJsR5cUrsz 

As recent posting on social media is once again hyping up alleged atrocities of the Assad government (to obfuscate on the ongoing atrocities of the Jolani terrorist regime in Syria), let's revisit one of the very hyped places in 2016/17, Madaya, where media and social media claimed Assad was starving civilians. As it turned out, just like in Homs, in Aleppo districts, al-Waer (Homs), Douma and other towns in eastern Ghouta, etc, it was the terrorist factions who hoarded food—including aid sent or allowed in by the Assad government—& either didn't share it with the civilians they held as human shields, or sold it at massively inflated prices no one could afford.

I went to each of these regions and spoke with civilians whose testimonies countered the claims of foreign media. Following are excerpts from an article I wrote in 2017 after going to both Madaya & al-Waer:

"...During my visit in June, I met with Syria’s Minister of Reconciliation, Dr. Ali Haidar (who I interviewed in 2014). Established by Syria in June 2012, the Ministry has successfully dialogued with 10s of 1000s of armed Syrians to enable & facilitate return to their civilian lives

Haidar explained that an agreement was reached at the end of 2015 that included Madaya, nearby Zabadani, and the Idlib villages Foua and Kafraya. 

…Adjacent to a munitions factory used by armed groups in Madaya, I found packaging of an ICRC-supported food parcel, a remnant of repeated aid convoys sent into the town. As in eastern Aleppo, in Madaya armed extremists hoarded food and medicines.

Owing to the presence of Ahrar al-Sham, al-Nusra and other groups, from around mid-2015 Madaya was under Syrian military siege. As noted in Part One of this series, siege is a common tactic of wars past, and one that the United States employed in Iraq (for example, the more than four-year siege of Sadr City).

The military sieges came with offers of amnesty to those armed Syrian men who hadn’t committed bloodshed, or safe passage to another area of Syria for those who refused reconciliation, including the non-Syrian extremists. During the siege, the Syrian government did continue to send in aid to Madaya, and continued to also approve the provision of aid from the ICRC, UN and other bodies, including in October 2015.

...Entering a small shop selling clothing, I was welcomed and offered apricots from a pail on the counter. The Madaya-Zabadani region is known for its rich agriculture and tasty fruits. It is also an area to which people from Damascus and environs would retreat in the summer, to picnic on farmland or to eat at one of the restaurants along the road leading to the towns.

According to Madaya’s mayor, the main armed factions that had been present were the terrorist groups of Ahrar al-Sham, al-Nusra and the FSA. 

I asked whether people had protested the presence of other militants. “Yes,” they said, “there were protests against the armed groups, and in support of the government, asking the government to come to Madaya."...

To my question whether Western media was right, that the Syrian government had starved them, the four men answered ‘no’ in unison, talking over one another to make their point.

[WATCH VIDEO HERE]

“It was not the government that starved us, it was the armed groups,” a middle-aged man said.

“We received aid convoys, but the armed groups would steal the supplies and monopolize them.”
He said he had sold his car in order to buy overpriced food from Ahrar al-Sham and al-Qaeda: “They sold us a kilogram of rice for 100,000 Syrian pounds.”

At current exchange rates, this came to around US$200.

An older man nicknamed Abu Sharif said repeatedly that militants had hoarded food and extorted civilians, and added: “After the Syrian army entered, they found 50 storage units of food, also medicine. They are still uncovering storages.” According to this man, the militants also stole jewelry from women, and forced them to dress fully covered. “They called us ‘kuffars’ and said we weren’t real Muslims.”

...Further on among the hillside dwellings, we stood near an apartment that had been occupied, one floor turned into a prison to hold locals until their fates (including execution) were decided in terrorists’ Sharia trials.

Nestled behind the apartment, out of view, was a factory where terrorists manufactured mortars and rockets. Above that factory, one of the food storage caches was found after militants had left Madaya. 

Watch | Hidden factory where mortars and rockets were manufactured by terrorists

Down the lane, another villa had also been used as a headquarters and prison until it was hit by Syrian army shelling, forcing the “rebels” to relocate. Another mass food storage was found in a neighboring building, the mayor said.

Entering the relocated prison through a hole blown into the wall, I walked past a room containing a cooking stove and refrigerator, both booby-trapped by terrorists to kill whoever tried to move them. I had learned of this tactic in 2014 in the old city of Homs.

Watch |Visit to the relocated prison

“They left booby-trapped explosives in the houses, all over, even behind paintings on the wall,” I was told. Similarly, in Maaloula in June 2016, I was told: “They rigged houses so that when someone opened the door, an electrical trigger with a small charge would detonate and explode a gas canister.”

Two rooms, metal doors welded onto the entrances, had been used as cells. In the middle of another room, a metal bed frame with a piece of cloth tethered at one end. 

“They interrogated and tortured people here,” a former FSA militant said. An unwilling participant, he said he was forced by other militants to join, and that he was among the first to take the government-offered amnesty when peace was restored to Madaya in May 2017.

In neighboring Buqayn, Ahrar al-Sham transformed the municipality building into a prison, fortified with sandbagging and bricks. The dank cells were sealed with the same solid metal doors.

A soft-spoken employee of the municipality, limping as he walked, came over to tell me how he was shot at close range. Leaning on a crutch with prayer beads wrapped around the handle, he explained his injury. Recounting that terrorists had shot at the truck he and three others were in, he said, “the driver was killed and we were all injured. … We were subject to shooting many times.”

Watch | Municipal employee describes being shot by terrorists as part of intimidation campaign

The reason for the attacks? To intimidate them from returning to work at the municipality. Three surgeries later, still needing another, the man said his wounded leg is now seven centimeters shorter than his good leg.

Below and beyond the village, in a sitting room away from the June sun, a farmer-turned-soldier, still wearing his military uniform, spoke of why he took up arms in support of the Syrian army:

Life was good here, we were living well. When things turned violent in the area, I and other men from the area volunteered to support the Syrian army.”

He and others warned Madaya locals not to fall for the political game that originated from America, Israel, Turkey and others, he said — also pointing out that sectarianism was never a way for most Syrians, that it came from Saudi Arabia and other outside forces…

THE ARTICLE CONTINUES WITH AL-WAER, HOMS: https://t.co/8WZTnNC9DK

This is just one report (or two if you continue reading) from an area heavily propagandized about by Western and Gulf media, to incriminate the Syrian army and government. text:
Dark magic drew power from other sources. Blood. Pain. Sacrifice. Necromancy offered him something more. A soul retained traces of its magic after death. Tharn argued that allowing such power to pass beyond reach was a waste. His earliest experiments used the lingering echoes within old bones. Later, he learned to summon spirits, bind them and draw their strength into himself. Each stolen fragment increased the power available to him. Soon, the limits recorded at his Awakening no longer applied.

NuNew’s fingers tighten around the edge of the page.

By the time the academy discovered what Tharn was doing, several bodies had disappeared from burial sites. The mages sent to detain him never returned. Three days later, witnesses saw them walking behind him.

NuNew closes his eyes. When he could bear to continue, he reads more.

Tharn promised freeborn mages access to powers the ancient Houses could never inherit. He promised recognition to overlooked scholars and a place beside him to anyone tired of being told that their gifts were insufficient. To the grieving, he offered something even harder to refuse. The Return of their loved ones. Thousands joined him. They taught him that power determined a person’s worth, NuNew’s ancestor has written. He chose to answer by making himself powerful enough that nobody could refuse him.

Tharn began calling himself the King of the Dead. Those who willingly surrendered their lives became soldiers. Those who resisted him joined the same army by force. Villages were emptied, burial grounds stripped, and every soul he bound added to the strength of the man commanding them.

NuNew turns a page and finds a list of settlements. Besides several names, there is only a brief notation. No known survivors. He sits very still for a bit and then forces himself to keep reading.

The bodies Tharn raised continued to decay. Stronger spells could hold them together for longer but could not restore the decaying flesh to that of living. Bound souls weakened beneath the strain of his command, forcing him to seek replacements. He could compel the dead to move but he could not truly heal them. No matter how powerful his necromancy became, Tharn could imitate life but never truly create it.

Beneath that passage, his ancestor has drawn the crest of a pearl mage. NuNew’s stomach tightens.

Only a pearl mage could do that. Pearl magic can restore what he cannot. In the hands of a willing mage or under coercion, this legacy gift could be used to maintain the bodies he commands.

The next sentence is written more heavily, as though the pen pressed hard over each word.

He must never be permitted to command the bearer of pearl magic.

NuNew reads it twice. Then he looks down at his hands. The instructor had known. ‘You aren’t weak. They don’t understand what you are. I can help you.’

NuNew had believed he was finally being seen. Instead he was used. NuNew was not merely the key capable of opening Tharn’s prison. His power was the final thing Tharn needed to restore his dead army permanently, creating soldiers who would never decay and could never truly die.
It was why Tharn’s followers spent generations waiting for pearl magic to return. Opening the prison was probably only the first thing they needed him for.

He does not want to think about it. He cannot afford not to. NuNew turns to the account of Tharn’s defeat.

A pearl mage possessed the power to restore what death had taken, while a shadow mage could sever the chains holding a soul and return it to its proper resting place. Together, they were the only two forces capable of undoing Tharn’s necromancy. As the dead were released, Tharn’s stolen power diminished. Only then could the shadow mage recite the incantations preserved within the Book of Death and imprison him beneath the earth in a crypt. Which was then reinforced by the pearl mage +

PHANEROO MINISTRIES INTERNATIONAL DEVOTION

Wednesday, 9th September 2026 

By Apostle Grace Lubega

1 Timothy 2:1 (NKJV): "Therefore I exhort first of all that supplications, prayers, intercessions, and giving of thanks be made for all men."

FAMILY SERIES: THE DUTY TO PRAY FOR YOUR FAMILY

When the Apostle Paul urges us to pray for "all people," the scope of that command begins far closer to home than many realize. While we may readily pray for our immediate household, our spouses, and children, many believers completely overlook their duty to intercede for their extended family. Somewhere along the line, a disconnect occurs, and we forget that our spiritual responsibility extends to the many who are part of our family.

Too often, our response to trouble in the extended family is purely natural rather than spiritual. When news arrives that a relative is battling a severe illness, the best many can offer is a brief expression of pity or sympathy. When a niece or nephew falls into drug addiction or alcohol abuse, the immediate reaction is often to critique the parents' methods or gossip about the family's decline. It rarely occurs to us to fall to our knees in earnest intercession. We witness long-standing generational cycles: recurring divorces, chronic poverty, premature deaths, or obvious spiritual oppression, yet we remain oddly unconcerned, treating these patterns as mere bad luck or unavoidable family traits.

God did not place you in your family by accident; He positioned you there as a watchman. You have a sacred obligation to stand in the gap for your relatives. Pity will not break an addiction, and criticism will not stop negative cycles. Only Spirit-led prayer can usher in God’s healing and redemption. It is time to wake up to your duty. Look beyond your immediate walls, take stock of the spiritual state of your entire family, and begin to stand in the gap for them.

FURTHER STUDY: Joshua 24:15; 1 Samuel 12:23

GOLDEN NUGGET: God did not place you in your family by accident; He positioned you there as a watchman. Look beyond your immediate walls, take stock of the spiritual state of your entire family, and begin to stand in the gap for them.

I pray for every relative struggling with disease, addiction, broken marriages, or financial hardship. I pray that You send labourers to those that must be saved and if no labourer is found, make me a worthy one. Open their hearts to the Gospel, and draw them by Your mercy. In Jesus' name, Amen.

text:
I am 28, and I have this neighbour in her mid-40s who lives alone and is very introverted. She is always in the house, with her doors and windows usually shut. The scary thing is that she lives alone but drives herself to work.

Sometime back in June, I greeted her, “Good morning, ma’am,” as she drove off the gate and she replied in a warm, soft voice. I didn’t even expect that, considering how quiet she always is and how much she minds her own business.I think this was the genesis of my worries. 

So, here is what makes this turning point interesting—and a little scary.

I don’t have a car yet. For the past month, she has been friendly, and seemingly, I’m the only person she talks to in the whole apartment estate. She offers me a ride to work every morning because she also works in the same direction as I do. The same happens in the evening. As a result, I’ve managed saved KSh 7,000 in transport costs from my peanut salary.

However, I feel quite uncomfortable in her car. She keeps asking me why I’m so timid. Sometimes, she insists that I sit in the front seat. At other times, I drive, and she insists on entering our company compound and dropping me right in front of the office before driving off.

I’m afraid the office ladies, who are my colleagues, will soon start biting me. 😰 Imagine having to wake up at 4 a.m. even though we report to work at 8:30 a.m., just to fit into her schedule.

My biggest goal and achievement in all this is the money I’m saving.

But this whole situation has been bothering me, especially because my wife works in a different city and usually comes home on weekends and her days off. This woman seems like a caring motherly figure, but then again, you never really know someone’s intentions.

What should I do?
