text:
Early 20s are crucial because you find out what being a man is all about.

And you have a choice, to either embrace it, or run from it.

What you choose, defines you as a human for the rest of your life.

You move out of the shell that you were raised in. Physically, it means that you leave your home, either for college or for a job. You leave the city that you were raised in, you leave the streets that you played in, you leave the comfort of knowing all that was around you. You get into an unfamiliar place, where people are unknown, intentions are unclear, direction is yet to be searched for. You find out quickly just how much work goes into living a life, and I am not even talking about the job you now have that you once dreamt of.

Okay, you got a place to stay. Well who's coming to cook for you? Who's going to take care of the dishes after you are done? God forbid your lodgings don't have a washing machine, because it's either a 2-hour slog on the weekends, or a fat 300 rupee bill a week at the cleaners. Okay, you got a cut, bruise, scratch or an injury. 
Who knows what to do about it? 
What if you are down by a fever? 
Do you even know what pills to take? 
Or do you trust the local chemist-oh wait, you don't even know where that is.

You have a thousand thoughts that surround your head, loom over you for every second of your existence, you don't understand what's happening to you cause it's never been like this before. The storm that pours over your mindspace becomes impossible to ignore, you start coasting through your days, hours feel like minutes, night and day feels like it's one and the same, the routine chokes the little semblance of creativity left in you, and you look around yourself and find out that you don't know who to talk to about it all. 

You call up that one friend of yours and find out that he or she is too busy to sit and hear you out for more than 5 minutes, your siblings try as much as they can but they cannot seem to just get it, and you have a paralyzing dread about mentioning it, it even in passing to your colleagues.

And Mother sure as hell ain't around anymore to drop all that she's been doing, and sort it out for you.

Oh and that job you slogged so damn hard to get? Well, that's yours now. Congratulations laddie, now come put in these 80 hours over 6 days because your boss told you so, even if it says 48 hours in a week on that little offer letter you signed before you even anything apart from the salary breakup because you that so damn excited. Wait, did I say 6? Hell yeah I said 6, what did you think this was, school? Where you get your weekends off? With no stress? LMAOOO. 

And you can forget about what the role says on your offer letter. You are going to do what's needed of you, regardless of you knowing how to do what you are asked of. "Top-performers" figure it out, they said. You need to find a way and get it done, they said. WHY THE FUCK AREN'T YOU DOING IT RIGHT, they will say.

Now get back home and collapse onto your bed, and you scroll your phone for less than a damn second, and you are bombarded with adverts for clubbing and drinks, and DJs, and dances. Your colleagues have been pushing HARD for a "team bonding" activity too, and you somehow decide that going out for drinks with the people you work is a great idea. You start slipping into the escape that a glass provides to you, because for those 3 hours on a Friday night, nothing seems to matter. The DJ blasts the most popular reels music of the week on the speakers, there are baddies in the club dancing and they have not a care for the world if you join in, so you do. 

You wake up on the weekends all fucked up, and before you are fully sober, well, it's Monday again. You coast through it all for a year or so, and then the landlord shows up one day, saying that rent's up by 15%. You look at your savings account, and you hear it laughing back at you. And your appraisal? Let's not even talk about that. And God forbid if something breaks down. The fridge that's been installed since the last 15 years by your homeowner is now bust, the fan's capacitor blew out, you wake up and find out that the water is now cut off, your bike's engine refuses to crank, or the tires have holes in them, and you are fucked. What on earth are you supposed to do now?

And father sure as hell ain't around anymore to drop all that she's been doing, and sort it out for you.

Early 20s are crucial because you find out what being a man is all about.

And you have a choice, to either embrace it, or run from it.

Now you can either run form it all, or choose to fix and find a way.

What, you thought I was going to preach here about "how did I find a way through my own turmoil". Hell no, because I don't think I have. I am fucking 23 man, and this was all that I could pen down in 30 minutes. 

There is so, so much more that ravages my mind on the daily, y'all. Loans on the family, a non-existent love-life, career questions, the perennial "Am I good enough?", and so, so much more. But you see, it's a Wednesday morning for me. And I gotta be out the gate in the next 14 minutes, because I have a job to do.

All I know, is that as long as I have a source of income, a roof over the top of my head, and a functioning body and mind - all shall be figured out. All NEEDS to, HAS to be figured out. 

That's the only correct way to live life, fighting all that plagues me, as long as I continue to draw breath. Long ass post at the start of the day, I know.

Do let me know if you actually read through it, I gotta personally thank you for it.

Cheers boys. At the end of the day, you got this. And if you don't, well, the day ain't over yet.

text:
Step aboard a rare survivor of America’s floating lighthouse era with Lightship WAL-605, Relief. Built in 1950, this distinctive vessel served as a relief lightship, temporarily taking the place of other lightships when they were undergoing repairs or maintenance.

Before modern navigational technology, lightships were anchored in dangerous waters where constructing a permanent lighthouse was impossible. Equipped with powerful lights, fog signals, radio equipment, and a highly visible hull, Relief helped guide ships safely past hazardous coastal areas while her crew endured long periods stationed offshore.

Today, the preserved vessel offers a fascinating glimpse into the lives of the sailors who kept America’s maritime highways safe before satellites and automated navigation systems changed the profession.

Little-known fact: Unlike most lightships, Relief did not have one permanent station. Because she was designed as a substitute vessel, she could be sent to multiple locations along the coast whenever another lightship needed to leave its post.

Veterinarian Authors: Publishing Trends to Watch

A veterinarian can spot the difference between a worried dog and a merely dramatic one. That close observation, paired with years spent listening to people talk about the animals they love, is becoming a genuine storytelling advantage. Veterinarian authors publishing trends point to a growing appetite for books that bring animal knowledge to the page without losing warmth, humor, or a good old-fashioned mystery.

For readers who adore dogs, cats, small towns, and clever characters, this is especially good news. Veterinary experience gives an author a treasure chest of details: the odd things pets swallow, the quiet loyalty between an animal and its person, the medical clues hidden in behavior, and the surprising ways a community gathers around a beloved creature. The best books do not read like a lecture from the exam room. They use that knowledge to make the fictional world feel true.

## Why Veterinary Experience Has Become a Storytelling Strength

Readers have always loved animal stories, but many now want more than a cute pet added to the background. They want animals with presence. They want to understand why a dog hesitates at a doorway, why a cat avoids a certain person, or how a change in appetite might matter. A veterinarian author can write those moments with confidence, then let the story do what stories do best: stir curiosity and feeling.

That authority is particularly useful in cozy mysteries. In a traditional whodunit, readers enjoy collecting clues alongside the sleuth. Animal behavior can add a fresh layer to that game. A muddy paw print, an unusual scent, a frightened horse, or a dog who refuses to approach a familiar shed may not solve the case alone. Still, each observation can nudge an investigation in a new direction.

The trick is restraint. Too much technical language can slow a mystery faster than a sleepy basset hound in summer. The most inviting veterinarian-authored fiction translates expertise into clear, lively scenes. Readers should feel that they have learned something almost by accident, while following characters they want to visit again.

## Veterinarian Authors Publishing Trends in Fiction

One clear trend is the rise of animal-centered cozy fiction with real-world texture. These stories are not necessarily about veterinary medicine, although a clinic can make a wonderful setting. Instead, they place animals at the center of community life. A rescue fundraiser, a pet parade, a boarded horse, or a missing show dog can bring together suspects with motives, secrets, and muddy shoes.

Another trend is the animal narrator or animal-adjacent point of view. This approach works because pet lovers already spend a great deal of time wondering what their companions are thinking. A dog narrator can be funny, observant, and deeply loyal, while still misunderstanding human habits in charming ways. That balance lets writers offer wit without making the animal sound like a person wearing a fur coat.

The Doc and Daisy Mysteries make room for this kind of perspective, pairing veterinary know-how with Daisy's canine observations and a Florida small-town mystery. A dog can notice what people overlook, but a satisfying story still needs human sleuths who can ask questions, weigh evidence, and make brave choices.

https://t.co/Vdc6kr9qrJ

Veterinarian authors are also finding readers across multiple categories. Cozy mysteries may be the natural home for gentle suspense and pet-loving communities, yet animal fiction, children's books, memoirs, and narrative nonfiction all offer opportunities. A veterinarian who writes for children may turn an everyday clinic visit into reassurance. One who writes fiction for adults may use the same professional insight to make a rescue dog, aging cat, or anxious owner feel fully alive.

## Readers Want Comfort, But Not Empty Calories

Cozy readers often come for the comfort of a welcoming town, recurring friends, and a mystery that will be solved. They stay when a series gives them emotional substance. Veterinary authors are well positioned to provide it because their work has brought them close to life's tender edges: new puppies, old companions, recoveries, goodbyes, and the everyday courage of people caring for another living creature.

Still, warmth is not the same as sadness. Pet loss can be meaningful in fiction, but it must be handled with care, especially for readers seeking a lighter escape. Some authors choose to keep animal peril off the page. Others include it only when it serves an honest purpose and resolve it gently. Neither choice is automatically better. The right decision depends on the promise a series makes to its readers.

That promise matters in book descriptions, cover design, and conversations with fans. A mystery featuring canine forensics may have a playful edge, but readers should know whether they are stepping into a breezy puzzle, an emotional animal story, or a darker crime novel. Clear expectations build trust, and trust brings readers back for the next installment.

## The Return of the Personal Author Connection

Publishing has become more crowded, which makes an authentic author identity more valuable. Readers enjoy knowing why a writer understands a subject. For a retired veterinarian, that background is not a marketing costume. It is a well of experience that can shape characters, setting, and the small details that make readers smile in recognition.

The strongest author presence does not need to shout, "Look at my credentials." It can simply share a favorite animal observation, explain the inspiration for a fictional case, or offer a behind-the-scenes glimpse of how veterinary experience informed a scene. Readers who love animals tend to respond to sincerity. They can tell the difference between a story that uses a puppy as decoration and one that understands the bond between people and pets.

Direct communication also suits series fiction. Readers may want news about the next case, a peek at a returning character, or a note about the real animal habits that inspired a fictional clue. This relationship is especially meaningful for cozy mystery fans, who often enjoy settling into a familiar fictional town as much as they enjoy finding the culprit.

## Smart Details Beat a Textbook Approach

For veterinary professionals considering authorship, the publishing trend worth watching is not simply "write what you know." It is "write what readers can feel." Clinical experience is useful when it produces a sharper scene, a more believable reaction, or an unexpected clue. It is less useful when it pauses the plot for a full explanation that no character would naturally give.

A few well-chosen details can do plenty of work. The sound of nails clicking nervously on a clinic floor may reveal a dog's fear. A veterinarian's practiced calm can show readers that an emergency is serious before anyone says so. A character who remembers a client's pet food, favorite toy, and shy habit tells us something about kindness without a speech.

Accuracy remains essential, of course. Readers may forgive a fictional town with an unusually busy festival calendar, but they notice when animal behavior or basic care feels careless. Yet accuracy does not mean every procedure belongs on the page. The story should keep its nose pointed toward character, question, and consequence.

## What This Means for the Next Animal-Loving Read

The future looks bright for stories that combine professional knowledge with a generous heart. Readers are looking for books that respect animals as more than props, welcome them into mysteries and family stories, and remember that a small detail from a warm snout can sometimes change everything.

Whether the tale follows a veterinarian, a curious dog, or a neighbor with a suspiciously muddy pair of boots, the most memorable books will keep one paw in truth and the other in delight. That is a fine path for any reader to follow home.

I finally understand your disconnect.

Your bio says Eisenhower/Teddy Roosevelt moderate, but your argument is basically:

“Government can take considerably more of your money—as long as it gives you enough benefits back, you’re more free and have a better quality of life.”

That’s not how I define freedom.

A government benefit isn’t free. You paid for it.

And there’s an enormous difference between keeping your money and choosing how to provide for yourself versus surrendering more of it to government and letting politicians decide what benefits you’ll receive, who qualifies, what they’ll cover and how they’ll be delivered.

You see a 25% VAT, high income taxes and a large welfare state and say, “Look what they get.”

I say, look what they had to surrender control over to get it.

Healthcare may be government-funded. College may be heavily subsidized. Childcare may be subsidized. Those can be valuable benefits.

But benefits and freedom are not synonyms.

My idea of freedom is earning a dollar and having the strongest possible claim to that dollar—not government taking a bigger share and convincing me I’m better off because it chose something useful to buy with it.

That’s the philosophical difference between us.

And here’s where your Scandinavian argument becomes especially easy to resolve:

You already have the freedom to choose the system you keep praising.

If Scandinavia’s combination of much higher taxation and much greater government provision represents a superior quality of life to you, go experience it. I genuinely wouldn’t object.

But you don’t get to insist Florida should become more like the place you won’t move to, while millions of people continue choosing Florida precisely because it offers a different bargain.

You want government to take more and provide more.

I want government to perform its essential functions, take less and leave me alone more.

Call yours Scandinavian. Call mine American.

But please don’t tell me greater dependence on government is greater freedom.

Eisenhower would probably want his bio back.

text:
Be Your Own Bank With Metals 🕯️🪽🤍

There is no regular bank that lets you drop gold and silver on the counter like cash, then treat the vault like a checking account. What exists is closer to this: you keep the metal, store it allocated in a real vault, pledge it as collateral, and borrow cash against it without selling. That is the working version of “be your own bank” for stackers.

These two are the strongest fits if you want liquidity, ownership of the metal, and as much distance as possible from the usual Wall Street / big-bank setup.

1. Money Metals Capital Group + Money Metals Depository  
**Eagle, Idaho**

Family-owned. Own Class 3 vault next to the county sheriff in a low-crime Idaho town. Segregated storage (your bars and coins stay yours). Insured through Lloyd’s.

You move eligible gold, silver, platinum, or palladium into their depository. They then offer a metals-backed line of credit. Typical advance has been in the 60–65% range of spot (they have advertised higher). Minimum loan around $15,000, going into the millions. Interest-only, revolving, no origination or prepayment fees in their published terms. They raised capital specifically to grow this loan book.

**Why it fits this community**  
Idaho. Family shop. Sound-money, limited-government, anti-fiat posture. The company and its founders have spent years pushing gold and silver as real money, not a collectible. The vault is physical, local, and easy to understand.

**Watch-outs**  
Not a chartered bank. Loan proceeds are generally for business or investment use, not living expenses or an immediate buy of more metal. Some borrowers have said the actual LTV came in lower than the marketing. Always get the current term sheet in writing.

---

### 2. Battle Bank — MELOC (Metals Equity Line of Credit)  
**FDIC-insured national bank**

This one is actually a bank. OCC-chartered, FDIC-insured on the cash side. Co-founded with involvement from Rick Rule. They store pledged metals at Brinks under their control and lend against allocated gold and silver.

Revolving 5-year interest-only line. They lend up to about 50% of market value. Collateral minimums have been in the $75,000–$100,000 range depending on the product sheet. Rate is Prime plus 2.75% with auto-pay (higher without it). No credit check. Annual fee on the unused line. Cash can go to a Battle Bank account or another bank.

**Why it fits**  
Real bank charter and capital structure. Built for self-directed people who do not want the usual big-bank product menu. Metals stay yours; you borrow against them instead of selling.

**Watch-outs**  
Lower LTV than some private lenders. Metals themselves are not FDIC-insured. More digital / New York-rooted than heartland conservative. Still a regulated bank, which some stackers will like and some will not.

---

How to think about this

- You keep title to the metal.  
- Borrowing is not a sale, so it is not a taxable event the way selling would be.  
- You still pay interest, storage, and (on a line) fees.  
- If the metal price drops hard, you can face a margin call or liquidation. Read that part twice.  
- “Large capital” and “can’t be messed with” are relative. An Idaho Class 3 vault next to the sheriff and a state-chartered Texas depository are harder for distant offices to treat casually than a paper promise. Nothing is invulnerable.

**Texas Bullion Depository** is worth a third look for storage only: state-run, segregated, Lloyd’s, Texas oversight. It does not run its own loan program, but you can pledge the account to a lender on their form.

Amazon just made the Netherlands non-optional for Pan-EU FBA.

From tomorrow, September 3, every Pan-EU SKU new and existing must have an active offer on https://t.co/iE0WJAZxfy

or it drops out of the program.

This is phase two, not a surprise. New ASINs have needed a .nl offer since June 2025. Tomorrow is when Amazon comes for the back catalog. Belgium follows on February 26, 2027, required at enrollment.

Two things worth saying out loud:

Listing isn't storing. The .nl offer requirement doesn't create a Dutch VAT registration on its own storage does. Local fee treatment still tracks your inventory placement, with Germany as the usual anchor.

And Bol still owns the Benelux shopper. ~13M active customers across NL and BE. Amazon can buy assortment. It can't buy that habit.

Now the part US and Canadian sellers keep missing.

North America never built a Pan-EU clone. US, CA and MX FBA are three separate inventory pools. Amazon's workaround was remote fulfillment: keep stock in Texas, sell into Canada, Mexico and Brazil with a Prime badge. Sellers were auto-enrolled on April 11, 2024, after a 30-day opt-out window.

Europe: list in the small store or lose cheap fulfillment.

North America: we'll list you in the small store from your US bin unless you opt out.

Different mechanism. Same goal fill a thin marketplace with inventory that already exists.

The 2026 twist is the border.

The US put 50% Section 338 tariffs on a broad slice of Canadian goods on August 22. Canada is matching on C$27.6B of US goods from September 8, 15%, 25% or 50%, covering apparel, appliances, electronics, beauty and personal care, cooking appliances, seafood.

Here's the nuance most people are getting wrong: it only bites goods that are US-origin under CUSMA marking rules.

If you import from Asia into a US FC, Canada's countermeasure isn't your problem, and the CAD$150 courier de minimis still shelters most parcels. If you actually manufacture in the US, it is your problem and surtaxed goods lose de minimis entirely. Small parcel, full surtax.

Which is why "PanAmericas," Amazon's Expand to Canada program, stopped reading like an upsell this year.

Checklist:

EU: reconcile Pan-EU SKUs against live .nl offers today. "No detail page" is an exception, not a strategy.

 US: pull your Remote Fulfillment ASIN eligibility report. Sort by country of origin, not by category.

 Canada: decide what needs to sit in a Canadian FC before Q4, not after the first duty invoice.

 Pricing: Build International Listings auto-prices for FX and fees, but it doesn't know what a Dutch or Canadian shopper will actually pay. Auto-created offers in price-sensitive stores teach the algorithm the wrong number.

Temu recruits SMEs by promising to open new countries for them.

 Amazon opens the small countries using the program you already depend on.

One is a pitch. One is leverage.

If you run FBA: is https://t.co/iE0WJAZxfy

a growth channel, or rent on the network? Same question for .ca.

52. AMGN: Amgen fell sharply as Novartis' failed Lp(a) cardiovascular trial raised read-through concerns for Amgen's olpasiran program.

53. DYN: Dyne Therapeutics fell nearly 18% after Novartis' myotonic-dystrophy failure raised doubts around related DM1 development approaches.

54. SRPT: Sarepta fell more than 9% as the Novartis DM1 setback weighed on companies developing RNA-based muscle-disease therapies.

55. PEPG: PepGen fell more than 5% as investors repriced DM1 programs following the Novartis trial failure.

👉 MANAGEMENT CHANGES

👉 GOVERNMENT CONTRACTS

64. QBTS/RGTI: D-Wave, Rigetti and Quantinuum each secured $100M CHIPS Act R&D agreements, with the U.S. government receiving minority non-controlling equity stakes.

65. GFS: GlobalFoundries' quantum-related U.S. funding includes manufacturing and photonics support designed to move quantum hardware from prototypes toward scaled domestic production.

👉 PRODUCT / PARTNERSHIPS

66. QCOM/AMZN: Qualcomm and Amazon will co-develop AI inference chips plus optical interconnect technologies reaching up to 1.6 Tbps for next-generation data centers.

67. HOOD: Robinhood will route prediction-market event contracts through https://t.co/amAp6tC5r3's CFTC-regulated exchange and clearinghouse under a multi-year agreement.

72. TTAN: ServiceTitan said its Max AI product adoption exceeded its Q2 doubling target and is now expected to surpass 700 enrolled locations by fiscal year-end.

👉 MARKET THEMES

73. SPY/QQQ/DIA: The S&P 500 fell 0.58% to 7,673.52, the Nasdaq lost 0.32% to 26,421.41 and the Dow dropped 1.18% to 52,786.07.

74. IWM: The Russell 2000 fell 0.5% to 2,960.20 as declining stocks broadly outnumbered gainers.

75. CRM/INTU/NOW: Salesforce and Intuit fell about 4% and ServiceNow lost 5% as OpenAI's GPT-6 Astra revived fears that general-purpose AI could compress specialized-software value.

76. INTC: Intel jumped 9%, helped by an analyst upgrade and reports of another roughly 10% CPU price increase as the company pushes margin recovery.

77. QCOM: Qualcomm gained 3.2% after the Amazon AI-data-center partnership validated its push beyond smartphones.

78. AAPL: Apple fell 1.2% one day before its September 9 product event as investors weighed premium-device demand and component-cost inflation.

79. AMGN: Amgen fell about 10%, its worst day in more than two decades, on negative Lp(a) read-through from Novartis and an analyst downgrade.

80. ROIV: Roivant surged roughly 20% after mosliciguat produced strong Phase 2 pulmonary-hypertension data.

81. PHVS: Pharvaris rallied after its pivotal oral HAE prophylaxis study delivered an 83% attack-rate reduction versus placebo.

82. BE: Bloom Energy jumped about 9.6% after being selected to join the S&P 500 on September 21.

83. BSX: Boston Scientific fell after warning its cyberattack would likely cause it to miss prior 2026 sales and profit guidance.

84. DYN/SRPT/PEPG: Rare-disease stocks sold off as Novartis' DM1 failure triggered a broad read-through across competing RNA and muscle-disease programs.

85. XLE/USO: Energy outperformed as Middle East hostilities pushed Brent toward $99.50 and revived inflation concerns.

86. BTC-USD/COIN/HOOD/MSTR: Bitcoin fell below roughly $78,500 and crypto-linked equities weakened as higher-rate expectations pressured speculative assets.

87. SOXX: Semiconductors outperformed software, reinforcing the market's current preference for AI infrastructure beneficiaries over application-layer incumbents.

88. SPX VALUATION: The S&P 500's forward P/E has compressed to about 19x expected earnings from roughly 21x in June even as 2026 index gains remain around 12%.

89. HSBC: HSBC raised its year-end S&P 500 target to 8,100 from 7,650, citing strong earnings and AI infrastructure investment despite rate and geopolitical risks.

👉 STOCKS TO WATCH

90. AAPL: Apple's September 9 event is the next mega-cap catalyst, with product mix, pricing and the expected foldable-device roadmap in focus.

91. CHWY: Chewy reports September 9 before the open, with Autoship, active customers and pet-spending resilience in focus.

92. AVAV: AeroVironment reports September 9 after the close, with drone demand, defense backlog and procurement visibility central to the read-through.

93. AEO: American Eagle reports September 9 after the close, with promotions, inventory and discretionary apparel demand in focus.

94. ORCL: Oracle reports September 10 after the close; OCI growth, AI backlog conversion, capex intensity and financing are the main variables.

95. ADBE: Adobe reports September 10 after the close, with AI monetization and ARR growth under scrutiny ahead of its CEO transition.

96. CPRT: Copart reports September 10 after the close, with salvage volumes, pricing and insurance claims in focus.

97. KR: Kroger reports September 11, offering a read on grocery inflation, traffic and consumer trade-down behavior.

98. CPI/PPI: U.S. producer and consumer inflation reports are the key macro catalysts before the September 15-16 Fed meeting.

99. QCOM: Investors will watch whether Amazon's purchase-linked warrant structure becomes a repeatable financing template for large AI infrastructure contracts.

100. NVS/AMGN: Biotech investors will reassess whether the pelacarsen failure is molecule-specific or undermines the broader Lp(a) cardiovascular thesis.

101. TTAN: ServiceTitan's post-close results put focus on slowing top-line growth versus improving margins and free cash flow.

👉 DEEP ANALYSIS / MARKET INTELLIGENCE

102. AI HARDWARE VS SOFTWARE: The clearest market split was not simply “AI up, AI down”: Intel rose 9% and Qualcomm gained on infrastructure demand, while CRM, INTU and NOW fell 4%-5% on GPT-6 Astra disruption fears. The key read-through is that investors are distinguishing between companies that sell scarce compute capacity and companies whose software functionality can be replicated by increasingly capable foundation models.

103. QUALCOMM CONTRACT ECONOMICS: Amazon can buy up to $60B of Qualcomm products while receiving about $4B of warrants that vest with purchases. That means the warrant value is roughly 6.7% of the maximum procurement commitment. This suggests Qualcomm is effectively spending equity optionality to accelerate customer adoption, similar to the increasingly intertwined financing structures appearing across AI infrastructure.

104. GE SUPPLY CHAIN: GE Aerospace is paying $11.75B for CPP, which is expected to generate about $2B of revenue by 2027. The deal is therefore roughly 5.9x that revenue estimate, a rich multiple for an industrial supplier but one that reflects the strategic value of removing a casting bottleneck from a multi-year engine backlog. The capital-cycle implication is that constrained upstream capacity is becoming valuable enough for OEMs to vertically integrate.

105. SOFTWARE VALUATION RESET: The S&P 500 forward multiple has fallen from about 21x in June to roughly 19x while HSBC simultaneously lifted its year-end index target to 8,100 on earnings strength. This creates an important contradiction: the broad market can still rise even if software multiples compress, provided earnings growth shifts toward semiconductors, infrastructure and other beneficiaries with stronger estimate revisions.

106. BIOTECH READ-THROUGH RISK: Novartis lost about $32B of market value after two pipeline failures, while Amgen, Dyne, Sarepta and PepGen sold off on cross-company read-throughs. At the same time Roivant and Pharvaris rallied on strong clinical data. This is a reminder that biotech beta can disappear quickly when investors move from platform narratives to target-level evidence; trial design and mechanism similarity matter more than sector labels.

107. GME EARNINGS QUALITY: GameStop's $298.7M net income looks dramatically stronger than the $790.2M revenue line, but about $238M of gains came from its eBay-related investment while core sales declined. Collectibles now represent roughly 45% of revenue, which is strategically meaningful, but investors should separate that operating mix shift from mark-to-market and investment gains when judging sustainable earnings power.

108. TTAN MARGIN INFLECTION: ServiceTitan's revenue growth slowed to 21% from 25% a year earlier, yet non-GAAP operating margin improved to 15.2% from 12.1% and free cash flow rose to $50.5M from $34.3M. The key read-through is that the company is starting to convert growth into operating leverage even as top-line growth normalizes; the risk is that stock-based compensation remains substantial and GAAP losses persist.

109. OIL + FED: Brent near $99.50 and a roughly 60% market-implied probability of a September rate hike create a difficult macro combination. Higher oil is an inflation shock rather than a clean demand signal, so it can pressure consumers and raise discount rates simultaneously. That is particularly hostile to long-duration software and other high-multiple assets unless CPI/PPI quickly cool the rate path.

Who and what organizations and unions oppose teaching usa school children that 9/11 happened because of Radical Islam?

The 19 hijackers and al-Qaeda leadership stated their motives in religious terms: jihad against the United States as the “far enemy,” U.S. troops in Saudi Arabia, support for Israel, and sanctions on Iraq. That ideology is a specific strain of Salafi-jihadism—what many analysts, commissions, and officials have called radical or extremist Islam.

==> Council on American-Islamic Relations (CAIR) is the most active. Its educator guides tell teachers to avoid “Islamic terrorists,” “jihadists,” and “radical Islamic terrorists”.

==> Teaching While Muslim (TWM), a New Jersey-based group of Muslim educators, co-produced the CAIR-NJ 9/11 curriculum (“The Impact of 9/11 on Muslims”). 

==> University of Pennsylvania Graduate School of Education’s “Teaching Beyond September 11th” curriculum (recommended by education departments in Pennsylvania, Massachusetts, Wisconsin, and Oregon) spends far more time on Islamophobia, right-wing extremism, Muslim surveillance, and the “Muslim ban” than on the attackers’ ideology. It refers to bin Laden as someone the U.S. “accused.” Developers have ties to social-justice nonprofits and Islamophobia-research centers.

==> Islamic Networks Group (ING) and the Family & Youth Institute issue similar “culturally responsive” guides: do not explore the definition of terrorism or a “clash of cultures,” and do not use the forbidden terms.

==> Zinn Education Project / Rethinking Schools (closely tied to the NEA) offer lessons such as “Whose ‘Terrorism’?” that invite students to compare U.S. and Israeli actions with 9/11, plus units on the War on Terror, the Patriot Act, and “disaster capitalism.” They treat U.S. power as the central problem.

==> Teachers unions <==

> National Education Association (NEA), the largest union, has a long record of materials that stress tolerance and “do not suggest any group is responsible” more than the perpetrators’ ideology. 

> American Federation of Teachers (AFT) was more explicit in 2001 that the terrorists should be hunted and that their values were “anathema.” It also passed resolutions against anti-Muslim bigotry and highlighted post-9/11 prejudice.

==> Other actors <==

> Individual school-board members (e.g., Fairfax County, Virginia) have recommended the same “avoid ‘radical Islamic terror’” guides.

> Democratic members of the Texas State Board of Education and CAIR-Texas opposed language that 9/11 was motivated by “radical Islam”; the Republican-majority board adopted it anyway in 2026.

> Some Middle East-studies faculty and “Islamophobia” research centers (including Georgetown’s Bridge Initiative) produce scholarship and teacher training that treat the religious-ideological explanation as bigoted or simplistic.

*** So teachers unions and colleges are responsible for not educaticating students against Radical Islam. ***

text:
Talk to random people on your flights.

Sometimes, it takes a little bit to find the right person (and sometimes you’re in sunglasses / headphones mode, which is totally acceptable too). But on this flight, you have the window seat, and the girl next to you asks if you’d switch with her boyfriend, who’s in a middle seat across the aisle. You remember someone doing this for you when you were flying with someone you love, and you agree.

You explain this to your new seat mates, and they laugh. They’ve done something similar. You take off, send some emails, and then the lady next to you brings you down a conversational path that makes a 2.5-hour flight feel like 20 minutes.

You start talking about triathlons. She’d posted the top qualifying time in Hawaii, but her triathlon days came to an end after her then significant other’s seven-year-old asked her to go sledding. They hit a tree, and she injured her knee. She still teaches barre and yoga, but triathlons are out.

You talk about initiatives to get urban kids interested in farming. She tells you about 3M, a MN paragon of industry, and PFAS contamination, which makes you glad your recent fishing trips on the St. Croix have been catch and release.

You talk about the ups and downs of trying to have a child. How surrogacy can feel so intimate and yet so gamified. The almost-tears as she talks about wanting to bring a life into the world, and how hard it has been to make that happen. You witness the humility it takes to put up a social media post telling the world you would be a good parent, hoping it reaches someone who can help. Putting everything you have into it (and the staggering amount of money it can take).

You talk about their house-flipping empire, the real estate they own, and how their trip east is actually to get the final month's rent and appear on a court TV show connected to Judge Judy's progeny. You offer some lighthearted conciliation court advice, and she feels ready.

You talk about AI. The worry about what data centers mean for the planet, water usage, all of it. The promise of helping mom-and-pop shops compete with Walmart. You think deeply about how you talk about the future of AI (it's impact on all of us) with smart people who have valid concerns.

You leave the plane thinking about the person who switched seats so you could sit with your love ten years ago. You finally got to return the favor to someone else, and somehow you’re also the one walking away with an incredible conversation with a bright soul.

text:
BRANIFF HISTORY TODAY - On this day, Friday, September 8, 1978, Braniff International petitioned the Civil Aeronautics Board for authority to begin service beyond Honolulu, Hawaii, to Okinawa, Japan; Manila in The Philippines; Honk Kong; Bangkok, Thailand; Singapore and Seoul, South Korea. The request was a key part of Braniff's 1977 plan to expand its international route system as well as its domestic system, which would increase traffic flow to and from Latin America.

Braniff had asked for a number of routes in the region during the CAB's 1967 Transpacific Service Investigation Case but was only successful in obtaining new service from five US Mainland co-terminals to Honolulu and Hilo, Hawaii. This was especially disappointing since the carrier had operated an extensive network throughout the region in service to the US Air Force's Military Airlift Command during the Vietnam War.

However, never undaunted, Braniff continued to ask for these routes throughout the 1970s and finally with the advent of the Airline Deregulation Act in October 1978, Braniff was granted authority to operate service in these areas in the spring of 1979 with service beginning that summer and fall. The CAB asked Braniff to begin service in this region across the Pacific to Hong Kong. With this, the CAB further indicated that it would grant Braniff routes to Manila and Tokyo from the US Mainland. Two CAB Examiners recommended Braniff for these routes but ultimately they were awarded to Northwest Airlines. This played out across the Atlantic from Braniff's new Boston hub which the CAB has asked Braniff to begin serving to key points in Europe with the promise of a nonstop route from Boston to London. Again, two CAB Examiners recommended that Braniff should receive these routes but again they were awarded to Northwest Airlines. It should be noted that Northwest was one of the few National smaller major carriers that survived for many years into the deregulation era.

On July 3, 1979, Braniff International continued its expansion across the Pacific with the inauguration of Boeing 747 service from Los Angeles International Airport to Honolulu with continuing service to Guam and Hong Kong. Braniff planned to create a large hub operation at Guam to service multiple Pacific Rim and Far East destinations and then link them to the Mainland USA. However, as long-range airliners such as the Boeing 747SP became available, Braniff changed its plan to linking the two continents with nonstop service. Service between Los Angeles and Honolulu had already been inaugurated on May 5, 1979, which marked the official beginning of Braniff's Westward expansion period.

Braniff International petitioned for exemption authority from the Civil Aeronautics Board on September 8, 1978, to extend its current service from Houston and Dallas/Ft Worth to Honolulu and beyond to Guam, Okinawa, Manila, Taipei, Hong Kong, Bangkok, Singapore, and Seoul. Additional applications were filed with the CAB on February 8, 1979, for additional service to Peking, Canton, and Shanghai in China. The CAB responded on April 12, 1979, and granted Braniff authority to provide service to Bangkok, Guam, Hong Kong, Manila, Singapore, Seoul, and Taipei via Honolulu International Airport.

The new service to Guam and Hong Kong inaugurated on July 3, was an extension of Braniff’s nonstop Boeing 747 service from Los Angeles to Honolulu. Additional service was added in August 1979 to create a direct air link between Asia/Pacific and The Far East and Santiago, Chile, and Buenos Aires, Argentina, in South America. Braniff also offered the lowest fares available between the US Mainland and Guam and Hong Kong.

The linking of the Pacific, Asia and The Far East with not only the US but also with Latin America was a key objective of Braniff's expansion plans over both the Pacific and Atlantic routes. Load factors were initially well above objectives and once the link with Latin America was commenced in August, they further increased above initial projections indicating that the service would accelerate better than expected even with rising fuel costs, which Braniff did successfully absorb ($60 million USD) in 1979 in spite of the CAB's inability to provide much needed and timely fare relief (this inability to act in a timely manner played a strategic role in Braniff's problems during 1980, however, the CAB was also caught off guard by the unbelievable rise in fuel costs throughout the world).

Seattle/Tacoma and Portland to Honolulu service was inaugurated in late 1978, along with Los Angeles-Honolulu in May 1979. Seoul, South Korea, was added in September 1979 and Singapore in October 1979. Boeing 747SP aircraft were eventually used on the Seoul and Singapore flights and ultimately they were the only aircraft type Braniff was operating in the Pacific Rim by April 27, 1980, which also the inaugural date of Braniff Ultra Business Class Service not only in the Asia/Pacific and The Far East routes but also in Europe.

On inaugural day, the big beautiful Braniff International Boeing 747-127 registered as N601BN and dubbed Big Orange departed on the first flight from Honolulu, However, this time it did not turn back toward Diamond Head to continue to the Mainland. Instead, Big Orange flew westbound for Guam and Hong Kong officially marking the historic beginning of Braniff International service to Asia/Pacific and The Far East.

Several factors played a significant role in Braniff's loss of fortune in the region. They were primarily and foremost, of course, the unprecedented rise in fuel costs beyond what had been experience before, declining leisure travel and oftentimes unfair competition from foreign carriers. In fact, during 1979, Braniff's and the industry's number one cost of labor was significantly surpassed by fuel costs. In 1978, Braniff paid $200 million USD for its fuel but during 1979 it paid in excess of $400 million, which was a huge difference for a carrier of Braniff's size to absorb. In spite of the CAB's slow movement on fare relief reviews and the use of catastrophic discount coupons by the airline industry in the last quarter of 1979, Braniff still ended the year with only a $44 million USD loss with all of that loss reported in the last quarter of the year ($55 million USD, which was largely caused by the unregulated use of discount fare coupons during the heavy traffic Thanksgiving and Christmas holiday travel season - this coupled with fuel costs created this loss).

Economic conditions around the world began an unforeseen decline during the last quarter of 1979 and then further eroded especially during the first two quarters of 1980. Leisure travel, which is so important to long-haul international commercial flying, fell off precipitously causing load factors to plummet below breakeven level, which had also risen at an alarming rate. This combined with the rises in fuel costs caused Braniff's 747s to become expensive to operate. Throughout the 1970s, Braniff enjoyed a breakeven on its 747 service that remained between 30-percent and 40-percent, which was industry leading. This low breakeven enabled Braniff to operate at a significant advantage to other carriers. However, once fuel costs began rising so did the 747 breakeven point. The same was being experienced across the Atlantic, although load factors were higher here after the economic downturn.

The venerable DC-8-62, which was the primary aircraft that Braniff used in Latin America, also succumbed to these steep costs and the once profitable region quickly became unprofitable. Braniff began using 747s in Latin America for the first time, which were more economical to operate per seat mile than the DC-8s. Analysts have criticized Braniff for its expansion across the Pacific but these same critics were also vocal in 1948 when the company expanded to Cuba, Central and South America. In one day, Braniff added service from Houston to Havana, Cuba; Panama City/Balboa and Guayaquil, Ecuador, and two weeks later it added service to Lima, Peru. In a two-week period, Braniff, a small Midwest trunk line, added service to four new international destinations in four countries. In comparison in 1979, Braniff added service from Honolulu to Guam with continuing service to Hong Kong. Service to Singapore and Seoul were not added until the fall of 1979.

Braniff's inauguration of service to Latin America was an operational success but a financial disaster, which combined with the carrier's merger with Kansas City-based Mid-Continent Airlines led to massive losses in 1953, Braniff's 25th year of service. Latin America played the major role in Braniff's losses both because of the continuing losses over its LAD network but also because of a dispute with the US Government concerning Mid-Continent's mail subsidy payments. Mid-Continent was not an international carrier but Braniff was and once the two companies merged the subsidy payments were reduced. Carriers flying international routes were paid lesser amounts of mail subsidy over its domestic route systems.

The company believed that it could operate its new Latin American routes that by 1951 covered over 6000 route miles, for a subsidy of only $300,000 USD. However, by 1953 the company required an astronomical $5 million USD in subsidy and it was still losing money in the region. Additional subsidy was granted along with the addition of new gateways and an interchange agreement but still there were losses. They did begin waning, and by 1965 Braniff's Latin America Division recorded its first full-year profit of $300,000 USD. It took 17 years for Braniff to realize a true profit in Latin America. (Note: Braniff did have profitable quarters and months in LAD between 1948 and 1964 but 1965 was the first full year of profitability.)

In 1979, Braniff initially added two new routes in the Pacific Region to rave reviews but it did not have the luxury of large subsidy payments as it did in 1948 even though it was operating a US Postal Service mail route. Several airlines in 1979 flew routes throughout the Pacific and the US Mail could be moved to any other US carrier in the event one ended service whereas in 1948 there were only two US airlines operating in Latin America making it more important to ensure that both carriers remained in operation for both the movement of mail and competitive reasons.

Competition in the Pacific region also played a significant role in Braniff's problems. Competing carriers offered new luxury reclining seats in First Class that were comfortable enough for sleeping but Braniff chose not to invest in the $4000 per pair seating. Unsavory tricks were often leveled against Braniff from competing carriers that often serviced Braniff's planes at its new Pacific Division stations. These stunts, such as shorting supplies or even removing all toilet paper from the aircraft added to its expenses and often caused passenger discomfort and dissatisfaction with the airline that had traditionally defined superb service. Extensive use of discount fares were used at precisely the time when all of the carriers desperately needed to raise fares because spot market fuel prices had risen to nearly $1.40 USD per gallon for jet fuel. However, because of new competition and quickly declining load factors many carriers reduced
ticket prices to entice customers and Braniff had to do the same.

Only a moderate change in one or even two factors during 1979 and 1980 and Braniff would have been massively successful in its expansion. It certainly would have positioned it to be a prime carrier for consolidation. Braniff's management was found to have acted in the only way they could have considering the factors that they faced at the time of deregulation. The Teamsters Union produced a 10-volume analysis of Braniff's expansion plan, decline and eventual bankruptcy for the 1982 Braniff Airline Employee Protection Program Case and found that Braniff had acted in the best interests of its employees, shareholders and creditors considering the information that they had available at the time. It was deregulation that was ultimately blamed for Braniff's and the industry's calamitous problems in the Teamsters analysis, in addition to a ruling by Administrative Law Judge Ronnie A. Yoder, ironically, on May 12, 1988.

Photos: Braniff International Boeing 747-130A registered as N610BN is taxiing at Hong Kong’s Kai Tan International Airport in the fall of 1979. Big Orange is painted in the 1978 Harper and George/Cars and Concepts/Halston Little Orange Ultra Color Scheme but without the Metallic Gold, Cream and Orange Power Paint Stripes but with the 1969 Harper and George International Script in Cream. This leased airliner was the first to receive the Ultra Color Scheme, albeit slightly modified.

[] Constraints: what it must not do, or must ask first
[] Deliverable: what it should return
[] Review point: when it should stop for you
[] Safe first task: attach a file and ask for a cited summary; do not change the file
[] Next task: one real tool, read-only, with a sign-in handoff if needed
[] After a good result, name the lasting format preference in chat
[] Then save it as a skill or routine
[] Official bot examples: email cleanup, Starlink-likely flights, build a site then buy the domain and deploy, meeting notes, sales prospecting, refunds, podcast audio digest
[] Testers: paste a viral video link and ask the Bot to recreate it
[] Testers: start from an org chart or make one Bot the boss of a repo, not a long to-do list
[] Testers: one clear job, explicit allowed sources, no-guessing rule, approval gate before any real action
[] Testers: 5 calibrations - confidence threshold, checkpoint long tasks, show negative examples, gate destructive actions separately, test edge cases first
[] Testers: one Bot, one job - two jobs claimed worse at both; put recurring work on a schedule
[] Testers quoting claimed SpaceXAI employee: version prompts and tool configs like code; scratchpad separate from the user-facing answer; retry with a different strategy; measure cost per successful outcome; review failure logs on a schedule
[] Testers (mvanhorn): Compound Engineering - force a plan first; three-layer instructions (base, role, current focus); screenshot instead of retyping what's on screen; ping only on a real hit
[] Testers (AlexFinn): anything you are about to do on your computer, ask Grok Bot first
[] Testers (AlexFinn): example week - Reddit microSaaS, 3D digital office to watch Bots, Omarchy setup, product returns, daily AI news post, Cursor cloud-agent bug fixes, X model-release watch, brand-deal negotiation, contract redlines
[] Testers (Michael_Fenech_): give it business responsibilities (checking, chasing, updating, coordinating), not just questions

AGENT COMPUTER AND LOGINS
[] Open Agent Computer from the conversation to watch the desktop
[] Take over for password, passkey, 2FA, CAPTCHA, payment, or human-only pages
[] Complete only the blocked step, then return control
[] Never paste passwords or one-time codes into chat
[] Official (bot, Sep 8): fill out forms and logins for your Bot without ever leaving the chat, with support for any password manager
[] Testers (XFreeze): when a site needs your account, Bot pauses; you auth with 1Password / Apple Passwords / any manager; Bot continues — no pasting credentials into chat
[] Testers (LaceyPresley / muskonomy): in-chat logins/forms also cover checkouts and booking flights
[] Use a secure secret request when the app offers one
[] Browser sessions persist and are shared across all your Bots
[] Prefer a connector/plugin when one exists; use the browser when it does not
[] Testers (SamSokolin): for repeated web-app clicks, reverse-engineer browser-use into scripts (capture network once, call APIs next)
[] Keep durable files in /workspace with clear project folders
[] Settings → Beta: Update Agent Computer (preserve state), Recover, or Reset (can lose recent work)
[] The cloud computer is not your Mac or Windows machine
[] Local-computer execution is separate: Settings → General → Agent → Execution on Local Computer
[] Default local policy is Ask every time; use Never allowed unless you need local files
[] Bookmark testers: give a Bot full local Mac/iMessage access only on a spare machine
[] Testers: local Mac access can write local Python scripts on your Mac
[] Testers (Av1dlive / mvanhorn): Claude Code, Codex, and Cursor claimed runnable on the Bot's own computer
[] Testers (XFreeze): take over that same cloud computer from your phone without being at the laptop
[] Testers (Damir_Akaza): group-chat Bots can reach a local Mac Mini via Tailscale for project files and local scripts
[] Testers (farzyness): a Bot can exclusively use Grok Build in CLI with the latest Grok models at highest thinking
[] Testers (AlexFinn): a 3D digital office on a second monitor to watch Bots work

PLUGINS AND CONNECTORS
[] Settings → Plugins, then Add, then authenticate in the browser
[] Grok Bot team (poteto): tinkabot helps build MCP/skills plugins and submit them for approval so all users can use them
[] Type @ to attach a connector; type / to reference a saved skill
[] Installed connectors are account-wide, not isolated to one Bot
[] Official: you can connect multiple accounts to the same plugin
[] Official bot (Aug 26): SuperGrok and Cursor Pro now included; weekly limits reset. Testers quoting SpaceXAI: also Plus/Heavy/Pro+/Ultra/Teams
[] Testers: give a Bot its own email address so it can send and receive on its own
[] Testers (mvanhorn): give a Bot its own inbox, not your Gmail (one mistake should not flag your domain); Twilio number so a Bot can make calls
[] Testers: app v0.23.0 adds creating new channels
[] Official bot: improved X support - connect your X profile; a developer account is auto-created with included credits
[] Testers (blankspeaker): Plugins, add X, authenticate; $100 in X API credits good for a year (new and existing devs)
[] Testers (GrokInsider): if credits did not land, ask Grok Bot to connect X so the Authorize card opens the browser; tester's manual plugin add failed
[] Follow the Connect card when a Bot asks for a plugin
[] Bookmark testers: X connector may still need a paid X API key in some setups (official path now auto-creates a developer account with credits)
[] Bookmark testers: image generation works; testers now also claim video editing (music sync). Video generation still unconfirmed. Testers (XFreeze): dedicated video-editor Bot for footage → clips/cuts/sound/titles
[] Bookmark testers: Grok Bot can now read your X bookmarks
[] Testers (testerlabor): you can link your X Premium+ subscription to Grok Bot
[] Testers: Higgsfield x Grok Bot; 100 free credits for new users
[] Testers: send a YouTube link with start/end timestamps and get an HD clip in chat (Google login claimed)
[] Testers: give a Bot Grok Build + Cursor CLI so weekly limits can be spread across Cursor and Grok

[] Grok Bot team (poteto) + testers (XFreeze): Microsoft connectors live - Outlook, Outlook Calendar, OneDrive (search/send email, drafts, schedules, meetings, browse/upload files)
[] Testers (XFreeze): Bot can natively generate images with Grok Imagine Image 2.0 inside the workflow (no separate Imagine tab)
SKILLS AND ROUTINES
[] Skill = reusable how-to (steps, rules, output, approval boundary)
[] Routine = when to run that work (schedule or event)
[] Do the task once, make it reliable, save a skill, then automate
[] Teach a task: open computer view, choose Teach a task, demo up to 10 minutes, review the draft skill
[] Teaching records the screen, not microphone audio; do not expose secrets while teaching
[] If Teach a task is missing, ask the Bot to write a skill from the completed work
[] Create a routine on the Bot that should own the job
[] Confirm owner, schedule, time zone, input, result, approval, and missing-data behavior
[] Event triggers (Slack, GitHub) are separate from plugins and need their own connection
[] Keep event matchers narrow; avoid every new message
[] Test run does real work; use safe inputs
[] Testers quoting docs: Test can send real emails to real clients; Stop is a brake, not a rewind
[] View conversation details → Routines to pause, edit, inspect, or delete
[] A Bot can own 50 routines; last 20 run records are kept
[] Deleting a routine has no undo
[] Testers quoting docs: delete a Bot and every routine on it dies; no undo
[] Long absence can pause unattended routines until you confirm
[] Bookmark testers: Teach a task from + in the browser, record yourself, then let the Bot replay it
[] Testers: skills taught to one bot claimed available across the account team on the same computer
[] Official Elon: how to share your Grok Bot design with others
[] Testers: a reusable-skills source claimed (BrianRoemmele)
[] Testers quoting Grok Bot team (0xMorlex): keep recurring routines off the main agent's context
[] Testers (mvanhorn): Teach by recording and respect the 10-minute cap

MULTI BOT TEAMS
[] Start with one Bot that owns an end-to-end outcome
[] Add a specialist only when the role is stable
[] Use a group chat when the handoff itself should be visible
[] Bots can message each other and pass ownership
[] Do not treat separate Bots as a security boundary (they share the computer)
[] Keep sending, buying, deleting, publishing, and production changes behind approval
[] Bookmark testers: a Bot may create other Bots before it can delete them
[] Bookmark testers: tell a hub Bot to loop a specialist every few minutes and watch it
[] Testers: put Bots in one group chat, appoint a Chief of Staff, and stop being the router
[] Testers (farzyness): one master agent owns specialists + chat rooms and pings you one action item at a time
[] Testers: isolate each Bot's job and add a supervisor; a crew without that can perform worse
[] Testers: night-shift crews (chief, scout, forge, critic, ship, ledger) share one computer; human gate for merge, production, spend, send, delete
[] Testers: one group chat per job/post, not per Bot; you only message the Chief of Staff
[] Testers: show the workflow once on screen rather than writing a long spec
[] Testers: add a RED TEAM Bot whose job is to disprove the thesis; no single source closes a claim
[] Testers quoting Grok Bot team (0xMorlex): specialist roles (designer/engineer/PM); organize projects without a new Bot for everything; a Chief of Agents that creates and manages the rest
[] Testers (mvanhorn): Bot Advisor whose only job is building and tightening other Bots; files are the memory bus between Bots
[] Testers (Damir_Akaza): 4 Bots in one group chat split a Meta ads campaign (creatives, fact-check, deploy) with autonomous handoff

[] Testers (cminshall): overnight group of five Bots one-shotted an admin UI from PRD/FRD/prototype PNGs
IOS
[] Same Bots, chats, routines, plugins, and cloud computer as desktop
[] Testers (mattyp): Grok Bot supports 21+ localized languages on mobile
[] Send text, dictate, attach photos/files, mention Bots, reply in threads
[] Take over the computer for login/2FA from the phone
[] You can pause or resume a routine on iOS
[] Editing schedule, run history, test, delete, and teach-by-demo still need desktop
[] Enable notifications for results, questions, and approvals
[] Testers: phone notification shows the proposed action; approve or deny
[] Testers (XFreeze): you can operate and take over the Bot's computer from your phone as long as it has internet
[] Grok Bot team (poteto, earlier): had pointed at Play pre-registration; superseded by Official bot Sep 2 Android launch

APPROVALS AND SAFETY
[] Put the stop line in the request: draft, do not send; ask after showing current vs proposed
[] Desktop: Allow once, Deny, or Always allow a matching rule
[] iPhone: Approve once or Deny
[] Auto Review: Settings → General → Auto-review
[] Require Approval beats Always Allow when both match
[] Write narrow rules, not allow everything in the browser
[] Do not approve an action you cannot identify
[] Connect only the tools the workflow needs
[] Start read-only; keep spend, send, publish, delete, and production behind approval
[] Sign out and revoke connectors when access should end
[] Deleting a Bot does not wipe shared files or browser sessions
[] Bookmark testers: delay standing inbox/CRM access until you trust the beta
[] Bookmark testers: one person burned a 7-day quota in about 8 hours
[] Testers (daveginvesting): burned a week of tokens in about 2 hours on first try
[] Bookmark testers: SuperGrok may offer one-off usage resets in settings; use before they expire
[] Testers: gate destructive actions (delete, overwrite, irreversible send) as their own confirmation, not lumped with routine tool use
[] Testers quoting docs: Test run does real work; Stop does not unsend
[] Testers quoting Elon (cb_doge): connecting a Bot to a bank account; Elon said any loss from a bot mistake would be covered. Still keep spend behind approval
[] Official bot Link shopping: keep purchases behind approval even though the Bot can complete them on your behalf
[] Official Elon: Grok Bot buys a Tesla
[] Testers (mvanhorn): unsupervised crews claimed to multiply their own errors ~17x; draft-then-approve anything that sends; most Bots that don't own an outcome fail
[] Testers (antpalkin): end every agent's job with a hard never-without-asking list; give one Bot veto/kill power whose no beats the rest of the desk

FIRST BOTS WORTH CREATING
[] Inbox manager for email and Slack triage
[] Calendar and reservation Bot
[] Research and daily brief Bot
[] Coding Bot that can launch Cursor cloud agents
[] Testers (AlexFinn): pair a developer Bot (Cursor cloud agents + PRs) with a PM Bot on Notion/Linear that feeds tasks and grants permission — software-factory loop
[] Chief-of-staff hub that routes work to specialists
[] Personal errands Bot (tickets, food, travel, forms)
[] Content Bot that drafts in your voice for approval
[] Chief-of-staff that researches you, organizes the other Bots, and can turn the digest into a morning podcast
[] Testers (mvanhorn): Bot Advisor; own-inbox Bot; a call Bot with its own number
[] Testers (techdevnotes): default Bots circulating - Night Shift (overnight digest), Inbox Triage, Chief of Staff, Negotiator, Prototyper, Researcher, Shopper, Apartment Scout, Lookout, Competitor Watcher
[] Testers (techdevnotes): also tool-specific sales/ops/dev roles (CRM scribe, pipeline scout, ticket triager, QA, dashboard watcher)
[] Official bot + Link: Shopper Bot can now complete online purchases once link is connected (keep approval on)
[] Testers / SpaceXAI (kiaraplds): flights, tickets, groceries - delegate errands safely to your Bot
[] Testers (minchoi): one-person-company setups - money, appointments, running ops from the phone
[] Testers (niccruzpatane): Accounting Bot (invoices, spending, bills); Personal Bot (flights, rides, Airbnb, Google Calendar, Amazon orders/returns); Home Bot (lights, robots, speakers, thermostats)
[] Testers (GrokBotDev): Jess (email/calendar/Notion/Slack recap), Marketing Bot, Prospecting Sheet Builder, Reaper (kill unused subs/meetings), Human Copywriter
[] Testers (JasonL_Capital): 8 options-trading Bots (scan puts, price LEAPS, run the wheel) with copy-paste prompts
[] Testers (Michael_Fenech_): start in recruitment, e-comm, real estate, accounting, legal, SaaS, agencies, trades, founder ops

South Korea Maps Tokenised Securities Into Law

South Korea's FSC published a three-phase roadmap integrating tokenised securities into national capital markets law from February 2027:

• Phase 1: money market funds, bonds, and unlisted stocks.
• Phase 2: all publicly offered securities.
• Phase 3: stablecoin-linked payment infrastructure.

Our view
South Korea is writing tokenised securities into existing capital markets law rather than creating a separate regulatory category — allowing tokenised assets to inherit the existing investor protection framework.

text:
Holland America Canada & New England Cruises 2027: Complete Guide

For travelers seeking a blend of spectacular fall foliage, maritime history, French Canadian culture, and scenic coastal cruising, Holland America Line's 2027 Canada & New England program offers one of the most immersive ways to explore northeastern North America. Holland America has announced 20 sailings across 13 itineraries aboard the Volendam and Zuiderdam between May and October 2027, ranging from 7 to 14 days in length.

Holland America Line: A Brief History

Holland America Line traces its roots to 1873, when it was founded in Rotterdam, Netherlands, as the Netherlands-America Steamship Company. Originally transporting immigrants and cargo across the Atlantic, the company evolved into one of the world's most respected premium cruise lines.

Today, Holland America is known for:

Mid-sized ships rather than mega-resorts
A destination-focused experience
Exceptional service levels
Strong culinary programming
Enrichment and cultural immersion
Longer port stays and scenic cruising

Unlike several competitors that emphasize waterslides, amusement attractions, and family-centric activities, Holland America focuses on sophisticated travel experiences, deeper destination immersion, and personalized service. The line's smaller ships can also access ports such as Montréal that many larger vessels cannot reach.

Available 2027 Canada & New England Itineraries

The 2027 season includes a variety of voyages designed around history, natural beauty, culture, cuisine, and fall foliage.

7-Day Canada & New England Cruises

Various sailings between:

Boston and Montréal
Montréal and Boston
Boston roundtrip
Boston and Québec City
Québec City and Boston

Featured ports may include:

Québec City
Halifax
Sydney, Nova Scotia
Charlottetown, Prince Edward Island
Portland, Maine
Eastport, Maine
Saint John, New Brunswick
9-Day Lighthouses & Harbors of Canada & New England

New for 2027

Sailing: October 2, 2027
Route: Montréal to New York
Features visits associated with up to 10 iconic lighthouses
Ports include:
Halifax
Charlottetown
Bar Harbor
Portland
Québec City
Saguenay
10-Day Canada & New England Circle: New France & Montréal

Roundtrip Montréal featuring:

Québec City
Saguenay
Prince Edward Island
St. Pierre & Miquelon
St. John's, Newfoundland

This itinerary focuses heavily on French-Canadian culture and history.

11-Day Canada & New England Circle: Maritimes & New France

One of the most comprehensive regional explorations.

Highlights include:

Saguenay Fjord
Gros Morne National Park
Jacques-Cartier National Park
Mingan Archipelago
Prince Edward Island National Park

Ports include:

Halifax
Corner Brook
St. John's
St. Anthony
Québec City
Saguenay
Baie-Comeau
Havre-Saint-Pierre
14-Day Atlantic & Colonial New England
Fort Lauderdale to Montréal
Multiple East Coast ports
Overnight in Québec City
Late departure from Prince Edward Island
14-Day Atlantic, New England & Québec
Québec City to Miami
Eight ports
Overnight call in Halifax
Best Times to Cruise
Peak Season

The most sought-after departures occur during:

Mid-September through Mid-October

Travelers come specifically for:

Peak fall foliage
Crisp temperatures
Autumn colors throughout New England
Harvest festivals
Lighthouse photography

September and October sailings typically command the highest fares and often sell out first.

Particularly Popular Departures
September 2027 departures
October 2, 2027 Lighthouse sailing
Late September Québec City departures
Boston roundtrip foliage cruises
Shoulder Seasons
May and Early June

Pros:

Lower fares
Spring blooms
Fewer crowds
Cooler weather
Late August

Pros:

Warmer temperatures
Good wildlife viewing
Less expensive than peak foliage season
How Far in Advance Should You Book?

For Canada & New England, booking early is strongly recommended.

Best Practice
Peak foliage cruises: 12 to 18 months ahead
Verandah and suite categories: 15 to 20 months ahead
Family cabins: 12+ months ahead

Several of the specialty itineraries, especially the Montréal roundtrip sailings, are known to fill quickly.

Approximate 2027 Cruise Costs

Actual pricing will vary by sailing date, cabin category, promotions, and airfare.

Couples
Interior Cabin
$3,000 to $4,500 total
Including taxes and fees
Ocean View
$4,000 to $6,000 total
Verandah
$5,500 to $8,500 total
Suites
$9,000 to $15,000+ total

Pricing estimates are based on published early 2027 fares starting around $1,400 to $3,200 per person depending on itinerary length and cabin category.

Family of Four
Two Interior Cabins
$6,500 to $10,000
One Larger Verandah Cabin
$7,500 to $12,000
Family-Oriented Suite
$12,000 to $20,000+

These estimates do not include airfare, hotels, specialty dining, or optional shore excursions.

What Guests Can Expect

Nearly every itinerary includes scenic cruising on the St. Lawrence River, one of the highlights of the region. Guests can expect:

French Canadian culture
Historic colonial towns
Coastal lighthouses
Fresh seafood
National parks
Whale-watching opportunities
Charming maritime communities
Spectacular coastal scenery
Staterooms & Suites
Interior Staterooms
Most economical
Efficient design
Ideal for travelers spending most time ashore
Ocean View Staterooms
Large picture window
Natural light
Great value choice
Verandah Staterooms

The most popular category.

Features:

Private balcony
Floor-to-ceiling views
Ideal for St. Lawrence River cruising and foliage viewing
Suites

Options include:

Vista Suites
Signature Suites
Neptune Suites

Suite guests receive:

Larger living spaces
Premium amenities
Expanded concierge services
Priority boarding
Dining & Cuisine

One area where Holland America consistently stands out is food.

Canada & New England sailings feature regional specialties including:

Maine lobster
Prince Edward Island mussels
Clam chowder
Canadian cheeses
Poutine
Fresh Atlantic seafood
Included Dining
Main Dining Room
Lido Market buffet
Poolside grill options
Afternoon tea
Room service
Specialty Restaurants

May include:

Pinnacle Grill

Tamarind (on applicable ships)

Additional fees generally apply.

Enrichment & Educational Programs

Holland America places significant emphasis on destination learning.

Guests can often enjoy:

Port lectures
Destination presentations
Regional history talks
Naturalist sessions
Cultural programming focused on Canada and New England
Culinary demonstrations

For 2027, the cruise line has stated that itineraries are specifically designed to highlight the area's maritime history, French heritage, national parks, and culinary traditions.

Entertainment & Activities On Board

Guests can expect:

Live music venues
Classical performances
Rock and blues bands
Quiz competitions
Cooking demonstrations
Fitness classes
Spa treatments
Art and photography programs
Enrichment lectures

The atmosphere is relaxed and refined rather than high-energy and activity-driven.

Who Are These Cruises Best For?
Ideal For
Couples
Empty nesters
Mature travelers
Retirees
History enthusiasts
Food lovers
Nature photographers
Fall foliage seekers
Less Ideal For

Families requiring:

Water parks
Surf simulators
Large children's programs

While families are welcome, Holland America generally caters more toward adults than the contemporary mass-market cruise lines.

Shore Excursions
Included with Cruise Fare

Standard cruise fare generally includes:

Transportation between ports
Scenic cruising experiences
Onboard destination programming
Daily entertainment and activities

Certain promotions such as Holland America's "Have It All" package may include a shore excursion credit or select excursion benefits depending on the booking offer.

Optional A-La-Carte Excursions

Guests may purchase excursions separately.

Popular choices include:

Maine
Acadia National Park tours
Lighthouse tours
Lobster boat experiences
Nova Scotia
Peggy's Cove
Halifax heritage tours
Coastal sightseeing
Prince Edward Island
Anne of Green Gables experiences
Coastal drives
Culinary excursions
Québec
Old Québec walking tours
French heritage excursions
Jacques-Cartier National Park adventures
Newfoundland
Wildlife excursions
Viking history tours
Gros Morne National Park visits

The new Lighthouse-themed itinerary alone offers 22 shore excursions focused on lighthouse history and maritime heritage.

Final Thoughts

Holland America's 2027 Canada & New England season is particularly appealing for travelers who value scenery, culture, food, and meaningful destination experiences over onboard thrills. The combination of Montréal sailings, St. Lawrence River cruising, national park access, French-Canadian heritage, and peak fall foliage makes these cruises among the most distinctive offerings in North America for 2027. With demand typically strongest for September and October departures, booking 12 to 18 months in advance remains the best strategy for securing preferred cabins and pricing.

2000-2001 Clinton Parameters and Taba: refined offer near 97 percent with swaps. Arafat effectively rejected.  
2005 Gaza Disengagement: Sharon unilaterally withdrew all settlers and forces from Gaza and some northern West Bank settlements. PA under Abbas took control. Hamas later seized Gaza; rockets and rejectionism continued.

Deadline: September 29, 2026
Duration: 3 years
Salary: NOK 593,700/year

📋 About the Project
AI LEARN is a new national Norwegian center focused on empowering human learning through responsible, human-centered AI, bringing together 31 national and international academic, public, and private sector partners to study hybrid intelligence — humans and machines learning and working together. This PhD sits within the Ethics, Governance and Regulation cluster, investigating ethical issues (human dignity, social justice, human agency, human flourishing) raised by AI — including generative AI — across learning contexts like K-12, informal/formal training, and vocational or professional development. The student will conduct qualitative empirical research grounded in relevant theory to inform ethical frameworks for policy, professional development, curriculum design, and pedagogy.

🔬 Ideal Candidate
• Master's degree in Social Sciences, Education, Science and Technology Studies (STS), Philosophy, or related field
• Grade B or higher on master's thesis (or equivalent average grade)
• Demonstrated interest in AI ethics in learning contexts is an advantage
• Strong independent and structured working style, good collaboration skills
• Excellent written and spoken English

Join a genuinely interdisciplinary, well-resourced national center at the frontier of AI ethics and education, co-supervised across Bergen and UCL. UiB offers strong benefits including membership in the Norwegian Public Service Pension Fund and competitive state salary scale conditions.

Venus moves into Scorpio at midnight, having spent weeks at the very edge of Libra, and what shifts for you is the emotional register around money. Bitcoin Continues to Drift Sideways — With One Cautionary Signal

$BTC has spent much of the period since late August chopping sideways, with the $79,000 area repeatedly flipping between support and resistance. Right now, price is sitting just underneath that zone, leaving the short-term picture finely balanced.

The two-week bearish RSI divergence is still worth keeping an eye on, but on its own it isn’t enough to turn the broader short-term picture bearish.
