text:
Three egos, one ticket: The coalition’s 2027 math problem

Step down or stand by: The choice facing Atiku, Obi and Makinde

There is a peculiar Nigerian tragedy replaying itself in real time, and it has nothing to do with the ruling party. It is the opposition, once again, doing the APC’s work for it — for free.

With the January 16, 2027 election drawing closer, and INEC set to publish its final list of candidates on September 12, Nigeria’s opposition finds itself exactly where it was in 2023: fragmented, self-important, and one bad arithmetic lesson away from handing President Bola Tinubu a second term he arguably has not earned. Tinubu polled just under 8.8 million votes in 2023. Atiku Abubakar took close to 7 million. Peter Obi took just over 6 million. Add them together, and the opposition commanded roughly 13 million votes to Tinubu’s 8.8 million — and still lost, because those votes were never united behind one name. That is not a moral failing. It is arithmetic, plain and brutal, and according to a report by BusinessDay, even the candidates know it. Former Cross River governor and Peoples Redemption Party candidate Donald Duke put it bluntly: a divided opposition will hand Tinubu victory, and he — unlike his more famous rivals — says he is ready to step down for a genuine consensus candidate.

That offer alone should embarrass the field. Duke has no illusions about winning outright. He has looked at the numbers, looked at the incumbency machinery arrayed against the opposition — the police, the governors, the federal purse — and concluded that ego is a luxury the opposition cannot afford. Compare that to Atiku, Obi, and Seyi Makinde, three men who have each, at various points, been told plainly that unity is the only path to defeating an incumbent president in Nigeria, and who have each, in various ways, responded with a version of: let the other man step down first.

The candidates: three men, zero sacrifices

Start with Atiku. His camp’s argument, relayed to The Punch, is that he “thought about” the coalition idea years ago, built the ADC around it, and is therefore entitled to the ticket while everyone else — implicitly including Obi, who left the original coalition talks to join the NDC — should fall in line behind him. It’s a tidy story, except it ignores the inconvenient fact that Atiku has lost every previous presidential bid he has mounted, going back decades. At some point, seniority in the queue stops being a credential and starts being a warning sign.

Then there is Obi, whose camp argues the presidency is “the turn of the South” and that Atiku, at nearly 80 by 2031, should simply wait his turn behind a one-term Obi presidency. It is a plausible-sounding argument until you remember that Obi made an identical promise in 2023 — to serve one term — with no binding mechanism behind it, and that promises made on the campaign trail in Nigeria have a long and undistinguished history of evaporating the moment power is secured. Ask Nigerians how many “restructuring” and “one-term” pledges have survived contact with Aso Rock.

And then there is Makinde, whose party insists he is “in the race to win” even as it simultaneously courts consensus-candidate status — a position that amounts to keeping every door open while committing to none of them. It is the political equivalent of wanting to be picked as team captain while refusing to say whether you’re even willing to be on the team.

None of these men, according to reporting by The Punch and Leadership, has agreed to step aside. All three skipped the actual G-100 summit in Abuja in person — a detail their aides insist means nothing, but which analysts like Professor Elijah Agbaje and Professor Major Adeyi read, more plausibly, as three men who do not trust each other enough to sit in the same room while their proxies discuss which of them should quit the race.

The G-100: a name that undersells its own stakes

Then there is the matter of the coalition’s name itself — the “G-100.” It sounds less like a serious political vehicle capable of unseating an incumbent president and more like a WhatsApp group chat or a vague corporate strategy retreat. Compare it to the ADC’s 2013–2015 predecessor coalition, which had a clear, singular identity and produced Muhammadu Buhari as a genuinely agreed consensus candidate — the only time in Nigeria’s Fourth Republic an opposition alliance has actually defeated a sitting president. The G-100, by contrast, has produced committees, working groups, a “Transition Charter,” a “Government of National Competence,” and, as of this writing, zero candidates willing to withdraw. It has all the architecture of seriousness and none of the substance. A coalition should be judged by what it forces its members to give up, not by how many acronymed subcommittees it can spin off. On that test, the G-100 has so far asked nothing of anyone and gotten exactly what it asked for: nothing.

What actually needs to happen

If Nigeria’s opposition is serious about 2027, it needs less summitry and more spine. It needs one of Atiku, Obi, or Makinde to do what Donald Duke has already volunteered to do — put the country ahead of personal ambition and step aside for whichever candidate genuinely commands the broadest coalition of 2023’s 13 million opposition votes. Anything short of that is theatre, and Nigerians have seen this play before. The APC did not defeat Goodluck Jonathan in 2015 by holding summits about summits. It did it by making a hard, unsentimental choice about who would carry the ticket, and then closing ranks behind it.

Until Atiku, Obi, or Makinde is willing to make that same sacrifice, the G-100’s fine-sounding transition charters are just paperwork — and Tinubu, watching from Europe or wherever else he happens to be this week, has every reason to relax.

HOUSTON, WE HAVE A PROBLEM

PRESIDENT NO. 44: B. OBAMA

NOTHING CAN STOP WHAT IS COMING 

THE FEDERAL GOVERNMENT'S GREATEST MAGIC TRICK

The Internet's favorite conspiracy theory franchise.

According to one of the Internet's most enduring sagas, Barack Obama was supposedly born abroad and was constitutionally ineligible, Michelle was secretly a man, and—somehow—the entire federal apparatus participated, collaborated, or looked the other way.

That wouldn't just be a presidency.

MISSION: IMPOSSIBLE Series — OVAL OFFICE EDITION.

No Green Card.
No Gold Card.
No waiting in line at Immigration.

Just the keys to the White House.

That’s not immigration.
That would be the PLATINUM EXECUTIVE PACKAGE.

Forget forms, interviews, and six months of waiting for someone to figure out where the hell they left your file.

The premium package, apparently, came with Air Force One, the Secret Service, nuclear codes, and eight years of free parking at 1600 Pennsylvania Avenue.

Even Marriott doesn't offer a rewards program like that.

THE GREAT FEDERAL HOUDINI

AND NOBODY NOTICED?

According to this theory, the detail somehow slipped past:

Congress.
The FBI.
Intelligence agencies.
The courts.
The military.
The Secret Service.
Hundreds or thousands of journalists.
Legions of lawyers.
Millions of political adversaries.

EVERYONE ASLEEP AT THE WHEEL!

Luckily, there was the Internet.

Because nothing beats the combined resources of the U.S. government quite like a guy on Facebook with Wi-Fi, reading glasses, a coffee maker, and three hours of free time.

The FBI has legions of employees.

But "Juan from the couch" has screenshots.

Checkmate, Washington!

THE INTERNATIONAL MONEY EXPRESS

Next stop: WHO THE HELL KNOWS? Then come the astronomical net-worth estimates circulating online, accompanied by accusations regarding money sent to various countries—including Iran—as well as NGOs, USAID, and an endless alphabet soup of government agencies.

According to these narratives, Obama is living the American Dream in first-class style: eight years in the White House and access to the planet’s most important financial hub.

Meanwhile, Lyndon B. Johnson sits in a corner of history, clutching the metaphorical championship belt and saying:

“Kid, you still need more training.”

WASHINGTON: LAS VEGAS WITH SUBPOENAS

Because, according to the Internet, Washington isn’t just the capital.

It’s a Las Vegas-style show, complete with flags, lawyers, and the federal budget.

Money comes in.
Money goes out.
NGOs appear.
USAID appears.
Foreign governments appear.
Consultants appear, charging fees to explain what the consultants themselves discovered.

Finally, Congress holds a seven-hour hearing.

Forty cameras.
Twenty lawyers.
Fifteen classified folders.
Twelve outraged politicians.

And after spending another three million dollars trying to figure out where the first three million went, the most important official phrase in Washington is uttered:

“I DO NOT RECALL.”

Perfect!

An ordinary citizen forgets to pay the IRS $47 and gets six letters.

Washington loses millions and gets a hearing, free coffee, and five extra minutes to answer.

Houston, we do indeed have a problem.

text:
Little House on the Prairie does not survive because it is gentle. It survives because it is honest about how hard it is to stay gentle when the world is hungry, cold, prejudiced, and unfinished. Other family stories of its era offered living rooms and punchlines. Other Westerns offered guns and glory. This one offered a house so small it could barely hold a family, and then asked that family to hold an entire moral universe. That is why it stands apart. It is not merely a period piece. It is a long argument, week after week, that character is built in ordinary weather.

Laura Ingalls Wilder wrote the books in the Great Depression, looking backward at a childhood spent crossing Wisconsin woods, Kansas prairie, Minnesota creek banks, and Dakota winters. She wrote about a father who could make a fiddle sound like hope and a mother who could make a house out of almost nothing. The television series that began with a two hour pilot in March 1974 and ran through 1983 took those books as seed, not scripture. Michael Landon, already famous from Bonanza, directed the pilot on the condition that he play Charles Ingalls. He understood something the books could not do on a page. A chapter about apple fritters will not hold a camera. A father carrying his daughter through fever will. So the show planted the Ingalls in Walnut Grove, Minnesota, stretched time, invented neighbors, and turned pioneer scarcity into a weekly test of the soul.

Watch the family leave land they thought they owned. In the books they are pushed off Osage territory when soldiers enforce a boundary they never fully understood. On screen they arrive at Plum Creek with a mortgage, a dog named Jack, and the stubborn belief that work can purchase belonging. Charles takes more jobs than a body can hold. Wheat needs stacking. Bills need paying. Pride wants to refuse help. Then the men of Walnut Grove appear with their hands already dirty. The lesson is not that neighbors are nice. The lesson is that independence without community is a pretty lie. Home, Laura says early, is the nicest word there is. The show spends years proving that home is not a building. Home is the people who will still come when the mill shuts down and the crop fails and the money turns out to be counterfeit.

Mary goes blind after scarlet fever. That happened in life in 1879. The series does not restore her sight because a miracle would be cheaper than truth. Two episodes, I’ll Be Waving as You Drive Away, sit among the finest hours American television ever made. You are supposed to learn that a life can be rewritten without being cancelled. Mary does not become an inspiration poster. She becomes a person who must invent a future with her hands on Braille and her pride in her throat. Albert, the adopted son who never existed in the books, later falls into morphine after a harvest injury. The camera does not wink. Addiction is not a moral stain that soap can wash. It is a winter that comes inside the body. Charles does not lecture the boy into purity. He stays. That is the harder pedagogy.

The show looks like calico and hymnals. It is not soft. Children die. A son is lost. Mr. Edwards loses a child and the grief does not resolve on schedule. There is plague and quarantine and fire at a school for the blind. There is rape, racism, antisemitism, child cruelty, and the slow poison of a town that would rather look away. In The Wisdom of Solomon a Black child arrives hoping to sell himself for an education and Charles refuses the transaction because a human being is not a price. In The Craftsman Charles tells Laura that if you do not speak up to bigots you are no better than they are. These are not modern insertions glued onto a cozy antique. They are the reason the antique still cuts. In an age of All in the Family and Maude, when television was learning to shout about the present, Little House smuggled the present into the 1870s and made the argument look like weather.

Nellie Oleson is the necessary villain and the secret joke. Alison Arngrim’s curls were a heavy wig that hurt. The character is a composite of girls Laura remembered, inflated into a monument of spoiled cruelty. Without Nellie the prairie would be a sermon. With Nellie it becomes a schoolyard, which is where most of us first meet injustice. Laura’s temper, her hunger to win, her boyish restlessness, her later uncomfortable first kiss with Almanzo when Melissa Gilbert was fifteen and Dean Butler was twenty three, all of that keeps the heroine from becoming a porcelain saint. You are meant to love Laura because she is unfinished. Half Pint is not good. She is becoming.

Why is it unique among Westerns? Because the land is not a prize to be cleared. The land is a teacher that can kill you. Pa is not a lone gunman. He is a man who cries, who fails, who dyes his prematurely gray hair and wears lifted boots so he will still look like the tallest moral fact in the room. Ma is not scenery. Caroline Ingalls holds the family when Charles’s optimism outruns the harvest. The town is a character. Doc Baker, Reverend Alden, Nels Oleson standing against his own wife’s vanity, Miss Beadle trying to keep a school alive in a place that would rather use children as labor. Other Westerns measure manhood by the draw. This one measures it by whether you will haul another man’s wheat when your own back is already breaking.

It became a cultural icon because it arrived when America was exhausted by Vietnam, Watergate, inflation, and the feeling that institutions had gone hollow. Rural self sufficiency looked like a moral technology. Families watched together. Children grew up on screen. Melissa Gilbert, Melissa Sue Anderson, the Greenbush twins sharing Carrie so child labor laws would not stop the work. The series lived in the Nielsen top twenty for most of its run, collected Emmy nominations for light and music, and then refused to die. It has never really left syndication. Decades later it still racks up billions of minutes on streaming, especially among people who want the clock to slow down. During lockdowns, viewers returned to episodes about plague and quarantine and recognized the old fear in a new mask. A wagon takes a long time to cross a road. Butter takes a long time to churn. The slowness is the point. Modern life sells speed as virtue. This story sells attention as survival.

The books themselves are more complicated than the glow around them. Wilder and her daughter Rose Wilder Lane shaped memory into myth. Real Charles Ingalls moved restlessly, carried debts, and sat his family on land that was not empty. The Osage were not extras in someone else’s destiny. Later debates stripped Wilder’s name from an award and forced readers to hold two truths at once. The pioneer story can teach courage and still participate in a taking. The 1970s series already knew some of this and still flinched from all of it. That tension is part of the icon. America keeps projecting onto the little house whatever it needs the past to be: faith, grit, innocence, empire, motherhood, the dream of starting over with only a wagon and a will. A story that can carry that much projection is not simple. It is a national Rorschach in a sunbonnet.

What you are supposed to take away is not that the old days were better. The old days were lethal. Pregnancy could kill. Winter could starve. A prairie fire could unmake a year in an afternoon. What you take away is that meaning is made in the repair. When Charles thinks he has inherited a fortune and the fortune is fake, friends buy the farm back for pennies so dignity can be restored without charity’s sting. When Walnut Grove finally faces a tycoon who has purchased the land out from under the people who built it, they do not win in court. They blow up their own town rather than let it become a company possession. The last farewell is outrageous, operatic, and perfectly on theme. If you cannot keep the soul of a place, you will not hand the shell to a man who only wants the deed. Then they walk out singing. Starting over is the Ingalls religion.

The mastery is formal as much as moral. David Rose’s music does not decorate scenes. It remembers them for you. The cinematography treats grass like an ocean. Landon directed dozens of episodes with a taskmaster’s clock and a clown’s timing. The show can go from a funeral to a Halloween nightmare in which Laura thinks she saw Mrs. Oleson’s head come off, a prairie Rear Window in pigtails. That range is why it outlasted prettier nostalgia. It is sincere enough for church and strange enough for memory. You do not remember The Waltons the way you remember anthrax in Walnut Grove, an orangutan in a late season, a stone altar of desperate prayer, Ma nearly losing a leg, a father who would rather work himself to collapse than admit the frontier has beaten him.

It is a masterpiece of popular art because it never confused goodness with ease. It is a legend because generations can enter at different doors. Some come for faith quoted on network television, Psalm 23 spoken without embarrassment. Some come for the lesson that prejudice is a laziness the soul cannot afford. Some come because they were once a child who wanted a father like that, or a sister who would still love them after the world went dark. Some come because the house is little and the sky is not, and the mismatch feels like life.

Behind the scenes the myth was made by sweat, jokes, and fracture. They built Walnut Grove at Big Sky Ranch in Simi Valley, California, far from Minnesota snow, and made the false town feel more real than many true ones. Landon hid frogs in his mouth and let them leap at the script supervisor. He told Melissa Gilbert to keep backing up until she was a field away. He put rocks in a chair so a tiny woman would think she had grown suddenly weak. The children retaliated with plastic wrap on toilet seats. He bought the company Christmas gifts with money he earned announcing the Rose Parade at dawn. He nurtured unpolished kids on purpose so they would not act cute. He also chain smoked, crushed cigarettes into leather gloves, left his marriage for a makeup artist on the set, and for a time lost the offscreen daughter who had called him Pa. Gilbert stayed away for years and then appeared when he was dying. The man who taught millions how a father should look could not keep every room in his own house in order. That does not cancel the work. It completes the argument. The show was always about trying.

So you watch it not because it is safe. You watch it because it insists that a life is a series of harvests, some ruined, some shared, and that the person you become is the sum of who you refused to abandon. Other stories in its field sell the West as conquest or the family as furniture. This one sells the West as weather and the family as a verb. A little house cannot hold the prairie. It can only teach you how to stand in it without becoming cruel. That is why it remains a must watch, a classic, a legend that will not stay buried under newer versions or older doubts. The wagon is still coming down the road. It is still taking a long time. You are still supposed to learn how to wait, how to work, how to speak, how to grieve, and how to begin again when the land you loved is no longer yours to keep.

text:
Gulf Shores Airport Positioned for Growth with Key FAA Grants and $15M Terminal Expansion

During the Gulf Shores City Council work session held this week, city leaders reviewed critical infrastructure proposals ahead of an upcoming vote to ratify key Federal Aviation Administration (FAA) grants and received an in-depth progress report on the airport's ambitious $15 million terminal expansion project.

This major facility overhaul is critical to keeping pace with extraordinary passenger growth, expanding carrier offerings, and the overall economic transformation of Alabama's Gulf Coast.

Airport Authority FAA Grants Ratification
To maintain momentum, the Airport Authority Board is seeking official City Council ratification for three federal grants totaling $2.6 million in federal funding, backed by $130,000 in local matching funds from the airport, detailed in the FAA grant matching funds briefing:

Airport Infrastructure Grant: A $324,800 award representing the final installment of a five-year federal initiative that has delivered $1.5 million in total support, per the Airport Infrastructure Grant overview.
Airport Improvement Program Grant: Allocating $253,353 explicitly earmarked for ongoing terminal construction costs, outlined in the Airport Improvement Program discussion.
Airport Terminal Program (ATP) Grant: A competitive federal award bringing total program funding to $7 million, following a previously secured $5 million award, highlighted in the Airport Terminal Program presentation.

Since its inception, the terminal expansion project has successfully secured between $10.5 million and $10.7 million in state and federal funding, according to the terminal financial history report. Major contributions include a $5 million federal grant in 2024, $215,000 from the Alabama Department of Transportation (LDOT) for parking infrastructure, and an initial airport infrastructure grant of $448,000.

Capitalizing on Terminal Expansion Progress
Following the official groundbreaking ceremony on July 21, 2026, as noted in the official groundbreaking announcement, general contractor TripTek Construction LLC was awarded the $15 million build contract to fast-track construction.

The project remains fully on schedule for its grand opening on May 21, 2027, confirmed in the May 21, 2027 Grand Opening timeline update. Key construction updates include:

Upcoming Milestones: The erection of vertical structural steel is scheduled to commence within weeks, as outlined in the vertical steel erection phase briefing.
Site Management: The parking lot nearest the terminal is temporarily closed for utility integration and heavy construction work but will reopen to passengers upon completion, per the parking lot update.

Layout & Passenger Amenities
The expanded terminal facility is designed to deliver a modern travel experience:

Dual Operations Capacity: Engineered to easily process two simultaneous commercial aircraft operations, detailed in the dual aircraft operations layout review.
Phased Buildout: Phase 1 focuses on delivering a gate area with two operational gates, while Phase 2 will completely renovate the interior of the existing terminal building, outlined in the phased terminal construction plan.
Enhanced Experience: Passengers will enjoy an outdoor patio beyond security screening, a quiet mothers' nursing room, an expanded baggage claim carousel, larger curbside drop-off zones, expanded rental car queuing, and elevated food, beverage, and retail offerings, detailed in the passenger amenity design plans. Regional favorites like Lucy Buffett's LuLu's are already serving passengers in the terminal, as reported in the terminal dining update.

Allegiant Air Fueling the Local Tourism Boom
The arrival of commercial service via Allegiant Air on May 21, 2025, marked a turning point for regional travel, as noted in the Allegiant Air inaugural flight announcement. Since commercial flights launched, approximately 176,000 total passengers have traveled through the airport, according to the airport passenger throughput report.

Passenger traffic reached historic highs in summer 2026. June set an all-time record with over 34,000 passengers and a 78% average load factor, detailed in the June 2026 traffic report. July followed closely with 18,000 passengers, recorded in the July 2026 passenger statistics update.

A recent survey revealed that 43% of airport passengers had never visited Alabama's beaches prior to the introduction of commercial flights. By replacing grueling 14+ hour round-trip drives from markets like Nashville with a quick flight under 75 minutes, non-stop service saves travelers fuel and travel fatigue while maximizing leisure time on the coast.

Expansive Non-Stop Flight Network
During peak season, Gulf Shores International Airport offers 30 weekly non-stop flights connecting to 13 key markets across the United States.

The airport's non-stop flight destinations include:

Huntsville, AL
Louisville, KY
Omaha, NE
Springfield, MO
Oklahoma City, OK
Cincinnati, OH
Appleton, WI
Des Moines, IA
Belleville/St. Louis, IL/MO
Northwest Arkansas/Bentonville, AR
Knoxville, TN
Kansas City, MO
Nashville, TN

Notably, the Huntsville-to-Gulf Shores route stands as Alabama's only intrastate commercial flight path, as noted in the Huntsville-to-Gulf Shores route announcement. This connection allows North Alabama residents to bypass a lengthy highway trip in favor of a one-hour flight that frequently costs less than a single tank of gas.

Looking ahead to next summer, airport authorities expect flight frequencies on existing routes to increase from twice weekly to three or four times per week.

PUBLIC SERVICE ANNOUNCEMENT

Amateur OSINT briefing. Raw records, FOIAs, cables, leaks, and public filings only. No press releases, no think-tank spin, no “experts say.” Draw your own line from the documents.

George Soros built a fortune speculating on currencies and markets, then parked tens of billions into the Open Society network. That network funds NGOs, prosecutors, media projects, and “civil society” groups that often operate in the same countries and on the same issues as U.S. State Department and USAID programs. The paper trail shows repeated overlap, access, and coordination—not a cartoon puppet master, but a private fortune acting as a force-multiplier for specific policy outcomes.

Family business and early State Department cables
Paul Soros (George’s older brother) ran shipping, ports, and infrastructure. WikiLeaks State Department cables from the 1970s show U.S. diplomats helping Soros Associates land contracts. In Gabon, cables describe Brown & Root (later Halliburton, with long intelligence-community ties) pushing a Santa Clara port project while embassy staff tracked the bidding. One cable notes meetings inside the Gabonese government that would “eliminate all but a few offers” and that “Soros was in a very good position.” Another states Soros Associates was “virtually certain to get [the] engineering contract.” Similar facilitation appears in pre-revolution Iran.

This is commercial diplomacy: U.S. officials advancing an American businessman’s bids in strategic locations. George’s later philanthropic work sits on top of that family-state relationship, not in a vacuum.

Direct access to Obama-era State Department
FOIA releases obtained by Citizens United show Soros Fund Management and Open Society staff corresponding with then-Assistant Secretary Victoria Nuland in 2016. A May 25 email from Chris Canavan of Soros Fund Management briefs Nuland on Russia’s sovereign bond issue using the familiar “Toria.” Days later Soros and his Ukraine foundation official get a hastily arranged call on European migration policy. Nuland’s team later tells a Soros adviser that one EU country “has changed its mind” on Ukraine visa liberalization and that they are “working it.”

Private finance and official U.S. policy on Ukraine and Russia were talking in real time. That is documented access, not rumor.

Prosecutor pipeline — public records, not theory
The Media Research Center filed 48 public-records requests. The returns include thousands of pages of communications between Soros-funded groups (Fair and Just Prosecution and others) and district attorneys whose campaigns received large independent expenditures. Named offices include Alvin Bragg (Manhattan), George Gascón (Los Angeles), Larry Krasner (Philadelphia), Chesa Boudin (San Francisco, later recalled), Kim Foxx (Cook County), and others. The documents show policy alignment on charging decisions, bail, and “progressive prosecution” after the money arrived.

This is not hidden. It is campaign finance plus subsequent email traffic. The pattern is consistent: fund the candidate, then the office adopts the funder’s preferred charging philosophy.

FOIA black holes and withheld records
Obama Presidential Library FOIA 22-17537-F sought “all emails to George Soros.” 172 assets identified. 7 released in full, 1 in part, 164 withheld entirely. No public content summary exists. Judicial Watch sued State and USAID for grant and contract records involving Open Society entities in Romania, Colombia, Albania, and Macedonia after agencies stalled. Overlap between U.S. taxpayer money and Soros-network groups in those countries is documented in the complaints.

Withholding at that volume is itself a data point.

Durham annex and 2016 emails
A declassified annex to the Durham report describes Russian-hacked material that included purported emails from Open Society’s Leonard Benardo discussing a Clinton-campaign plan to tie Trump to Russia and predicting FBI involvement. Durham’s office assessed the specific Benardo texts as likely composites assembled from multiple hacked think-tank emails (Open Society, Carnegie, others). Benardo denied writing them. The intelligence existed; the FBI did not treat it as a predicate to examine the Clinton side with the same intensity it applied to the Trump side.

Russian services had OSF mail. That is a fact from the annex. Whether the exact wording was authentic or stitched is the contested part.

Other paper
- Panama Papers list Soros-controlled offshore vehicles (Panama, BVI, Bermuda). One vehicle co-invested with Carlyle Group alongside Bin Laden family members. Legal, but opaque.
- 1990s: Radio Free Europe/Radio Liberty research institute and archives transferred to a Soros-funded entity in Prague. U.S. government broadcasting infrastructure handed to a private foundation.
- Earlier regulatory history: CFTC fine for position limits, SEC consent decree on stock activity, French insider-trading conviction (later appealed). Public record.

Amateur conclusion from the stack
The documents do not prove Soros “controls” the State Department, the FBI, or American elections. They do prove a decades-long working relationship between the Soros family businesses, the Open Society grant machine, and U.S. foreign-policy and law-enforcement bureaucracies. Money flows both ways—private grants plus U.S. government contracts to overlapping NGOs. Access is granted at high levels when interests align (Ukraine 2016, prosecutor races, Eastern Europe “open society” programs). Large volumes of relevant emails stay withheld.

That is influence architecture, not magic. Anyone who treats the man as either a cartoon villain or an untouchable saint is ignoring the paper. The paper is sitting in FOIA reading rooms, WikiLeaks cables, campaign-finance filings, and prosecutor inboxes. Read it yourself.

text:
From Karl Streed -

I BET YOU DIDN'Y KNOW ABOUT THIS: AFTER FLIGHT 77 HIT THE PENTAGON ON 9/11, THE FOLLOWING HAPPENED.

A daycare facility inside the Pentagon had many children, including infants who were in heavy cribs. The daycare supervisor, looking at all the children they needed to evacuate, was in a panic over what they could do.

There were many children, mostly toddlers, as well as the infants who would need to be taken out with the cribs. There was no time to try to bundle them into carriers and strollers.

Just then a young Marine came running into the center and asked what they needed. After hearing what the center director was trying to do, he ran back out into the hallway and disappeared. The director thought, "Well, here we are, on our own."

About 2 minutes later, that Marine returned with 40 other Marines in tow.

Each of them grabbed a crib with a child, and the rest started gathering up toddlers.

The director and her staff then helped them take all the children out of the center and down toward the park near the Potomac .

Once they got about 3/4 of a mile outside the building, the Marines stopped in the park, and then did a fabulous thing - they formed a circle with the cribs, which were quite sturdy and heavy, like the covered wagons in the Old West.

Inside this circle of cribs, they put the toddlers, to keep them from wandering off. 

Outside this circle were the 40 Marines, forming a perimeter around the children and waiting for instructions. There they remained until the parents could be notified and come get their children.

The chaplain then said, "I don't think any of us saw nor heard of this on any of the news stories of the day. It was an incredible story of our men there.” There wasn't a dry eye in the room.

The thought of those Marines and what they did and how fast they reacted; could we expect any less from them? It was one of the most touching stories from the Pentagon.

It's the military, not the politicians that ensures our right to life, liberty, and the pursuit of happiness. 

It's the military who salutes the flag, who serves beneath the flag, and whose coffin is draped by the flag.

If you care to offer the smallest token of recognition and appreciation for the military, please pass this on and pray for our men and women, who have served and are currently serving our country, and honor the memory of those who have given the ultimate sacrifice!

God Bless The USA!

Never forget!!!

text:
"It was late in the evening when I made love once more with the Brazilian Princess. She received the tribute of my passion as our river boat emerged from a unknown tributary and finally onto the main Amazon River. The Brazilian Princess pulled me back into bed but it was too hot and humid to lay in her arms. As beautiful as she was and as tired as I was from days of traveling, I wanted to have a smoke before going sleep. I gave her a kiss and put on my linen trousers. Stepping out of the river boat cabin, the thin tattered door swung backwards and closed in the wind.

To no surprise it was those same two strange Brazilian guys sitting down the gangway in the same exact place they were sitting hours before when the Brazilian Princess and I had first returned from our dinner on the main deck. One of them looked my way as I began walking in the other direction.

I had never seen them go inside. Out here a private cabin was rare money and they sat on the floor as if they did not have one. I kept my guard up but wasn't scared of them for just the day before I offered them gifts of tobacco as an attempt to get on their good side. God only knows if they were to throw me overboard nobody would find me.

Though, a lost American might make the news unlike the local guy that was featured on the missing person flyer above the mess deck.

Our little three story wooden boat was sailing upriver from Belém to Manaus and it swayed up and down like it knew that. I walked further up the gangway to the bow, out of sight from anybody on the ship except for an old man with a Brazil Navy hat who standing there, unbothered by the smell of my American smoke. I didn't bother starting a conversation with him. My Portuguese was bad at best and I was already pushing my luck just trying to maintain my balance as the boat rocked back and forth in the heavenly river current. It's lonesome fog light a floating lighthouse in the middle of the world's largest rainforest.

The thunder roared a deathly sound I hadn't heard since Texas, Oklahoma and Louisiana.

What a time to be alive. I couldn't believe I was sailing up the Amazon River. Such a profoundly down to Earth experience. Never in my life had I been surrounded by so much life. No domir. No sonho. Just an unexplainable feeling of pure freedom.

The rain hammered down as I sparked one up. I could just barely make out the silhouette of the Amazon Rainforest behind a mirage of lighting.

I was so far away from Home."

An excerpt from my debut autobiography CALIPOCALYPSE by Darren Stallcup

text:
◆ Meat Is Not Core to the Shakta Tradition

It is a misconception that Shakta Hindus must necessarily be meat-eaters, or that meat somehow occupies a position of primacy in Shakta worship. Across much of northern and western India, the Shakta tradition has predominantly remained sāttvika. 

From Rajasthan to Bihar, Bhagavati is propitiated with offerings of kheer, puri and halwa. Who is there who does not offer these to the Goddess? Or are we now to believe that Bhagavati is somehow not pleased by them?

Animal sacrifice has historically been practised only among very limited sections here. Traditions such as Aṭhāvarī Pūjan and similar rites are themselves forms of sāttvika bali. The scriptures are filled with injunctions prohibiting a Brahmin from performing animal sacrifice. Some texts go so far as to say that a Brahmin incurs the sin of Brahmahatyā by offering animal sacrifice. That is precisely why, throughout much of this part of India, animal sacrifice has generally not existed among Brahmins. It remained largely confined to kings and certain limited communities.

And even there, it was never the sole means of pleasing Bhagavati.

Meat is not the core of the Shakta Dharma.

Some of the greatest stalwarts of the Shakta tradition were strict vegetarians.

Take the great siddha worshipper of Bhagavati Bagalamukhi of Datia, Rashtra-Rishi Swamiji Maharaj, who was completely vegetarian. Or the great Tantracharya and Jaipur Rajpandit Shri Saryu Prasad Dwivedi Ji, author of Saptashati-Sarvasva. Or even the Bengali-born supreme Shakta scholar, Mahamahopadhyaya Pandit Shri Gopinath Kaviraj.

All of them, and innumerable great Shakta scholars, sādhakas and ācāryas like them, were strict vegetarians.

Study the traditions of Shakta sādhakas and ācāryas and, throughout northern and western India, you will find perhaps 90% of them vegetarian. Dakshinachara predominates almost everywhere.

The Shankaracharyas of Sringeri, Puri, Kanchi, Dwarka and other Peethas are themselves profound Shaktas and worshippers of Bhagavati. Yet there is not the slightest use of meat in their mathas, nor is meat offered to the forms of Bhagavati worshipped there.

So are they not Shaktas? Are they not devotees of Bhagavati?

Calling meat the “core” of Shaktism is rather like calling the manjira the core of Vaishnavism.

If someone does not play the manjira, will we refuse to recognise him as a Vaishnava?

You may not know this, but many rare goddesses of the Tantra-Agama tradition, deities whose elaborate descriptions and ritual procedures are preserved in the Sanatana Agamas but whose living worship has become uncommon, continue to be worshipped extensively among Jains.

Jvalamalini, Chakreshwari, Tvarita and others are examples. Padmavati, Ambika, Lakshmi and Saraswati are, of course, widely prominent already.

But I am speaking specifically of the rarer Tantric devis.

The worship of devis is a deeply established tradition among Jains, and the elaborate ritual systems of several such deities are remarkably similar in both Sanatani and Jain traditions.

Yet among Jains the question of using meat does not arise at all.

So does that mean the devi simply refuses to be pleased there?

In Rajasthan, Karni Mata Ji, herself a supreme devotee of Bhagavati and revered as a manifestation of the Goddess, is worshipped through an entirely sāttvika tradition.

Except for a very limited number of ancient temples, most old Devi temples and Shakta Peethas have had no practice involving meat whatsoever. In those few places where such a custom did exist, it generally consisted of bali on specific ritual occasions.

It certainly did not mean rows upon rows of meat shops standing outside the temple.

There is absolutely no sanction anywhere in the Shakta tradition for turning the surroundings of a Devi temple into a marketplace of meat.

And bali and meat are themselves entirely separate questions.

To imagine that Bhagavati cannot even be worshipped without meat is sheer foolishness.

Take water in your hand and make a sankalpa:

“I surrender my own bala, my strength to Bhagavati.”

That too is bali.

The moment the sankalpa is made, one’s own strength has been offered in sacrifice, and the body even appears momentarily weakened.

The truly intense, exalted devotees who always crawl at the feet of the Bhagawati have even been known to offer themselves as bali.

King Suratha and the Vaishya Samadhi did precisely this.

The Devi Mahatmya says:

“nijagātrāsṛgukṣitam”

For three years, while performing tapas before an earthen image of Bhagavati, they offered bali sprinkled with their own blood and their own flesh.

That is the Shakta idea of sacrifice at its highest.

To reduce Shakta Dharma to meat is therefore not merely historically shallow; it completely misunderstands what bali, sādhana and surrender mean within the tradition.

◆―― Mudit ――◆

“Here are the main ones, with the core facts and why they failed.
1937 – Peel Commission (British)
The first formal two-state proposal. It recommended a small Jewish state and a larger Arab state (linked to Transjordan), plus population transfers. Jewish leaders accepted the principle of partition. Arab leadership rejected it outright and violence followed.
1947 – UN Partition Plan (Resolution 181)
The UN voted to create a Jewish state and an Arab state, with Jerusalem under international administration. The Jewish Agency accepted it. The Arab Higher Committee and surrounding Arab states rejected it and went to war after Israel declared independence. No Arab state was established in the portion allocated to it.
Mahmoud Abbas later called the 1947 rejection “our mistake” as well as an Arab one.
After 1967
Israel captured the West Bank and Gaza. It offered to return land to the Arab states that had controlled those territories in exchange for peace. The Arab League’s Khartoum summit responded with the “Three Noes”: no peace, no recognition, no negotiations.
The 1978 Camp David Accords between Israel and Egypt included a framework for Palestinian autonomy leading to negotiations on final status. The PLO rejected it.
Oslo process (1993–2000)
The PLO accepted a phased process toward self-government and eventual final-status talks on a state. Hamas rejected Oslo. Final-status negotiations never produced an agreement.
2000 Camp David + Clinton Parameters
Israeli Prime Minister Ehud Barak, with U.S. mediation, offered a Palestinian state on roughly 91–97% of the West Bank plus all of Gaza, land swaps, and arrangements for Jerusalem. Yasser Arafat rejected the offer and did not present a detailed counter-proposal. The Second Intifada followed. Palestinians argued the map left them with non-contiguous “cantons,” insufficient control of borders/airspace, and no adequate resolution of refugees or East Jerusalem.
2008 Olmert offer
Prime Minister Ehud Olmert presented Mahmoud Abbas a map for a state on about 93–94% of the West Bank with 1:1 land swaps, shared arrangements in Jerusalem, and a limited number of refugees admitted to Israel. Abbas did not accept it. He later said the gaps were too wide and that he was not given the map to study properly; Olmert has said Abbas never formally said no.
Later U.S.-brokered efforts (Kerry framework 2014, Trump plan 2020) were also rejected or not engaged with by the Palestinian Authority.
Context that is often omitted
•From 1948 to 1967 the West Bank was annexed by Jordan and Gaza was administered by Egypt. Neither created an independent Palestinian state.
•Palestinian leadership has also unilaterally declared a state (1988) and pursued recognition at the UN without a negotiated settlement with Israel.
•Recurring Palestinian objections have been: incomplete sovereignty, settlements, Jerusalem (especially the Temple Mount/Haram), and the demand for a large-scale “right of return” of 1948 refugees and descendants into Israel itself, not only into a Palestinian state. Israeli governments have treated that last demand as incompatible with Israel remaining a Jewish-majority state.
So the short answer is: a Palestinian state was formally proposed or placed on the table multiple times (Peel 1937, UN 1947, and several Israeli/U.S. offers after 2000). Arab and later Palestinian leadership declined or did not close those deals. Whether those offers were “generous enough” or “genuine” is still bitterly disputed; the historical record of the proposals and the rejections is not.”

text:
Modern secularism treats the body as personal property, yours to use, lease, or sell as you see fit.

The trial of Saint Lucy of Syracuse in 304 AD rests on the exact opposite claim: your body is a temple, and it belongs to God before it belongs to you or to the state.

Lucy, a young Christian virgin from Sicily, was hauled before a Roman magistrate during Diocletian's persecution and ordered to sacrifice to the pagan gods. She refused.

The Acta, the ancient trial accounts, record the logic behind her refusal. Lucy did not argue that sacrifice was merely distasteful or that she preferred a different religion. Her defense was theological: she was consecrated to Christ, and her body was a dwelling place of the Holy Spirit. It could not be offered to another god because it had already been claimed.

The magistrate understood the challenge perfectly. According to the traditional account, he ordered her dragged to a brothel, a deliberate judicial tactic. If the state could not win her worship, it would desecrate what she called a temple. The point was to prove that Rome, not God, held final title over the human body.

The tradition holds that she could not be moved. She was killed, and the Church has remembered her ever since.

Here is what most people miss. Lucy is named in the Roman Canon of the Mass, the oldest Eucharistic prayer in the Latin Church, alongside the apostles and the earliest martyrs. Every time that prayer is said, the Church asserts her argument as its own.

Two claims about the body collided in that courtroom. Rome said the body is state property. Lucy said it is a temple of the Holy Spirit.

Which claim do you think won, and why does it still matter?

The earliest records of vegetarianism as a concept and practice amongst a significant number of people are from ancient India, especially among the Buddhists and Jains.

Jain and Buddhist sources show that the principle of nonviolence - ahimsa toward animals was an established rule in both religions as early as the 6th century BCE.

Vegetarianism among Brahmins and upper castes in India evolved as a social and religious response to the rise of Buddhism and Jainism. 

Temple Priests needed to keep their high status, hence brahmins began adopting vegetarianism so that these two new sects couldn't claim moral superiority.

They adopted non-violence to match popular public morals. Diet became a tool to show ritual purity. Vegetarianism is much higher among upper caste Hindus.

Traditionally identified with the Kshatriya (warrior and ruler) caste, historical Rajput lifestyle included hunting (shikar) and meat consumption to build physical strength. 

Iconic dishes like Laal Maas and Junglee Maas originated from these royal and camp-style hunting traditions.

Animal sacrifices (Bali) to deities like Chamunda Devi are part of certain traditional Rajput rituals, where the meat is served as consecrated Prasad. 

Dietary practices differ widely by location; for example, some communities in Uttar Pradesh or Madhya Pradesh may observe household vegetarianism or prepare non-vegetarian food separately from the main kitchen, while others in different regions maintain regular meat or fish consumption. 

Historical records and traditions show that meat consumption was a common and accepted part of the martial lifestyle for many Suryavanshi and other Rajput clans, though dietary practices vary today.

Ancient texts like the Valmiki Ramayana - from which Suryavanshi Rajputs claim descent through Lord Rama - describe heroic figures participating in hunting and consuming game. 

Meat from hunted game or ritual animal sacrifices (bali) was frequently offered to clan deities (kuldevi) and later consumed as consecrated food (mahaprasad). 

Several regional Brahmin communities in India traditionally consume non-vegetarian food, such as fish, mutton, and seafood, depending on their geography, local culture, and religious traditions.

Bengali Brahmins consume fish daily as a staple from local rivers, though Vaishnava families usually stay vegetarian.

Gaud Saraswat Brahmins (GSB) & Chitpavan Brahmins, the communities along the Konkan coast and parts of Karnataka frequently consume seafood and fish cooked in coconut gravies.

Assamese and Odia Brahmins incorporate fish or meat into their meals, particularly connected to regional temple traditions.

Even before Jesus was crucified, he underwent a merciless beating and public mocking that were meant not only to inflict maximum pain but also to humiliate him. Isaiah prophesies this torture and abuse that the Messiah would have to endure.

Isaiah 50:6 foretells that the Savior would offer his back to those who beat him, which prophesies the vicious flogging that Jesus endured. In ancient Roman times, flogging was often administered before crucifixion and was done with a whip made of strips of leather embedded with lead balls and shards of bone to inflict gaping wounds that caused the victim unbelievable agony. The church historian Eusebius described a later Roman flogging by saying, “[The victim’s] veins were laid bare, and the inner muscles and sinews, and even the bowels, were exposed.” The New Testament confirms that Jesus received the prophesied flogging (see Matthew 27:26; John 19:1).

Isaiah also predicts that the Messiah would endure mocking and spitting. Jesus experienced the cruel taunts of the temple guards (see Luke 22:63–65), of the Roman guards (see Matthew 27:27–31), of the onlookers, of the religious leaders and even of the robbers crucified with him (see Matthew 27:39–44).

NuNew stops. He glances at the volume beneath his hand, then back at the letter.

The book before you contains what I learned of pearl magic. It may help you understand your gift but it cannot defeat Tharn. The spell that imprisoned him is preserved in another tome, entrusted to the House of Black. It is called the Book of Death.

Its last recorded resting place is the Temple of Lux. The House of Black has the knowledge required to reach it.

Although I should warn you. Do not mistake possession of the tome for the means to wield it. Tharn’s original defeat required both a pearl mage and a shadow mage. Their combined magic is what freed the souls from whom he drew his strength and then bound what remained of him. You will need to do the same.

NuNew lowers the page.

The empty space beneath the black banner rises in his mind. Nobody has stood there in decades.

He looks around the little room, suddenly aching for its owner to be alive. To be sitting across the desk instead of speaking to him through a letter.

“What if I can’t find them?” he whispers. The letter offers no answer. There is only one final paragraph.

I have left you all that I could preserve. Read carefully. Do not be ashamed of needing help, however much power the world tells you, that you possess. I needed it too.

NuNew covers his mouth. For the first time since yesterday his tears come quietly. He lets them. Then he wipes his face, lays the letter beside him and opens the Book of Life to its first page.

NuNew skims through the book but a name on the next page catches his attention.
Tharn.

Beneath it, his ancestor has written some information. NuNew draws the lamp closer.

Tharn was born with no exceptional gift.
He reads the sentence again. During his Rite of Awakening, the Origin Stone identified Tharn as an arcane mage with no specialised affinity and only modest magical reserves. He was freeborn, with no ancient House behind him. But he was brilliant.

His instructors’ earliest assessments describe a student who mastered complex runes with extraordinary speed. He corrected calculations in textbooks. Designed enchantments that required less power than the academy’s standard spells. Found solutions to problems students with far larger reserves could barely understand.

NuNew traces a line copied from one of those assessments.

Remarkable ingenuity. Unfortunately limited by the capacity of his core.

His ancestor has underlined the sentence. In the margin, he has written: They recognised his accomplishments but still thought of him as less.

NuNew looks away. He knows what it is to hear disappointment after praise. For Tharn, the judgment had been reversed. So much ability. So little power.

NuNew turns the page.

Tharn began questioning why the result of a single ceremony should determine the limits of his future. While heirs received private instruction in techniques guarded by their families, he searched for knowledge nobody would willingly teach him. His search led him into the forbidden archives. There, he discovered magic that did not depend entirely upon the strength of the caster’s core +

The day after the Feast of the Nativity of the Most Holy Theotokos, the Greek Catholic Church commemorates her parents, Saints Joachim and Anna.

The names of today’s saints are of Hebrew origin.  
Joachim means "God will raise him up", and Anna means "gracious" or "beloved."

According to the Protoevangelium of James, Joachim was the husband of Saint Anna and the father of the Mother of God, Mary. 

Tradition connected with accounts of Mary’s life says that Joachim and Anna later lived in Jerusalem; St. John Damascene specifies that it was near the Sheep Gate. Because they were childless, Joachim was deprived of the right to offer sacrifices in the Temple. He withdrew into solitude but continued to live piously and charitably. After 20 years of marriage, an angel announced to him that a child would be born to them; according to one tradition, this happened in Nazareth.

Another tradition, originating from the ancient Jerusalem church dedicated to the Virgin Mary, claims that Mary was born and lived in Jerusalem. However, the crypt and burial place of Joachim and Anna in that church were established much later.

In the Eastern Church, Epiphanius of Salamis mentions Joachim repeatedly, and a lasting tradition of veneration for him developed in the 7th century.

Anna is first mentioned in the Protoevangelium of James (2nd century). According to tradition, she died in Jerusalem and was buried in her own home. In 710, her relics were transferred to Constantinople. The cult of Saint Anna in the East reaches back to the 6th century...

text:
25 More Trump Achievements: The First List Was Just the Beginning

The Top 25 barely scratched the surface. Here are 25 more laws, victories, reforms, and measurable results from the most consequential Presidency of the modern era.

My original list of Trump’s Top 25 achievements was supposed to be a cheat sheet. Instead, it drew a million views on X, thousands of new followers, and coverage from Dan Bongino’s show to Roger Stone’s.

Why? Because millions know something extraordinary is happening, but almost no one gives them the receipts. The Enemedia buries every victory. Republicans announce today’s win and forget yesterday’s. Voters sense that Trump is transforming the country but can’t explain how.

So here's the sequel. These are achievements, not promises.

You don’t have to memorize all 25. Learn five. And when somebody says Trump “hasn’t done much,” show them how wrong they are.

Trump Restored Speech, Sovereignty, and Safety

1. He dismantled the federal censorship machine at home—and confronted government censorship abroad.

On his first day back in office, Trump prohibited federal employees and agencies from coercing or paying private companies to censor constitutionally protected speech. He ordered an investigation of the Biden Administration’s abuses, gutted CISA’s censorship apparatus, and made free speech a foreign-policy priority. He also imposed visa restrictions on foreign officials and NGO operatives who pressured American platforms to silence Americans.

2. He ended state-run “public” broadcasting.

Not only was government unconstitutionally censoring Americans’ free speech: it was subsidizing Democrats’ talking points. Republicans have talked for decades, but Trump delivered, cutting off funding for the Corporation for Public Broadcasting. Now PBS and NPR must compete for audiences and donors like everyone else.

3. He ended catch-and-release.

Sealing the border was No. 1 in my first list. But what happened after illegal aliens were caught deserves its own place. Under Biden, arrest often meant a bus ticket, a court date years away, and easy disappearance into the country. 

Under Trump, it means detention and removal. The Border Patrol has now recorded 15 consecutive months without releasing a single apprehended illegal alien into America.

4. He helped drive fentanyl trafficking—and fentanyl deaths—sharply downward.

Under President Trump, fentanyl trafficking at the southern border fell 56 percent compared with the same period in 2024. CDC figures showed synthetic-opioid deaths falling from 48,913 in 2024 to 38,084 in 2025 — a 22 percent plunge.

5. He designated the cartels as terrorists—and took the counter-narcotics war to sea.

Trump designated eight cartels and transnational criminal organizations as terrorist groups, thus unlocking powerful sanctions, intelligence, and enforcement tools. He stopped treating them like ordinary criminals and started treating them as the government-sponsored paramilitary forces they actually are. 

The Coast Guard also set an all-time record, seizing nearly 510,000 pounds of cocaine across the Eastern Pacific and Caribbean in fiscal 2025, and blowing up even more.

6. He crushed Washington, D.C.’s violent-crime wave.

Trump refused to let America’s capital remain a cesspool of murders, rapes, carjackings, and municipal incompetence. He flooded Washington with federal law-enforcement resources and forced cooperation among police, prosecutors, and federal agencies. One year later, homicides are down 45 percent, carjackings 64 percent, and authorities have seized nearly 2,000 illegal guns.

Urban violence disproportionately victimizes the poor. Restoring order is not oppression: it’s liberation.

7. He restored Second Amendment rights.

Trump ordered the entire executive branch to identify and reverse policies that infringed the right to keep and bear arms. DOJ created a Second Amendment Enforcement Task Force. ATF repealed Biden’s punitive “Zero Tolerance” policy for gun dealers and other unreasonable restrictions on selling firearms.

Then Trump’s DOJ filed the first affirmative civil-rights lawsuit in Department history, forcing Los Angeles County to end nine-month delays for concealed-carry permits. It also restored the congressionally authorized process through which deserving Americans may regain federal firearms rights — and zeroed out the $200 federal tax on suppressors.

Trump Encouraged Work, Savings, and Ownership

8. He ended federal income tax on tips and overtime pay.

Trump’s One Big Beautiful Bill allows eligible workers to deduct up to $25,000 in qualified tips through 2028. It also created a deduction for the overtime premium — up to $12,500 for an individual or $25,000 for a married couple. It’s hard to think of a more pro-working-class reform than that.

9. He eliminated the tax on Social Security for nearly all seniors.

Under the One Big Beautiful Bill, seniors may deduct an additional $6,000 apiece or $12,000 for a qualifying married couple. For most seniors, that eliminates federal income tax on retirement income, including Social Security.

The fact that Democrats taxed Social Security in the first place is obscene. Trump reversed it.

10. He made Opportunity Zones permanent.

Trump’s Opportunity Zones steer private capital toward distressed communities by rewarding long-term investment. The One Big Beautiful Bill made them permanent and established recurring qualifying rounds, giving investors and local leaders the certainty to build for decades.

The Left’s answer to poverty is always another federal program. Trump’s is capital, ownership, businesses, homes, and jobs.

11. He protected farms and family businesses from the death tax.

The death tax can force a grieving family to sell family farms, homes, and businesses just to pay Washington. But Trump made it easier to pass a lifetime’s work and dreams on to the next generation. He increased the federal estate-and-gift-tax exclusion to $15 million per person in 2026, with inflation adjustments and no scheduled expiration — potentially $30 million for a married couple.

Trump Put Families and Good Health First

12. He expanded Health Savings Accounts — and created a $50 billion rural-health fund.

Thanks to the One Big Beautiful Bill, millions more Americans can use Health Savings Accounts. The result? More personal control and fewer gatekeepers between doctor and patient.

Trump also created a $50 billion Rural Health Transformation Program, reversing years of rural hospital closures under Biden.

13. He used TrumpRx and most-favored-nation agreements to force down drug prices.

For decades, Americans paid the world’s highest drug prices while socialist governments imposed price controls and freeloaded on American innovation. Trump turned that arrangement on its head, securing most-favored-nation agreements with 26 drugmakers covering 89 percent of the branded-drug market. 

It’s not a price control: it’s the end of a free ride. Foreign governments must now pay more for American drugs so Americans can pay less.

Moreover, the President’s new TrumpRx program gives patients direct access to steep discounts. Patients have already saved more than $700 million, while the latest nine deals added $19.6 billion in American manufacturing commitments.

14. He turned MAHA from a slogan into reality.

Trump, Robert F. Kennedy Jr., and MAHA forced a reckoning. HHS and FDA began moving manufacturers away from petroleum-based dyes, approved natural alternatives, changed labeling rules, and created a public tracker of corporate promises.

For the first time in generations, Washington is asking why American children are fat and sick — and fixing the problem instead of prescribing another drug.

15. He prioritized adoption and family formation.

Trump made the adoption tax credit partly refundable, allowing eligible families to receive up to $5,000 per adopted child even when they owe less tax. He also raised tax-free dependent-care assistance from $5,000 to $7,500 in 2026. Trump is forcing government to stop making it harder to adopt, care for dependents, or build families.

16. He stood up for victims of revenge porn and sexual deepfakes.

The TAKE IT DOWN Act criminalized specified nonconsensual intimate imagery, including AI-generated sexual deepfakes. Covered platforms must now provide a reporting process and must remove all qualifying images within 48 hours. Perps go to prison.

17. He stopped federal support for dangerous gain-of-function research in sketchy foreign labs.

Wuhan should have ended this debate. Instead, the Fauci-led bureaucracy doubled down on reckless experimentation and dangerous gain-of-function research, not just in the United States but in sketchy foreign labs, even in China. Trump put a stop to it, terminating projects in countries of concern and suspending other high-risk programs.

Trump Built America’s Economic Future

18. He turned valuable access to the world’s largest consumer market into leverage and revenue.

Washington treated access to the richest consumer market on Earth into a global entitlement, while allowing them to maintain huge trade barriers against U.S. producers. Trump turned that on its head. By January 2026, the Administration reported $300 billion in gross tariff collections.

The President used those tariffs to negotiate new trade deals with countries representing two-thirds of the global economy. In the process, he opened their markets, increased their purchases of U.S. energy, farm produce, and goods, supported industries vital to national security, and made companies begin building factories here.

19. He began breaking China’s rare-earth chokehold.

China dominates the minerals and magnets inside everything from smartphones to submarines. It controls 92 percent of global rare-earths refining. That’s not free trade: It’s a strategic hostage situation.

Trump’s Pentagon partnered with MP Materials to expand American rare-earth separation and magnet production, backed by long-term purchases and a domestic price floor. He also made deals with allied nations to bring their own production and refining online.

20. He created a Strategic Bitcoin Reserve — and made America the center of digital finance.

Trump created a Strategic Bitcoin Reserve by ordering the government to keep, rather than auction off, Bitcoin forfeited in criminal and civil cases. He also championed and signed the GENIUS Act, America’s first national framework for dollar-backed stablecoins, replacing Biden’s war on crypto with rules establishing global leadership and dollar dominance.

A stablecoin is a digital dollar that anyone with a smartphone can hold and spend, anywhere on Earth, without all the expensive banking fees. Under Trump’s law, the companies issuing those coins must back them with safe dollar assets, especially short-term U.S. Treasuries. So as stablecoins spread, they expand the dollar’s reach and dominance, even in countries with strict currency controls.

In short: instead of depending on the goodwill of foreign central banks, America can distribute the dollar system directly to billions of people and businesses.

21. He launched the AI Action Plan and Genesis Mission.

Trump’s AI Action Plan attacks the energy, permitting, infrastructure, and regulatory bottlenecks that could hand this century’s most important technology to China. Genesis brings federal data, national labs, supercomputers, and private AI companies together to accelerate discovery. So far, the Energy Department has secured more than $800 million in partner commitments.

22. He restored the Moon to the center of American national strategy.

Trump ordered America back to the Moon by 2028, with initial elements of a permanent base at its strategically vital South Pole by 2030. He also directed development of space-based nuclear power and nuclear rockets, and greater use of America’s unmatched commercial-space industry.

The Moon is the high ground of twenty-first-century industry, science, logistics, and defense — the first great arena of Astropolitics. Trump gave America the means to beat China and make the future free.

Trump Reasserted American Power Around the World

23. He brought American hostages home.

By March 2026, the Administration had secured the release of 105 detained Americans. Marc Fogel came home after years in a Russian prison. George Glezmann came home after two years in Taliban captivity. So did prisoners held by Hamas, Belarus, Venezuela, and others.

24. He replaced foreign aid with investment and trade.

For a century, Washington measured compassion by how many dollars it spent, regardless of the often abysmal results. Trump put a stop to that: his “Trade Over Aid” doctrine offers not a handout but investment, markets, infrastructure, and partnership.

The December 2025 agreement with the Democratic Republic of the Congo is a perfect example. It tied American investment to secure critical-mineral supply chains. This creates Congolese jobs and infrastructure while rewarding American investors and securing American supply chains. It also rescues impoverished Third World countries from Chinese Communist debt traps.

25. He launched a $76.6 billion American undersea buildup — and began rebuilding the shipyards to sustain it.

China is on track to outnumber the U.S. submarine fleet by 2030. Biden did nothing about it. But in July 2026, Trump’s Navy awarded contracts for five Columbia-class ballistic-missile submarines and nine Block VI Virginia-class attack submarines. The package totals $76.6 billion — an historic contract allowing shipbuilders to expand production lines and train skilled workers.

The President also ordered plans for a fifth Navy shipyard — the first new one in more than 80 years — along with acquisition, workforce, and repair reforms.

Now Act Like It Matters

Trump produced all of these “25 more” accomplishments in just a year and a half, while also accumulating that earlier Top 25 achievements list, accomplishments so consequential that these didn’t make the original cut.

The Republican Party’s greatest political problem this fall is not a lack of victories. It’s that too many Republicans have no idea what — or how much — they’ve accomplished.

It’s up to each of us to tell our story. Donald Trump is delivering great things, whether or not heaven on earth has broken out quite yet. Do the work, send him the team he needs to finish the job, and then get ready for 2028.

Take the time to learn at least five of these victories. Share this list with someone who needs it. Take friends to the polls. And vote as though the most consequential Presidency in modern history depends on what you do.

Because it does.

A video purportedly showing the early stages of construction of the #Somalia–Türkiye #spaceport project offers a glimpse of what could become one of #Africa’s most strategically important technological developments.

The project, which is already under construction, represents a remarkable convergence of #Somali geography and Turkish aerospace capabilities. Somalia’s position close to the #Equator, combined with its vast eastern coastline facing the Indian Ocean, gives the country significant natural advantages as a potential launch location. Launching near the Equator can provide rockets with an additional boost from Earth’s rotation, potentially reducing fuel requirements and increasing payload capacity for suitable missions. Somalia’s open ocean to the east also provides a vast downrange area for launches.

For Somalia, however, the significance of the project goes far beyond rockets and satellites.

A successful spaceport could become the foundation of an entirely new #SpaceEconomy, attracting international #satellite operators, aerospace companies, engineers, researchers, universities and technology investors to the country. Türkiye has stated that the facility is intended to serve the growing global commercial space market, while also providing Türkiye with independent access to orbit and strengthening bilateral cooperation in science and technology.

The long-term vision could encompass launch facilities, spacecraft and launch-vehicle integration areas, propellant infrastructure, engineering and research facilities, mission-control capabilities, educational institutions and accommodation for the thousands of people who could eventually work around the emerging spaceport ecosystem.

Such an ecosystem could create opportunities for Somali engineers, scientists, technicians, entrepreneurs and students, allowing the country's young population to participate directly in one of the world's fastest-growing high-technology industries. Knowledge transfer and capacity building are already identified as important objectives of the Somalia–Türkiye space partnership.

The economic potential is equally significant. In addition to revenue from satellite launches, a mature space industry could generate income through spacecraft testing and integration, engineering services, manufacturing, research and development, education, logistics, hospitality and space-related tourism. Some projections circulating around the project envisage hundreds of millions of dollars in annual launch-related revenue, potentially complemented by billions of dollars in wider economic activity as an industrial ecosystem develops.

For #Mogadishu, this could ultimately mean far more than simply hosting a launchpad. Somalia could become a gateway between Earth and space for an entire region.

For Türkiye, the partnership offers an opportunity to establish independent access to space while expanding its rapidly developing aerospace and satellite industries. For Somalia, it offers something potentially even more transformative: the chance to develop an entirely new high-technology economic sector on #African soil.

The Somalia–Türkiye partnership has already expanded across infrastructure, healthcare, education, defense, energy and economic development. Space could become the next great frontier of that partnership.

If developed transparently, sustainably and with substantial Somali participation, the project could help transform Somalia's Indian Ocean coastline into a hub for science, technology, investment and innovation—turning the country's unique geographical position into a long-term national economic asset.

Somalia has spent decades looking toward the horizon. With the right partnerships, it may soon be looking beyond it. 🇸🇴🤝🇹🇷🚀

A nuanced take about the recent UK sanctions, with other European countries joining.

If I believed that dismantling all the settlements would lead to genuine peace, I would support it. In fact, the Palestinians have been offered generous proposals that would have given them exactly that, and they rejected them.

Unfortunately, we have tried this before, in Gaza, 2005. What we got was Hamas, tens of thousands of rockets fired at Israeli communities, and a massacre involving r*ape, looting, and kidnapping.

At the heart of this conflict is a refusal to accept that Jews should be able to live under their own sovereignty in the one place in the world where they have more than 3,000 years of continuous, archaeologically documented history of presence.

And I have to ask: how can countries that are members of NATO remain so vocal about Israel while saying so little about the occupation of Northern Cyprus by another NATO member, Turkey?

How does it not concern these countries that Turkey, a NATO member, has in recent years restricted access to water for around a million Kurds? That it has persecuted and repressed them? How is this acceptable to countries that are so quick to condemn Israel, when some of them are NATO members themselves?

All of this leads me to the uncomfortable conclusion that perhaps too many European countries are, in practice, far too comfortable with the continuation of this conflict, and are keen on seeing more people suffer. 

As for the Israeli government, let me criticize it as an Israeli: there isn’t a single moral or political card left for us to play that you haven’t already burned.

You threw our moral legitimacy out the window by failing to enforce the law against extremist violence in Judea and Samaria, and even by tolerating outrageous conduct by members of the Knesset.

Whatever legitimate arguments we have, and we do have legitimate arguments (!), you undermine through sheer incompetence.

text:
When your own flesh and blood steps in front of a camera to dismantle your image, you know the family dynamics run deeper than any corporate feud.
Alex Gibney’s upcoming four-hour documentary "Musk" features extensive interviews with the tech mogul's estranged father, Errol Musk. For a father to sit down for a major cinematic deep dive into his son’s life opens a window into a profoundly complicated, often toxic psychological landscape.  
The dynamic between the two reads like a masterclass in modern resentment:
 The Shadow of the Giant: To watch your child ascend to become one of the most powerful and wealthiest figures on earth while you remain in the background is a heavy psychological burden. When Errol publicly downplays his son, critiques his appearance, or refuses to offer standard paternal praise, it often feels like a desperate bid to reclaim authority—positioning himself as the patriarch looking down from above, rather than a man entirely eclipsed by his offspring's global footprint.  
 Capitalizing on the Brand: Errol has long understood that the "Musk" surname is a massive global currency. By frequently courting podcasters, journalists, and tabloid media to air family grievances, he secures his own platform. Trading on family friction and airing personal linen in public guarantees headlines, turning controversy into a steady stream of attention.
When a father uses public media to take jabs at a son who has largely distanced himself, it stops looking like ordinary parental concern and turns into a persistent tug-of-war for relevance—proving that all the power, rockets, and capital in the world can't outrun a broken family tree. #ErrolMusk
