text:
Pop star Katy Perry completed a brief foray into space Monday, roaring to the edge of the cosmos with an all-women crew on one of billionaire Jeff Bezos’s rockets.
The “Firework” and “California Gurls” singer was lofted more than 60 miles (100 kilometers) above the Earth’s surface in a vessel from Blue Origin, the space company owned by the Amazon founder.
Five other women — including Bezos’s fiancee Lauren Sanchez — were on the flight, which took off from western Texas shortly after 8:30 am (1330 GMT) before safely landing again some 10 minutes later.
The flight brought the passengers beyond the Karman line — the internationally recognized boundary of space.
One of the other passengers, TV presenter Gayle King, said Perry sang “What a wonderful world” in space.
“It’s a 10 out of 10. That’s my review. Definitely go for it,” the singer said after she was safely back on Earth.
Their fully automated craft rose vertically before the crew capsule detached mid-flight, later falling back to the ground slowed by parachutes and a retro rocket.
The jubilant women then emerged, with Perry kissing the ground after exiting the capsule.
“I think this experience has shown me you never know how much love is inside of you, like how much love you have to give and how loved you are until the day you launch,” she said.
Monday’s mission was the first all-woman space crew since Valentina Tereshkova’s historic solo flight in 1963.
It is also the 11th sub-orbital crewed operation by Blue Origin, which has offered space tourism experiences for several years.
The company does not publicly communicate the price of trips made possible by its New Shepard rocket.
They were expected to have a brief period when the women could unbuckle from their seats and float in zero gravity.
– ‘Inspiration’ –
Perry, launched onto the international stage with her 2008 hit “I Kissed a Girl,” was also travelling alongside Sanchez, King, film producer Kerianne Flynn, former NASA scientist Aisha Bowe and Amanda Nguyen, founder of a campaign group against sexual violence.
They follow 52 previous Blue Origin passengers, including longtime “Star Trek” leading man William Shatner.
King’s close friend — talk show legend Oprah Winfrey — was among those watching the launch in Texas.
“It’s oddly quiet when you get up there… you look down at the planet and think, ‘That’s where we came from?’ And to me it’s such a reminder about how we need to do better and be better,” King said.
Perry recently told Elle magazine that she was taking part “for my daughter Daisy,” whom she shares with actor Orlando Bloom, “to inspire her to never have limits on her dreams.”
Such high-profile guests are intended to keep public interest in Blue Origin’s work, as it battles multiple rival firms in the space tourism field.
Bezos’ top challenger in passenger flights is Virgin Galactic, which offers a similar sub-orbital experience.
But Blue Origin aims in the future to bring space tourists into orbit, competing directly with Elon Musk’s SpaceX.
In January, Blue Origin’s much more powerful New Glenn rocket successfully completed its first unmanned orbital mission.

Apple origin : 

The rugged mountain slopes of the Tian Shan range in Kazakhstan.
Wild Ancestor: The wild species Malus sieversii is the direct ancestor of the modern cultivated apple.
Spread: Ancient traders and animals carried the seeds along the Silk Road.
Genetics: Modern DNA studies prove that most cultivated apples trace their roots back to these Kazakh forests.
Wild Ancestor: The tough and sweet Malus sieversii is the primary genetic parent of nearly all modern apples.
Almaty's Name: The largest city in Kazakhstan, Almaty, translates to "father of apples" or "full of apples".
Early Spread: Bears and birds first carried the seeds, and human traders along the Silk Road later spread them toward Europe and Asia.

    The apple of discord (lesser known myths,Greek mythology)

    The apple of discord is a Greek mythology tale where Eris, the goddess of chaos, tossed a golden apple inscribed "To the fairest" into a royal wedding. It sparked a fierce quarrel among three goddesses Hera, Athena, and Aphrodite that led directly to the Trojan War.

The Wedding and the Golden Apple The Snub: 
     The sea goddess Thetis and her husband Peleus held a grand wedding. They did not invite Eris, the goddess of strife, because she only brought fights and bad moods.The Revenge: Mad about the slight, Eris crashed the party anyway. She threw a bright golden apple onto the banquet table.The Inscription: Words were carved into the apple that said "Kalliste" or "To the fairest"

The Fight of the Goddesses The Claims:
     Three powerful goddesses immediately wanted the apple: Hera (queen of the gods), Athena (goddess of wisdom), and Aphrodite (goddess of love).The Deadlock: No other god dared to say who was the best or most beautiful, as picking one meant making the other two enemies for life.The Choice: Zeus refused to pick, so he sent them to a young shepherd and prince of Troy named Paris.

The Judgment of Paris The Bribes: 

    The goddesses tried to buy his vote. Hera promised him supreme power and control over Asia. Athena promised him glory and skill in every battle. Aphrodite made the best offer: she promised him Helen, the most beautiful mortal woman alive.The Winner: Paris gave the golden apple to Aphrodite.

The Result The Abduction: Paris sailed to Sparta and won Helen away from her husband, King Menelaus. Some versions say she fell in love with him, while others say Aphrodite used magic.
     The War: When Paris took Helen back to Troy, the angry Greek kings joined forces under Agamemnon and sailed to attack Troy, starting a ten year war....

More known religious concepts about the apple:

    In the Book of Genesis, the forbidden fruit in the Garden of Eden is only called peri, a generic Hebrew word for "fruit". The popular idea that Eve ate an apple comes from a Latin wordplay in the 4th century and old European art.

The Biblical story the rule: 

      God told Adam and Eve they could eat from any tree in the garden except one. That was the tree of the knowledge of good and evil.The Test: A talking serpent tempted Eve. It told her she would not die, but would become like God.The Choice: Eve saw that the fruit looked good and wanted wisdom. She picked it, ate it, and gave some to Adam, who was with her.The Result: Their eyes opened to their nakedness, they felt shame, and God sent them out of the garden.

How the Apple Became Famous The Latin Pun: 

       When St. Jerome translated the Bible into Latin, he used the word malum. In Latin, malum means both "evil" and an apple-like fruit.The Art: Medieval and Renaissance painters in Europe used the familiar local apple as a symbol for sin and the forbidden fruit in their artwork...  

        Summarising: What is the concept of the apple in history religion and conceptual meaning.

    The apple is a rich symbol across human history, representing temptation and original sin in Christianity, immortality and wisdom in Greek mythology, and health or discord in secular culture, bridging ideas of desire, knowledge, and mortality for thousands of years.

    Religion and Myth Forbidden Fruit: 
    Abrahamic traditions link the apple to the tree of knowledge of good and evil in Eden, though the Bible just says "fruit."Greek Mythology: Oranges and apples mixed in tales; the Golden Apple of Discord sparked the Trojan War, and the Garden of the Hesperides held immortal apples.Norse Tradition: Goddess Idun kept golden apples that gave the Norse gods eternal youth.

History and Science Origins: 

     Wild apples started in the mountains of Central Asia.The Silk Road: Travelers carried seeds across Asia and Europe.Newton's Apple: A falling apple helped Isaac Newton think about gravity.

Conceptual Meaning Knowledge, Symbolism: 

It stands for learning, truth, and forbidden wisdom.Temptation: It represents human desire and choice. Health: The old saying links eating one to good wellness.

Desire and Refreshment:
     In poetic books, the apple represents physical delight, fragrance, and comfort.
    The Myth of Temptation: Culturally, the conceptual idea of the "apple" shifted to symbolize human disobedience, the loss of innocence, and the transition from a state of pure trust to moral accountability.
      In Western art, the apple stands for the sin of Adam and Eve. Love and Beauty: Ancient Greek art links the apple to Aphrodite, the goddess of love. Life and Death: Decaying apples or apple cores represent the passing of time and human mortality (vanitas).

text:
SYRIO FOREL DID NOT DIE IN THAT ROOM.
HE CHANGED HIS FACE AND KEPT TEACHING HER.

They showed you a dancing master with a wooden sword against Meryn Trant and called it a noble death.
Watch it again.
You never see the body.
You hear steel. You hear a man shout what do we say to the god of death. Then Arya runs. The camera stays with the girl. That is not how this show treats important corpses. Ned gets a basket. The Hound gets a pile of bodies. Syrio gets a cutaway.
Braavos does not send its First Sword across the sea to teach a lord’s daughter footwork for pocket change. The Sealord’s champion is a political weapon. He knows every style because he has worn every kind of man who used one.

That is Faceless Men doctrine dressed as charm.
See with your eyes.
Not your fear. Not the story in front of you. The thing that is actually there.
That sentence is the entire religion of the House of Black and White. They say it in a courtyard with sticks. Later they say it in a temple with dead faces on the walls. Same lesson. Same student.
Then Jaqen H’ghar appears in a cage on the Kingsroad like a coincidence. A Lorathi who talks in riddles, offers three deaths, and smiles when a child outplays him. He does not recruit her in Braavos. He meets her in Westeros, after her first teacher has “died,” and finishes the sentence.
One man. Two faces. One apprenticeship.
Why a Stark.

The Faceless Men do not collect random orphans. They collect people who can stop being themselves. Arya is a warg. She already slips into Nymeria in her sleep. Wearing a face is the same muscle as wearing a wolf, you leave your name on a hook and walk around in someone else’s skin. A normal girl can learn the lie. A skinchanger can make the lie breathe.
That is why they let her fail the Waif test and live. They were not building an assassin for hire. They were building a needle that could pass through any door in Westeros, including the ones that only open for wolves.

Syrio’s last stand is the first gift. He buys her the seconds she needs and then ceases to be Syria. Jaqen later takes the face off in front of her so she will understand the trick was never magic. It was craft. The man who taught her to look is the man who taught her to vanish.
The show turned it into a revenge list and a night-king stab.
The older reading is colder and cleaner.
Death had a favorite.
It sent a dancing master to find her before the war even started.
By the time she walked into the House of Black and White, she was not applying. She was coming home.
What do we say to the god of death.
Not today.
That was never a joke.
That was the motto of the people who wear him.

text:
Commemoration.

Righteous Joachim and Anna
St Joachim was of the tribe of Judah and a descendant of King David. St Anna was of the tribe of Levi, the daughter of a priest named Matthan. Matthan’s three daughters were Mary, Zoia and Anna. Mary became the mother of Salome the Myrrhbearer; Zoia bore Elizabeth, mother of St John the Baptist; and Anna married Joachim in Nazareth. Joachim and Anna, to their great sorrow, were barren for fifty years. They lived prayerfully and kept only a third of their income for themselves, giving a third to the poor and a third to the Temple. Once when they had come to Jerusalem to offer sacrifice at the Temple, Joachim was publicly scorned by the High Priest Issachar for his childlessness. Joachim and Anna, greatly grieved, prayed fervently that God would grant them the miracle that he had wrought for Abraham and Sarah, and give them a child in their old age. Once, as each was praying separately in a secluded place, angels appeared to each of them and revealed to them that they would be given a blessed daughter, `by whom all nations will be blessed, and through whom will come the salvation of the world.’ They both rushed home to tell one another the joyous news, and embraced when they met. (This is the moment depicted in their icon.) Anna conceived and gave birth to the Most Holy Theotokos. Both reposed in peace, not long after they had sent her to live in the Temple.

Commemoration of the Third Ecumenical Council (431)
The Council, called by the Emperor Theodosius the Younger, met in Ephesus. The two hundred fathers gathered there condemned the teaching of Nestorius, Patriarch of Constantinople, who would not call the holy Virgin Mary Theotokos (God-bearer) but only Christotokos (Christ-bearer). The holy fathers of the Council clearly affirmed that the Virgin Mary is, and is to be called, Mother of God. They also confirmed the teaching of the first two Councils and decreed that the Nicene Creed may not be altered (as it later was by the Western church).

Holy Martyr Severian of Sebaste (320)
He was a prominent citizen of Sebaste during the reign of Licinius. When the Forty Martyrs of Sebaste (March 9) were in prison, he encouraged and comforted them. For this, and for his Christian example which had converted many pagans in the region, the Provincial Governor Lysias ordered his arrest. But before the soldiers could find him, he presented himself before the Governor and openly proclaimed his faith. For this he was subjected to many days of horrible tortures, during which he constantly exhorted the believers who followed him to stand firm in their confession of Christ. After astonishing endurance of his torments, he gave up his spirit to God.

At the Saint’s burial, the husband of one of his servants was miraculously raised from the dead, living for another fifteen years. The Christians could not decide where to bury Severian, so they wove a crown of flowers and laid it on his body to await a sign from heaven. An eagle took up the crown and dropped it in a nearby forest. The Christians buried the Martyr where the crown fell; his tomb became a fount of miracles, and the man who had been raised from the dead tended it for the rest of his life.

Our Holy Father Ciaran of Clonmacnoise (549)
Born to the family of a cartwright in Ireland, he entered monastic life when he was very young at the Monastery of Clonard, where he became a disciple of St Finnian (December 12). He became one of the ‘Twelve Apostles of Ireland’, all of them disciples of St Finnian. Ciaran founded the great monastery of Clonmacnoise (pronounced clon-mac-neesh) on the Shannon River, which became one of Ireland’s great monasteries. Once, during a great famine, He distributed all of the monastery’s food to the people, entrusting his monks’ survival, and his own, to providence. Saint Ciaran reposed in peace, aged only thirty-three, in 549.

Saint Theophanes the Confessor and Faster
After a God-pleasing life and much suffering, Theophanes reposed peacefully in the year 299.

Saint Nicetas the God-Pleaser
Nicetas lived in Constantinople in the twelfth century. He so pleased God by his life that the church doors opened of themselves before him, and the icon lamps lit by themselves. Such was the power of his prayer. At the wish of Deacon Sozon, and by the prayer of Nicetas, a priest appeared from the other world, from whom Sozon had been estranged and had remained unreconciled. There first appeared a row of priests vested in white and then another row of priests in red vestments. Sozon recognized his former opponent among them, and made peace with him. This occurred at night, in the Blachernae Church.

Venerable Joseph of Volotsk

text:
The Roman Goat
If the Greek goat has a mythological career worthy of Olympus,the Roman one apparently decided that fame is all very well,but a contract with the state is more secure: it provides milk,cheese, meat,hide and manure,clears scrubland, enters religion and eventually makes its way even into the Roman army.
A very Roman development for a goat.
Varro devotes serious attention to it in De Re Rustica and explains why it is so useful in Italy:it prefers wooded and scrubby places to meadows and eats vegetation that other animals leave behind. He warns,however,that its teeth are dangerous to cultivated plants, which is why lease agreements could explicitly prohibit goats from the property. The Romans, who managed to turn almost everything into a legal matter, made no exception for the goat. Varro even connects capra with carpere, “to pluck,to pick,”because the goat is constantly tearing something off.
This is possibly the most Roman description of an animal: useful, profitable and in need of regulation.
Cato, Varro and later Columella return us to the life behind Rome’s marble façade, where a good estate depends not only on land, slaves and harvests, but also on what each animal eats,produces and leaves behind. Goat’s milk enters the diet, caseus is made from it, the hide has numerous uses, and the manure is turned back into fertility. Between mythology and empire stands accounting, and the Romans never pretended that civilisation could function without a well-organised farmyard.
Ovid mentions him in the Fasti, while Aulus Gellius tells us that a goat was sacrificed to Vejovis according to a particular rite; in his temple between the two sacred groves on the Capitoline, his image was also associated with a goat. When a civilisation is old enough, apparently even gods can retain their cult after their biography has become debatable.
There is also Juno Caprotina, whose festival, the Nonae Caprotinae,was celebrated in July,and around whose name the goat, the wild fig caprificus, women’s rituals and several ancient explanations become intertwined. Plutarch himself transmits competing versions. This is one of the charms of Roman religion: it does not always offer mythological clarity,but it does offer a ritual, a calendar and the confidence that if the ancestors did it,there was probably a good reason.
And above all this stands Faunus, the ancient Italic god of fields, flocks and the wild, whom later Greco-Roman tradition increasingly brought closer to Pan. We must be careful with the beautiful pictures: the goat legs and horns we now automatically associate with Faunus belong largely to his later iconographic assimilation with the Greek Pan and the satyrs. Rome,even when borrowing a foreign god,likes gradually to issue him Roman papers.
And when religion has finished with the goat, the army arrives.
Roman campaign tents were made from animal hides,and experimental archaeology shows how much material was required. In one reconstruction of a tent for a contubernium, the group of eight legionaries, around 77 large goat hides were used. We should not turn this number into a universal Roman standard, but the scale is eloquent enough: behind the legion with its eagles, helmets, shields and standards stands an invisible economy of herds, tanners, stitchers, mules and people who have to make sure that the conqueror of the world does not sleep in the rain.
And perhaps it is precisely here that the Roman goat becomes perfectly Roman.
The Greek goat nurses Zeus, walks with Pan and climbs through mythology. The Roman one enters the farm, the cheese, the manure, the lease agreement, the calendar, the sacrifice and the legion’s baggage.
The Greeks give the goat a place among the gods.
The Romans give it a job.
And if there is an animal capable of explaining the difference between the two civilisations without having read either Plato or Cicero, I suspect we have just found it.

text:
"Come Back to Me"

My wife, Jennifer, and I booked a trip to Israel as part of a tour group led by Johnny and Elizabeth Enlow of Restore Seven Ministries.  Fulfillment of this bucket list trip to the Holy Land has been a long time in the making.  While every day thus far was amazing, truthfully, I was most looking forward to seeing the Western Wall in Jerusalem.  This historic site is considered by the Jews to be the second most holiest site in Israel - second only to Mount Moriah on the Temple Mount, currently beneath the Dome of the Rock.

We arrived at the Wall as the sun’s shadows were growing long and the afternoon heat radiated from the large limestone blocks making up the Wall.  Finding a small opening amongst the Jewish worshipers, I placed my hand on the Wall and began to pray.  Almost immediately, the Lord’s presence enveloped me in a loving, divine, “Here I AM.”
Maybe I noticed his approaching shadow or maybe Holy Spirit nudged me out of prayer, I don’t know, but I turned to see a disheveled old man standing behind me.  He had a kind face behind a long, grey beard and was wearing the kippah in accordance with Jewish tradition as well as a tallit over his shoulders.  He wore a long, black, coat that was torn revealing the inner lining.  His shoes were well-worn and seemed over-sized for his feet.  His right leg was bare between his black sock and the bottom of the tattered old coat.  He had the look of a homeless man and seemed very out of place at this most holy site.

Since arriving in Israel six days earlier, I had not seen any indications there were homeless people in Israel.  He was the kind of man most people would ignore and pass by without a thought, maybe throw a couple bucks his way to make oneself feel good.  But this man wasn’t wasn’t begging for money.

That’s not why he was standing there.

He wanted my place at the Wall so he could spend time with his God – our God, and he appeared to be waiting patiently for me to finish praying so he could take my place.  
My wife and I flew almost 7,000 miles to visit Israel, the culmination of that bucket list trip, for me at least, being able to spend time in prayer at the Western Wall.  I easily could have justified turning back toward the Wall and ignoring him, but for some reason I felt very humbled by his presence.

“I’m grafted in.” I thought, “He’s blood.”

The third veil’s been torn for me.  I have access to the Father wherever I am.  This Jewish man with the kind face does not have the privilege of entering into the throne room of God in the same way I do through the blood of Jesus Christ.  In that flash of a moment, standing before this man of Israel, there was only one thing I could do.

Still feeling the heavy presence of the Lord, I took a step back and motioned with my hand for him to take my place at the Wall.  He returned the gesture as if to say, “No, go ahead.”  I took another step back, bowing my head in respect and gestured again for him to take my place.  I backed away from the Wall and soon joined a fellow tour group member.  We chatted for a few minutes about the wonderful presence of God and the inspiring experience of being at this most holy site.

As our conversation wound down, I heard the Lord say, “Come back to Me.”

The God was summoning me back to the Wall to spend more time with Him in prayer!  Obviously, He was returning back to me the time with Him that I had given up so the man could have a place at the Wall.  As I returned to the Wall and laid my hand on those warm limestone blocks I felt in my spirit this was a time of purpose, a time of conducting the Lord’s business.  Yes, I felt the love and peace of His presence surround my spirit as before but I knew the time I would spend with Him would be deeper.  God wanted to accomplish His Kingdom purpose so I began to listen for His direction.

Biblically, the Temple Mount is a very significant location to God, as it is where the first and second Temple stood.  The Western Wall was and is part of the Temple Mount complex even though it is currently barren of His Temple.  This is where the Temple was dedicated  There are a few verses that make this location unlike any other in the world.

Many are familiar with 2 Chronicles 7:14 which states, “If my people, who are called by my name, will humble themselves and pray and seek my face and turn from their wicked ways, then I will hear from heaven, and I will forgive their sin and will heal their land.” 

The importance of praying at this location begins to reveal itself in the next 2 verses: “Now my eyes will be open and my ears attentive to the prayers offered in this place.  I have chosen and consecrated this Temple so that my Name may be there forever.  My eyes and my heart will always be there.” (1 Chronicles 7:15-16)

Perhaps more significant is Solomon’s prayer in 2 Chronicles 6:32-33 which reads, “As for the foreigner who does not belong to your people Israel but has come from a distant land because of your great name and your mighty hand and your outstretched arm—when they come and pray toward this temple, then hear from heaven, your dwelling place. Do whatever the foreigner asks of you, so that all the peoples of the earth may know your name and fear you, as do your own people Israel, and may know that this house I have built bears your Name.”

Notice that this is not a request for Israel, but for the nations who come to seek the Lord in Jerusalem.  As a gentile, God was calling me back to the Wall for a purpose - His purpose.

God has absolute authority and sovereignty over the universe He created.  He does not need Man to accomplish His Kingdom purpose on the earth and yet, He choses to use us to do so.  I fully understood that as I entered into prayer with Him.  Calling me back to the Wall, He had invited me into the sphere of His absolute sovereignty.  By seeking His direction in prayer, I was acting on a small piece of that sovereignty given to me by revelation of Holy Spirit.  My prayer, in full agreement with the leading of Holy Spirit, would ascend into the very throne room of God via the Alter of Incense to accomplish His purpose on earth.  As I prayed, I had no doubt He was releasing angels to accomplish the words I spoke at the Wall.

You would be very mistaken if you thought I was a sooper dooper prayer warrior.  I’m a normal Joe Believer who understands that God desires to use His kings and priests (Revelation 1:6) to accomplish His Will “on earth as it is in heaven” (Matthew 6:10).  I’ve been teaching and declaring to the Body of Christ for over 20 years the need for each of us to find His kingdom purpose in our life.  The vast majority of Christians live as peasants and paupers not fully realizing their heritage as sons and daughters of the Living God!

God is calling His kings and priests to come into agreement with His Kingdom purpose on earth.  We are to be "as one who serves by the strength that God supplies—in order that in everything God may be glorified through Jesus Christ" (1 Peter 4:11).  Colossians 4:2 tells us we are to "Continue steadfastly in prayer, being watchful in it with thanksgiving."

Serving God is the highest use of your time. 1 Corinthians 15:58 says, “Always give yourselves fully to the work of the Lord."  Therefore, “serve the Lord with gladness” (Psalm 100:2) by offering up a pure and holy incense prayer to Him.

text:
Prayer in honor of the Third Sorrow of Mary,
the Finding of Jesus in the Temple:

Most sorrowful Mother, grief, sorrow and anxiety filled your Immaculate Heart when you found you were separated from your Son on leaving Jerusalem. For three days He remained lost to you and to your holy spouse. For three days you sought Him who was the light of your life. And for three days you failed to find Him.

Let me join you in this pain, O Queen of Martyrs, and obtain for me the grace to never lose Jesus through sin, but to stay united to Him by the help of His grace. If I have the misfortune of falling, may I never doubt His mercy and always return through the Sacrament of Confession, which He instituted.

Hail Mary…

Prayer to our Sorrowful Mother for a particular grace:

O mother most holy and sorrowful, Queen of Martyrs, you who stood by your Son as He agonized on the cross. By the sufferings of your life, by that sword of pain that pierced your heart, by your perfect joy in heaven, look down on me kindly as I kneel before you, sympathizing with your sorrows and offering you my petition with childlike trust.

Dear Mother, because your Son refuses you nothing, ask of His Sacred Heart to mercifully hear my prayer and to grant this prayer in accord with His most perfect will. Therefore, through the merits of His Sacred Passion, along with those of your sufferings at the foot of the cross, I pray…

(Mention your intention here…)

Mother most merciful, to whom shall I go in my misery if not to you who pities us poor sinful exiles in this valley of tears? I beseech you to offer Jesus but one drop of His most Precious Blood and but one pang of His Loving Heart. Remind Him that you are our sweetness, our life and our hope, and your prayer will be heard. Amen

Memorare:

Remember, O most gracious Virgin Mary, that never was it known that anyone who fled to your protection, implored your help or sought your intercession, was left unaided. Inspired by this confidence, I fly unto you, O Virgin of Virgins, my Mother. To you do I come, before you I stand, sinful and sorrowful. O Mother of the Word Incarnate, despise not my petitions, but in your clemency, hear and answer me. Amen.

text:
Today’s (Sept 9, 2026) promise of God to believers is from the Book of Acts.

Acts 3:26
To you first, God, having raised up His Servant Jesus, sent Him to bless you, in turning away every one of you from your iniquities.

Commentary 
Peter is still preaching in the temple after the healing at the gate. He has recalled the covenant with Abraham—that in his seed all the families of the earth would be blessed. Then he names how that blessing arrives: God raised up His Servant Jesus and sent Him to bless you, in turning away every one of you from your iniquities.
The blessing is not first prosperity or ease. It is the gift of being turned from sin. God does not merely offer advice; He sent the risen Jesus to do the turning. “Every one of you” keeps the promise personal. The same Servant who was sent to Israel first is the One through whom the blessing now reaches the nations.
That purpose has not expired. God still sends Christ to bless people by turning them from their sins. Anyone who receives that Servant receives the blessing this verse names.

text:
Made with Seedance 2.5

⚔️😲“My Friend from the Ming Dynasty”—when you realize the person standing right in front of you is someone from the Ming Dynasty, 500 years ago! The atmosphere suddenly feels a little different.

Seedance 2.5 prompt👇
Seedance 2.5, 30 seconds, 16:9 horizontal, fine realistic 3D character animation, controlled multi-shot sequence, real-time motion except brief selective slow motion on key detail beats. All dialogue and narration are in English only. No subtitles. In reality, the three women never leave the car; the ten-second memory happens in a single instant of hand contact.

ACTIVE REFERENCES
Image 1 — Alin: adult woman, light platinum-blonde straight hair with bangs, white sleeveless top, blue jeans, brown belt, tall brown boots. Match face, body, hair, clothing.
Image 2 — Lisa: adult woman, short side-parted blonde hair, orange-brown leather jacket with shearling collar, brown corset short skirt, lace-up ankle boots. Her name is Lisa. Preserve actual colors and outfit.
Image 3 — Car: rust-red vintage modified two-door car with black patched door, roof rack lights and luggage, old paint, rust, modified structure.
Image 4 — Hia: adult Chinese female warrior, black braided updo and bun, gold hair ornaments and long earrings, dark red ribbons, dark blue-black and dark red embroidered robe, black-gold shoulder and wrist armor. She always holds a cool silver straight sword in her right hand. Black-gold scabbard stays on her left waist.
Image 5 — Reality location: abandoned highway, elevated roadway, wrecked cars, broken billboards, distant ruined towers, dust haze. Use it as real 3D geography, not as copied framing.
The multi-view boards are one single person each. No duplicate characters, no white background, no labels, no collage borders.
The memory section contains only Hia in a pink blossom forest on stone ground. No Alin, no Lisa, no car, no apocalypse structures.

LOCATION MAP
The parked car sits behind Alin and Lisa with engine off and doors closed, hood pointing frame-left in the opening reality shot.
Alin and Lisa stand side by side outside the visible side doors, about half a meter apart, car directly behind them.
Hia approaches from the road side and stops about 70 centimeters in front of them, centered between them, forming a small triangle that allows easy hand contact in the middle.
Reality camera stays on the same side of the Hia-to-two-friends line for every reality shot. The speaking mouth is never blocked by shoulders. Everyone looks at each other, never at camera.

FIRST FRAME AND SPATIAL BLOCKING
The first visible frame already contains all three women and the car. No empty establishing frame.
Hia’s right hand always holds the sword low outside her body line, tip toward the ground and safely away from Alin and Lisa. She uses only her left hand for the hand stack.
Hand order is fixed and always readable:
Hia left hand on bottom,
Alin right hand in the middle,
Lisa left hand on top.
In the overhead shot, Hia’s left forearm enters from the bottom of frame, Alin’s right forearm from upper left, Lisa’s left forearm from upper right. Distinguish the three arms clearly by Hia’s black-gold sleeve, Alin’s bare forearm, Lisa’s orange-brown sleeve.

FORMAT MODE
Controlled multi-shot sequence. Hard cuts only where stated. Real-time performance continuity across all cuts. No subtitles.

OPTICS
Reality medium and close shots use a natural 47° diagonal field of view with grounded human-eye perspective and no lens drift.
The top-down hand shot is a true vertical overhead.
The memory combat wide shot uses an 84° diagonal field of view to keep full body, footwork, hips, and full sword path readable.
The final Hia close-up shifts to a tighter portrait lens character without changing geography.

ACTION TIMING
0.00–1.00 — APPROACH
All three women and the car are already visible in frame. Alin stands steadier, lips slightly parted, eyes fixed on Hia’s face. Lisa leans subtly toward Alin and unconsciously pinches the hem of her jacket. Hia completes her last step, plants firmly, and her robe settles a beat later. Camera makes a small push-in while preserving the triangular spacing.

1.00–3.40 — QUESTION
Hia looks first at Alin, then at Lisa, with only a small head turn, and says in a low, steady adult female English voice:
“Want to know who I am?”
Light stress on “who,” calm and controlled. While she speaks, Alin closes her lips and studies Hia more intently. Lisa stops pinching her jacket, checks Alin once, then looks back to Hia.

3.40–6.00 — INVITATION
Hia extends her left hand first, palm up, holding it still at waist height between the three of them. Her right hand and sword remain low and unmoving.
From 3.70–5.90 she says:
“Come on. Give me your hands.”
The first phrase is gentle, then a short pause, then the second phrase is firm. Alin looks down to the palm, then back up to confirm, and reaches out her right hand. Lisa follows by extending her left hand, but hesitates slightly just before contact. Both women begin moving before the line finishes.

6.00–7.70 — OVERHEAD HAND STACK
Hard cut to a strict vertical overhead shot. Camera stays fixed and clearly shows all three forearms and sleeve identifiers.
Hia’s left palm is already steady and facing up. Alin’s right hand settles first into Hia’s palm. Lisa’s left hand lands last on top of Alin’s hand. The entire hand stack happens once, compact and clean. Fingers stay natural, skin compresses slightly at contact.
The effect does not begin until Lisa’s hand is fully placed at 7.70.

7.70–9.00 — MEMORY OPENS FROM THE HAND STACK
Thin antique-gold light leaks from the seams of the three hands and expands into a transparent circular refractive surface above them. Inside the circle, a top-down view of a blossom forest stone clearing with Hia appears directly; outside the circle, the real hands and grey highway ground remain visible.
Camera stays vertical and slowly pushes in. The circular memory image expands until it fills the full frame. The swap completes exactly at 9.00 seconds on the same downward-facing angle in the blossom clearing. The hands remain behind the refractive surface and are gradually hidden; they do not melt and do not turn into petals.

9.00–11.00 — MEMORY COMBAT PHRASE
High oblique full-body shot, camera descends slightly and follows half a step while keeping both feet, hips, and full sword path visible.
9.00–9.55: Hia drops her weight and drives a rising diagonal slash from lower left to upper right, feet gripping the stone, hips leading, shoulder and arm transmitting force.
9.55–10.45: without pausing, she advances half a meter with the right foot and turns the waist into a fast horizontal cut from right to left.
10.45–11.00: she absorbs the momentum into her left side, bends the right elbow, and brakes the sword in front of her left side, still clear of the body.
This entire phrase is one continuous action: rising slash, advancing horizontal cut, controlled stop. Robe panels and ribbons trail behind. Low petals lift from the ground. Natural motion blur appears only on the blade; the body and footwork stay crisp. No enemies, no energy wave.

10.60–17.00 — NARRATION OVER MEMORY
A deep, steady adult male English voice says clearly:
“Five hundred years ago, Hia was the greatest Jinyiwei warrior in Ming dynasty China.”
This narration continues across the following memory detail shots. Hia’s lips remain closed. The male speaker is never seen.

11.00–12.40 — EYES
Cut from the end of the horizontal cut into a face close-up that inherits the same rotational energy and gradually slows. Hia’s chin lowers slightly; her eyes lock forward with intent. The shoulders finish moving after the eyes settle. Her jaw is firm but not stiff. Lips closed. Camera pushes in slightly. One loose strand brushes her temple.

12.40–13.30 — HAIR AND RIBBONS
Cut to a tight rear-side detail. Maintain the same motion carry-through. Her braided updo and gold ornaments stay fixed while loose hairs and dark red ribbons whip out and settle back under side-backlight. This is brief and fluid, not a static beauty pose.

13.30–14.10 — EARRING
Match cut to a macro detail at the ear. The gold earring swings once with slight chain delay and catches one realistic highlight. Focus follows the earring briefly, then moves on. No repeated back-and-forth loop.

14.10–15.60 — PETAL ON THE SWORD
Carry the sword from its existing position. Hia subtly rotates her forearm so the broad side of the blade faces upward while she continues the slow recovery.
In close view, the hilt sits lower right and the tip points upper left. One petal lands on the middle flat of the blade, shows a tiny reflection, then slips over the edge nearest camera and falls out of frame. Camera stays on the middle of the blade and does not chase the falling petal. This beat is slightly slowed so contact, slide, and release are clearly readable. The petal does not slide along the sharp cutting edge and does not pass through metal.

15.60–17.70 — FINISHING THE FORM
Cut to a medium three-quarter side shot and return close to normal speed. Hia completes the recovery from the existing sword position, drawing the unsheathed straight sword back toward her waist with the tip angled outward. Her weight settles fully, shoulders release on the exhale, robe, ribbons, and earring settle in their own delayed timing. Her gaze remains forward. She does not re-attack and does not sheath the sword.

17.70–19.00 — MEMORY CLOSES BACK INTO THE HAND STACK
The blossom clearing remains whole while an antique-gold circular border appears at the edges of frame and contracts inward. Outside the shrinking circle, the original reality overhead shot gradually reappears: grey ground, three forearms, three stacked hands still in the same order.
The blossom memory collapses back into a deep circular image above the hands and disappears precisely into the contact point at 19.00. This is a closing memory window, not a body morph.
Camera returns to the same vertical overhead position from 6.00–7.70. Hand order is unchanged.

19.00–20.50 — HANDS BREAK APART
From overhead, the three hands separate quickly and clearly:
Alin’s right hand pulls back toward upper left,
Lisa’s left hand pulls back toward upper right,
Hia’s left hand withdraws slightly downward.
Hard cut back to the reality side medium shot and catch the same withdrawal in motion. Alin takes a short breath but steadies herself. Lisa recoils through her shoulders and immediately covers her mouth with her withdrawn left hand. Hia’s right hand still holds the sword low and steady. Car, spacing, and background match the original reality setup exactly.

20.50–23.00 — ALIN CONTAINS HER REACTION
Close-up on Alin, with Lisa still readable behind her. Alin holds her right hand in front of her torso, fingers curling slightly then releasing. Her gaze moves from Hia’s wrist armor up to Hia’s face. Her jaw tightens briefly, she swallows once, then exhales slowly. Her lips part but she says nothing. She does not step back and does not overreact.
Lisa remains in the background already covering her mouth, eyes widened, breathing shallow. She does not wait for her own close-up to begin reacting.

23.00–26.50 — LISA SPEAKS
Camera glides smoothly toward Lisa and transfers focus to her. Lisa’s left hand still covers her mouth at first. She darts a quick look to Alin, sees Alin still fixed on Hia, then looks back to Hia.
She inhales, lowers her hand below the chin so her mouth is fully visible, leans back slightly but keeps her footing planted.
At 24.00 seconds she says in a bright, slightly rough adult female English voice:
“Holy shit... five hundred years ago?!”
“Holy shit” breaks out like a muffled reflex escaping from behind the hand, then a half-beat pause, then another inhale, with strong stress on “five hundred” and a disbelieving rise on “years ago.” Fast, sensitive, shocked, but not cartoonish and not screaming. She never covers her mouth while speaking and never looks at camera. The line trails out until about 26.70.

26.50–30.00 — HIA CLOSE-UP ENDING
Cut along Lisa’s eyeline to a three-quarter front close-up of Hia against a soft blurred grey-blue apocalypse background. Lisa’s last syllable finishes offscreen. Hia does not move her lips.
26.50–27.60: Hia quietly listens, eyes resting on Lisa just off camera, gaze alive with small natural scanning, breathing low and steady.
27.60–29.00: the tension around the eyes releases first, then the chin dips slightly, then one corner of the mouth lifts into the smallest restrained smile. No teeth. No obvious eyebrow lift.
29.00–30.00: camera completes an extremely slow push-in and settles. The earring’s residual motion nearly stops, a few loose hairs still move lightly, and the shot ends on her eyes and faint smile. No extra line, no fade to black.

ACTING TASK — HIA
SCENE DIRECTION (shared, unspoken): let them receive the truth without breaking the connection.
MOTIVE: she is certain of who she is and chooses to reveal it on her own terms.
GOAL: lead both women across the threshold calmly and keep control of the moment.
OBSTACLE: their uncertainty could break the contact or turn the moment into fear.
TACTIC: she measures both women, offers certainty, and keeps checking whether they stay with her.
Moment to moment:
— “Want to know who I am?” — test Alin first, then test Lisa, checking whether each one will hold the gaze and accept the invitation.
— “Come on. Give me your hands.” — open the path, hold the palm steady, read who commits first, keep the eyes engaged in the choice.
Safety: gaze always stays active and task-driven; natural blink cadence; no frozen stare.

ACTING TASK — ALIN
SCENE DIRECTION (shared, unspoken): stay contained and make room for the truth without losing control.
MOTIVE: she wants to verify whether Hia is real and dangerous or trustworthy.
GOAL: hold herself steady and read Hia correctly before committing.
OBSTACLE: the memory shocks her, but showing fear would break her authority.
TACTIC: study Hia, check the hand, return to the eyes, confirm before moving, then keep reassessing after the contact.
Safety: eyes always working on Hia, never glassy.

ACTING TASK — LISA
SCENE DIRECTION (shared, unspoken): stay with the others through the unknown.
MOTIVE: she is frightened but deeply wants to know the truth.
GOAL: keep close to Alin, then survive the shock of what she has seen.
OBSTACLE: curiosity and fear hit her at the same time.
TACTIC: borrow courage from Alin, test Hia through quick checks, then lose verbal control only once the truth lands.
Moment to moment:
— before contact — check Alin for permission, then snap back to Hia.
— “Holy shit... five hundred years ago?!” — let the thought escape after the hand drops, searching Alin once and then throwing the question back at Hia.
Safety: she listens and reacts through the eyes first; no empty staring, no repeated exaggerated mouth pose.

PHYSICS
Real body weight, foot pressure, cloth delay, hair delay, metal weight, sword inertia, skin compression at hand contact, grounded breath, correct gravity. The car remains stationary and off. The sword never drifts, bends, or changes hands. The memory transition uses only thin antique-gold light and transparent refraction around the contact point, never a full-screen yellow wash, never white flash replacement, never black flash replacement.

LIGHTING
Reality uses low-saturation grey-cyan, dust grey, and grey-brown from the highway reference. Soft sunlight comes from high camera-right through thin haze, creating gentle side-backlight; cool grey sky fills the shadows; skin keeps natural warmth. Keep the rust-red car, Lisa’s orange-brown jacket, Hia’s dark red textiles, Alin’s neutral white top, and the blonde hair tones cleanly separated.
Memory keeps the same skin realism and shadow density but shifts the environment to cool mist, soft pink petals, dark blue-black robe, dark red textiles, old gold ornaments, and cold silver blade. Sunlight still comes from high frame-right through leaves, with stronger rim light. When reality returns, exposure and white balance return exactly to the opening state.

AUDIO
Reality: empty wind, light footwear contact, leather and cloth movement, no engine.
Memory: low guqin overtones and sparse low drum. The rising slash gets one short upward air-tear; the horizontal cut gets one fuller sword-wind and low drum hit. After that, sound narrows to leave room for narration and detail shots.
The two transition beats produce only a brief low-frequency pulse, refraction sweep, and metallic overtone. No continuous roaring.
After the return, music falls away. Keep breath, cloth, and ambience clear. No comedic sound on Lisa’s line.
Final Hia close-up holds only wind, soft breath, and a fading trace of guqin.
Three voices stay distinct: Hia, Lisa, male narrator. Alin never speaks. Characters keep lips closed when not speaking.

POSITIVE CONSTRAINTS
Stable identity, stable spacing, stable hand order, stable sword hand, stable scabbard on left waist, stable wardrobe structure, stable eyelines, stable car orientation.
No duplicate characters, no face mixing, no color drift, no hand fusion, no extra fingers, no extra arms, no left-right swap, no weapon drift, no body morph, no copied gesture loops.
No new enemies, no zombies, no explosions, no extra sword techniques, no energy wave in the memory combat, no full-screen effect cover, no premature effect trigger before full hand contact.
No title cards, no labels, no collage layout, no watermark, no subtitles, no extra dialogue.

text:
The livestreamer who faced fierce backlash for posing beside the wreckage of the Amazon Prime Air 767 in Miami says he won’t delete the posts and doesn’t believe he did anything wrong.

ChickenAndy was among a group of streamers who arrived at the crash site around four hours after the accident and photographed themselves with the wreckage behind them.

Five people had been killed on the ground.

Speaking to The Independent after the backlash, he said:

“I don’t think I did anything wrong. I’m not hiding from anything.”

He claimed he did not know anyone had died when the group arrived and stressed that he did not film any bodies.

But he isn’t backing down.

ChickenAndy said removing the content would make him feel as though he were “trying to hide something” and even claimed he is considering legal action after losing followers and income following the controversy.

The streamer also offered prayers to those who died.

#AmazonAir #Miami #Aviation

The idea of Messi and Ronaldo reuniting in Miami sounds amazing for fans, but let’s separate the rumors from the real news.
The claim that David Beckham offered Ronaldo €1.4 billion in 2025 came from a satirical social media account. There was never any such offer from Inter Miami.
Instead, Ronaldo chose to stay with Al Nassr. In June 2025, he signed a contract extension that keeps him at the club until 2027.
His decision is already paying off. By April 24, 2026, Ronaldo had helped Al Nassr achieve a 15-match winning streak and build an 8-point lead in the Saudi Pro League.
Ronaldo is focused on his legacy. He wants to reach 1,000 career goals and win a historic double in Asia before the World Cup.

A CRITICAL MOMENT ON RUNWAY 30: NTSB DATA REVEALS THE FINAL 30 SECONDS OF THE MIAMI CARGO CRASH

The data from the NTSB investigation into the fatal overrun of Amazon Air Flight 7598 offers a detailed, second-by-second account of the final moments before the Boeing 767 crashed through a fence and into vehicles, killing five people . The timeline, drawn from the recovered flight data recorder, paints a picture of a landing that quickly became a struggle to stop a heavy jet at 65 knots .

A LATE TOUCHDOWN AND A DECISION TO GO AROUND

The sequence begins 30 seconds before the end of the flight data recording, when the nose and right main landing gear touched down at a ground speed of 158 knots . However, the left main landing gear did not touch until 19 seconds later, at a speed of 134 knots—a significant delay . With the aircraft already far down the runway, the pilots made a critical decision: 15 seconds before the recording's end, they released the brakes and increased throttles to go-around power . This indicates they attempted to abort the landing and take off again, but the window for a safe maneuver had likely passed.

REVERSED DECISION AND A SHORTFALL IN BRAKING

Just four seconds later, at the 11-second mark, the throttles were reduced to idle and the brakes were reapplied as the aircraft, still travelling at 117 knots, continued its ground roll . Crucially, the NTSB found no evidence that the crew had deployed either the speed brakes or thrust reversers, two systems designed to help slow the aircraft after touchdown . By the end of the recording, the aircraft's final ground speed was still 65 knots .

A DEVASTATING OUTCOME IN THE FINAL METRES

The overrun was catastrophic. The aircraft travelled approximately 1,300 feet beyond the paved surface, striking a white Ford Econoline van carrying seven airline cleaning crew employees . It then broke through a perimeter fence and slammed into a Toyota Corolla on a public road before coming to rest near a parking area . All five fatalities were in the vehicles on the ground . The NTSB has recovered the flight data and cockpit voice recorders, and will interview the pilots . A key focus of the investigation is whether the airport's lack of an Engineered Materials Arresting System (EMAS) contributed to the severity of the accident .

text:
Did you know⁉️

Vlad and Nore had history before this blew up. Nore sat on VladTV more than once in the late 2000s‼️. Around 2019–2020 he asked those interviews taken down, citing disrespect to hip-hop and Farrakhan‼️. That should have closed it‼️.

It didn’t‼️. In March 2024 Vlad flew to Miami and did Drink Champs‼️. The episode did huge numbers — Vlad later cited about 1.9 million views‼️. The deal, as Vlad tells it, was simple: he does yours, you do mine‼️. Dates got booked‼️. Dates got canceled‼️. Vlad says he was already in Nore’s city some of those times‼️. After a year of that, he said it on Akademiks: Nore is a snake, his word doesn’t mean anything‼️.

Nore answered on Drink Champs. He didn’t deny the runaround‼️. He said he fronted, he’s grown, he can change his mind‼️. Then he made it bigger than a booking. He said he did to Vlad what Vlad does to the culture. He used the “bent you over” line‼️. He called Vlad a rat over the 2008 Rick Ross case — a civil assault suit after the Ozone Awards, not a criminal charge; a jury later awarded Vlad $300,000‼️. He called him Jerry Springer living off Black drama‼️. Culture vulture‼️. Welcome to the party‼️.

Vlad came back with a long Charleston White sit-down: texts, view counts, who owns what (Vlad owns his channel; Drink Champs sits on Revolt), civil vs. criminal on Ross, pressure to drink on camera. He flushed a Drink Champs bouquet in a toilet‼️.

That’s when it stopped being about an interview‼️.

Nore went to X: “Vladren,” old photos of Vlad in hip-hop clothes, dares about the N-word, an offer to pay for a lie detector‼️. Vlad answered with short clips. One of them, posted September 8, 2026, is titled “The Truth About NORE’s Wife…”‼️

 Vlad took Nore’s “I’m protecting Black culture from a white extractor” speech and tried to flip it‼️. The point he made: you talk like a gatekeeper for Black people, but look at who you married‼️. He framed Nore’s wife — a lighter-skinned Latina — as the contradiction‼️. Name, look, the implication that the sermon doesn’t match the house‼️.

A lot of people said he reached‼️. She’s Latina, not a white woman in the way Vlad was using the word‼️. Nore has been loud about Puerto Rican roots since “Esta Loca.” He’s mixed himself — Puerto Rican father, African-American mother, born Victor Santiago Jr. Dragging the wife was the cheap shot‼️. Whether it was accurate is a different argument than whether it was the point‼️.

By then the original beef was almost gone‼️. It started as “you promised a sit-down.” It became who gets to speak for the culture, who is extracting from it, and whether your personal life is fair game once you make “the culture” the weapon‼️. Vlad used Nore’s own authenticity talk against him‼️. That’s how a canceled interview turned into a wife clip‼️.

And we are yet to see how far they can go‼️

text:
Prefiero decir una verdad incómoda antes que una mentira confortable.” (I’d rather tell an uncomfortable truth than a comfortable lie.) — Javier Milei
The non-profit company that publishes The European Conservative, which I founded in 2021, is now in the hands of the Hungarian state.
Established in 2008 as an unfunded four-page newsletter, The European Conservative was started by members of the Center for European Renewal (CER), which organizes the annual Vanenburg meeting. Five editions were published over approximately two years and then it ceased for two years. So, in 2012, I volunteered to serve as editor-in-chief. I redesigned the publication, gave it a proper cover, added images, expanded its features and contributors (all of whom wrote for free), and established a social media presence.
I also had friends in print shops in different parts of the world volunteer to print 100, 200, and even 300 copies of the glossy, full-color, 60-page magazine. I still remember carrying early versions of the magazine to conferences—like samizdat. It was unknown, but people loved it. We published interesting pieces by interesting writers.
Our mission was to explore the Right, in all its forms. I sought to create a place where philosophy, art, theology, and politics all could be treated as parts of one inheritance, and where the Right could appear as it actually is—a colorful, richly diverse (if at times unwieldy) mix of sovereigntists, radical localists, and classical liberals; Catholics, Protestants, and Jews; agrarians, monarchists, national conservatives, and the unfashionable defenders of what used to be called Christendom.
I did all of this with volunteer editors for several years. In 2014, we received a small grant from the now-defunct Earhart Foundation (due to the tremendous generosity of the late David Kennedy) to publish two issues. And in 2018, we received additional funding from the Center for Transatlantic Renewal to launch our first website and produce a few more issues of the magazine. Our readership began to grow—especially once I began to send the PDF of the entire magazine to people around the world. Gratis.
In 2018, after publishing 13 issues over six years, I was offered the opportunity to expand and professionalize The European Conservative with funding from a Hungarian foundation. Despite some personal misgivings—and very complicated, lengthy negotiations—I agreed to accept the funding in the end because it was the only way to keep the publication alive. There were no other donors knocking on our doors.
I was grateful for that support, and I retained complete editorial control over the magazine. The arrangement meant we could finally pay our many writers and editors; it also meant we could send the magazine—expanded to 132 pages—to retail shops and print subscribers around the world. And we began to grow even more, both in Europe and beyond, also branching out to daily news, and audio-visual content.
We grew because there was nothing like The European Conservative: a publication where philosophy, theology, culture, and politics could be treated as parts of one civilizational inheritance. No one else was translating forgotten or unknown European thinkers into English; no one else combined right-wing political thought with Western art and high culture. Other publications talked about beauty—but no one showed it like we did. We were the first. And by doing so, we created what Irish philosopher Mark Dooley called “a cultural monument” the likes of which had never been seen.
After a series of unfortunate events (about which I may someday write in a memoir), all control of my company (registered in Budapest) which published The European Conservative was transferred to the Matthias Corvinus Collegium (MCC) at the tail-end of 2024. Immediately thereafter, MCC’s leadership took the ill-advised decision to split the entire project into two “divisions”: the online site https://t.co/OY3vepi3nX

When I was in 11th grade I was on lunch break where they used to let us leave campus and was at a friend’s house where they found a bottle of Irish whiskey and they said let’s take a shot and I took a shot. 

I got bored at school and knew that my sister worked around the corner I called her to come and pick me up to go home early and the vice principal in the office asked me to step back into her office and told me she smelled alcohol and had I been drinking. 

I denied denied denied. They called the police and I denied some more. Then they pulled out a breathalyzer and she said “now I’m looking at these breathalyzer results and they are not agreeing with what you’re telling me.”

I told her that I think the breathalyzer shows that I haven’t been drinking and that if it showed that I had been drinking then she wouldn’t need to keep asking me if I had been drinking. 

Then she pulled a tactic I wasn’t expecting. She lowered my guard by appealing to my vanity She said “you’re a smart one aren’t you”, and then offered to show me the results and she held the screen in front of my face to look at and here’s where I made the mistake

I finally admitted the whole thing and got suspended.

But I learned a valuable lesson. The alcohol amount on the breathalyzer would’ve not been enough to get me kicked out.

That’s why you have to commit to your story no matter what

It’s like that old shaggy song “It wasn’t me” 😂

text:
Diplomatic exploratory talks regarding a potential summit between Donald Trump, Vladimir Putin, and Xi Jinping on the sidelines of the APEC summit (November 18–19 in Shenzhen) are attracting significant international attention. While Moscow is actively publicizing the plan, Washington and Beijing remain reserved regarding official commitments.

**Official reports and signals from Moscow**

The Russian news agency TASS and Kremlin spokesman Dmitry Peskov confirmed that the initiative stems from a one-hour telephone conversation between Vladimir Putin and Donald Trump.

**Diplomatic framework:** Moscow views a trilateral meeting in Shenzhen as an ideal platform for negotiations on the Ukraine war and global security issues among the three major powers on equal footing.

**Willingness to negotiate:** Peskov emphasized the existence of a shared political will to resume trilateral talks, although no binding roadmap or written agenda is yet in place. While Russia signals openness to mediation efforts, it continues to insist on safeguarding its own security interests and territorial gains.

**Official stance from Washington**

Caution prevails within the White House and the US State Department.

**No travel confirmation:** The White House has neither confirmed nor scheduled Donald Trump’s participation in the APEC summit in Shenzhen.

**Strategic skepticism:** Government sources indicate that while bilateral calls with Moscow are part of Trump’s announced negotiation strategy for a swift end to the war, formal summits would need to be contingent upon tangible concessions from Moscow. US special envoys such as Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner have recently been gauging Ukraine’s willingness to compromise during parallel discussions in Kyiv.  Perspectives from five leading global media outlets

The New York Times (USA): Views Moscow’s move as an attempt to increase negotiating pressure on Washington and completely bypass European involvement in future peace talks. A trilateral format involving China would also spare Russia the appearance of being an isolated supplicant.

The Wall Street Journal (USA): Focuses on the economic and geopolitical dimensions. A meeting in Shenzhen carries risks for Trump, as China and Russia could present a united front to undermine Western sanctions regimes and export controls.

The Washington Post (USA): Highlights significant skepticism in Kyiv and within NATO. An agreement negotiated between Washington, Moscow, and Beijing—over the heads of Ukraine and Europe—threatens to deeply divide the Western alliance.

Financial Times (UK): Analyzes Beijing’s role. For leader Xi Jinping, hosting the event would offer a historic opportunity to firmly establish China as a dominant global peacemaker. At the same time, Beijing is hesitant to provide guarantees for a ceasefire that Putin could violate at any moment.

The Guardian (UK): Views Peskov’s announcement primarily as a Kremlin PR maneuver. By floating the mere possibility of a summit, Moscow demonstrates its capacity for action to a domestic audience and tests Trump’s willingness to abandon traditional US diplomacy in favor of a personalized "deal-making" format.

Whether the historic meeting in Shenzhen actually takes place depends largely on whether Washington can secure firm conditions from Moscow in advance and on the extent to which Beijing is willing to commit to the role of mediator.

text:
Pointing Outward While the Machine Keeps Running

In patterns of domestic abuse, the one with greater power fixates on the other’s flaws while refusing to examine their own behavior or impact. 

The same dynamic plays out at the scale of nations.

We spend enormous energy condemning other countries’ ambitions—Russia, governments labeled socialist or authoritarian—while rarely examining the costs of our own policies. 

Sanctions that quietly devastate civilian economies stay offstage. 

At home, debates rage over labels while most working people simply want fair wages, affordable health care, and a government that puts them ahead of corporate donors and defense contractors. 

Every major power pursues its interests. The question is whether America’s version still serves ordinary Americans.

The United States maintains the world’s largest network of overseas bases—roughly 750 sites in more than 80 countries. Places like Okinawa function as self-contained American communities far from home. 

Iraqi oil revenues have long moved through the Federal Reserve Bank of New York; recent actions have given Washington similar leverage over Venezuelan oil proceeds. 

These arrangements project power and lock us into permanent commitments that drain resources from problems here.

For decades, U.S. policy backed right-wing forces across Central and South America under the banners of anti-communism and the drug war. The result was not mere neglect of local interests—it was systematic terror, mass killings, disappearances, and the destruction of democratic possibilities for generations of ordinary people.

The human toll of the post-9/11 wars is staggering. Brown University’s Costs of War project counts 905,000–940,000 direct deaths and another 3.6–3.8 million indirect deaths—more than 4.5 million total. Earlier Lancet studies recorded massive excess mortality in Iraq. Sanctions have added further preventable deaths. 
Venezuela has seen direct U.S. intervention. In Syria, a group that evolved from an al-Qaeda affiliate now leads the interim government. Cuba and Iran remain under pressure. NATO continues to define a European front against Russia.

This is sustained by a bipartisan permanent war economy. One side prioritizes Europe; the other the Middle East. Both keep the machinery running. 

The result is continuity: 

endless commitments, trillions spent, and working families left to pay the bill.

America First means ending wars that do not make Americans safer or more prosperous. 

Standing against ethnic cleansing/genocide means applying the same standard everywhere. 

Prioritizing the working class over the corporate and military-industrial class means questioning an empire that serves neither.

History shows the pattern. During the Gilded Age and Great Depression, workers and farmers asked for fair wages, safer conditions, and basic security. 

Elites resisted or offered minimal concessions. 

The reforms that came—labor protections, Social Security, the right to organize—were forced by sustained pressure from below. 

Ordinary people had to keep organizing and fighting. 

Socialists and communists helped build the movements that made the status quo untenable. 

Meaningful change has never arrived by waiting for elites to decide the time is right. 

And when that pressure mounts, those in power will often deny the harm, attack the critics, and reverse the roles—claiming they are the real victims.

text:
No Deal Beats a Bad Deal—Unless You’re Paying the Bill

At midnight Tuesday, Canada’s 15–50% tariffs hit about $20–28 billion of U.S. goods—steel, appliances, farm kit, electronics, clothing, cheese. 

It matched Trump’s August 50% Section 338 levies on a similar slice of Canadian exports after talks died on August 21. 

Washington then piled on: bans on Canadian dairy, most alcohol and motorcycles, procurement cuts, Bombardier threats. 

Canada ships ~70% of its goods south. The U.S. economy is an order of magnitude larger. Ottawa takes the heavier GDP and jobs hit; America feels it in Ohio, Michigan, Pennsylvania and Maine—and at the checkout.

Was there a “good” deal on the table? Trump said yes. USTR Jamieson Greer said Canada would have gotten the best treatment of any major exporter: auto tariffs cut toward 15% (with U.S. content relief), steel/aluminum cuts, lumber relief, a path to reopen USMCA.

Carney walked. He says last-minute U.S. changes excluded the pickup trucks that keep Oakville and Oshawa alive, left steel and aluminum too high, tried to limit Canada’s other trade deals, and poked French-language rules and cultural policy. “They asked too much and offered too little.”

Washington says Canada kept moving the goalposts. Both can be true: a headline deal that still left Canada’s auto and metals industries uneconomic over time.

Is this about the midterms? Officials won’t say “defeat Trump.” They do say the list is “strategic” and “targets states.” 

Industry Minister Mélanie Joly: products chosen to hit U.S. states and create political pressure. Ohio is the most exposed. Michigan and Maine send huge export shares north and have tight Senate races. That is leverage, not a secret. It is also standard tariff warfare. 

Whether Carney’s main aim is Canadian sovereignty or Republican pain, the timing—nine weeks before November—is not an accident.

The City of London “puppet” line is a charge, not a document. Carney did 13 years at Goldman, ran the Bank of England, sat at Brookfield, and speaks the language of global capital. 

That network shaped how he thinks about risk, diversification and not being locked to one buyer. It does not prove Threadneedle Street ordered him to blow up a North American deal.

What is proven is his wager: take pain now, refuse “dependency,” and hope swing-state politics force Washington back. Canada is smaller. 

The clock favors the larger market.

text:
This Indian startup is building what we used to import!

India imported over ₹2000 crore worth of MRI apparatus, spare parts and components in FY2022–23 alone.

Arjun Arunachalam wanted to change that.

He trained as an MRI scientist at the University of Wisconsin-Madison and later worked at GE’s Global Research Center in the US.

Then he returned to India with an idea that sounded almost unreasonable:

Why couldn’t India build its own MRI scanner?

Building one, however, is ridiculously difficult.

An MRI brings together a powerful superconducting magnet, radio-frequency systems, electronics, cooling, software and image reconstruction, all of which have to work with enough precision that a doctor can trust the image with a human life.

And India imported almost all major diagnostic imaging equipment. Even the government’s National Biopharma Mission identified this dependence as a major problem.

So Arunachalam started building.

The early years were difficult enough that he joined IIT Bombay as faculty while keeping the research alive. His family even relocated to Singapore, where a SPRING Singapore grant around 2013 helped fund an early test scanner.

Tata Trusts and FISE backed the effort a few years later.

Then COVID arrived.

Eight years of work were behind him, money was running dangerously low and a multinational medical technology company offered to acquire his startup.

For a founder who had spent years trying to build one of the hardest pieces of medical hardware imaginable, it was a perfectly reasonable exit.

Arunachalam said no.

And that decision could easily have killed the company.

Instead, Tata Trusts continued supporting the effort and in 2021, Zoho (@Zoho) invested around $5 million into VoxelGrids.

The team kept building.

What eventually emerged was a 1.5 Tesla clinical-class MRI scanner designed and built in India.

And they tackled one particularly painful problem along the way: helium.

Conventional superconducting MRI systems use liquid helium to keep their magnets extremely cold. India imports helium too, adding another dependency and recurring cost to an already expensive machine.

VoxelGrids (@voxelgrids) developed its system around a helium-free, conduction-cooled dry magnet.

The company says this makes its scanner roughly 40% cheaper to build. At around 2.3 tonnes, it is also about half the weight of many conventional MRI systems.

There is an important caveat.

Indian-designed and built does not mean every single component comes from India. The superconducting wire, for instance, is still imported.

But that is precisely what makes this story interesting.

DeepTech self-reliance happens layer by layer.

First you learn to build the system. Then you own the engineering and manufacturing knowledge. Then you start moving deeper into the supply chain.

By late 2025, more than a decade of work had finally made it out of the laboratory.

A VoxelGrids scanner went into clinical use at the Chandrapur Cancer Care Foundation in Maharashtra.

From an early test scanner around 2013 to a machine on a hospital floor, the journey took roughly 12 years.

That is the part of DeepTech we often forget.

Building technology that a doctor can trust with a human life can consume a decade. Sometimes the money runs out. Sometimes the ecosystem doesn’t exist yet. Sometimes someone offers you an easier exit.

Arjun Arunachalam got that offer.

He chose to keep building.

And somewhere in Chandrapur today, a patient can walk into a hospital and get scanned on a machine that an Indian team spent more than a decade learning how to build.

"There is still no evidence that AI is replacing workers: a new survey from the New York Fed carried out in August shows that 34% of service firms and 22% of manufacturers using AI are retraining staff, while only 4% and 0% report layoffs. This is consistent with our core view that AI is putting downward pressure on wages in AI-exposed occupations without a significant negative impact on employment."

As I dissect in my new report on "The AI Trade" (https://t.co/kEx5Z4BJH7):

As Goldman Sachs analysts noted in July: “There is still no ‘statistically significant’ correlation between AI and unemployment figures.” If anything, it appears AI is leading to increased hiring rather than displacing workers, including for entry-level roles. For one, Stanford researchers in July calculated that: “The unemployment rate for the top quintile of AI-exposed workers has risen by 0.77 percentage points since 2022, while the unemployment rate for the least-exposed workers rose slightly more, by 0.85 percentage points over the same period.” For another, a study released in July by enterprise fintech company Ramp found that companies adopting AI grow their headcount 10% over the two years following adoption, including 12% growth for entry-level roles. This is likely for a very rudimentary reason: by-and-large, AI doesn’t offer turnkey solutions for enterprises, meaning workload is added in the integration process, requiring more workers.

As we argued back in December, the enterprise capital required to subsidize the AI buildout would have to come from savings generated via labor replacement or growth driven by increased productivity or a combination of both. To date, there is little evidence either is manifesting. S&P 493 profit margins have barely budged since ChatGPT’s launch. To quote Apollo’s analysis of the significance of that relative stagnation: “The bottom line is that the AI CAPEX boom is so far only showing up in the sellers’ margins, not the buyers’. This is important because the longer it takes the S&P 493 to generate ROI, the bigger the downside risks to an economy and a market this concentrated in the AI trade.” Q2 earnings season sent a similar message. Roughly 11% of S&P 500 companies quantified productivity benefits from AI for a specific business application during their earnings calls. And as Goldman noted about those companies: “Q2 results showed a small and statistically insignificant difference in earnings growth between the companies quantifying AI productivity gains this quarter and other S&P 500 companies.”
