text:
LET US DO THE ACTUAL HISTORY

You said action was required because saying settlers are in the wrong changed nothing for decades.

Let me concede your strongest point immediately, because I always do.

Settler violence in the West Bank is real, documented, and largely unprosecuted. Shin Bet has designated some settler groups as terrorist entities. Israel sanctions its own citizens over this. Anyone defending all of it is defending something Israel itself will not.

Now the parts that keep getting left out.

There has never been a sovereign Arab state called Palestine. Ottoman provinces until 1917, British Mandate until 1948. That is the administrative record.

In November 1947, the UN voted to partition the Mandate into a Jewish state and an Arab state. The Jewish Agency accepted. The Arab Higher Committee and every Arab state rejected it.

The day after Israel declared independence, five Arab armies invaded.

From 1948 to 1967, Jordan held the West Bank and Egypt held Gaza. Nineteen years of Arab control. No Palestinian state was created in either territory. Jordan annexed the West Bank in 1950 and only Britain and Pakistan recognised it.

The PLO was founded in 1964. Three years before Israel controlled one inch of the West Bank or Gaza. Its founding charter called for liberating Palestine, and in 1964 the only thing there was to liberate was Israel itself.

That single fact answers what the conflict was ever about.

Camp David, 2000. Barak offered roughly ninety percent of the West Bank, Gaza, and a capital in East Jerusalem. Arafat rejected it and made no counteroffer. Clinton said so publicly and blamed him.

2008. Olmert offered more. Abbas never responded.

2005. Israel withdrew every soldier and settler from Gaza. Israel removed eight thousand people with its own army. Hamas won the 2006 election, seized the strip in a 2007 coup against Fatah, and there has not been another election since.

October the seventh, 2023. Eleven hundred and ninety-five people murdered. Two hundred and fifty-one taken hostage.

Now, the citizenship point, and I want to be precise rather than convenient.

There are roughly two million Arab citizens of Israel, about twenty-one percent of the population. They vote. They sit in the Knesset. Ra'am was part of the governing coalition in 2021. An Arab justice, Salim Joubran, sat on the Supreme Court panel that convicted an Israeli president and sent him to prison.

That is real, and it demolishes the apartheid framing as usually deployed.

And here is the honest half. Palestinians in the West Bank and Gaza are not Israeli citizens and cannot vote in Israeli elections. That is a genuine unresolved problem, and pretending otherwise is the same selective editing I am objecting to.

Two more receipts.

The Palestinian Authority operated a payment system for imprisoned attackers and the families of those who killed Israelis, scaled to sentence length. Longer sentence, larger payment. That was policy, partly funded by international aid, and Abbas only decreed reform in February of last year under pressure.

And the legal question, honestly stated. The ICJ and most states hold that the settlements violate the Fourth Geneva Convention. Israel disputes this and argues the territory was never under recognised sovereignty. That is a real legal dispute with serious lawyers on both sides, and anybody telling you it is simple is selling you something.

So here is where I land.

You can believe settlement expansion is wrong. I do. You can believe this Israeli government has made peace harder. Many Israelis believe that and say so every week in Tel Aviv.

But you cannot hold that position honestly while omitting 1947, 1948, 1964, 2000, 2005, 2008, and October the seventh.

A movement that rejected a state in 1947, in 2000, and in 2008, then used the one territory it was handed to build tunnels, has not been waiting for an offer.

Both things are true. Only one side is required to say so.

text:
Palestinians dont have a state because of decades of Palestinian rejectionism as follows.

●1937 Peel Commission**: British proposal to partition Mandatory Palestine into a small Jewish state and a larger Arab state (linked to Transjordan), with population transfers. The Arab Higher Committee, led by Haj Amin al-Husseini, rejected it and demanded a single Arab state.

●1947 UN Partition Plan (Resolution 181)**: Proposed a Jewish state and an Arab state with Jerusalem under international administration. The Jewish Agency accepted it as a basis for a state. The Arab Higher Committee and surrounding Arab states rejected it and launched war after Israel’s declaration of independence in 1948.

●1967 Khartoum Resolution (“Three Noes”)**: After the Six-Day War, the Arab League (with Palestinian representation aligned) declared no peace with Israel, no recognition of Israel, and no negotiations with Israel.
PLO founding documents and early strategy**: The original Palestine National Charter called for the elimination of Israel. Even after the 1974 “phased plan,” parts of the leadership described a West Bank/Gaza entity as a stage toward reclaiming all of historic Palestine.

●Hamas 1988 Covenant**: Explicitly rejected Israel’s right to exist, framed the conflict in religious terms, and treated armed struggle as obligatory. Later documents (2017) softened some language but still rejected recognizing Israel as a Jewish state and insisted on the “right of return.”

●Camp David Summit, 2000**: Israeli Prime Minister Ehud Barak, with U.S. mediation by President Clinton, offered a Palestinian state on most of the West Bank plus Gaza, land swaps, and shared arrangements in Jerusalem. Yasser Arafat rejected the package and did not present a formal counter-offer; the Second Intifada followed.

●Taba talks, 2001**: Follow-on negotiations that closed some gaps from Camp David ended without an agreement as the Israeli government changed and violence continued.

●Olmert offer, 2008**: After dozens of meetings, Prime Minister Ehud Olmert presented Mahmoud Abbas a map and package involving roughly 93–97% of the West Bank with 1:1 land swaps, Gaza, and a special regime for the Holy Basin. Abbas did not accept it; he later said the gaps were too wide or that he did not receive sufficient time/details.

●Trump “Peace to Prosperity” plan, 2020**: The Palestinian Authority rejected the plan outright before and after publication and refused to negotiate on its terms.

●Recurring positions in later talks**: Palestinian leadership has consistently rejected recognizing Israel as the nation-state of the Jewish people, insisted on an unrestricted “right of return” for refugees and descendants into Israel proper (which is the demographic negation of a Jewish state), and declined to end claims or fully dismantle armed groups as part of a final-status deal.

Haven't even raised the matter of both Gaza and PA governance being terrorists.

Je suis sick of this shit. 

People invariably will start droning on about 1967 borders. Excuse me but there wasnt peace in 67 either. 

Im done being polite about the lies, the liars who tell them and the apologists who think these people should be rewarded with statehood. 

Whats this? Why yes its a fabulous Gazan retail shops titled Hitler 2. Mannequins were neatly accessorized with the latest jihadi chic accoutrements. The obligatory keffiyeh,  bataclavas and of course knives for stabbing Jews. 

The people who, from their safe, lofty perches in the West, wag their greasy little fingers at Israel about a 2 state solution disgust me. 

Especially  after October 7th. They would NEVER wish for themselves, their parents, their children to be subjected to THIS as a neighbor. 

That they have a different standard for Jews tells ne EVERYTHING I need to know about them.

The memo says a combat camp run by Alfa-Metal, a military training company, in Mejdeni, northern Bulgaria, employs instructors from “a range of backgrounds” including the SAS, the Australian Commando Regiment, US police forces and the US Navy Seals.

The Alfa-Metal centre offers special forces training and advanced sniper courses for around €4,000 (£3,400) per head, targeting prospective members of private military companies, bodyguards and corporate security teams.

However, the intelligence document says that since 2022, when Russia invaded Ukraine, private training camps in Europe have continued to accept Russian citizens for training courses including “advanced close quarters combat”.

The special forces veterans interviewed to collect intelligence on the camp said they had been told by current employees that it continued to train Russian nationals as of 2025, three years after Vladimir Putin’s invasion of Ukraine.

The claims have been denied by Alfa-Metal.

text:
In the winter of 1938 a Jewish parent in Berlin, Vienna or Prague was not choosing between countries. The map had already closed. Hitler had taken Austria in March. He had begun the destruction of Czechoslovakia. Kristallnacht in November had shown what came next: synagogues burned, shops smashed, thirty thousand men dragged to camps. Anyone who still pretended this was a passing spasm was lying to himself. The question was not whether the Reich would stop at the German border. It was how far the Wehrmacht would go, and how quickly every neighbouring state would become a trap.

That is why the comparison with today’s Channel crossings is not sentimental. It is historical. The Kindertransport children at Liverpool Street were not shopping for a welfare state. Their parents put them on trains because they understood that when Germany overran the Continent those children would be murdered. France, the Netherlands and Belgium looked like refuge in 1938. In May and June 1940 they were occupied. Jews who had fled there were registered, rounded up and sent east. Of the Jewish children who reached the Netherlands and were still there when the Germans arrived, most were later deported and most of those deported were killed. The same pattern held in Belgium and in occupied France. A “safe country” on the Continent was a waiting room. Britain was not. The Channel, the Navy and the fact that Britain did not fall meant that a child who reached Harwich in 1939 was not going to be handed to the Gestapo in 1942.

The rest of the world had already given its answer. In July 1938 thirty-two governments met at Évian. They expressed sympathy and then explained why they could take almost no one. America kept the 1924 quotas. Waiting lists at consulates ran into the hundreds of thousands; the visas did not. Australia said it did not wish to import a racial problem. Canada found reasons. Latin American republics spoke of traders and intellectuals, which everyone understood to mean Jews. The Dominican Republic made a gesture; the numbers that actually arrived were tiny. Britain itself would not open Palestine. The 1939 White Paper cut Jewish immigration into the Mandate just as the killing machine was being assembled. Shanghai later took people because for a time it required no visa; it was a distant, overcrowded last resort, not a plan a mother in Vienna could use for a ten-year-old in December 1938. The St Louis was turned away from Cuba and the United States and sent back towards Europe. Some of those passengers later died in the camps.

So when British Jewish leaders went to Chamberlain after Kristallnacht and asked for the children, they were not asking Britain to be one option among many. They were asking for the last large European country that would still be standing when the others were not. The government agreed on terms that would be unthinkable in the present asylum system. The children had to be under seventeen. Parents could not come. Private citizens and Jewish organisations had to guarantee that no child would become a charge on public funds. A bond was required. The first transport left Berlin on 1 December 1938; about two hundred children from a burned orphanage reached Harwich the next day. Further trains left Vienna, Prague, Danzig and the German cities. They crossed the Dutch border, boarded the ferry, and arrived at Liverpool Street with labels round their necks and a suitcase. Roughly ten thousand came before war stopped the scheme. A last boat got out of IJmuiden on the day the Netherlands surrendered.

They were not housed in hotels at a hundred and seventy pounds a night. They went to foster families, hostels and holiday camps. Some were treated well. Some were used as cheap labour. In 1940 many of the older boys were interned as enemy aliens; a few were shipped to Canada and Australia on the Dunera. That was an ugly chapter. It does not cancel the larger fact. These were children selected, sponsored and expected to work. About a thousand later served in British uniform. After 1945 most never saw their parents again. They stayed, learned the language, took jobs, started firms, paid tax and raised British children. Refugee industrialists from the same years opened factories in the Special Areas, brought trades Britain did not have, and employed local people. Publishing houses, high-street businesses and professional families that still exist came out of that intake. They were not a net on the Treasury. The condition of entry had been that they would not be.

That is the standard against which the small-boat traffic has to be judged, and it fails it on every material point.

Since 2018 more than two hundred thousand people have been detected crossing the Channel in inflatables. The peak year was over forty-five thousand. Later years have stayed in the tens of thousands. About three-quarters of those arrivals are adult men. Children and women are a minority on that route. The leading nationalities in the latest official figures have been Eritrean, Sudanese, Afghan, Somali and Iranian. Almost every arrival claims asylum. They have not come from a continent about to be occupied by a regime whose published programme was their extermination. They have come through France. France is a safe country. So are Belgium, the Netherlands, Italy, Greece and the other states they passed before they paid a smuggler for the last twenty-one miles of water. That is not the Kindertransport. It is a chosen destination after safety has already been reached.

The pull is not mysterious. Arrival usually means a claim, accommodation and support while the claim is processed. Hotels have cost the taxpayer billions. In one recent year hotel bills alone were more than two billion pounds, at several times the cost of ordinary housing. The ten-year accommodation contracts were first put at four and a half billion and have been revised toward fifteen. Processing is slow. Removal of the refused is harder still. A young man who destroys his papers, crosses from a safe third country and says the word asylum enters a machine that feeds and houses him. That machine did not exist for the Jewish child of 1939. His keep was guaranteed by people who would have been bankrupted if they had defaulted.

Some of those now crossing come from states that persecute. Eritrea, Taliban Afghanistan, Sudan and Iran are not holiday destinations. A proper system would take a limited number of genuine cases by organised routes, identify them, and refuse the rest. What Britain has instead is an irregular sea crossing run by gangs, dominated by military-age men, landing in a country that already offers legal asylum and resettlement paths, and then a political class that cannot say the obvious: France is not Dachau, and Calais is not 1938.

The failure is not the work of one party. The Conservatives held office for fourteen years while the boats went from a few hundred a year to a mass route. They passed Acts, announced Rwanda, and watched the numbers climb. They left a backlog, a hotel estate and a smuggling industry intact. Labour took over in 2024 promising control. Crossings continued in the tens of thousands. Some returns have increased and some hotels have closed; the route has not been closed. The Liberal Democrats and the Greens have treated deterrence itself as the scandal. They have opposed the measures that would make a young man in a French camp decide the last crossing is not worth it. Local government, contractors and the legal-aid and charity complex have lived off the volume. A large part of the professional class has decided that any distinction between a sponsored Jewish child fleeing industrial murder and an unknown adult male who has walked through half of safe Europe is a moral crime. That is not compassion. It is a refusal to use words as they were used when the words still meant something.

The statues at Liverpool Street show children who were sent away because their parents knew the Continent would not remain a place of life. Those parents were right. When Hitler overran Europe the Jews who had stopped in France, Holland and Belgium were hunted. The Jews who reached Britain were not. That is the whole difference. The present traffic is the opposite movement: people leaving safety to reach a particular benefits and legal system, facilitated by a political settlement that will not enforce a border and will not admit that a safe third country is safe. The Jewish refugees of 1938–39 were told they must not sponge. They did not. They worked. The men on the boats are told, in practice, that Britain will put them up and argue about them for years. That is why they come, and that is why the comparison with the Kindertransport is not a compliment to the present. It is an indictment.

text:
Ness, if you mean the Portsmouth incident involving around 140 people, there is a factual core to what you say, but several parts go beyond what the evidence actually establishes.

The French Maritime Prefecture says CROSS Jobourg deployed substantial resources: four SNSM rescue craft, the rescue tug Abeille Liberté, a French Navy H160 helicopter and the Civil Security Dragon 50 helicopter. So yes, five French surface assets and two helicopters were involved at various stages.

But that is not the same as saying all seven “shadowed them from the moment they left French soil until England”.

The official account says the boat was reported to CROSS Jobourg during the night, west of the Bay of Seine. It does not say those assets accompanied it from the beach. Indeed, Abeille Liberté arrived later and took over from some of the SNSM vessels, which rather demonstrates that this was a changing rescue deployment, not seven assets travelling alongside throughout.

Nor does the French authority describe its purpose as delivering the boat to Britain. It says the assets were deployed to monitor the vessel and be able to rescue its occupants if necessary. The occupants declined the assistance being offered and continued towards the UK. At midday, French reporting said no rescue or disembarkation had taken place.

And there is another important distinction: four of those surface vessels were SNSM lifeboats, France's volunteer maritime rescue service, not five French naval vessels escorting a migrant boat.

When the vessel subsequently came within UK responsibility, @HMCoastguard deployed British search-and-rescue assets, including RNLI lifeboats. That is how neighbouring maritime rescue systems manage a potentially hazardous vessel travelling between their areas of responsibility.

So I am perfectly happy to acknowledge what the evidence shows: a very substantial French safety operation followed and monitored this exceptionally large and potentially dangerous boat.

What I would not do is turn that into the much stronger claim that seven French assets collected it from the beach and deliberately escorted it all the way into England.

The official evidence does not say that.

As ever, the facts are interesting enough without adding anything to them.

text:
Pastor Jailed by Biden's Fascist ATF ~ PARDONED by Pres. Trump

By Lee Williams

The Sunday after he decided to accept a federal plea offer, in which he agreed to plead guilty to one count of selling ammunition to a prohibited person, Pastor Russell Fincher submitted his resignation to the board of his small Oklahoma church, but the board refused to accept his resignation.

“You didn’t change,” he recalls one board member told him. “The government changed.”

Pastor Fincher has continued to preach the gospel to his small flock ever since.

“They kept me going,” Fincher said Tuesday. “God told me the whole time: ‘You trust me.’”

Like Patrick “Tate” Adamiak and others, Fincher was the victim of Joe Biden’s ATF.

He recalls the hellish day in 2023 when a dozen ATF agents wearing tactical gear and carrying AR-15s stormed into his home.

They handcuffed him and laid him out on his porch. Several agents yelled and screamed at him for more than an hour while others ripped apart his home. He offered to relinquish his Federal Firearm License, and an agent quickly had him sign three forms.

The ATF took more than 50 of his personal firearms, including a Colt Commander, five Glocks and a mint AK—a Polytech Pre-ban milled under-folder, which was worth thousands of dollars.

“You’re done. We have to shut you down,” Fincher recalls the lead ATF agent saying. “You tell all your FFL buddies we are coming for them. We are shutting the gun shows down.”

Months later, a federal grand jury issued a three-count indictment charging Fincher with two felonies and one misdemeanor:

Count one: Engaging in the business of dealing firearms without a license, a felony.

Count two: Selling ammunition to a prohibited person, a felony.

Count three: Making false entry in records by a federal firearms dealer, a misdemeanor.

Fincher’s Federal Public Defender negotiated the plea agreement, which kept Fincher out of federal prison. Both sides agreed that three years of probation would be “the appropriate disposition of the case.” The plea agreement also specified that Fincher would not contest the forfeiture of his personal firearms.

Last week, Fincher received a letter from his Teachers’ Retirement Fund, which scared him.

“They said they were kicking me out—I spent 10 years as a teacher—because I was a felon,” he said.

Things changed just a few days later when he received a call from the Federal Public Defender who had handled his criminal case.

“You’re not gonna believe this, but you just got a full presidential pardon,” Fincher said the attorney told him.

text:
Oklahoma pastor targeted by ATF thrilled by President Trump’s pardon

The Sunday after he decided to accept a federal plea offer, in which he agreed to plead guilty to one count of selling ammunition to a prohibited person, Pastor Russell Fincher submitted his resignation to the board of his small Oklahoma church, but the board refused to accept his resignation.

“You didn’t change,” he recalls one board member told him. “The government changed.”

Pastor Fincher has continued to preach the gospel to his small flock ever since.

“They kept me going,” Fincher said Tuesday. “God told me the whole time: ‘You trust me.’”

Like Patrick “Tate” Adamiak and others, Fincher was the victim of Joe Biden’s ATF.

He recalls the hellish day in 2023 when a dozen ATF agents wearing tactical gear and carrying AR-15sstormed into his home.

They handcuffed him and laid him out on his porch. Several agents yelled and screamed at him for more than an hour while others ripped apart his home. He offered to relinquish his Federal Firearm License, and an agent quickly had him sign three forms.

The ATF took more than 50 of his personal firearms, including a Colt Commander, five Glocks and a mint AK—a Polytech Pre-ban milled under-folder, which was worth thousands of dollars.

“You’re done. We have to shut you down,” Fincher recalls the lead ATF agent saying. “You tell all your FFL buddies we are coming for them. We are shutting the gun shows down.”

Months later, a federal grand jury issued a three-count indictment charging Fincher with two felonies and one misdemeanor:

· Count one: Engaging in the business of dealing firearms without a license, a felony.
· Count two: Selling ammunition to a prohibited person, a felony.
· Count three: Making false entry in records by a federal firearms dealer, a misdemeanor.

Fincher’s Federal Public Defender negotiated the plea agreement, which kept Fincher out of federal prison. Both sides agreed that three years of probation would be “the appropriate disposition of the case.” The plea agreement also specified that Fincher would not contest the forfeiture of his personal firearms.

Last week, Fincher received a letter from his Teachers’ Retirement Fund, which scared him.

“They said they were kicking me out—I spent 10 years as a teacher—because I was a felon,” he said.

Things changed just a few days later when he received a call from the Federal Public Defender who had handled his criminal case.

“You’re not gonna believe this, but you just got a full presidential pardon,” Fincher said the attorney told him.

President Donald Trump gave Fincher and several others a “full and unconditional” pardon last week.

Now, with no criminal record, Fincher has been busy answering calls from friends, family and supporters.

He hopes he can return to teaching and coaching, in addition to his pastoral work. However, he has no plans to return to selling guns.

“There’s no way I am going to invite the federal government back into my world,” he said. “I am still so petrified of the federal government.”

He hopes he can retrieve his personal firearms from the ATF, and he wants to meet and personally thank President Trump.

“I never thought I’d be here,” he said. “I never thought I’d get a pardon. I serve a mighty God, and as much as I love President Trump, God orchestrated this pardon.”

HERMANVILLE, Miss. — Sept. 7, 2026 — Claiborne County Sheriff’s Deputy Terrian Bailey, 45, was fatally shot shortly after midnight Monday while deputies were responding to a crowd at Michael Dean’s Convenience Store on Highway 18 near Hermanville, authorities said.

According to the Mississippi Bureau of Investigation, deputies were attempting to disperse a crowd that had gathered after a Labor Day weekend festival when gunfire was directed toward the crowd. Bailey was struck and transported to a local hospital, where he later died. A female bystander was also shot and hospitalized with injuries described as non-life-threatening.

Sheriff Edward Goods said investigators believe gunfire came from two groups and that Bailey was struck in the lower right torso. Three firearms were later recovered from a book bag about one mile from the scene, according to the sheriff. Authorities have not publicly identified a suspect, and no arrests had been announced as of Sept. 9.

The MBI is leading the investigation and is collecting evidence for review by the local district attorney and Mississippi Attorney General’s Office. Investigators returned to the scene Tuesday for additional processing, and Bailey’s body was taken to the state crime laboratory in Biloxi for an autopsy.

The FBI has offered a reward of up to $25,000 for information leading to an arrest and conviction. Officials have asked anyone with information to contact the Claiborne County Sheriff’s Office or investigators.

Bailey had served with the Claiborne County Sheriff’s Department for six years. He was a husband and father of four, according to the sheriff’s office.

Sources: Mississippi Bureau of Investigation; Claiborne County Sheriff’s Office; Sheriff Edward Goods

text:
There's lots of talk about the tokenpath, but it has never been more important for startups to also be on the tweetpath.

I've been discussing this with various folks and I know it sounds crazy/the result of being a terminally online VC, so here's why it matters (and how to do it):

First, many of today's great companies (@tryramp, @cognition, @modal, @openAI, @anthropic, @fal etc.) have cultures where a significant share of employees (and the founders) are regularly updating the world on what's going on here. It's hard to argue this is working against any of them, and it's also very different from history. I can't remember a single SaaS company that had this culture. 

So something has changed- and without a doubt, it is the pace of innovation in the fundamental primitive products that underpin what it means to be a startup today. SaaS was about blocking and tackling on top of cloud infrastructure building blocks (e.g., S3, EC2, etc.) that are still recognizable almost two decades later. In AI, new models drop on a weekly basis that have the potential to transform the value proposition of a product. Astra is a step-function change in computer use. H3 Max is a step-function change in text-to-video speed. Both dropped in the last few weeks (!!).

For better or worse, X is the platform on which news and analysis about these releases propagates. You can literally have access to @thsottiaux's commentary around Astra adoption, @Yuchenj_UW's read of model tradeoffs, @burkaygur's generative media insights, etc. in real time, and if you don't have them, you're behind by months in an era where months really matter. This can determine product decisions, spawn partnerships, etc. 

That's an argument for scrolling, but there's an equally compelling argument for participating. 

For a start, this critically important conversation is happening here and it is better to be a part of it than apart from it. It also feels/is fundamentally different than the navel-gazing that dominated X of yore- because almost every day there's a new thing to talk about/analyze/contribute. I used to have flashes of annoyance when I saw VCs dip into politics- don't see much of that on the timeline anymore, because there's so much to talk about in tech. 

Because of that, there's an opportunity to really express/brand oneself and build up a reputation/point of view that arguably didn't exist before and is way more valuable now. I know startups that have gotten acquisition offers, employees who have been poached to amazing companies, etc. all because they demonstrated progress or competence here (in part by showing that they are in the top 1% at consuming/processing the aforementioned constant information flow). The gap between employees who are on the exponential and not has never been larger, and this is the best/most observable way to demonstrate that you are on the exponential... and yes, exactly the  same logic applies for companies too, and then it gets recursive, because employees who are on the exponential want to work for companies who are on the exponential, and so on. 

And that's the last argument- the effort of demonstrating that you're on the information exponential (by participating in conversations that feature social risk if you haven't kept up) will necessarily help you stay there while inertia/human nature fight to drag you down. That alone is mega valuable on top of everything else. You will learn more, faster, if you force yourself to be engaging with folks on the frontier. It isn't the distraction it used to be- it is a learning accelerant. And keeping your head down/locking in/plowing forward on a strategy without staying abreast of the news of the day is less advantaged approach today than perhaps at any time in human history.

If I've convinced you- here's my advice on how to kickstart this as an individual/company. 

As an individual- post about cool stuff you're doing or learning about, get into a habit of thinking about what other people might find interesting/incremental and then send it and never think about it again unless someone replies. I'm writing this in one fell swoop and won't even reread it. If there's something you want to understand better, odds are someone else is thinking about it too. The bar is lower than you think- and if it catalyzes you to learn/sharpen up on an important topic, all the better- but you first have to get past the fear that makes you edit a post 20x before sending. That's a time suck for little incremental benefit.

As a company- for one, the culture needs to encourage and promote that employees sharing neat things they've done is good for the aura of the company. Ramp Labs under @alexstauffer_  posted a blog post on Opus playing Roller Coaster Tycoon that I still think about as a canonical example of org culture marketing. Companies need to grok that this isn't a distraction; it's core- and founders can really lead by example here. I've heard case studies where employees post their wins to X because they have a hunch that the CEO has a better chance of seeing it here than on Slack... and I don't think that's a cultural bug per se. 

The only real rules are: there can't be a super onerous process for getting posts approved (high trust), it works best as a mafia of people supporting each other, and, of course, one has to be doing/learning cool stuff that relates to their business problems. If you don't have that, you have another set of problems.

Very curious if others have thoughts/pushback here! That's part of the point, after all

text:
My deepest respect to Col Anurag and his family. A person who has served the nation deserves the very best care, support and rehabilitation that modern medicine can offer.

Locked-in syndrome is one of the most devastating neurological conditions. 
Col Anurag is conscious and aware, but is unable to speak or move most muscles. I understand why the family is asking: “Is there anything more that can be done?”

The honest answer is: There is currently no medicine or injection proven to reverse established locked-in syndrome. But that does NOT mean that nothing can be done.

Even after 13 months, I would strongly recommend assessment at a specialised centre with experience in long-term neurorehabilitation and assistive technology.

Important interventions include:
1. Detailed reassessment by a multidisciplinary team
A neurologist, rehabilitation physician, physiotherapist, occupational therapist, speech/swallow therapist, respiratory therapist, psychologist and specialist nurses should reassess him periodically. It is important to look carefully for even small voluntary movements that may have been missed or may have emerged over time.

2. Intensive, individualized neurorehabilitation
Regular physiotherapy should focus on maintaining joint mobility, preventing contractures, improving head/trunk control, sitting tolerance and any residual voluntary movement. Even a small movement of a finger, thumb, head or eye can sometimes become functionally very important.

3. Communication should be a top priority
If eye movements are preserved, an eye-gaze or eye tracking communication system can allow the person to communicate independently with family and healthcare professionals, use a computer and potentially access the internet. Simple low-tech communication methods should also be optimized. Restoring a reliable means of communication can dramatically improve autonomy and  quality of life.

4. Speech and swallowing rehabilitation
Periodic reassessment of swallowing and bulbar function is important. Some patients can recover partial swallowing or other bulbar functions. Speech-language therapy should continue whenever there is potential for improvement.

5. Respiratory rehabilitation
Chest physiotherapy, respiratory exercises, secretion management and periodic reassessment of ventilatory requirements are essential. Preventing aspiration and chest infections is extremely important.

6. Mental health and quality of life
Never assume that a person with locked-in syndrome does not understand what is happening around them.

What about newer technologies?
There is exciting ongoing research into:
1. Eye-tracking and advanced communication systems
2. Brain-computer interfaces (BCI) that translate brain signals into computer commands
3. BCI-assisted communication for people with severe paralysis
4. Robotics and functional electrical stimulation
5. Virtual reality and technology-assisted rehabilitation
6. Non-invasive brain stimulation, such as transcranial direct current stimulation, currently being explored as an adjunct to rehabilitation.

These technologies are promising, but it is important to be realistic: most are not yet proven treatments capable of reliably reversing locked-in syndrome.

▶️A recent report in 2026 described eye-tracker-assisted communication as part of multidisciplinary rehabilitation in locked-in syndrome, with improvement in communication and psychosocial adaptation. 
▶️Research into brain-computer interfaces is also progressing rapidly, particularly to restore communication and interaction for people with severe paralysis.

▶️Importantly, recovery from locked-in syndrome is not always confined to the first few months. While major recovery becomes less likely with time, some patients have shown meaningful improvement over many months and even longer. 
▶️The extent of recovery depends greatly on the cause, location and severity of brain injury and whether the syndrome is complete or incomplete.

For a man who has served our country, we owe him continued care, respect and access to every evidence-based opportunity for rehabilitation🙏 
There may not be a miracle medicine today. But there is still meaningful medicine to be practiced and meaningful hope to be offered.

text:
FOR IMMEDIATE RELEASE

Apple Introduces iPhone Fold — Because Two Halves Are Better Than One Whole

CUPERTINO, CALIFORNIA — Apple today unveiled iPhone Fold, the first iPhone engineered from the ground up to be worse in two separate configurations.

"We asked ourselves a simple question," said an Apple SVP of Product Marketing, holding the device at an angle where the crease was not visible. "What if a phone, but broken? And what if that was on purpose?"

The Hinge

At the heart of iPhone Fold is the Unibody Titanium Hinge Assembly, comprising 219 individual components, each one a future warranty claim. Apple engineers rated it for 300,000 folds. Internal testing found that users fold it an average of nine times, film it once, and then leave it open on a desk for the rest of its life like a tiny abandoned laptop.

The Display

Unfolded, iPhone Fold offers a 7.6-inch Ultra Retina XDR display with Continuity Crease™ — a permanent horizontal valley running through the center of every photo of your children. Apple's engineering team spent four years trying to eliminate it before pivoting to a strategy internally referred to as "mentioning it less."

Folded, iPhone Fold provides a 5.1-inch outer display, roughly the surface area of a hotel key card, on which you may view approximately one and a half text messages.

Additional Innovations

•Adaptive Thickness — twice as thick as iPhone 17 Pro. Apple has classified this as "presence."
•Dual-Cell Battery delivering all-day battery life, where "day" refers to a partial day
•Fold Sensor which detects when the phone has been folded and does nothing with that information
•Crease Mode — an accessibility feature that moves the Dock down slightly so it isn't inside the crack
•Cannot survive sand. Apple recommends customers avoid beaches, deserts, playgrounds, construction sites, and Arizona.
•Available in Natural Titanium, Black Titanium, and Titanium

Development

iPhone Fold represents seven years of research, 4,100 engineers reassigned from the car project, and approximately $19 billion in development costs — a sum roughly equal to the GDP of Iceland, spent so that a phone can do the thing a wallet already does.

"Some people will say we didn't need to build this," the SVP said. "Those people are correct. But they're not thinking about it in terms of a hinge."

Pricing and Availability

iPhone Fold starts at $2,899 for the 256GB model, or $34.99/month for 84 months. Apple has secured manufacturing capacity for 12 million units and internal forecasts project sales of "several."

Confirmed pre-orders to date: three YouTubers, one guy who is going to return it, and the SVP's mother.

Apple encourages customers to consider the standard iPhone, which costs one-third as much, weighs less, survives sand, and has no crease in it.

Apple revolutionized personal technology with Macintosh in 1984 and reinvented the phone with iPhone in 2007. Today Apple continues to lead the industry with iPhone, iPad, Mac, Apple Watch, and a product that is fundamentally two iPhones held together by a hope.

text:
The Polemic of Suffering
(Scars are a blessing*)

Before I even drew a full breath from the womb, before the first cry could escape my lips I was a statistical ghost to the machine of man. Born on October 3rd, 1989-right inside the tens days of repentance between Rosh Hashanah & Yom Kippur.

Tradition teaches that during these days, the books of life and death are actively open, and humanity stands in direct, unshielded judgment before the King. And such we are permanently tied to the theme of ultimate reckoning, trial, and the piercing of divine strictness.

the 4th of Tishrei corresponds directly with the Fast of Gedaliah (Tzom Gedaliah), a minor solemn fast day that commemorates the assassination of the Jewish governor of Judah, an event that plunged the remnants of the Jewish commonwealth into total desolation and forced exile. It is a day marking the brutal aftermath of betrayal, the collapse of civil order, and the bitter struggle of a remnant trying to survive against impossible odds in a ruined land.

Being born in the shadow of Yom Kippur stamps a life with the ethos of absolute survival through atonement, resilience, and the refusal to let destruction have the final word. It is the spiritual equivalent of being forged in a blast furnace where everything weak is burned away so that only an unyielding core remains.

Yet, what is life when it starts with a failing machinery of organs?

I was born in the shape of a C, my right shoulder touching my right ankle. My small intestine was attached to my liver and bladder. There was no way for me to remove the bile from my bowels-and thus I was rushed from where I was born 90 miles SE where my heart stopped near midnight, and Surgery began as my Mother still bled and my father stood wondering in the waiting room.

For six months, six long months I have no recollection of-I underwent surgery on my intestines, kidneys, liver, bladder-and the medical establishment quietly stamped an expiration date on my head: I'm sorry but he'll dead at 8, dead at 12, dead at 18, dead at 30. I'm sorry, your son will be a vegetable. I'm sorry, your son will never speak, nor write, nor communicate. You will need to be his guardian forever. On the 8th day, I was circumsized in the fashion of my ancestors (my mother being A Catholic of Sephardic history and of Levitic descent*) for my body was failing and further surgery would add too much scar tissue to let me heal properly.

Yet the body persisted, it grew stronger, more resilient. The spine was painstakingly bent into place over weeks, and months until my spine was as corrected as it would be. Asthma attacks nearly killed me, several times in my youth, the memory of the racing heart and the graying fuzzy world in my vision as you cannot breathe-does not fade from conscience when it occurs daily, or weekly as a child.

 Achieving the age of 36 was not something either I or the doctors, expected. Yet the Lord God, works in mysterious ways, as many have stated in the past.

Modern civilization loves to boast of its clinical omniscience, yet it offered me nothing but a countdown timer and a stack of operating tables while the world demanded perfection from a broken child, who bore the storm and pressed onwards anyways.

When my young body refused to cooperate with the statistics of the medical 'clergy' stating I should be dead or dying, the domestic sphere stepped in to finish the job. 

Home was not a sanctuary in my youth; it was a psychological prison administered by an opioid-addicted tyrant who traded a father's duty for a pair of fists and a wooden cane which I would learn, could break upon contact with human bone and flesh. 

I learned the taste of concrete, grass, dirt and blood from the floorboards early-knocked out from behind while doing the dishes-but not fast enough. Dragged into a garage, berated for bleeding, and forced to endure the hypocrisy of a household that demanded total subjugation while offering nothing but chaos as my soul kept my broken body from faltering. 

The culture preaches endlessly about "family values," while young men are left to absorb the blows of broken men in silence, told that enduring domestic terrorism is just character building.

And when I finally broke free of that roof, the macro-economy was waiting with its jaws open. I walked across scorched towns in 105-degree heat because they wouldn't even spot a ride, my feet blistering and my groin chafing in the heat under muscles never meant for strain, while the surrounding society crumbled beneath the weight of the 2008 financial collapse. I watched gas hit seven dollars a gallon, watched my generation get chewed up by gang violence, and watched every safety net vanish into thin air, only for it to appear later to illegals, heathens, and criminals.

 Every time I managed to claw together a scrap of savings-whether working night shifts through sub-zero Montana winters, coughing up yellow bile as my weight plummeted to 101 pounds (I'm 187 naturally*), or sleeping in a car on a bear-infested mountain—some systemic failure, some broken promise, or some parasitic leech stripped it away.

For years, the world demanded that I pay for its sins, because I chose kindness, good will, and hard work. I was expected to carry the weight of a broken father, abusive, manipulative, aggressive. An unmoored sister, faithless partners, and an economy built on quicksand. I was expected to be a sacrificial lamb, broken down in body with fused joints, a displaced hip, and lungs scarred by pneumonia twice, COVID TWICE, scarred by Asthma and Bronchitis, walking alone across frozen parking lots at thirty-seven below zero so I could afford to eat, and live another day.

Yet here is my indictment against the world that tried to bury me: I refused to stay in the ground, as Levite, my death will lay in Sacrifice. Not lonliness.

I didn't find my salvation in the empty promises of smooth-talking institutions or the comforting delusions of a soft culture that is slowly being burned away in the light. 

I dragged my battered frame out of the dirt through sheer, bloody-minded willpower, classical philosophy, and an unyielding faith in Christ that wasn't handed to me on a silver platter, or through inheritance, for I did not know the Christ in my youth. But wrenched out of the jaws of despair itself. 

I didn't just survive the wreckage of my youth-I inherited the ruins and dragged them with me to remind myself of the failures I have committed, or have had suffered upon me. I cleaned out the hoarder's nest I found myself in, took in scared children who knew nothing, taught the children to read. Where another had left ashes, I built a sanctuary out of the very scrap wood at my feet. I chose a life and walked towards it, knowing it wouldn't be an easy path.

Let the comfortable and the cowardly read the smooth, sanitized histories of men who never bled. My life is a living, breathing polemic against a world that builds its houses on sand-a testament that when the systems fail, the institutions rot, and the demons come calling, a hardened soul can still look the abyss in the eye, stand upright, and refuse to break.

My birth and circumstances, should have been death. Yet the Lord God Judged me on those days and I yet live. During the Ten Days of Repentance-the exact window of my birth-the illusion is stripped away. 

The books are open, the King is on His throne, and every soul is weighed on the cosmic scales. By all earthly logic, medical charts, and biological laws, my scale should have tipped decisively toward the dust.

The verdict was rendered before I even took my first breath: terminal, broken, and erased.

The medical establishment, the statistics, and wicked ways of the world all acted as petty judges handing down a permanent sentence. 

But a higher Court intervened. When God judged me on those days, He looked past the failing organs, the torn flesh, and the stacked odds, and He issued a counter-decree: I shall live. Every trial, every scar, and every near-death collapse since then has been living proof that man’s judgment is powerless against divine election.

I tell you, when you survive a trial that was mathematically designed to kill you, you no longer belong to the normal rules of the world nor do you look through the same lenses as you did before.

I am living on divine overtime. That is why the suffering doesn't break me-the forge, it refines me. The pain that has left me motionless on the floor, the betrayals that have led me and my own heart bleeding, and the physical decay of this mortal flesh are just the hammer blows shaping an instrument that was specifically spared to bear witness, to stand upright in the ruins, and to mock the systems that thought they could bury me.

And to who do I owe this honor? These hardships? My scars, my badges of life? Surely, it was the devil! Some would say. Others, poor luck. Yet devils and Luck have nothing to do with it.

 The Lord God Himself, the most High. The Blessed One of Heaven was my salvation and my armor before I even knew Him, He knew me in the womb and preserved me my life for the future.

He, The Lord God, is the Refiner who throws a man into the hottest fire not to consume him, but to burn away every ounce of dross until nothing is left but pure, unyielding steel. "Hoilha-Paz: Fine Gold is the best offering*"

When I trace my scars-the missing organs, the dog and wolf bites, the shattered bones, the decades of relentless trials and work I should have never engaged in-back to the hand of the Blessed One of Heaven, it changes everything. 

They are no longer random accidents of a cold universe, nor are they merely the malicious handiwork of broken men who tried to crush me. They are the deliberate, sovereign strokes of the Master Builder, carving out a vessel strong enough to carry the weight of an unshakeable faith so that one day I could kneel and bring it to you, where you sit.

A lesser God builds men for comfort, wraps them in cotton, and shields them from the storms of life. But the Most High builds warriors in the furnace, dragging them through the valley of the shadow of death so they can stand among the ruins and declare that His mercy endures forever.

He, The Lord God, didn't spare me from the crucible; He sustained me in it. Every badge of honor, every stripe, and every deep-set scar I carry on this weathered frame of just a few decades is a permanent testament to the God who weighed my soul, looked at the grave as the doctors, surgeons and specialists frantically worked on me in that Operating room in Fresno, California, and said: Not yet. Live child. And I lived.

My life began like an Almond tree dropping its fruit in October. And when the world looked at me...a stripped, battered trunk and saw only harshness, it failed to recognize a tree being forged to withstand the frost, knowing that its true bloom would come in its own time, defiant and untouched by the winter around it.

from what should have been a stump, I arose like a new shoot of life to live and proclaim through my body and my words-the glory of Our Lord God.

The LordGod who numbers the hairs of our heads and watches over the broken in spirit does not abandon those marked by affliction or cradled in the shadow of peril. They are the ones refined in the fire, held fast by the hand of the Blessed One, and kept for His purpose.

Children are a blessing. Not a curse.

Woe unto those, who deny the child life, and the Lord Gods words.

Go in peace. 

Amen.

text:
Secret courts issuing secret warrants betray the very bedrock of American liberty. The Fourth Amendment is not a suggestion.

The Foreign Intelligence Surveillance Act of 1978, codified in 50 U.S.C. chapter 36, established a framework for surveillance that stands in stark opposition to transparent justice. Though authorities have recently lapsed, such as Title VII under Public Law No. 119-87, enacted April 30, 2026, the underlying framework remains a threat. This Act, "To amend the FISA Amendments Act of 2008 to extend the authorities of title VII of the Foreign Intelligence Surveillance Act of 1978, and for other purposes," illustrates the creeping expansion of federal power.

Public Law No. 119-87 explicitly extended these intrusive powers by striking "April 30, 2026" and inserting "June 12, 2026" in the FISA Amendments Act of 2008. Even with its recent expiration, the constant legislative dance to reauthorize these powers, as seen in the failure of H.R.9238 on June 11, 2026, reveals an enduring appetite for unchecked surveillance authority. This legislative maneuvering consistently seeks to maintain a system inherently at odds with constitutional due process.

The Fourth Amendment to the U.S. Constitution unequivocally declares: "The right of the people to be secure in their persons, houses, papers, and effects, against unreasonable searches and seizures, shall not be violated, and no Warrants shall issue, but upon probable cause, supported by Oath or affirmation, and particularly describing the place to be searched, and the persons or things to be seized." ( Secret courts with opaque proceedings and historically near-perfect approval rates undermine the very spirit of this protection, rendering its safeguards nugatory.

James Madison, in Federalist No. 47, warned against the concentration of power, stating, "The accumulation of all powers, legislative, executive, and judiciary, in the same hands, whether of one, a few, or many, and whether hereditary, self-appointed, or elective, may justly be pronounced the very definition of tyranny." ( The FISA court's cloistered operation and its relationship with executive branch agencies create precisely this dangerous blend, eroding the separation of powers vital to liberty.

Such an arrangement stands in direct defiance of the principles of transparency and accountability upon which our republic was founded. The very concept of a "secret court" to authorize searches against American citizens, without public scrutiny or rigorous adversarial challenge, is anathema to the rule of law and the sanctity of individual rights.

To restore constitutional fidelity, we must advocate for the complete repeal of FISA's surveillance authorities, especially those that permit bulk collection and warrantless access to American data. The 'Protect Liberty and End Warrantless Surveillance Act of 2026' (H.R.7816) offers a path forward, seeking to dismantle these tools of overreach. We must return to the standard of individual, particularized warrants based on probable cause, as mandated by the Fourth Amendment, without exception for 'national security' pretexts that devour liberty. Should not our government be bound by the very charter it swears to uphold?

What are the new heaven and the new earth?
Answer
In Revelation 21:1, John sees something spectacular: “Then I saw ‘a new heaven and a new earth,’ for the first heaven and the first earth had passed away.” This new earth and new heaven are sometimes referred to as the “eternal state.” As seen in Revelation chapters 21—22, the new earth will be the eternal dwelling place of believers in Jesus Christ. Scripture gives us a few details of the new heaven and new earth.

The current heaven and earth have long been subject to God’s curse because of mankind’s sin. All creation “has been groaning as in the pains of childbirth” (Romans 8:22) as it awaits the fulfillment of God’s plan and “the children of God to be revealed” (verse 19). Heaven and earth will pass away (Mark 13:31), and they will be replaced by the new heaven and the new earth. At that time, the Lord, seated on His throne, says, “I am making everything new!” (Revelation 21:5). In the new creation, sin will be totally eradicated, and “there shall be no more curse” (Revelation 22:3, NKJV).

The new heaven and new earth are also mentioned in Isaiah 65:17; 66:22; and 2 Peter 3:13. Peter says that the new heaven and new earth will be “where righteousness dwells.” Isaiah says that “the former things will not be remembered, nor will they come to mind.” Things will be completely new, and the old order of things, with the accompanying sorrow and tragedy, will be gone.

The new earth will be free from sin, evil, sickness, suffering, and death. It will be earth as God originally intended it to be, prior to the curse of sin. It will be Eden restored.

A major feature of the new earth will be the New Jerusalem. John calls it “the Holy City . . . coming down out of heaven from God, prepared as a bride beautifully dressed for her husband” (Revelation 21:2). This glorious city, with its streets of gold and pearly gates, is situated on a new, glorious earth. The tree of life will be there (Revelation 22:2). This city represents the final state of redeemed mankind, forever in fellowship with God: “God’s dwelling place is now among the people, and he will dwell with them. They will be his people, and God himself will be with them and be their God. . . . His servants will serve him. They will see his face” (Revelation 21:3; 22:3–4).

In the new heaven and new earth, Scripture says, there are seven things notable for their absence—seven things that are “no more”:
• no more sea (Revelation 21:1)
• no more death (Revelation 21:4)
• no more mourning (Revelation 21:4)
• no more weeping (Revelation 21:4)
• no more pain (Revelation 21:4)
• no more curse (Revelation 22:3)
• no more night (Revelation 22:5)

The creation of the new heaven and new earth brings the promise that God “will wipe every tear from their eyes” (Revelation 21:4). This event comes after the tribulation, after the Lord’s second coming, after the millennial kingdom, after the final rebellion, after the final judgment of Satan, and after the great white throne judgment. The brief description of the new heaven and new earth is the last glimpse into eternity that the Bible gives.

Crop Progress Snapshot
The initial combining of the 2026 U.S. corn harvest is officially underway, according to Tuesday afternoon's delayed USDA NASS report for the week ending September 6. National corn harvest progress reached 5% complete, pacing slightly ahead of both last year's 4% and the 3% five year average. 

National corn condition ratings dipped 1 percentage point to 56% G/E, marking a new seasonal low. Maturation continues ahead of schedule, with 96% of the corn crop in the dough stage, 76% dented (4 points ahead of normal), and 25% reaching full maturity. Iowa continues to lead state level performance with 77% G/E.

Soybean condition ratings held steady week-over-week at 58% good-to-excellent. Crop maturity is accelerating rapidly across major production counties, with 26% of national soybean acreage now dropping leaves, running 6 percentage points ahead of both last year and the five year average of 20%. 

Concurrently, the spring wheat harvest reached 86% complete nationwide, while initial 2027 winter wheat seeding stands at 2%.

Weather and Outlook
Weather patterns across the Corn Belt are transitioning into a wetter early autumn cycle. A series of frontal systems moving across the central and northern Midwest is bringing repeated rounds of rain. 

While these showers offer late moisture relief to drought stressed fields, the precipitation is beginning to create localized delays for early harvesting operations. 

Temperatures remain near seasonal averages, and producers are watching for extended dry windows to keep combines rolling as crop maturity advances.

Markets and Prices
Grain traders on the Chicago board are balancing the first official national harvest pace against deteriorating crop quality ratings. 

Corn futures have found underlying support from the drop in national conditions to 56% G/E, even as seasonal supply pressure builds. 

Soybean contracts remain attentive to the rapid expansion of leaf-drop metrics and steady domestic crush demand. Interior basis bids at river terminals and ethanol plants remain relatively stable, though elevators are increasingly focusing on logistics as new crop receipts gain momentum.

Policy and Farm Bill Update
Legislative attention remains fixed on the Senate following the House passage of the Farm, Food, and National Security Act of 2026 (H.R. 7567). The multi-year legislation, which extends core agricultural safety nets and risk management programs through 2031, is facing rigorous committee debate as lawmakers attempt to reconcile stark regional priorities. 

Key debates continue to center around the expansion of precision agriculture funding, enhancements to crop insurance structures, and guidelines for rural energy investments.

 The national security components of the bill, particularly those expanding federal scrutiny over foreign investment in domestic agricultural land and limiting financial assistance for foreign sourced energy developments on prime ground, remain a central point of bipartisan interest.

Ethanol Outlook
The domestic ethanol complex maintains strong operational run rates heading into the fall. In the latest EIA weekly release, domestic fuel ethanol output remained supported by solid plant processing margins and active regional blending demand. 

Commercial inventories remain at comfortable operational levels, while growing field-level carbon intensity data tracking continues to position Midwest processors for upcoming clean fuel tax credit frameworks.

Fuel and Fertilizer
On farm operating budgets continue to monitor volatile energy markets. Regional Midwest diesel prices are holding near recent ranges, maintaining elevated baseline transportation and field expenses for early harvest passes. In the retail fertilizer sector, nitrogen suppliers are keeping early fall booking structures firm for liquid solution and anhydrous ammonia as producers finalize post-harvest application schedules.

Diversification and Resilience
Midwest operations are continuing to expand risk-mitigation strategies through extended crop rotations, the integration of small grains, and the strategic use of perennials. 

These practices are being paired with localized bioenergy projects and targeted livestock integration to diversify revenue streams. 

The broader adoption of these systems is designed to improve long term soil health, optimize internal nutrient cycling, and provide financial buffers against intense market volatility and unpredictable weather patterns.

Ag Tech and Innovations
The adoption of advanced biological inputs, targeted precision tools, autonomous field robotics, and real-time sensor networks continues to accelerate across the Corn Belt. 

Producers are leveraging integrated data platforms to optimize input efficiency, reduce total fuel consumption, and scale back variable operational expenses. 

These automated solutions are increasingly viewed as essential tools for maintaining strict environmental compliance and protecting profit margins during challenging production seasons.

Livestock and Feed
Late season forage limitations continue to impact livestock operations across the Midwest and Plains. According to the latest USDA metrics, 53% of national pasture and rangeland is rated in poor to very poor condition. Feedlot operators are actively securing early harvest grain deliveries and adjusting water management protocols as early corn picking expands.

Farmland Sales and Values
The 2026 Corn Belt real estate market is displaying noticeable resilience with moderation, marking a clear transition from rapid capital appreciation to a stable, highly selective environment. This shift is driven by tight overall inventory, heightened buyer caution amid compressed crop returns, and localized demand focused strictly on premium acreage. 

While national farm real estate averages hover around $4,350 per acre, prime cropland throughout the Corn Belt routinely commands double that figure, averaging between $8,000 and $9,000+ per acre.

State level metrics highlight a distinct two-tiered market where Class A ground holds firm while marginal acres experience minor softening:

Iowa: Overall values remain stable to slightly softer, with high-quality tillable ground holding firm despite benchmark surveys noting minor aggregate declines of 1.5%. Public auctions average $11,900 per acre for disclosed sales, though highly productive soils with top CSR2 ratings frequently command premiums between $20,000 and $25,600 per acre in strong counties such as Lyon, Sioux, and Johnson.

Illinois, Indiana, and Ohio: Strong competition for premium tracts persists, pushing exceptional farms to auction results between $14,000 and $22,000+ per acre. The broader eastern Corn Belt shows signs of stabilization, with lower quality or blemished parcels drawing fewer bidders due to rising input costs and geopolitical uncertainty.

Nebraska: Trends are mixed across the state, balancing localized benchmark gains with an overall statewide average decline of roughly 1% to $3,905 per acre. High quality irrigated tracts in counties like Butler remain highly sought after at $13,000+ per acre, while pasture prices are well supported by strong cattle market fundamentals.

Broader Midwest (MN, MO, SD): Performance remains highly variable. High-quality row-crop land easily commands auction premiums ranging from $8,000 to $19,000 per acre. Meanwhile, recreational parcels and properties near urban development zones exhibit higher price volatility, though a historically low supply of available farms prevents broad downward price pressure.

The combination of limited inventory, steady investor interest, and 1031 tax-deferred exchanges keeps the market selective rather than weak. Tight margins and elevated interest rates will likely maintain this steady to soft trend for the remainder of 2026, though well marketed, highly productive tracts will continue to draw active bidding.

Other Notes
Recent export inspections confirm steady grain shipments to primary international destinations, offering vital demand relief to local terminals. Concurrently, regional supply chains are adapting to shifting environmental standards as biofuel advocates push back against restrictive out of state greenhouse gas regulations that impact Midwest ethanol markets.

Looking Ahead
Future weekly editions will rotate to feature deep dives into regional pest management, state specific policy impacts, and early harvest preparations. Producers are encouraged to share local field observations and specific topic requests while continually monitoring updated extension data, localized auction results, and Federal Reserve agricultural economic letters.

text:
He said he was the man to get a deal and save the country.
Here we are.
No deal. A fireside chat. “As long as it takes.” Tariffs on the mascara and the stove so Ohio feels it in November. A summit next week with our pension on the letterhead. Strasbourg after that.
That is not a man trying to win this fight with the United States. That is a man trying to wait it out while he lines up everybody else — Europe, China, India, whoever will take a meeting.
Use common sense.
The United States is the kitchen table’s customer. You do not replace that overnight. You do not replace it in a speech. The decades it would take to rebuild that book, this country does not have. The middle class does not have. Kids in the basement do not have.
If he thought that market was as important as it is, he would show the offer he walked away from, recall the House, and stop talking like we have gas in the tank.
We do not.
Alignment is not a grocery bill.
Time is not a strategy when you are the one who cannot wait.
Kitchen table first.
This path kills the middle.

authorBio: Proud nana to nine wonderful grandchildren. Want their future to be bright.
