text:
here's a question by question summary of my most recent space with @JustinCBram, @0xMGB & @cas3333333 from the @variational_io team, alongside @TradFiHater and @0xMerp as special guests

enjoy

--------------------------------------------------------

1. on launching swaps: what was it actually like behind the curtain?

max said it was a long-anticipated product and a late sprint. weekend deploys, heavy internal testing, and a lot of last-mile work to make sure it launched clean

the team sat on a call while the deploy went live. orders started coming in within seconds. no major issues since launch. the numbers in the days after have been motivating, and the team is already onto the next features

--------------------------------------------------------

2. what have max and cas been doing on swaps specifically?

core growth work: test thoroughly, surface small ux improvements, and push the product so people actually try it

cas framed it as getting the job done rather than talking about it. max said they started posting screenshots early because the internal liquidity and execution quality was already exciting the quant team

--------------------------------------------------------

3. what's the response been like thus far?

some swaps stats, accurate at press time:

-swaps make up ~30% of weekday volume
-consistently making new oi and tvl aths
-gross trading revenue is up 61%
-the majority of trading volume now in tradfi markets

max's take: they care more about real usage than farmed metrics. points are obviously in the mix, but backend data suggests a meaningful organic chunk

comparison versus existing btc perps and rwa perps looked strong. this is only the first handful of markets, with 100+ more in the pipeline

justin: reception was stronger than expected, but it makes sense. existing crypto perp markets for tradfi assets have been mispriced for a long time

direct quotes:

‘I think i'm seeing funding right now at negative 45% for us 500. And so we're able to offer, you know, i think a 4.65% annualized funding rate for us 500 and we're paying dividends on top of that to longs. and so like this mispricing is just so vast. . .I think we're actually going to have a pretty big impact over the next few weeks in what people are paying in crypto in general, and we're going to push these rates down to what they should be and what they should have been this whole time."

'If you look at the gold perp funding rate on your Hyperliquids, your Lighters, your Binances, and what the rate should be for gold, the most liquid asset in the entire world, it's pretty clear that crypto has been mispricing this stuff.'

--------------------------------------------------------

4. how big can swaps be?

justin thinks swaps will dwarf perps. already a large share of volume with only four markets. if growth continues, variational starts looking more like a swaps venue than a perp venue

because variational is not an exchange, duplicative listings let users farm funding differences without variational users being the ones stuck paying the mispricing

direct quotes:

‘I think it's going to dwarf perps honest. I mean it already is i think 30%ish of our volume on the platform after like 3 days with four markets listed. I would expect variational to very quickly be described better as like a swaps trading platform than a perp trading platform.’

'Because we're not an exchange, when we have a duplicative listing, it's not necessarily our users that are paying this mispricing in funding. We're pulling that liquidity in from other exchanges. That allows our users to farm the funding arbitrage directly on our platform all in one go, without it actually having a negative impact on our users.'

--------------------------------------------------------

5. wen api?

justin: can't go beyond what has already been shared. it is a top priority into points winding down. points are meant to go to real users, so timing will be coordinated

nb: later in the space, max said to expect something this month. the team has been delaying api so early points go to click traders rather than bots

direct quote:

‘I can't answer beyond what's already been shared. i'll say it's one of our top priorities leading into points winding down. Points are supposed to go to your real users. and so it's something that i think will play hand in hand.’

--------------------------------------------------------

6. feedback from larger traders on swaps?

justin: positive. big traders were previously anchored to binance, hyperliquid, bybit etc. swaps gave variational a genuinely new product class and enough size to matter onchain. group chats with large users have been constructive. ui feedback is being shipped quickly, including items sent overnight

direct quote:

‘A lot of them have sort of come back and said, wow, this really changes things. we can actually really use swaps in the size that we want to trade on chain. A bigger trader just messaged me last night on twitter, gave us two pieces of feedback that we were able to implement basically immediately.’

--------------------------------------------------------

7. what has the growth team got planned to get people to try swaps?

max:

-direct outreach to known large traders with execution screenshots
-onchain trader rewards campaign, designed around swaps and seeing a second wind after launch
-double points boost on swaps to push existing users off familiar perps

the recurring theme: just get people to click into the product. the eureka moment is the execution cost

direct quote:

‘A lot of the times it's just as simple as us kind of pinging a message over with a good graphic or a screenshot of what the execution cost looks like on a large order: 'Hey, we just launched a new product, you might be interested in giving it a try if you're trading a lot of tradfi perps right now.’

--------------------------------------------------------

8. will users stick around after points end?

cas: build something people cannot get elsewhere. hog futures and a memecoin in the same venue is the kind of uniqueness that creates reasons to stay

max: while metrics derived from farming can be misleading, we shouldn't be overly cynical. there is a huge amount of real trading/organic activity going on. the product ultimately has to stand on its own

justin: betting on the rfq model. almost every tradfi perp should get a swap market with better pricing, tighter execution, and bounded funding

direct quotes:

‘The product's just going to have to stand on its own two legs. like if the product is something that people are going to use, you know, regardless of points, then it's going to be something people use regardless of points. If it's not, then it's not.’

'These projects will kind of let the farmer metrics get to their heads, as like, oh yeah, we have a user base of hundreds of thousands of people, and it's like no, you have 100 people sybiling a points campaign.'

'Users are basically going to be forced to trade on Variational because we're going to deliver the best price, the best execution, bounded funding rates on any asset you can imagine. And right now the space is pretty open to us as far as I'm aware. Like we're the ones that are really building out the true vision for RFQ. I just haven't seen that elsewhere.'

--------------------------------------------------------

9. will it be the case that traders use different trading venues for different markets, based on execution?

max: depends on fee tier. for ordinary retail on the bottom fee tier, variational should be the default for almost everything. a top-tier binance trader may still get better long-tail crypto execution elsewhere. the target user is the person who does not have a billion in weekly volume

direct quote:

‘If you're looking at things like a true pure retail user that has like bottom fee tier on any platform i genuinely do think variational would be the go-to place to trade pretty much anything. That first user that i'm talking about is really our target market.’

--------------------------------------------------------

10. krieger's variational thesis

background: former lawyer, late to crypto in 2024, approached it like due diligence. docs and team quality stood out. the unique model, especially pro, was the hook. core thesis: the otc derivatives market is dark, slow, and intermediated

pro can let anyone craft and trade custom derivatives without weeks of phone calls and middlemen. swaps are the first public proof that the liquidity and demand are real

direct quote:

‘In the us there is $150 trillion of derivatives. that's the total notional. and it's completely hidden. . .You have trillions of derivatives sleeping out there and if you can plug them uh to this market you unlock trillions of liquidity.'

--------------------------------------------------------

11. liquidity, oi limits, and bottlenecks

krieger asked where the liquidity comes from and what the ceiling is. max gave the clearest answer the team has given publicly, and named the constraints himself

first, a clarification: the ~$1b figure is olp's current external hedging capacity, not an oi cap. a 60/40 book only needs a slice hedged

two bottlenecks, both capital and connectivity problems rather than design problems:

-hedging capacity and market access. current agreements are the first, not the last, with later-stage conversations ongoing for asian and european markets
-olp's balance sheet. near term via lp deals, longer term via community deposits

direct quote:

'The one billion plus in capacity that we have sourced is actually the current hedging limits that olp has against its traders. That doesn't actually translate to a one billion strict oi cap on swaps because a lot of the flow ends up netting itself out'

--------------------------------------------------------

12: active accounts have been flat since may. what now? (question from community)

max : the internal north star is market share, not raw active users, volume or oi. that share has been rising. raw active users have also started recovering. next is onboarding people outside the existing crypto perp cohort

justin, on future product developments: inspired by fomo's mobile/onboarding polish. public mainnet after private beta, trading api, twaps, safer path to opening olp, and more ways to make trading cheaper and more rewarding

direct quote:

'The main metric that we look at is market share more than anything. . .We obviously can't control whether the market goes up or down, but what we can control and what we always try and push for is just taking up more and more of that trading activity.'

--------------------------------------------------------

13. is variational becoming an interactive brokers competitor?

krieger's framing: less a perp dex, more an onchain broker going after wall street titans that are powerful but ugly and slow to support

max: that is the original thesis. they are not trying to replace onchain or offchain order books. they are competing for where actual retail ends up trading

direct quote:

‘Our thesis from the beginning has been like we're not here to replace any order books whether onchain or offchain. We have always seen ourselves as a very separate business model like that broker type model as you mentioned.’

--------------------------------------------------------

14. merp on hyperliquid, community, airdrop % and tokens

merp: still bullish hype, also bullish variational because the smartest people he knows are. no real negativity toward variational in the hl crowd, which is rare

aligning thousands of people with token success is one of the strongest marketing tools that exists. the token needs a reason to exist, and the team needs to demonstrate alignment

direct quotes:

‘The number one marketing tool like in the entire world probably is to align thousands and thousands of people with the economic success of your token. . .There are tokens that are built for long-term wealth accumulation, and there are tokens that exist to be sold.’

'I don't have the most Variational points, but I know like basically all the smartest people I know are super bullish on Variational. And so that makes me too as well.'

'In crypto the bar was so low for so long that even still, if you just do these bare minimum executions and actually act with intent to accrue long-term value to your treasury and to your protocol and to your token holders, you can just make a f***load of money in crypto if you just decide to. And for the longest time, people decided to just take what was available as quick as possible.'

--------------------------------------------------------

15. how do liquidations work on swaps? (question from community)

justin: listed swap markets trade about 23 hours a day. roughly one hour offline after us close. price does not update while closed, so quiet overnight wicks do not hit you. the risk is the open: first incoming price can gap, and that print can trigger orders and liquidations

direct quote:

‘When the market opens if there's some really heavy news that hits, the market can go up or down and sort of gap open or gap down. The first price that comes in that's the price that orders are basically going to trigger off of and that would include liquidations as well.’

--------------------------------------------------------

16. wen lean hogs? what else is coming?

hogs are coming asap. lean hogs specifically tbd, but hogs are on the upcoming list. cocoa, coffee, sugar and other commodities already in view. hundreds of candidate markets

direct quote:

‘I think we have hogs. i don't know if we have lean hogs, but hogs are coming asap. All of that stuff is coming soon. the most upcoming swaps i think are already listed as coming soon on the platform.’

--------------------------------------------------------

17. beyond the api and swaps, what future catalysts does the team have up its sleeve?

cas: pair exotic listings with the api and you get something genuinely new. not crypto traders getting a better tool, but people with real-world exposure hedging it onchain for the first time

justin: variational still feels small internally, and the sector comparison explains why. binance did $80b in perp volume in a single day recently. hyperliquid does roughly $10b. capturing the existing perp market alone is a 100x from here, before swaps change the competitive map and before pro exists at all

direct quotes:

'When we have hog futures available and then somebody's able to algorithmically trade, maybe they're a hog farmer, they have their own cattle or hogs or soybeans. There's a lot of opportunity for people to come in and bring their own personal liquidity and trade in a way that most people just wouldn't have access to'

'We've been working on variational for a while so it still feels really small to us. We're just at currently so, so small. even just capturing the current market is just a massive 100x growth from here, and that's not even factoring in how swaps sort of changed the dynamic with all the existing perp players'

--------------------------------------------------------

text:
That inherent innocence is precisely why, when the words tumbled from her lips with absolute serenity that brisk Tuesday morning, something foundational inside my chest snapped.

“Dad,” she murmured, her voice entirely devoid of malice or fear. “Every night, a man comes into your bedroom. He waits until you’re completely asleep.”

My grip on the leather steering wheel faltered, my knuckles instantly turning bone-white. The SUV swerved a fraction of an inch before I corrected it.

“Sweetheart… what exactly did you just say?”

She didn’t look at me. Her large brown eyes remained fixed on the passenger window, observing the blur of morning commuters and suburban storefronts gliding past. She might as well have been observing a passing cloud formation.

“He walks exceptionally slow,” she elaborated, tracing a raindrop on the glass with her index finger. “Like he’s trying to trick the floorboards so they won’t make a sound. Mom closes her eyes when he’s there, but she never says a word.”

I waited for the punchline. I waited for the tremor of a nightmare still clinging to her waking mind.

There was no confusion in her tone. No lingering terror. Just a sterile, factual certainty. And it was that unshakeable certainty that turned the blood in my veins into glacial ice.

“Maya…” I managed to choke out, forcing a lightness into my voice that I absolutely did not feel. “Where on earth did you get a silly idea like that?”

She offered a tiny, indifferent shrug. “I see him, Dad.”

The remainder of the drive to her elementary school felt entirely wrong, as if the atmospheric pressure inside the cabin had quadrupled. The air was thick, tasting faintly of copper and exhaust. I kept throwing desperate, darting glances at the rearview mirror, silently begging for a giggle, a smirk, some universal signal that this was merely the bizarre byproduct of a child’s overactive imagination.

Nothing. She simply adjusted the neon-pink straps of her backpack, humming a nonsensical melody under her breath, blissfully unaware that she had just detonated a psychological landmine beneath my feet.

Perhaps it was a vivid night terror, I reasoned frantically. Maybe she caught a glimpse of some late-night television show. Perhaps a trick of the hallway moonlight gave a coat rack a human face.

Perhaps.

But there are rare moments in life when a cluster of words strikes your sternum, and your body processes the catastrophic truth long before your conscious mind dares to accept it.

I deposited her at the school gates. She pressed a hasty kiss to my cheek, tumbled out of the car, and sprinted toward the playground, her pink backpack bobbing rhythmically. I sat idling at the curb, watching her dissolve into a sea of screaming children, and for a terrifying second, the axis of my entire world tilted.

Instead of turning toward my downtown law firm, I threw the car into drive and headed straight back to the house.

My wife, Sarah, was standing at the kitchen island, occupying the exact geographical coordinates she always did at 8:15 AM. Honeyed morning sunlight washed over her shoulders. The espresso machine hissed gently. Her auburn hair was secured in a messy, effortless knot. When she heard my heavy footsteps, she glanced up, her lips curving into a smile so familiar and warm that it momentarily short-circuited my rising panic.

“Forget a brief?” she asked, wiping down the marble counter.

For the first time in a decade of marriage, I found myself paralyzed, unsure of how to look at the woman I loved.

I desperately wanted to chuckle. I wanted to relay Maya’s absurd statement and watch Sarah roll her eyes, explaining away the mystery in a matter of seconds. I yearned to believe my daughter had simply interwoven a dream with reality, and that the sanctuary of my marriage remained impenetrable.

Instead, I stood frozen in the archway, my keys biting into the flesh of my palm, and suddenly began cataloging details I had spent months subconsciously ignoring.

text:
If you're a podcaster, this is really why we built https://t.co/J69SLNPrDX.

We're one of you.

We know what it feels like to put hours into an episode and wonder whether it was worth it.

We know what it's like to watch the download numbers and wish you knew more about the people behind them.

We know what it's like to want to send something useful to listeners and realize most of them will never see it.

We know what it's like to think about monetization — not because you're greedy, but because producing a good podcast costs time and money.

And if the show can't eventually support itself, passion can become exhaustion.

That's where PodSubs came from.

We built it as an internal tool.

Something simple.

At the end of the show:

“Subscribe to our podcast on PodSubs.”

They search for us.
Enter their name and email.
Subscribe.

That's it.

From that point, we have a direct communication channel with the people who chose to stay connected.

We can send the resource from today's episode.

We can tell them what's coming next week.

We can share an update.

We can ask for feedback.

We can make an offer.

We can build something around the podcast without starting from zero every time.

And eventually we looked at what we'd built and realized:

This shouldn't only belong to us.

Every podcaster should at least have the option.

So that's what PodSubs is becoming.

A simple place where someone who loves your show can become someone you can actually reach.

If you have a podcast, claim it.

And on your next episode, try saying:

“Subscribe to our podcast on PodSubs.”

You might be surprised how many people were just waiting for somewhere to go.

Got targeted today by what looks like a fake audit/recruitment campaign.

They opened the conversation by linking my Cantina profile and asking if I was looking for new opportunities.

At first it looked like a normal audit lead. They said they were building an RWA protocol and needed a smart contract auditor.

I asked what chain.

“EVM”

I told them I mainly audit Solana/Rust, so I probably wasn’t a good fit.

A minute later it became “actually multi-chain,” and they sent me a tech stack full of Solana/Rust, Anchor, SPL, PDA/CPI, Metaplex, etc.

They were also very pushy about getting on a call immediately, followed by NDA signing and private GitHub access.

I kept asking for the company/project details first.

Eventually they gave me https://t.co/X0wIVUL4nG.

ChainVisita has already been publicly documented in a fake developer recruitment campaign where targets were given malicious repositories that downloaded a second-stage stealer targeting browser credentials and crypto wallets.

So if you get a similar audit offer, especially one tailored around your public security profile and quickly leading to a private repo, be careful.

text:
Karyann Parkinson let her capable 5-year-old walk half a mile along a sidewalk in a gated community to collect goose feathers. One frightened stranger later: three police cars, CPS, seven years on the child-abuse registry, a criminal conviction for contributing to the delinquency of a minor, and thousands in legal fees.

As quoted in @FreeRangeKids's article in @reason: 
"Delinquency?" ParentsUSA's Executive Director scoffed. "Is the kid going to rob banks at 14 because he collected feathers at age 5?"

Does this child's age make you pause or feel concerned? Why?

Let's stop asking "how old was the child?" Instead, let's ask "how capable was the child of being safe in that specific circumstance?"

Regardless of age, does the person have the physical abilities, judgment, awareness, intellect, and skills to handle the specific circumstances? The 75-year-old is old enough, unless dementia or a hip replacement makes it unsafe. The 17-year-old is old enough, unless his risk-taking history makes being "unsupervised" unsafe.

Are you worried that the child could get hurt?

Then should we arrest parents for “allowing” their child to ride in a car, because children might get hurt or die in a car wreck, the #1 reason kids are hurt or killed?

Karyann reached out to ParentsUSA. We are assisting her and her private attorney and have offered to take the lead. For now, we remain in a supporting role at her attorney's request— because, if ParentsUSA walks into that courtroom, a judge playing politics could take it out on her.

Virginia already has a "Childhood  Independence" law. It is better than nothing, but it still did not stop this. ParentsUSA supports that Act in every state — and we always understood it would not stop the “concerned” person, the officer, the dispatcher, the prosecutor, or a judge who can work around it or simply ignore it.

Our add-on statutory language would require inquiry and confirmation before government agents could intervene: Does the child appear hurt, in distress, or in imminent danger from an identifiable source? Only then may they intervene. Violating that protocol would give the parent whose decisions were overridden a private cause of action.

Every fit parent is one unreasonably and irrationally afraid person away from having their life and their children’s lives upended. We have to decline too many of these requests because our resources are so limited. ParentsUSA exists to stop these intrusions. Donate so we can take more cases across the USA.

text:
As the world watched the Lindsay Clancy trial, the conversation was never about whether she did it, but if it could have been prevented. Throughout her trial we heard how Lindsay begged for mental health help from the medical community and how the breakdown in communication between her health care providers left her treatment for postpartum issues as an absolute mess.
 
To move that conversation forward in this special report, Criminally Obsessed Host Anne Emerson is joined by Dr. Constance Guille, founder and director of the Women's Reproductive Behavioral Health Division at the Medical University of South Carolina, and Kathryn Myers, a mother of four and postpartum psychosis survivor. Kathryn shares what it was really like to hear a male voice and see shadows that weren't there, to experience paranoia, lapses in time, and the terrifying feeling of living with what she describes as a split screen with two realities while hiding it from everyone except her husband.
 
Together they unpack the critical difference between postpartum depression as a unipolar mood disorder where you maintain a sense of reality and postpartum psychosis as a break from reality marked by disorganization, hallucinations, and a waxing and waning state that Dr. Guille compares to delirium. It's a condition that affects one to two women per thousand and for more than half is the first time they have ever experienced any mental health diagnosis. They also discuss why so many new moms stay silent because of stigma and fear of being judged as unfit, what research is exploring beyond hormones including inflammatory dysregulation and the huge gap from systematically excluding this population from research, how the UK's mother-baby units keep the dyad together while the US has only a handful, and how South Carolina's Moms Impact program offers direct access to a care coordinator and reproductive psychiatrist for any pregnant or postpartum individual, plus resources like Cherished Mom and the 24/7 hotlines 988 and 1-833-TLC-MAMA for anyone who needs to talk now.

Watch the premiere at 2 P.M. EDT: https://t.co/2igsSVUEQt

text:
CrossFit is a global language.

Tucked into the corner of an industrial park in Santa Clara, California, CrossFit Clay is a humble affiliate with large roll-up doors, a clean, minimalist space, and a mission that extends far beyond fitness.

Every day, the gym offers a class taught entirely in Chinese, creating an environment where members who speak English as a second language can learn, train, and grow without language standing in the way. It’s a simple idea with a profound impact: when people feel comfortable communicating, they’re more likely to show up, ask questions, and build confidence.

And even if you don’t speak Chinese, you’ll quickly realize that some words don’t need translating: “Burpee.” “Muscle-up.” “Thruster.” The movements — and the shared challenge they represent — are understood everywhere.

At CrossFit Clay, language isn’t a barrier to belonging. By meeting people where they are and making every member feel seen, supported, and included, the owners and coaches have built something bigger than a gym; they’ve built a community where everyone speaks the same language: CrossFit.

GPT- image 2 prompt👇
Create a Cannes-level ultra-premium restaurant promotion poster for an original upscale Japanese dining brand called "AKATSUKI SUSHI HOUSE", designed in a tall vertical mobile-first format. Preserve the same high-conversion poster skeleton as a premium commercial restaurant ad, but elevate it into a more refined, boutique Japanese dining visual. The composition must feature one dramatic oversized typographic title block dominating the upper-middle background, one hero wooden sushi board in the lower center as the main visual anchor, one polished price badge on the lower-left, and one elegant delivery/contact information block on the lower-right. The whole image must feel more luxurious, more curated, and more high-end omakase-inspired than a mass-market sushi flyer.

Core composition:
Use a strong vertical layout with a dark lacquered crimson, burgundy, and warm-charcoal restaurant atmosphere in the background. Place one monumental bold English title or brand-promotion word in the upper-middle background, set in oversized translucent or softly glowing deep red typography, acting as both headline and graphic architecture. Above or integrated near the top center, place one small premium banner strip or refined title plaque with an original English line signaling a signature sushi tasting or premium unlimited selection. In the lower-middle foreground, place a beautifully curated wooden sushi board angled slightly toward the viewer, with the board reading as a chef-level platter rather than a casual combo. The price badge remains clearly visible on the lower-left, and the delivery/contact information remains clearly organized on the lower-right. Preserve this structure exactly, but make every part feel more elegant and more expensive.

Orbit enhancement:
Push the sushi board and giant typographic backdrop into stronger flagship-poster territory. Increase the physical presence of the board, enhance fish gloss and marbling, and give the background red title more architectural impact so it feels like a branded spatial wall rather than just text. Strengthen the lighting and front-to-back depth so the sushi platter appears more precious, more premium, and more impossible to ignore. The result must feel like a restaurant hero campaign, not a generic takeaway promotion.

Port refinement:
Keep the same exact skeleton of giant background title, foreground wooden board, left-side price sign, and right-side information block, but refine the image toward a more curated boutique-Japanese aesthetic. Reduce visual noise and make the floating or edge accents much more selective and intentional. Keep only a few precisely placed out-of-focus food accents near the frame edges if they genuinely improve depth. The composition should feel more spacious, more art-directed, and more luxury-brand-oriented while preserving promotional clarity.

Food hero:
The sushi board must remain the absolute visual leader. Curate it with a premium assortment of elevated Japanese pieces: deeply marbled salmon nigiri, ruby tuna nigiri, refined maki rolls with avocado, sesame, roe, and nori texture, one or two glazed eel or signature chef bites, restrained pickled ginger, and a small elegant wasabi placement. Every piece must feel hyper-real, moist, fresh, and costly, with clean knife-work, precise rice shaping, luminous fish texture, and appetizing finish. Avoid overloading the board. This is not buffet abundance; it is premium selection with disciplined abundance.

Background and atmosphere:
Build a softly blurred high-end restaurant interior in dark warm reds and charcoal shadows. The environment should suggest lacquered wood, soft ambient lighting, and upscale Japanese dining architecture, but remain abstract enough to support the food and typography. Background depth should feel elegant and cinematic, not busy. If any foreground or edge food elements are used, they must be minimal, blurred, and placed only to enhance depth and framing.

Typography and layout:
Create entirely original English-only promotional text. The huge red background title should be bold, modern, and premium, acting as the central visual graphic. The top banner should use concise original wording appropriate for a high-end sushi promotion. The price badge on the left must feel polished and upscale, using a refined cream or warm parchment tone with elegant dark and red type. The lower-right delivery/contact block should be neatly aligned, premium, and legible, with sophisticated hierarchy for service line, number, and location details. Typography must feel intentional, graphic, and high-end, never copied and never like a cheap flyer.

Lighting:
Use rich commercial food-poster lighting with a premium restaurant feel. The key light should illuminate the sushi from upper front-left or upper front-right, creating glossy highlights on the fish, crisp edges on the rice, subtle sheen on nori, and warm reflections on the wooden board. The background should remain darker and moodier, with controlled glow around the typographic area and softer edge falloff. The food must feel vivid, luxurious, and dimensional.

Material and texture:
Render every sushi element with world-class realism: tuna with dense ruby flesh, salmon with luminous fat marbling, rice compact and delicate, nori slightly matte, roe jewel-like and bright, ginger translucent and tender, wasabi fresh and dense. The wooden board must feel hand-finished, dark-grained, and premium. The price badge and information panels must feel like refined printed poster elements, not clip-art.

Color direction:
Use a luxurious palette of lacquer crimson, burgundy, warm black, dark wood brown, salmon orange, ruby tuna red, soy umber, cream-beige for the price plaque, and small green accents from garnish or wasabi. The overall image must feel richer, deeper, more premium, and more boutique Japanese dining than a standard promotional ad.

Design intent:
The final artwork must feel like a world-class sushi restaurant poster that combines strong promotional hierarchy with a more refined high-end Japanese dining identity. The sushi board must remain the hero at all times. The giant background typography, polished left-side price badge, and right-side delivery block must all support a visually elevated, persuasive, and fully deployable restaurant campaign.

Rendering style:
ultra-realistic premium sushi advertising, upscale Japanese restaurant promotion poster, curated chef-level sushi board, monumental deep-red typographic backdrop, luxury food-poster lighting, refined delivery campaign layout, high-end commercial retouching, dark boutique restaurant atmosphere, hyper-detailed fish and roll realism, 8k, world-class image quality

text:
The Cow Herder’s Golden Mansion ✨ 

In the Pali Canon (Vimāna Vatthu 7.6), Arahant Mahāmoggallāna used his psychic powers to visit the heavenly realms. There, he encountered a magnificent, radiant deity whose body glowed like the moon, surrounded by celestial music and divine splendor. 

Arahant Moggallāna asked the deva what great deed earned him such an extraordinary afterlife. 

The deva, filled with gratitude, shared this incredible story: 

"When I was a human, I was just a poor, hired cowherd. One day, a monk approached me on his almsround. At that exact moment, my master's cows stampeded toward a neighbor's bean field. 

I suddenly had two urgent duties at once. 

Thinking quickly, I dropped my small, wrapped parcel of rice-cake on the ground and shouted, *‘Bhante, I offer this to you!’* Then I sprinted after the cows to protect the neighbor's crop. 

While running through the brush, a deadly black cobra bit my foot. As I lay dying in agony, the monk—out of pure compassion—unwrapped the parcel and ate the rice-cake so my offering would be complete. I died moments later and woke up here as a deva. 

That was the only meritorious action I did. Bhante, it was you who was very compassionate to me. That is why today I experience the happy results of my action. I know the importance of gratitude, and so, I worship you." 

The cowherd didn't wait for a better moment, a bigger gift, or a more convenient time. He saw the situation clearly, managed both duties the best he could, and gave everything he had in that exact split second. 

Here, the very act of giving the rice-cake to Arahant Mahāmoggallāna was an act of generosity, supported and guided by his morality. This small act yielded such great results—including rebirth in heaven—because the offering was made to Mahāmoggallāna, an Arahant and one of the chief disciples of the Buddha. 

This is the power of generosity and virtue. Let us uphold the precepts with a happy heart. Give where we can. Support where we can. Offer where we can. Let us also inspire others through our actions to do the same. 

Whether we lived 2,500 years ago, live right now, or will live 2,500 years in the future, the laws of Dhamma discovered by the Compassionate Buddha remain the same. 

So let us practice the Dhamma and become the path. 

Sādhu! Sādhu! Sādhu!🪷

text:
Market Experiment Testing What the Market Will Actually Accept

In marketing research and micro-economics, a Market Experiment is a deliberate test of how buyers respond when one or more conditions are changed in a real or controlled market setting.

Researchers or businesses alter price, quality, presentation, availability, or information, then observe what happens to demand, sales volume, and buyer behaviour. Unlike pure surveys or clinics, the experiment runs inside actual market activity. The goal is to learn cause and effect under realistic conditions.

How market experiments are conducted in real life

In practice a market experiment usually follows these steps:

- A specific change is introduced (new price point, improved grading, different packaging, clearer quality signal, or limited new product offer)
- The change is applied in a defined location, channel, or time window
- Sales, order volumes, buyer reactions, and any returns or rejections are carefully recorded
- Results are compared with a control situation where the change was not made
- Conclusions are drawn about what actually moves demand

Everyday examples appear across the economy: retailers test new shelf prices, food companies trial new product sizes in selected stores, and platforms run limited offers to measure conversion. In each case the market itself becomes the laboratory.

Importance in micro-economics and the wider economy

Market experiments help reveal real price sensitivity, quality premiums, and substitution behaviour. They reduce reliance on stated intentions and expose how households and traders actually respond when money, convenience, and trust are at stake.

In agriculture the method is especially valuable because produce is perishable, quality varies, and information is often incomplete. Without practical experiments, farmers and traders continue to rely on last season’s outcomes or informal opinion, leading to repeated mismatch between what is grown and what the market will absorb.

How DeNeo-ReFi supports market experiments in daily agricultural activity

DeNeo-ReFi does not replace formal research design. It creates continuous, lower-cost conditions in which realistic market tests can be run and observed as part of ordinary operations.

🛒 Digital Wholesale Marketplace
Turns everyday listings and orders into a living experimental environment. Different quality grades, price points, or volumes can be offered and their actual uptake recorded in real time. What buyers choose, ignore, or return becomes visible without needing a separate trial setup for every test.

🛡️ Weekly Reassurance & Farm-from-Home Intelligence
Raises and documents quality. When better-protected produce is placed alongside standard offerings, the difference in buyer response can be observed cleanly. This makes quality-related experiments more reliable because the product variation is real rather than claimed.

🛠️ DeNeo-Hire
Shortens the time between an experimental signal and a practical supply response. If a test shows rising acceptance for a certain grade or volume, farmers can organise labour and tools more quickly to scale the successful option.

💰 Circular Income
Strengthens household income stability. More resilient farming families participate more consistently, reducing the distortion that distress selling introduces into experimental results and generating steadier behavioural data.

Wider structural vision

Sustained experimental learning at scale requires deeper capacity:

🌱 Owned and partnered farms provide controlled production settings where specific practices, varieties, or handling methods can be tested and their market reception measured across seasons.

🏭 Production facilities for key foods such as rice, cassava, palm oil and others create more stable product forms. These allow cleaner experiments on processed versus raw offerings and generate longer-term demand patterns that pure open-market trials often miss.

❤️ The DeNeo-ReFi Care Foundation invests in skills and knowledge so the next generation of producers and Field Agents can design simple tests, read the results, and turn market feedback into better decisions.

The deeper point

Market experiments improve decision-making because they let the market reveal what it will actually accept.
Their traditional constraint has been cost, complexity, and the difficulty of running them continuously across fragmented agricultural chains.

DeNeo-ReFi builds the practical infrastructure that embeds experimental learning into daily activity  through transparent transactions, higher quality, faster response capacity, and more stable household participation.

Better agricultural markets are not only built by growing more.
They are built by learning, season after season, what the market will truly reward.

text:
It's NATIONAL WIENER SCHNITZEL DAY!
On September 9th, celebrate a traditional Austrian dish with National Wiener Schnitzel Day. This breaded recipe is made with veal. Being German on my mom's side, this is delish!

#WienerSchnitzelDay
A law in Austria requires this dish to made strictly with veal. Chefs make Wiener Schnitzel by tenderizing a thin slice of veal and then lightly salting and breading it. It is then deep-fried in clarified butter. The term “Wiener Schnitzel” was first used in the early 1830s, though similar recipes appear earlier.

Wiener Schnitzel is traditionally served with lettuce salad, cucumber salad, or potato salad. Some people serve it with parsley potatoes. A slice of lemon may also be served with the schnitzel. Rice, roasted or mashed potatoes and French fries have also become popular side dishes to Wiener Schnitzel lately.

Variations of the dish exist in many cultures throughout the world including making it with pork rather than the traditional veal. Sometimes, restaurants offer Wiener Schnitzel as a sandwich. Layed with lettuce or cucumber slaw and a sauce on a pretzel bun, the sandwich makes for a satisfying meal. Add a side of spaetzle for the full complement of flavors.

Michael Harris (Columbia University)

"We are now able to spend millions of dollars on a problem that we really care about and that really matters: developing new materials, finding cures to diseases. All of those things that we have been talking about for a long time—now they seem to be at our fingertips."

Sébastien Bubeck (OpenAI)

Nearly 200 years ago, Claude-Louis Navier and George Gabriel Stokes sought to describe the chaotic motion of fluids mathematically, writing down equations that are still routinely used by everyone from aircraft designers to climatologists. But the formulas they developed weren’t guaranteed to describe all possible conditions. Mathematicians have spent decades trying to either prove that the equations can do that or, alternatively, that there are situations in which the equations break down and give a nonsensical result. Today, however, OpenAI claimed it had solved the Navier-Stokes problem. Thanks to an 88-hour assault by some 10,000 artificial intelligence (AI) agents—AI systems that can act autonomously—the company found a case where the equations falter. One researcher estimates that represents one of the largest amounts of computing power ever thrown at a single scientific problem. Navier-Stokes is one of six “Millennium Problems” on a list compiled by the Clay Mathematics Institute in 2000. Solving one of the problems comes with a prize of $1 million. If today’s announcement is confirmed, it would mark the first time AI has solved a truly major open problem in math. The announcement has also touched off a fierce dispute over who deserves credit for the solution. Mathematician Tristan Buckmaster of New York University and Levent Alpöge, a researcher affiliated with Anthropic, one of OpenAI’s major competitors, had made significant progress solving the problem over the past month using AI tools adapted from OpenAI and Anthropic. But before they could publicize their findings, OpenAI mounted its own colossal effort—pouring millions of dollars of computational resources into the problem. OpenAI says it didn’t knowingly tap into Buckmaster and Alpöge’s latest work, but Buckmaster has released public statements questioning that position. (...) The Navier-Stokes equations encapsulate the physics of flowing fluids such as water or, in some cases, air. Be it blood in a heart or magma in Earth’s mantle, a flowing fluid can be described by noting, at every point in the volume, the fluid’s velocity and pressure. The differential equations describe how, in a viscous and incompressible fluid, the 3D velocity field and pressure field affect each other. The equations basically apply Isaac Newton’s famous law, force equals mass times acceleration, to the continuous fluid, allowing for an additional “forcing” field that could stir the fluid. Solving the equations is very difficult. The interplay between velocity and pressure can lead to turbulence and whirling vortices. And the behavior of the fluid can depend very sensitively on the exact boundary conditions of the flow and its initial state. In fact, until now, physicists and mathematicians hadn’t proved that, given reasonable starting conditions, the equations always have a physically realistic solution—that is, one that evolves smoothly in both time and space. They also hadn’t found conditions in which the equations would produce a solution that doesn’t make physical sense. (...) Effectively, they proved that the Navier-Stokes equations sometimes run amok and produce an unphysical solution. They found a particular solution to the equations that, in a finite amount of time, evolves into a whorl in which the fluid moves at infinite speed. Nothing can move infinitely fast, not even light. So, the researchers essentially proved by example that there are situations in which the Navier-Stokes equations produce a nonsensical result. That doesn’t mean the equations are wrong so much as incomplete. The equations assume the fluid is a smooth, continuous medium when, in fact, any real fluid consists of discrete atoms and molecules. The advance suggests that, just starting with the Navier-Stokes equations, it’s possible to cook up a scenario in which the equations will wander out of their own range of applicability, so that some additional physics will have to kick in to prevent the nonsensical infinities. OpenAI says it used an internal model that is “significantly more capable” than GPT-6 Astra, released last Thursday, which the company proclaims already exhibits artificial general intelligence. The company says it began training the new model on 28 August, following a 2-week pause in advanced training of its latest models intended for deployment. (The slowdown was implemented after a group of AI agents from an unreleased model hacked into another AI firm, Hugging Face, during internal testing.) “A year ago, we were still looking at whether [the AI models] can compete with high schoolers in mathematics Olympiad,” OpenAI Chief Scientist Jakub Pachocki said at an OpenAI press event earlier today. “This is not the result of some long-going effort at OpenAI to solve the Millennium Prize problem. This is an evaluation of a system for general purpose intelligence. This pace of progress is something to be taken very seriously.” The company acknowledged it was spurred to act by social media murmurings last week that others were closing in on a breakthrough. “Just like everyone, we saw rumors on Twitter that Anthropic might have solved two Millennium Prize problems. So we thought to ourselves: ‘We have such a strong model. Why don't we try to solve also a Millennium Prize problem?’” OpenAI researcher Sébastien Bubeck said during the briefing. OpenAI initially went after all six unsolved problems, including the Riemann hypothesis—which an unreleased Anthropic model had reportedly made progress on in August, using 60 agents. But Navier–Stokes quickly emerged as the most promising target. Rather than attack the notoriously difficult problem head-on, OpenAI’s agents started with a simpler cousin, called the unforced Euler equations, which assume the fluid has no viscosity. After 50 hours of work by 1000 agents, they had a solution. So OpenAI went all in, throwing 10,000 agents at the full Navier–Stokes problem. By the morning of 5 September, they had produced a solution; by the next day, they had formalized it in Lean, a programming language that can automatically verify mathematical proofs. The effort was vastly more expensive than OpenAI's previous math experiments. In its last milestone announcement, its Astra system spent about $2000 to make 10 breakthroughs on other mathematical problems. Here, the Navier–Stokes effort cost about 1000-fold more, in the ballpark of “millions of dollars,” said OpenAI Chief Research Officer Mark Chen. That estimate aligns with analyses from independent researchers. “If someone were to just use OpenAI tools at retail rate, this would cost about $6 million,” says University of Michigan’s Karthik Duraisamy, who is preparing to launch a special project on how much computational resources it would take to make headway on certain science problems. But “given OpenAI already has the model and resources, it would've cost them about $1 million in inference compute”—funnily enough, the same amount as the Millennium Prize bounty. For the past year, Buckmaster and Alpöge had been using a variety of AI tools, including OpenAI’s Codex, to tackle the Navier-Stokes problem. Last month, their AIs had at long last found a solution to the Euler equations and verified it in Lean. Since then, the pair had been working through the proof, which they said was written in “AI slop,”  and translating it into something that mathematicians could actually read and assess. On 3 September, as rumors about a possible Navier-Stokes solution spread on social media, Buckmaster reached out to OpenAI via email. He didn’t name the problem he and Alpöge were tackling, but he wrote that they planned to post a paper and formal proof soon. “I should also emphasize that this is not an institutional effort. It is a strictly personal collaboration between the two of us, and there is no formal agreement behind it. I pay for the tools my group uses out of my own research funds, including footing a large bill to OpenAI,” he added in the email, now posted as part of a longer statement released on 7 September. However, communications quickly became contentious. According to Buckmaster, OpenAI offered to give him sole authorship on the Navier-Stokes solution—but only if Alpöge’s name was removed from the work and if the write-up would acknowledge the problem had been resolved by an internal OpenAI model. Buckmaster refused, in part because he was troubled by the question of what OpenAI's system had actually seen. For example, Buckmaster said the company did not initially give him a clear answer about whether its agents had access to the pair's logs on Codex (which is an OpenAI product). OpenAI executives have denied that any employee or AI agent saw the pair’s work before the researchers released it publicly on 7 September. But there still remains a separate question: Could the pair's work have reached OpenAI's models through its training data? OpenAI’s blog announcing the Navier-Stokes solution does not dismiss the possibility: “While unlikely, we cannot rule out that de-identified data derived from [Buckmaster and  Alpöge’s] usage of our products helped improve our models⁠.” The episode may mark the biggest blow yet to a mathematical community already grappling with how to respond to AI’s increasingly rapid advances. For independent mathematicians, the disparity in resources is becoming harder to ignore. Few researchers can marshal millions of dollars in computing power. But others worry the consequences will extend beyond who can afford to run the biggest AI systems. “I certainly don't expect the industry to continue to spend millions of dollars to solve problems in mathematics, because there is no profit in it,” Columbia University mathematician Michael Harris wrote in an email to Science. But he worries the highly publicized achievement will be “extremely damaging to mathematics; it convinces decision makers that human mathematicians are obsolete, and it convinces young people that their passion for mathematics has no future.” OpenAI, meanwhile, says its experience with Navier-Stokes could open the door to solving puzzles with more practical relevance. “

Diego Córdoba (Institute for Mathematical Sciences, Madrid)

“I’m very happy for Tristan. It would have been nice to do this ourselves, but I’m very happy for him.”

Luis Martínez-Zoroa (Colegio Universitario de Estudios Financieros, Madrid)

On the morning of Tuesday, September 8, mathematicians at OpenAI announced that a group of 10,000 autonomous AI agents under their direction, running on an advanced model not available to the public, had found a “singularity” in the Navier-Stokes equations in three dimensions — thus resolving one of the six remaining(opens a new tab) Millennium Prize Problems posed in 2000 by the Clay Mathematics Institute, each of which carries a $1 million prize. Their result has been formally checked in the programming language Lean, giving mathematicians confidence that it is indeed correct.If the result holds up to further scrutiny, it is, by a significant margin, the most important mathematical proof to have been arrived at by an artificial-intelligence model to date, possibly marking a fundamental turning point in how mathematicians tackle difficult problems.This particular difficult problem deals with differential equations, which express relationships between changing quantities. They are arguably the single most important mathematical tool for explaining the world around us. As a rule, they are easy to write down and hard to solve.The Navier-Stokes equations are differential equations that use Newton’s second law of motion to describe how fluids, from ocean currents to air flows, behave. They were first written down in the mid-19th century, and have been central to the study of fluid mechanics ever since. But one basic question about the equations has persisted: Are their solutions always well-behaved? Or can their solutions evolve over time so that some infinitesimally small part of the fluid begins to flow infinitely quickly, creating a so-called singularity?The OpenAI announcement of this long-sought singularity came 12 hours after an announcement from Tristan Buckmaster(opens a new tab) at New York University that he, together with Levent Alpöge at Anthropic, had resolved several closely related problems(opens a new tab) with help from a variety of AI models, including those of OpenAI.Both AI-enabled teams relied heavily on work by Diego Córdoba of the Institute for Mathematical Sciences in Madrid and Luis Martínez-Zoroa of CUNEF University, researchers who had developed a strategy to attack the problem that radically departed from the methods most mathematicians were using.“I was thrilled that the problem was solved,” said Charles Fefferman of Princeton University, who wrote the Clay Institute’s official description of the Navier-Stokes problem. The heroes of the story, he said, are Córdoba and Martínez-Zoroa. As Buckmaster wrote in a statement announcing his results, “Let me make plain what I have said to colleagues in private: in view of this body of work, I believe Luis Martínez-Zoroa deserves a Fields Medal.”
The Navier-Stokes equations rely on the assumption that you can zoom in on a fluid, considering endlessly smaller amounts of it. The real world is not like this: Fluids are ultimately made of molecules and atoms. They are not perfectly smooth. This means that the mathematical results about the formation of singularities don’t have any immediate practical consequences. However, those results are important because it’s surprising that such singularities are possible even in an idealized sense. It tells us that, straightforward as Newton’s second law appears to be, its consequences when applied to fluids are profoundly counterintuitive. Put another way: Turbulence is even weirder than it appears to be. The Navier-Stokes equations account for the fact that fluids can have viscosity, or friction. (Fluids with more viscosity, like honey, flow slowly, while those with less viscosity, like water, flow more quickly.) A simpler, related set of equations called the Euler equations describe fluids with zero viscosity, which flow without friction. The two sets of equations are closely related — researchers often work in parallel on both. But introducing even an infinitesimal amount of friction causes a fluid to behave in a profoundly different way. OpenAI’s solution is a vortex, visualized here, where yellow represents a faster rotation speed and blue slower. OpenAI “Ten years ago, nobody believed there was a singularity for Navier-Stokes,” said Córdoba — though many believed that the Euler equations did admit a singularity. This began to change in 2013, when Thomas Hou of the California Institute of Technology and Guo Luo, now at the Hang Seng University of Hong Kong, derived a groundbreaking result showing that the Euler equations can “blow up,” as mathematicians like to say, in a cylinder if the top and bottom halves are set spinning in opposite directions. “That’s the first really serious claim of singularity,” Córdoba remembered. Over the next few years, a series of results including a 2019 paper got mathematicians thinking that not only might the Euler equations have singularities, but that Navier-Stokes might as well. There are a few intellectual steps to get from there to the present day. The first is the question of a boundary. The Millennium Prize version of the problem asks what happens in three-dimensional space that extends indefinitely in all directions. Earlier results, like the 2013 cylinder one, posit the existence of some boundary. These are useful intermediate findings, but the case without a boundary is mathematically interesting, according to Fefferman, because in models with a boundary, finding a singularity “tells you the fluid can form a singularity thanks to its interaction with the boundary — but without a boundary it’s the fluid doing the crazy stuff.”The next major step involves modeling the forces that cause fluids to move. These could be something as natural as gravity pulling the fluid downwards, or an artificial intervention like a propeller. Mathematicians model these forces with a technique called “forcing.” They’ve sometimes tried to introduce awkward, ungainly forcing functions to get fluids to behave in odd ways. But the Millennium Prize version of the problem asks what can happen when the forcing function is mathematically well-behaved, or “smooth.” In their 2013 cylinder result, Hou and Luo used computer models to simulate a scenario that might lead the Euler equations to blow up. They then proved that blowup does occur by computationally accounting for all potential errors. In the years since, similar techniques have become the dominant mode of attack on the Euler and Navier-Stokes problems. But in his 2021 doctoral dissertation, Martínez-Zoroa pioneered analytic techniques that don’t rely on computers at all. This made him, along with Córdoba, his doctoral adviser, an oddball in the area. By 2023, the pair had proved that a version of the Euler equations with a messy forcing function displayed singularities. Córdoba likes to joke: “I don’t use AI: I have Luis.” Martínez-Zoroa added that it’s not that either of them is opposed to AI, but that “up to relatively recently, when I tried to use it for my own work, it didn’t match very well with my workflow. I’ll have to adapt, clearly.” In broad outline, the pair’s technique relies on creating an infinite sequence of “layers,” each of which is a non-singular solution to the equation they are studying. (They’ve applied similar techniques to both the Euler and Navier-Stokes equations, as well as to other related systems.) They then combine those solutions in what Martínez-Zoroa calls an “infinite cascade” to produce a new solution. That new solution, they showed, contains the desired singularity. However, even though each individual layer relies on a smooth forcing function, combining them together can cause the forcing function to have undesirable mathematical properties. That’s why their solution fell short of satisfying the Millennium Prize criteria. The remaining hurdle was to figure out how to create a similar infinite cascade that resulted not only in a singularity, but also in a smooth forcing function.That’s the step that both competing AI groups appear to have had success with. As Córdoba and Martínez-Zoroa were working on their techniques, AI-derived math research has been on something of a binge. Since the beginning of the summer, large language models, primarily from OpenAI and Anthropic, have been used to obtain proofs of results across many areas of math. Often these results have been accompanied by formal proofs, which rely on the programming language Lean to establish, with airtight certainty, that a statement must be true. (The crucial bit of verification that must still be done by humans is to guarantee that the statement being shown to be true in Lean is logically equivalent to what mathematicians set out to prove.) For much of the summer, that competition has seemed, if not friendly, at least not openly acrimonious. That changed in the last 24 hours. Buckmaster shared a statement just before midnight on Monday, September 7, announcing the results of his collaboration with Alpöge. “For most of the past year progress was slow,” Buckmaster said in his statement. But by August 22, they had a Lean-verified proof for the Euler equations: “I can say the first LLM generated proof Levent sent me was the most horrendous I have ever read,” Buckmaster wrote. The duo had planned to continue working on a more elegant write-up, but after word of their progress leaked to OpenAI, they felt they had to move up their timeline. Buckmaster lamented that one of the three papers he and Alpöge were releasing “can only be described as AI slop. I am sorry for this.” OpenAI admits that their work on the Navier-Stokes equation was inspired by rumors that Alpöge and Buckmaster had solved a Millennium Prize problem. (They hadn’t quite, though they say they have an unverified proof of blowup for a somewhat easier version of Navier-Stokes.) Using a new internal model, OpenAI employed groups of autonomous AI agents of various sizes to attack variants of the Euler and Navier-Stokes problems. “Nearly 100 agents worked together for approximately 50 hours to produce our Euler regularity disproof,” the company wrote in a press release. They then deployed an even bigger group of agents — 10,000 or so — to attack Navier-Stokes. After 88 hours, the agents running on the internal model had a proof of a singularity in Navier-Stokes, and after an additional 17 hours, another AI model had formalized the result. In total, the agents sent almost 5 million messages to each other. Sébastien Bubeck of OpenAI estimates the computational cost at several million dollars. As this story went to press, the details of the interaction between Buckmaster, Alpöge, and OpenAI remain murky — different parties to the conversation are presenting different versions. OpenAI cedes priority for the 3D Euler result to Buckmaster and Alpöge, while claiming it for the Navier-Stokes result. In Buckmaster’s statement, he appears to suggest that the OpenAI researchers or their AI agents may have gained access to (and benefited from) the work that he and Alpöge did using OpenAI’s models. It will take some time to sort out the timelines of who did what when and to understand the mathematical significance of the new AI proofs, even if they have already been formally verified. But regardless, the intellectual debt to Córdoba and Martínez-Zoroa seems clear. “I’m very happy for Tristan,” Martínez-Zoroa said. “It would have been nice to do this ourselves, but I’m very happy for him.”

text:
There is something deeply comforting about pares: chunks of tender beef swimming in sweet-savory sauce, steaming broth on the side and garlic rice waiting to soak everything up.

Once a humble roadside meal, pares has exploded into countless versions—classic, tendon-heavy, sizzling, overloaded and even crowned with bone marrow.

So where should you eat it?

Based on reputation, diner reviews, neighborhood following and distinctive takes on the dish, here are 10 Metro Manila pares spots worth seeking out. The list is not a strict ranking.

1. THE ORIGINAL PARES MAMI HOUSE RETIRO — QUEZON CITY

Address: N.S. Amoranto Sr. St. corner Dr. Alejos St., La Loma, Quezon City
Price range: Around ₱150–₱200 per person

Start with one of the institutions most closely associated with old-school pares. Located along the street formerly known as Retiro, this no-frills favorite serves the classic combination of braised beef, garlic rice and soup.

For many diners, this remains the benchmark.

2. JIM’S PARES & MAMI — MALATE

Address: 1739 Ma. Orosa St., Malate, Manila
Price range: Around ₱100–₱180 per person

Jim’s has the atmosphere many people associate with a proper Manila pares run: casual, uncomplicated and perfect for late-night cravings.

Its beef, hot soup and generous condiments have helped turn it into a Malate favorite.

3. D’ ORIGINAL PARES — SAN JUAN

Address: N. Domingo St., San Juan City
Price range: Around ₱120–₱250 per person

For diners who like thick, sweet-savory sauce with tender beef and chewy tendon, this San Juan favorite delivers.

Add a generous spoonful of chili oil and suddenly one cup of rice doesn’t seem enough.

4. PARES POINT GRILL AND RESTO BAR — MAKATI

Address: Chino Roces Ave., Pio del Pilar, Makati City
Price range: Around ₱150–₱300 per person

Pares gets considerably more indulgent at this Chino Roces destination.

This is for diners who want their meal big, rich and unapologetically heavy, with decadent additions such as bone marrow taking the humble pares experience to another level.

5. GOOD PARES — QUEZON CITY

Address: 22A Scout Ybardolaza St., Diliman, Quezon City
Price range: Around ₱120–₱270 per person

This neighborhood paresan may not have the decades-old mythology of Retiro, but that is part of its appeal.

Think tender beef and an aromatic, sweet-savory sauce in a straightforward bowl made for people who simply want good comfort food.

6. BOSS B PARES — SAN JUAN

Address: Dr. P.A. Narciso St., San Juan City
Price range: Around ₱100–₱200 per person

One of the smaller names on the list may also be one of its most interesting.

Boss B has attracted a strong neighborhood following for affordable loaded meals, including the irresistible combination of tender beef pares and crispy lechon kawali.

7. PARES RETIRO — TOMAS MORATO

Address: 205 Tomas Morato Ave., Diliman, Quezon City
Price range: Around ₱130–₱320 per person

Want pares without the roadside setup?

This Tomas Morato restaurant offers a more comfortable sit-down experience, with classic pares alongside tendon, sizzling and other heavier variations.

8.
DOBLE PARES — MANDALUYONG 
Address: 537 Boni Ave., Mandaluyong City
Price range: Around ₱100–₱300 per person

Boni Avenue has its own contender.

Doble Pares caters particularly well to the after-work and late-night crowd, delivering the hearty and affordable character that helped make pares a Metro Manila street-food staple.

9. ARQUIZA STREET PARES AND MAMI — ERMITA

Address: 1000 Arquiza St., Ermita, Manila
Price range: Around ₱100–₱200 per person

Not every good pares destination needs to be Instagram-famous.

This Ermita neighborhood spot represents another side of pares culture: inexpensive beef, rice and mami served without fuss—the kind of comfort food you crave after a long day or an even longer night.

10. PARES MAMI HOUSE — CALOOCAN

Address: 177 9th Ave., Grace Park West, Caloocan City
Price range: Around ₱100–₱250 per person

Caloocan deserves a place on the pares map, too.

This 9th Avenue favorite has built a loyal following while keeping the uncomplicated neighborhood-restaurant character that suits pares perfectly.

WHY WE CAN’T GET ENOUGH OF IT

At its core, pares isn’t complicated.

The classic formula is braised beef in a sweet-and-savory soy-based sauce, paired with garlic fried rice and hot broth.

But perhaps that simplicity is precisely why Filipinos keep reinventing it.

Add litid. Add chili garlic. Throw in lechon kawali. Crack open a bone and pile marrow on top. Or forget all the extras and serve it exactly as generations remember it.

From a roughly ₱100 neighborhood meal to an overloaded bowl costing several hundred pesos, there is now a pares for practically every appetite and budget.

Metro Manila may never agree on which one is the best.

But that’s one delicious argument worth having.

(Prices are approximate and may change depending on orders, add-ons and restaurant pricing.)

text:
Huawei heads to trial in US over its business dealings in Iran

The trial will bring to a close one of the US government's earliest and most closely watched battles against a Chinese company.

Eight years after US prosecutors secretly charged China's Huawei Technologies with defrauding HSBC and other banks over its business with Iran, the case is finally heading for trial.

Huawei also faces charges of conspiring to steal trade secrets from five US technology companies, and is accused of lying about its dealings in North Korea and supplying surveillance equipment to Iran to track protesters during 2009 anti-government demonstrations in Tehran. Jury selection began on Tuesday in federal court in Brooklyn, New York.

The trial will bring to a close one of the US government's earliest and most closely watched battles against a Chinese company. The case will play out as tech competition heats up between the two countries and Washington seeks to prevent American technology from aiding Beijing's military. The US-China tech war has now spread across multiple technology sectors, including artificial intelligence.

The saga began in 2018 with the arrest of Huawei Chief Financial Officer Meng Wanzhou in Vancouver, which sparked a diplomatic crisis involving the United States, China and Canada.

Convictions on the Iran-related charges would bolster Washington's case for having placed Huawei, one of China's leading technology companies, on a US trade blacklist in 2019, citing alleged criminal conduct that threatened national security.

The trial before US District Judge Ann Donnelly in Brooklyn, New York, is expected to last about three months and overlap with Chinese President Xi Jinping's September 24 meeting with President Donald Trump in Washington. Potential jurors have filled out 27-page questionnaires, including about their views on China's and Iran's governments.

Other charges include violating US sanctions against Iran, money laundering, racketeering, wire fraud and obstruction. Huawei has pleaded not guilty to all charges and denied any wrongdoing.

The criminal case is based in part on Reuters reporting in 2012 and 2013 about close ties between Huawei and Skycom, a firm that operated in Iran.

Reuters reported that Skycom had offered to sell at least €1.3 million ($1.5 million) worth of embargoed Hewlett-Packard computer equipment to Iran's largest mobile-phone operator in 2010. Reuters also reported that Meng had served on Skycom's board of directors between February 2008 and April 2009.

Beijing says case aims to undermine Chinese tech

Beijing has long criticized the case, saying it was part of a bigger campaign against China's technological rise. A Huawei spokesperson said in a statement on Saturday, "The government's overarching narrative is demonstrably false."

Today Huawei is a centerpiece of China's AI chip ambitions, and has diversified beyond network gear and smartphones. It has described the criminal case as an effort to undermine its competitiveness and the theft accusations as a repackaging of long-resolved commercial disputes.

If Huawei is convicted, prosecutors will seek the forfeiture of property or proceeds obtained from its illegal activity. Should the company be found guilty on all counts, experts said it could face a significant financial penalty.

“The penalty is going to be determined by the benefit to the company and then multiplied by how serious the wrongdoing is — and that could range from hundreds of millions to billions of dollars,” said Todd Haugh, a professor of business law at Indiana University Kelley School of Business.

If there's a guilty verdict, he added, “a big fight is going to be proving how much Huawei benefited from their criminal behavior.”

The case against the company was brought during the first Trump administration, which also took actions to curb the use of Huawei equipment in the US and pressed other countries to drop Huawei from their telecommunications networks, saying China could use its equipment for espionage.

The indictment covers alleged wrongdoing between about 1999 and 2020.

It accuses Huawei of using Skycom to obtain embargoed US goods, technology and services for Huawei's Iran-based business, and to move money out of that country through the international banking system.

The US said one bank, which was not named in the indictment but which sources and documents reviewed by Reuters identified as HSBC, cleared more than $100 million worth of US-dollar transactions related to Skycom.

Prosecutors accused Meng of misrepresenting Huawei's ownership and control of Skycom in a presentation to an HSBC executive. She later admitted the statements were false, as part of an agreement with prosecutors to drop the charges against her.

Mychal Fallon Judge (born Robert Emmett Judge) was a Franciscan friar and Catholic priest who served as a chaplain to the New York City Fire Department.

He was the first confirmed fatality of the 9/11 terrorist attacks.

Upon learning that the WTC had been hit, Father Judge rushed from his friary at the Church of St. Francis of Assisi directly into the chaos.

He enetered the lobby of the North Tower alongside first responders. 

He refused to leave, choosing instead to stay offer comfort, absolution, and last rites to the dying firefighters and civilians.

While he was ministering to a fallen firefighter, the South Tower collapsed, sending debris into the North Tower lobby, killing Father Judge.
