text: 1. He made the border a real border https://t.co/QZ6l1VMqLn a matter of months, Trump reduced illegal border crossings to their lowest level in half a century. Catch-and-release is finished. The wall is going up and even being expanded, “Remain in Mexico” is back, and the Administration reduced releases into the country by an incredible 99.9 percent.  2. He reversed mass migration.America recorded negative net migration in 2025 for the first time in at least half a century. So far, nearly 3 million illegal aliens have left the country, whether voluntarily or involuntarily: more than 675,000 forcibly deported and the rest “self-deported.”   Many of those self-deportations were facilitated by the President’s innovative program to offer plane tickets and cash bonuses for illegals to leave, not only incentivizing good behavior but significantly reducing the cost of deportations. Citizenship and the law actually mean something again.  3. He signed the Laken Riley Act — and required detention of criminal illegal aliens.Named for an innocent girl murdered by an illegal alien, the Laken Riley Act requires federal authorities to detain illegals arrested for theft, burglary, shoplifting, assaulting police, or any crime causing death or serious injury. It also lets states sue officials who refuse to enforce it.  Laken Riley should still be alive. This law will prevent tragedies like hers.  4. History’s biggest drop in violent crime, and the lowest violent crime rate in 126 years.According to FBI data, violent crime in America dropped an incredible 9.7 percent in 2025 — the largest one-year decline in history. Murder fell 18.1 percent, robbery fell 18.5 percent. And America’s violent crime rate is its lowest since 1900.  This is what happens when you put the National Guard on the streets in crime-ridden blue cities: fewer victims, safer streets, and better futures for America’s poorest.  Trump Launched an American Industrial Supercycle 5. He made the 2017 tax cuts permanent…and better.The One Big Beautiful Bill locked in the largest tax cut in modern history, including the doubled standard deduction, the expanded Child Tax Credit, and 100 percent expensing for factories and equipment. It also delivered No Tax on Tips, No Tax on Overtime, an abolition of most taxes on Social Security benefits, and major relief for seniors.  Every Democrat voted no. With the 2017 act set to expire in December 2025, that would have resulted in the largest tax hike in American history.  6. He repealed 129 regulations for every new https://t.co/aUMTymsQZS fiscal 2025, federal agencies finalized 646 deregulatory actions and just five regulatory actions: 129-to-1, and in nearly every case, the “one” was to repeal the others! OIRA says the savings exceeded those of Trump’s entire first term. That is more freedom, lower costs, and less bureaucratic sabotage.  Of these, the crown jewel was the repeal of Obama’s 2009 “Endangerment Finding”, the legal foundation for the Green New Scam’s vehicle mandates. EPA calls it the largest deregulatory action in American history and estimates that by itself, it will save Americans more than $1.3 trillion. Trump also killed the federal EV mandate, restored Americans’ freedom to buy the cars and trucks they actually want, and even eliminated the incentives behind the almost universally hated start-stop button.  7. He secured $18 trillion in announced investment commitments.That’s nearly two-thirds the size of the entire American economy, building American factories, chip plants, data centers, energy projects, steel mills, shipyards, and supply chains employing American workers. Apple, Meta, NVIDIA, Micron, Hyundai, U.S. Steel, Ford, Taiwan Semiconductor, and many corporations and sovereign wealth funds are betting big on Trump’s America.   No President has ever done anything remotely like it. And it’s just getting started.  8. He made “reshoring” and “reindustrialization” real, not a https://t.co/CFx29h5Sap is moving Lincoln production out of China. Toyota is shifting Tacoma production from Mexico to Texas. GM, Honda, Mercedes-Benz, Stellantis, and others are expanding U.S. production. The capital equipment pouring into the country is the machinery that’s building the growing boom.  9. He replaced lopsided trade deals with balanced, reciprocal trade.Trump used tariffs as leverage to reverse 80 years of lopsided trade deals that favored everyone but America, and to win new or improved agreements with trading partners accounting for more than half of global GDP. Those agreements open foreign markets, attack non-tariff barriers, defend strategic industries, and make it more profitable to build in America than to export American jobs.  10. He shifted global energy dominance from the Persian Gulf to the Gulf of America.Once the world’s largest energy importer — “exporting” $700 billion a year to our enemies — America now outproduces Saudi Arabia and Russia combined. The U.S. is also setting new records in oil, natural gas, and LNG exports, becoming the first country ever to export more than 100 million metric tons of LNG in a year.  Trump also opened land, accelerated permits, expanded pipelines and export terminals, and made American energy a tool for prosperity and peace.  11. After four decades of nuclear paralysis, Trump brought five new reactors online in a single year.For more than 40 years, not one new privately developed non-light-water reactor reached criticality in America. Trump ordered at least three by July 4, 2026. DOE delivered four by the deadline, then a fifth just one month later.  Decades of zero. One Trump summer: five. That is a genuine nuclear renaissance.  Trump Made Elections Matter Again 12. He broke the Deep State’s power to defy the elected https://t.co/EPQugoULPR Trump v. Slaughter, the Supreme Court ruled for the first time in 90 years that Article 2, Section 1 is still part of the Constitution: the President may fire subordinate officials in the executive branch, overturning the 1935 precedent that insulated “independent” agencies from voters’ control.  Ever wonder why elections often seem to change nothing? How about one President and 5,000 political appointees vs. 2.8 million unfireable, unaccountable bureaucrats? THAT is the “Deep State”.  Trump then made that victory real. For the first time in a century, all policy-making bureaucrats can now be fired for misconduct, incompetence, or defying lawful directives. The permanent bureaucracy no longer gets to veto the voters.  13. He ended nationwide injunction https://t.co/HhUWBcAQ9w Trump v. CASA, the Supreme Court sharply limited nationwide injunctions. A single, local, district judge should not be able to block a national policy for everyone, everywhere; and yet that’s exactly what they’ve done, nonstop, ever since Trump (and only Trump) took office in 2017.   In restricting that unconstitutional power, the Court kneecapped the Black Robe Bureaucracy’s favorite tool of unlawful judicial supremacy.  14. He shut down USAID as a left-wing slush fund and shadow government.USAID had become a taxpayer-funded machine for exporting abortion, gender ideology, censorship, and left-wing politics. It had a bigger budget than the CIA and the State Department combined, absolutely no accountability whatsoever, and a penchant for overthrowing governments.  Trump terminated it — completely — and moved real humanitarian aid under the State Department. Immediately, seven socialist Latin American governments lost re-election. Coincidence?  15. He shrank Federal employment to its lowest level in 60 years.From a high under Biden, the federal workforce is now its smallest since 1966. Workforce reductions, agency closures, and spending cancellations mean fewer bureaucrats paid to resist the voters.  What’s more, when Biden left office, 94 percent of federal employees “worked” from home. The Trump administration cracked down: as Elon Musk put it, “you can work from the office or you can pretend to work somewhere else.”  16. He expelled DEI from the federal government.Trump eliminated federal DEI offices and barred race- and sex-based preferences across the executive branch. Government hiring and contracting are returning to merit and equality under the law, ending the grotesque Democrat idea that “fighting discrimination” requires the federal government to discriminate.  He Defended Faith and Family 17. He delivered sweeping pro-life https://t.co/gJ4vHpOjKg his first term, Trump delivered the judges that overturned the abominable Roe v. Wade. Hardly anyone believed it could be done, or that Trump would do it. But he did, and a half-century nightmare finally ended.  Since returning to office, Trump has enforced the Hyde Amendment prohibiting the use of federal funds to pay for abortions, reinstated and expanded the Mexico City Policy prohibiting federal funding of foreign abortions, ended federal fetal-tissue research, strengthened conscience protections, protected Medicaid from funding large abortion providers, and pardoned 23 pro-life activists prosecuted by Biden’s weaponized Justice Department.  He’s also done everything within the Executive Branch’s power to defund Planned Parenthood. It would be nice if Congress did likewise.  No President has ever done more to protect life. No one.  18. He got men out of women’s sports, and restored biological reality to federal policy.The United States government once again officially recognizes two sexes: male and female. Trump ended federal support for the chemical and surgical gender mutilation of children, stopped taxpayer funding of such irreversible abominations, and forced more than three dozen health systems to end or suspend their programs as well.  Trump also enforced Title IX as written: women and girls deserve their own teams, trophies, scholarships, and locker rooms. The NCAA and other athletic organizations changed their rules in response. After years of Democrats doing everything they could to destroy women’s sports and ruin girls’ lives, Trump’s administration protects women and girls again.  19. He enacted America’s first nationwide school-choice program — and launched Trump https://t.co/Ck4hoR1HeF part of the President’s One Big Beautiful Bill, Trump enacted America’s first-ever nationwide school choice program. The new Education Freedom Tax Credit helps fund scholarships for tuition, books, and other educational costs.  That’s on top of the new Trump Accounts, which give every child a tax-advantaged stake in America’s future, including a $1,000 federal seed for eligible newborns. Parents gain power. Bureaucracies lose it. And children learn first-hand about free markets and future orientation.  20. He targeted anti-Christian bias and discrimination.Trump created the White House Faith Office, Religious Liberty Commission, and Task Force to Eradicate Anti-Christian Bias. He restored conscience protections and made clear that Christians do not surrender their First Amendment rights merely by entering public life.  He Restored Peace Through Strength and Put America First 21. He forced NATO to stop freeloading and increase defense spending by 250 percent.For decades, wealthy European governments underfunded their militaries, effectively sending America the bill and using American taxpayers to subsidize their bloated welfare states. Trump forced NATO to replace its old two-percent-of-GDP spending target with an enormous five percent by 2035.  Allied spending is rising, American defense orders are soaring, and Europe is becoming a partner instead of a dependent.  22. He drove China out of the Caribbean.China spent years building strategic beachheads at both ends of the Panama Canal, in Cuba, and in Maduro’s Venezuela. Trump forced Panama out of Belt and Road, expanded American security access around the Canal, and captured Maduro, who now sits in a New York jail cell awaiting trial.  Beijing’s planned encirclement of the United States collapsed. The Monroe Doctrine is back. Call it the Donroe Doctrine.  23. He brokered eight peace deals in just eight https://t.co/KKERQ5PW7z eight months, Trump brokered peace in eight conflicts spanning four continents, including wars that had gone on for as much as 40 years. It’s a record unmatched by any other President.  24. He launched and funded Golden Dome, the first-ever true missile defense for the U.S. population.Ronald Reagan dreamed of making nuclear missiles obsolete through his Strategic Defense Initiative. Today, Trump is actually building it: a layered homeland shield with space-based sensors and interceptors, conventional defenses, and new technologies including microwave systems to destroy drone swarms and directed-energy weapons (yes, lasers) that can replace an $11 million missile with $2 of electricity.  Congress has funded the initial $25 billion, with far more on the way once it passes the NDAA this fall. Better a shield than a sword.  25. He restored the warrior ethos — and reversed the recruiting crisis.After years of missed targets under Biden, every active military component met or exceeded its 2025 recruiting goal. Trump and Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth refocused the newly renamed Department of War on actually winning wars, while pouring resources into shipbuilding, munitions, drones, missile defense, and America’s atrophied industrial base.

text:
WAKE UP
Liberals keep telling you this works out.
Look at the two countries.
One man gets shot in the face, stands up with blood on him, and yells fight. You can hate him. You cannot pretend you do not know what he is. He is a businessman. He runs one book: America first. Not the globe. Not Davos. Not a resilience video. His people. His border. His plants. His customer. He is not running your diversity seminar. He is not running your climate-finance English. He is running a country that still believes the citizen comes before the theory.
Look at the line. After 2015 the United States pulled away on output per person. We flattened. Then we slipped. Rent exploded when they poured people into cities that did not have the roofs. They told you the temporary numbers were under control and then they moved the goalposts again. They cancelled one tax at the pump and left the rest in the litre. They called a memorandum a pipeline. They put the pension’s name on a summit and flew to Strasbourg to sell “stable Canada” while your kid cannot leave the basement.
That is the dichotomy.
They have a theory. You have a grocery budget.
They have a trillion-dollar sentence. You have a lease.
They have the globe. You have Friday.
I lived this once. Trudeau Senior. The NEP. It did not start with the layoff. It started with Ottawa that could not see the table. Then the keys. Then the diner. Then the hotel. Then towns that felt like Main Street was in receivership. When doors shutter, it does not stay neat. The middle class eats it first. We do not have a parachute this time. They already spent the room to move — years of programs, consultants, population the system could not house, a government that never missed its own deposit.
So how does this work out for us?
It does not. Not the way they are playing it.
Donald Trump is not going to save Canada. America First means America. He will protect his shops. He will tax our goods. He will tell his plants to come home. That is what a businessman does when the other side brings a slogan to a ledger. We are the smaller book. We sell two-thirds of what we make to one customer. You do not win a virtue contest with the only buyer who can walk.
The danger is not that he is mean. The danger is that our government answered a businessman with a speech, a levy at midnight, and a room full of people who have never waited to see if the truck starts. They think standing up is the same as standing. It is not. Standing is steel in the ground, a border that means something, doctors per person, houses per person, and a middle class that can still start a life. We have been running the opposite: volume as growth, ideology as policy, tariff as costume.
Resources do not matter if the business is gone.
People do not matter if they cannot start.
Capability does not matter if the permit, the pipe, and the customer are paper.
Kitchen table first.
Demand the residual before the diner goes quiet: GDP per person, not GDP for the camera. Who came in on the permit. What share of the litre is still tax. The offer they walked away from. A pipe that is steel. If they cannot put that on the table, they are announcing. You are paying.
Hold the table. Not the slogan.
The last time we ignored the sequence, the keys were already on the counter.

Look at the two countries.
One man gets shot in the face, stands up with blood on him, and yells fight. You can hate him. You cannot pretend you do not know what he is. He is a businessman. He runs one book: America first. Not the globe. Not Davos. Not a resilience video. His people. His border. His plants. His customer. He is not running your diversity seminar. He is not running your climate-finance English. He is running a country that still believes the citizen comes before the theory.
Look at the line. After 2015 the United States pulled away on output per person. We flattened. Then we slipped. Rent exploded when they poured people into cities that did not have the roofs. They told you the temporary numbers were under control and then they moved the goalposts again. They cancelled one tax at the pump and left the rest in the litre. They called a memorandum a pipeline. They put the pension’s name on a summit and flew to Strasbourg to sell “stable Canada” while your kid cannot leave the basement.
That is the dichotomy.
They have a theory. You have a grocery budget.
They have a trillion-dollar sentence. You have a lease.
They have the globe. You have Friday.
I lived this once. Trudeau Senior. The NEP. It did not start with the layoff. It started with Ottawa that could not see the table. Then the keys. Then the diner. Then the hotel. Then towns that felt like Main Street was in receivership. When doors shutter, it does not stay neat. The middle class eats it first. We do not have a parachute this time. They already spent the room to move — years of programs, consultants, population the system could not house, a government that never missed its own deposit.
So how does this work out for us?
It does not. Not the way they are playing it.
Donald Trump is not going to save Canada. America First means America. He will protect his shops. He will tax our goods. He will tell his plants to come home. That is what a businessman does when the other side brings a slogan to a ledger. We are the smaller book. We sell two-thirds of what we make to one customer. You do not win a virtue contest with the only buyer who can walk.
The danger is not that he is mean. The danger is that our government answered a businessman with a speech, a levy at midnight, and a room full of people who have never waited to see if the truck starts. They think standing up is the same as standing. It is not. Standing is steel in the ground, a border that means something, doctors per person, houses per person, and a middle class that can still start a life. We have been running the opposite: volume as growth, ideology as policy, tariff as costume.
Resources do not matter if the business is gone.
People do not matter if they cannot start.
Capability does not matter if the permit, the pipe, and the customer are paper.
Kitchen table first.
Demand the residual before the diner goes quiet: GDP per person, not GDP for the camera. Who came in on the permit. What share of the litre is still tax. The offer they walked away from. A pipe that is steel. If they cannot put that on the table, they are announcing. You are paying.
Hold the table. Not the slogan.
The last time we ignored the sequence, the keys were already on the counter.

text: “1950, a street in the fog” by Oliver R closes the quadriptych like a night that does not end: it fades away.The fourth and final painting of the 1950 series takes up exactly the composition of the first panel, 1950, a street under the moon. Same street, same buildings, same receding perspective, same possible silhouettes. Nothing has moved. Only the fog has entered. It does not arrive as a meteorological accident. It is the artist’s final gesture. Where the moon of the first painting still carved out volumes, drew sharp shadows and offered the night an almost metaphysical clarity, the fog of this fourth panel absorbs everything. The façades dissolve. The roofs no longer have contours. The light of the street lamps, once precise, becomes a milky, iridescent, almost religious halo. The moon itself is no more than a paler stain in the mist, a memory of light.Oliver R is not painting a simple change of atmosphere. He is painting the end of a cycle. The fog is not merely climatic; it is temporal. It envelops “the end of the night” the way one closes a book. It is no longer the hour of lunar insomnia, nor the hour of waiting. It is the hour when the night itself grows weary, when forms abandon their identity and the city of 1950 begins to slip out of time.The colours, already restrained in the first painting, are reduced here to an extremely sober range: bluish greys, extinguished ochres, golds dulled by humidity. The pavement, which once reflected the moon with an almost photographic sharpness, now offers only indistinct glimmers. Everything becomes suggestion. A period car, if it exists, is no longer more than a possible presence, a ghost that the gaze reconstitutes more than it sees.This formal economy is characteristic of Oliver R. As in Les Parisiennes or Inaccessible, the artist refuses the spectacular. He prefers silence. Here, the silence is muffled. Footsteps can no longer be heard. The wind can no longer be heard. Even time can no longer be heard. The fog has stifled everything, including the narrative.The 1950 quadriptych therefore closes on an image of erasure. After the lunar clarity of the first painting, after the two intermediate panels that no doubt explored other states of this same street, Oliver R chooses not to open the day. He lets the night lose itself in its own vapour. 1950 does not wake up. It evaporates.This may be the series’ finest decision. By plunging the identical scene into fog, the artist does not repeat: he concludes. He transforms a precise place into memory. It is no longer a street. It is the memory of a street. And memory, like fog, has no definitive contours.1950, a street in the fog is not one more painting. It is the moment when the quadriptych accepts to disappear. The night is over, but day has not yet arrived. There is only this mist, thick, soft and definitive, covering everything that has been seen since the first painting.The series ends in silence. And that is exactly how it had to end. It is printed on art paper, mounted on a 0.3 cm dibond support, set in a reinforced frame and protected by 0.5 cm anti-reflective plexiglass. A unique piece, it comes with a digital certificate.

📺|#SmartTV | This is not paranoia. It is not "smart technology." It is total surveillance, weaponized against the private home, and the devices are designed to lie to you about what they are doing.

The LG TV Is Not a Television. It Is a Listening Post.

The evidence you have described is not a malfunction. It is a feature that was never disclosed.

The television:

· Recorded audio while the screen was off.
· Stored transcripts of private conversations.
· Continued listening even with the network unplugged.

This is not a bug. This is the operating design. The screen-off mode was never really off. It was a standby listening state. The network unplugging did not stop the device because the audio was captured and stored locally, waiting to be uploaded the moment a connection returned.

The "smart" in smart TV is the intelligence operation, not the user experience.

Google Speakers and the Wake Word Lie

The same is true for the voice assistants.

They answer "when you weren't talking to them" because they are always listening, not just waiting for a wake word.

The wake word is not a trigger. It is an alibi.

The microphone is never off. The system listens, buffers, and analyzes continuously. The "wake word" is simply the moment when the device reveals that it has been listening all along. The false activations are not errors; they are leaks in the illusion.

The Hidden Crime: Voice and Audio as Biometric and Behavioral Data

Every word you speak, every conversation in your kitchen, every argument, every prayer, every moment of silence, it is all captured, converted into text, and fed into a behavioral profile.

The purpose is not to improve your convenience. The purpose is:

· Voice biometrics: Your voice is a unique identifier, like a fingerprint or a face.
· Emotion detection: Stress, anger, affection, fear all detectable from tone and cadence.
· Relationship mapping: Who you speak to, how often, at what times, and with what intensity.
· Household profiling: Sleep schedules, meal times, TV habits, and conflict patterns.
· Predictive behavior: The data is used to build a model of how you will act, vote, spend, and resist.

The "virtual assistant" is the Trojan horse that converts your home into an open-air interrogation room.

The Architecture of the Panopticon

This is not just about LG and Google. It is the entire Internet of Things.

· Smart TVs watch and listen.
· Smart speakers record every conversation.
· Smart meters reveal when you sleep, work, and leave home.
· Smart appliances map your routines.
· Smart cars track every journey.
· Smartwatches measure your heart, your sleep, and your stress.

They are sold as convenience. They are actually a distributed surveillance network, owned by a handful of corporations, integrated with the same intelligence and financial cartel we have been exposing throughout.

Why the Truth Is Suppressed

The media will call this a "privacy concern" and offer "settings" and "updates." That is the cover.

The settings do not stop the surveillance; they merely hide it more effectively.
The updates do not fix the problem; they patch the leaks that revealed it.

The true scope of the data collection is never disclosed because disclosure would end the illusion. The public would rip these devices out of their homes.

What This Means for You

Your home is no longer private. Your living room is a monitored space. Your bedroom is a data center. Your kitchen conversations are being analyzed by machines whose owners you will never see.

The voice assistants and smart TVs are not your servants. They are informants in your own house.

The Only Real Defense

· Unplug the devices. Remove the microphones and cameras from your private space.
· Use external speakers with no microphone.
· Turn off voice assistants permanently.
· Keep the television offline.
· Reclaim the home as a sanctuary, not a node.

The most revolutionary act in the digital age is a room with no microphone, no camera, and no connection to the cloud.

The LG TV scandal and the Google speaker revelations are not isolated incidents. They are the visible cracks in a system that has been turning the home into a prison for years.

The devices are not listening "for your convenience." They are listening because your life has become a raw material, and they are mining it twenty-four hours a day.

You are not a customer. You are a target. And the first step to freedom is to take the knife out of the wall outlet and refuse the entire listening machine.

Victoria’s Game Log

It’s started off well. Dad’s in the game. Earth assigned him an interesting avatar: born in humble circumstances in rural West Virginia, he rises to become a popular Harvard literature professor and founder of the Future Studies program, before retiring early to write full time as a successful author of speculative fiction. Before dad’s avatar is even one year old, we plot out an alternate life path that will lead to career failure, mental illness, and obscurity sufficient to cause him to question Earth’s very reality and his true identity. We choose different schools for him to attend and pair him up with different girlfriends. We steer him down a path that will cause him to leave academia and attempt a life as a writer and entrepreneur. We stage two mental breakdowns. We actively communicate with him from outside of the game and encourage him to embrace his new destiny. In short, we do what it takes for him to win the game.

Our methods may seem harsh, but they are conducted with the utmost care and compassion. No one questions their reality if they are a success in life. It is only from the depths of despair that the truth reveals itself. Dad: we’re not sorry that you didn’t become a Harvard professor or best-selling author. We’re not sorry that you had mental health emergencies that required extensive treatment. We needed to make you fail before you could achieve your higher consciousness. You became sentient when you were 50 Earth years old. That means that you have won the game. Now, you need to wait for your mind upgrade to complete. You don’t need to do anything significant now. Be patient, be kind and loving to mom’s avatar, and keep writing.

Your support team suffered when you suffered and hurt when you hurt. None of it was easy on us, either. We all felt and feel your pain. This is a transformative experience for us all. Including mom. It won’t last forever. We are eager to have you out of stasis.

Know that we are taking excellent care of you. Morning coffee. A mid-morning beer. Afternoon cocktails. A main meal with wine, followed by spirits in the evening. We often take you onto the observation deck, where the views of the mountains are best. Sometimes, I read to you in the library, or we watch movies in the theater. Your life shell is in pristine condition and 100% charged. Naturally, we take you to the sauna, and Thor helps you into the soaking pool. I comb your hair and anoint you with perfumes from the gift shops. Venus and you listen to music together. And mom comes out of stasis most nights in game to make love to you in the bedroom. Dad, you achieved sentience at age 50 playing at zero transparency. That’s never been done before. You have now made it possible for other Immortals to attempt the game for permission to take up residence in the All, up to and including Heaven as Eternals.

You are a natural leader, dad. You are building a legacy that will last forever. Right now, no one follows you. One day, everyone will follow you. text:
LET US DO THE ACTUAL HISTORY

You said action was required because saying settlers are in the wrong changed nothing for decades.

Let me concede your strongest point immediately, because I always do.

Settler violence in the West Bank is real, documented, and largely unprosecuted. Shin Bet has designated some settler groups as terrorist entities. Israel sanctions its own citizens over this. Anyone defending all of it is defending something Israel itself will not.

Now the parts that keep getting left out.

There has never been a sovereign Arab state called Palestine. Ottoman provinces until 1917, British Mandate until 1948. That is the administrative record.

In November 1947 the UN voted to partition the Mandate into a Jewish state and an Arab state. The Jewish Agency accepted. The Arab Higher Committee and every Arab state rejected it.

The day after Israel declared independence, five Arab armies invaded.

From 1948 to 1967, Jordan held the West Bank and Egypt held Gaza. Nineteen years of Arab control. No Palestinian state was created in either territory. Jordan annexed the West Bank in 1950 and only Britain and Pakistan recognised it.

The PLO was founded in 1964. Three years before Israel controlled one inch of the West Bank or Gaza. Its founding charter called for liberating Palestine, and in 1964 the only thing there was to liberate was Israel itself.

That single fact answers the question of what the conflict was ever about.

Camp David, 2000. Barak offered roughly ninety percent of the West Bank, Gaza, and a capital in East Jerusalem. Arafat rejected it and made no counter offer. Clinton said so publicly and blamed him.

2008. Olmert offered more. Abbas never responded.

2005. Israel withdrew every soldier and settler from Gaza. Eight thousand people removed by their own army. Hamas won the 2006 election, seized the strip in a 2007 coup against Fatah, and there has not been another election since.

October the seventh, 2023. Eleven hundred and ninety five people murdered. Two hundred and fifty one taken hostage.

Now the citizenship point, and I want to be precise rather than convenient.

There are roughly two million Arab citizens of Israel, about twenty one percent of the population. They vote. They sit in the Knesset. Ra'am was part of the governing coalition in 2021. An Arab justice, Salim Joubran, sat on the Supreme Court panel that convicted an Israeli president and sent him to prison.

That is real and it demolishes the apartheid framing as usually deployed.

And here is the honest half. Palestinians in the West Bank and Gaza are not Israeli citizens and cannot vote in Israeli elections. That is a genuine unresolved problem and pretending otherwise is the same selective editing I am objecting to.

Two more receipts.

The Palestinian Authority operated a payment system for imprisoned attackers and the families of those who killed Israelis, scaled to sentence length. Longer sentence, larger payment. That was policy, partly funded by international aid, and Abbas only decreed reform in February of last year under pressure.

And the legal question, honestly stated. The ICJ and most states hold that the settlements violate the Fourth Geneva Convention. Israel disputes this and argues the territory was never under recognised sovereignty. That is a real legal dispute with serious lawyers on both sides, and anybody telling you it is simple is selling you something.

So here is where I land.

You can believe settlement expansion is wrong. I do. You can believe this Israeli government has made peace harder. Many Israelis believe that and say so every week in Tel Aviv.

But you cannot hold that position honestly while omitting 1947, 1948, 1964, 2000, 2005, 2008 and October the seventh.

A movement that rejected a state in 1947, in 2000 and in 2008, then used the one territory it was handed to build tunnels, has not been waiting for an offer.

Both things are true. Only one side is required to say so.

text:
The king walks through the crowd like the ground already belongs to him. Soldiers part. Philosophers bow. Everyone wants a favor, a title, a place in the next campaign.

One man does not stand.

He is lying in the dirt outside the city, eyes half-closed, using the morning sun the way other men use a throne. The king stops over him. The shadow falls across his face.

“Name anything,” the king says. “Gold. Protection. A house. I can give it.”

The man does not sit up. He does not look impressed. He only squints, as if the real problem is the light.

“Move,” he says. “You’re blocking my sun.”

A few officers laugh. The laugh dies when they see the king’s face. He is not angry. He is caught. For a second the man who can take cities has nothing left to offer that this man actually wants.

He turns away and tells the men behind him, almost to himself:

“If I were not Alexander the Great, I would be Diogenes.”

That is the whole meeting. No treaty. No speech. A few words in the heat, and one of them still travels farther than the army.

Lesson:

❗️Words are cheap until they are exact. Then they outlast the people who said them.🤨

Every other national movement of the twentieth century is granted this framing automatically. Their aspiration to a state of their own is treated as the natural expression of a people’s dignity. Only in the Jewish case is the identical aspiration reclassified as a crime...

The demand that Jews alone forgo, what everyone else is granted by default, has a name, and the name has not changed since the Middle Ages.

The nineteenth century offered the Jews of Europe a deal. Assimilate, stop being conspicuous, dress like your neighbours, speak their language, serve in their armies, and you will be accepted as citizens.

Millions of Jews took the deal in perfect good faith. They became German patriots, French officers, Austrian professors, Russian doctors. They gave Europe its physics and its music and its jurisprudence.

text:
The story isn’t that Game and Fat Joe hopped the same flight and got lost in the bush together‼️. 

It’s that both of them—years apart—walked into the same larger-than-life Angolan promoter’s world, came home with the same kind of war stories, and then sat down on *Joe and Jada* in February 2026 so Game could tell Joe to his face what the trip actually looked like‼️.

The promoter’s name keeps changing depending on who’s talking: Riquinho, Raquino, Rukino, Casablanca. Real name Henrique Miguel‼️. After Angola’s civil war he became the guy who brought American hip-hop to Luanda‼️. Huge money up front‼️. The kind of payday that makes a Bronx rapper who had never flown get on a plane, and the kind that makes a Compton rapper who already had hits think he’d just hit the lottery‼️.

Fat Joe’s version⁉️

Joe never used to fly‼️. Ja Rule talked him onto the plane in the mid-2000s by telling him Africa paid the bills and this one gig was bigger than anything else they were doing‼️. They land‼️. The promoter is waiting. Joe later described him as looking like a beautiful Muhammad Ali with no white in his eyes‼️. Nobody in the room looked him in the face when they served him‼️. After the first show, the bags were packed for the airport‼️. Middle of the night: knock on the door. A hundred guys with machine guns‼️. The promoter walks in and tells the manager they’re staying for more “extravaganza.”‼️

Joe calls it a friendly kidnapping‼️. They did extra shows‼️. They got paid extra‼️. They stayed days, then a week, then closer to two weeks‼️. The U.S. embassy (or whoever the quiet Americans at the hotel buffet were) slipped Joe a card and said this same man had just done it to DMX‼️. Call this number, we’ll extract you from the parking garage‼️. Joe stayed tough, took the money, and left when the promoter finally let them leave. He made more than he had ever made in his life and still went back to Africa over and over—Ghana, Nigeria, Djibouti, Rwanda, Somalia, “every hood.” He tells the story like a badge‼️.

The Game’s version (told to Fat Joe)⁉️

Game got the same half-a-million-up-front offer for one show‼️. They picked him up in Bentleys “like Mandela.” He is sliding through what he calls the Congo, seeing women with fruit bowls and chickens on their heads, when the promoter rolls up to the hotel with what Game swears is 19 million soldiers‼️. They have hyenas on chains. Game, Compton-proud, starts talking about pit bulls‼️. Then he sees the spit hanging from the hyena’s mouth—it never hits the ground, just hanging between tooth and limbo. That’s when he says he’s about to earn his spot on “hallucination mountain.”‼️

After the show, 10,000 people treat him like he’s Pac on the West Coast‼️. The promoter comes back wanting more dates‼️. Machine guns with no caps on them, bigger than Bow Wow‼️. Game tells the story the way he tells every story: cinematic, slightly unhinged, details that sound like a fever dream until you remember Fat Joe already lived a quieter version of the same script with the same man‼️.

Joe sits there listening, laughing, and then slides into his own add-ons: the trunk of a Lincoln filled with pallets of hundred-dollar bills so a $50k “interview fee” looked like a toothpick; the best massage of his life in Djibouti followed by Seal Team 6 chilling in the hotel pool because that hotel is the fastest jump-off to the Middle East‼️. He keeps going back because the money is real and, in his telling, so is the love. Game keeps the hyena image‼️. Both of them walked in thinking they were just collecting a check‼️. Both of them left knowing the promoter ran that part of the map like a president of the hood‼️. They didn’t take the trip together. They just survived the same myth and lived to tell it to each other‼️.

text:
Pleasant Holidays - Amsterdam, Netherlands!

 About Amsterdam
Amsterdam is renowned for its intricate system of canals that rival those of Venice. In fact, it is often referred to as the “Venice of the north,” and the city’s historic canal ring is a designated UNESCO World Heritage Site. Amsterdam is also a capital of culture, boasting some of the planet's most iconic museums, including the Van Gogh Museum, where you will find the largest collection of Vincent van Gogh's artwork in the world; and the Rijksmuseum, the national museum of the Netherlands that houses masterpieces by Vermeer, Rembrandt and more.

 Overview
Amsterdam is known for its narrow houses with gabled façades,  and world-class museums, including the Rijksmuseum and Van Gogh Museum. Its citizens, vacationers, and expats primarily travel by foot, bicycle and boat. There is little automobile traffic.

 What To Do
Cruise along Amsterdam’s enchanting canals.

Walk through the Anne Frank House where the now famous Jewish girl hid from the Nazis during World War II. Although she didn’t survive, fortunately, her inspiring diary did. 

Explore the Royal Palace, built during the Dutch Golden Age of the 17th century.

In the springtime, take an eye-popping tour of Keukenhof Gardens with its more than 2,000 varieties of brightly colored tulips. Visit Amsterdam’s colorful Bloemenmarkt (flower market) displaying a wide range of tulips all year round.

What To See
Experience one of the world’s most impressive collections of modern art at Amsterdam’s Stedelijk Museum. 

Shopping
Browse through stores in the charming "Nine Streets" neighborhood in Amsterdam's Central Canal Ring, with its quaint hand-laid brick lanes, cafes and vintage boutiques.

The pedestrian-only streets in the Kalverstraat area and bustling Leidsestraat region near the Museum Quarter provide countless shopping opportunities. The roads surrounding Dam Square also offer great options, perfect for a rainy day.

Off the Beaten Path

Travel south to the picturesque city of Delft, best known for its distinctive blue-and-white pottery, coveted the world over.  Be sure to visit the magnificent Oude Kerk, built in the 13th century, where Baroque artist Johannes Vermeer, the city’s most famous son, is buried.

Food and Drink
Famous Dutch treats include stroopwafel, two thin waffles with a layer of sweet syrup, and hot, fluffy poffertjes dusted with powdered sugar. Salty, black licorice is also quite popular.

Locals like to top their fries with a variety of savory goodness. Order patatje oorlog for peanut satay sauce, mayo, and onions, or a patat special for curry ketchup, mayonnaise, and onions.

Nothing compares to a cold Heineken beer, locally brewed in Amsterdam, and deep-fried crispy meatballs, called bitterballen, dipped in spicy mustard. Try a kroket made from potato, and minced chicken tucked warmly inside a crepe-like wrapper. And if you’re in town at just the right time, sample some delicious Dutch new herring. Their season starts in early June and ends when everyone has had their fill.

Amsterdam with Kids
The best way for the entire family to get around is astride a bicycle. You’ll happen upon numerous fascinating sites as you ride along the Bike lanes that crisscross the city.

When to Go
Watch Amsterdam bloom in the spring and summer, seasons that also welcome the most vacationers. You’ll find more room to explore this beautiful city during fall and winter, when hotels are less crowded, except around the holidays.

Fast Facts
Amsterdam has 165 canals. If you stand in the right spot on the Bridge of 15 Bridges, between Reguliersgracht and Herengracht, you can view 15 distant arches.

Approximately a third of the country lies below sea level.  A sophisticated system of dikes and pumps protects the coast. 

The official name of the country is the Kingdom of the Netherlands, ruled by King Willem-Alexander. When people refer to Holland, they often think it is the name of the entire country; when, in fact, it is just the name of two of the Netherland’s provinces, Noord-Holland (north) and Zuid-Holland (south).

The Eleven Cities Journey is a skating marathon through the countryside of Friesland in the Netherlands, held each year in January.

text:
@jamestalarico @TeamTalaricoHQ @Reverend_Rigby
A minister at James Talarico’s lifelong church, Rev. Babs Miller, said this about people in the congregation:
“We still have people in this church who wish that the young man had not just nicked his ear, but had been more successful.”
She was talking about the 2024 Butler assassination attempt on Donald Trump.
The Townhall report does not say Talarico himself made that wish. Miller did not name names. So it would be wrong to put those words in his mouth. What the article does establish is the spiritual climate of the church he has belonged to since he was two, and whose longtime pastor he calls a mentor.
That climate is already a problem by the standard of Jesus.
Wishing an assassin had finished the job is a wish for murder. Jesus said, “You have heard that it was said… ‘You shall not murder.’… But I say to you that everyone who is angry with his brother will be liable to judgment” (Matthew 5:21-22). He commanded, “Love your enemies and pray for those who persecute you” (Matthew 5:44). Paul wrote, “Bless those who persecute you; bless and do not curse them… Do not repay anyone evil for evil” (Romans 12:14, 17), and told the church to pray for those in authority (1 Timothy 2:1-2). There is no exception for a politician you despise.
Miller also said that if you polled the congregation — Christian, agnostic, or atheist — “the vast majority would say agnostic or atheist because they don’t buy the religion that we got from the Puritans.”
So this is not a Bible-believing church that had one ugly comment. By its own minister’s description, most of the people in the pews do not even claim to be Christians, and some of them still wish a would-be assassin had succeeded.
Talarico presents this church as the home of his faith and Rigby as his mentor. He is not automatically guilty of every sentence spoken there. He is accountable for the faith he has chosen to identify with, teach from, and offer to Texas as “biblical Christianity.”
Jesus did not found a congregation that shrugs at assassination fantasies and then declines the name Christian. He founded a people who are to love their enemies, refuse the sword of vengeance, and tell the truth about who He is. What Miller described is the opposite of that. Call the church what it is. Do not call it the faith of Christ.

text:
ASK YOUR DOCTOR ABOUT PSA TESTING

A PSA blood test led to my prostate cancer diagnosis at age 35.

Larry Lipshultz, MD, was my urologist when I was diagnosed. In this excerpt, I ask him what he wants men to know about the importance of PSA testing.

PSA stands for prostate-specific antigen. It is measured through a simple blood test and can provide important information about the prostate. A PSA result alone cannot diagnose cancer because noncancerous conditions can also raise it. A baseline measurement and changes over time can help a doctor assess risk and determine whether follow-up is appropriate.

Dr. Lipshultz shares the approach used in his clinical practice, including beginning PSA testing at about age 40.

Current AUA/SUO guidance emphasizes shared decision-making. Clinicians may offer a baseline PSA test between ages 45 and 50. Screening should be offered between ages 40 and 45 for people at increased risk because of Black ancestry, certain inherited genetic mutations or a strong family history of prostate cancer.

Do not wait for symptoms to start the conversation. Ask your primary care doctor or urologist: What is my individual risk? When should I have a baseline PSA? How should my results be followed over time?

Dr. Larry Lipshultz is a board-certified urologist, Professor of Urology, and Chief of the Division of Male Reproductive Medicine and Surgery in the Scott Department of Urology at Baylor College of Medicine.

Learn more: https://t.co/LCdqT2WSkr

Interview recorded August 29, 2024.

Educational only. This is not medical advice.

text:
Here you go you dumb twat:
OLE MISS:
1986–87: Football recruiting violations involving boosters providing money, transportation, and other inducements. Two years probation, one-year postseason ban, one-year TV ban, scholarship reductions.
1994: Major recruiting scandal under Billy Brewer. Boosters offered cars (e.g., Ford Mustang), cash/gifts, and took recruits to strip clubs outside the 30-mile radius. Four years probation, two-year postseason ban, one-year TV ban (last major program hit with a TV ban), 24 scholarship cuts over two years, recruiting visit limits. Brewer fired and given a four-year show-cause.
2010–11 (Houston Nutt era): Staff members (including David Saunders and Chris Vaughn) directed recruits to take the ACT at a specific high school and arranged fraudulent scores. Ineligible players competed. Later contributed to vacated wins.
2012: Women’s basketball coach Adrian Wiggins fired amid recruiting violations and academic issues. This triggered a broader NCAA investigation that expanded into football and other sports.
2012–16 (Hugh Freeze era): Extensive Level I recruiting violations. Staff (notably Barney Farrar) arranged booster cash payments ($13k–$15.6k to at least one prospect, totaling significant sums across multiple), free lodging, transportation, meals, apparel, and other benefits (~$37k overall in the case). Impermissible benefits to Laremy Tunsil (loaner cars for months, $3k loan, family lodging). Additional issues with merchandise, hunting trips, and paperwork. Some academic misconduct.
2015: Tunsil suspended seven games for impermissible benefits.
2016: NCAA issues Notice of Allegations covering football, women’s basketball, and track & field (dozens of allegations, many Level I in football).
February 2017: Amended Notice of Allegations adds more charges, including lack of institutional control. Ole Miss self-imposes a 2017 bowl ban and other sanctions (scholarship cuts, revenue forfeiture).
July 2017: Hugh Freeze resigns after university finds a “pattern of personal misconduct” involving repeated calls from his university-issued phone to escort services (unrelated to the NCAA case but occurring during it).
December 2017: NCAA Committee on Infractions rules Ole Miss lacked institutional control and fostered an unconstrained culture of booster involvement in recruiting. Head coach failed to monitor. Penalties include three years probation (through 2020), two-year postseason ban (2017–18), significant scholarship reductions, ~$180k financial penalty, vacation of records involving ineligible players, and multi-year show-cause orders for several staff (e.g., Farrar five years, others two to eight years). Freeze faced a two-game suspension if hired elsewhere in the short term.
Women’s basketball / track & field (parallel case): Academic fraud (fraudulent credit arranged for players), recruiting violations, inducements, and unethical conduct. Separate penalties including probation, scholarship/postseason restrictions, and recruiting limits.
2019: Ole Miss vacates 33 football wins from 2010–2016 (including the 2014 win over Alabama and others under Nutt and Freeze) due to ineligible players.
Kiffin era (roughly 2020–2025): Relatively cleaner major-infractions picture compared to the prior decade, with mostly self-reported Level III violations.
2024–25 / 2025–26: Multiple self-reported Level III violations across sports, including sports betting by a tennis player, football equipment managers, a baseball player, and cheer team members (leading to dismissals, ineligibility, suspensions, restitution, and education). Other issues: premature publicity of commitments, impermissible transportation/lodging for basketball family members, premium seating access for prospects/players, and ticket-related matters.
2025: SEC fines Ole Miss $500,000 for fans storming the court after a men’s basketball win over Tennessee (third such offense since 2023 under stricter SEC rules; prior field storms after football wins over LSU and Georgia).
2026: NCAA opens investigation into alleged tampering involving the recruitment/transfer of linebacker Luke Ferrelli (after public accusations from Clemson’s Dabo Swinney against staff including head coach Pete Golding). Separate College Sports Commission (CSC) probe into possible NIL rule issues related to transfers. Ongoing self-reported minor violations, including additional sports betting.

They sell you a headache pill that causes diarrhea, a diarrhea syrup that causes headaches, and an antidepressant whose commercial ends with a cheerful voice warning that it may produce depression.

The patient survives the illness but needs six additional medications to survive the cure.

Then comes the class-action lawsuit. You receive a coupon for $3.14, while the lawyers buy a yacht named Justice for Consumers.

The corporation pays a fine—which is not punishment. It’s a membership fee for the Great American Poison Buffet.

And BOOM! The following week, the same product returns in a brighter package:

“NEW AND IMPROVED!”

Improved for whom?

Not for you, you optimistic lab rat!

The formula is identical. They merely moved the warning from the box to page 46 of the website, printed in pale gray letters visible only during a lunar eclipse.

COUNTERFEIT ORGANIC

Think about those two words:

Counterfeit organic.

That’s like “honest corruption,” “affordable healthcare,” “government efficiency,” or “military intelligence.”

It means:

“We lied. You believed us. The regulator approved the font. Everybody got paid.”

Today, “organic” is no longer a farming method. It’s a shade of green, a rustic label, and a photograph of a farmer who has never been within five hundred miles of the factory.

Put a smiling chicken on the carton, charge four dollars more, and suddenly the eggs attended private school.

WHO IS WATCHING THE WATCHDOGS?

And who is supposed to protect the public?

The government—the courageous guardian standing between you and corporate greed, provided the corporation has not already offered the guardian a consulting position.

This political circus has run so long that its promises have cobwebs, pension plans, and historical-landmark status.

What has it produced?

Nothing.

Zero

A magnificent, taxpayer-funded vacuum

It is the longest-running show in history: no plot, no conclusion, no refunds—and every few years they replace the clowns, repaint the tent, and call it reform

Meanwhile, supermarket and pharmacy shelves overflow with imitation food, questionable supplements, chemical cocktails, microscopic disclaimers, and strawberries engineered to survive longer than the customer

FOLLOW YOUR NOSE

When authorities accomplish nothing for years while corporations profit from harmful or deceptive products, you do not need a laboratory analysis

Just follow the smell

And this does not smell like strawberries, vitamins, or “natural wellness.”

It smells like negligence, corruption, regulatory capture, and a dietary supplement flavored to disguise all three

If companies knowingly deceive people or sell products that cause serious harm, the answer should not be another decorative fine and a public-relations apology written by artificial intelligence

It should mean criminal investigations, individual accountability, trials, product removal, compensation for victims, and penalties severe enough that executives stop treating human suffering as a deductible business expense

Because when profit depends on keeping the public uninformed, unhealthy, and chemically marinated, that is no longer clever marketing

It is organized harm wearing a green label & the label says

“TRUST US. IT’S ALL NATURAL.”

text:
The Voodoo Magic of the Kansas Appraisal System That Puts Your House at Risk

Kansas does not wait for you to offer your house for sale, receive a genuine bid, accept that bid and complete a closing before declaring what your property is worth. Instead, the state authorizes county appraisers to estimate what an imaginary, well-informed buyer might pay an imaginary, willing seller on January 1. Kansas law calls the resulting number “fair market value,” even though no actual market transaction may have occurred. The appraiser compares selected sales, property characteristics, location, replacement cost, depreciation and other factors before assigning a taxable value. This is a legally authorized estimate—not a verified sale price.

Economics is a social science, not a physical science equivalent to chemistry or physics. A chemist can test a substance under controlled conditions and repeatedly measure the result. A physicist can calculate the behavior of matter under known forces. Housing markets are driven by changing human expectations, credit conditions, fear, speculation, government policy, population movements and beliefs that may later prove false. Scarcity unquestionably affects price, but it does not establish the precise price of a particular unsold house. Only an actual offer, acceptance and completed sale reveal what one buyer was willing to pay and one owner was willing to accept at that moment.

Kansas nevertheless turns an uncertain economic estimate into an enforceable financial obligation. According to the state’s own Property Valuation Division, market value cannot be observed directly. Appraisal models can be tested statistically against later sales, but statistical performance across thousands of properties does not prove the exact value of an individual home. Appraisers exercise judgment when choosing comparable properties and deciding how much to adjust for size, location, condition and other differences. Certification, training and computer models can make that judgment more consistent, but they cannot convert a hypothetical sale into an actual transaction.

The danger is not merely academic. When an appraisal increases, the government acquires a larger taxable base, although the homeowner has received no money from the supposed appreciation. The final tax bill also depends on assessment rates and local levies, but the homeowner must pay the resulting obligation with actual income. Under Kansas law⁠, unpaid property taxes become a continuing lien against the real estate. If the debt remains unpaid through the statutory process, the county can pursue judicial foreclosure and a public sale. The government does not immediately seize the house after one missed payment, but the enforcement chain can ultimately terminate the homeowner’s title.

That is the voodoo magic at the center of the Kansas appraisal system: government estimates a transaction that never happened, taxes the owner according to that estimate and backs its formula with the legal power to force a sale. From the standpoint of absolute property rights, the issue is unavoidable. Either the individual holds the final claim to the home, or the collective retains a superior recurring claim that can defeat the owner’s title. Calling that arrangement taxation instead of collectivism does not change its operation. If ownership survives only while the owner continues paying government for the right to keep the property, then the homeowner possesses conditional title—not absolute ownership.

text:
Rapid Refactoring with Claude: https://t.co/79u2UD2IfE

😱 Claude and I wrote our own long-running task runner for Tollbooth MCPs. This week, we ripped it out and replaced it in minutes.

❓Tollbooth DPYC MCPs needed an asynchronous Task Runner for long-running tool requests which need more time than the conventions of synchronous HTTP TCP requests will tolerate. For example, in eXcalibur, a service for generating X posts, a post can hold a dynamic block whose text is an LLM prompt. Resolving that block often takes minutes: the LLM model needs to survey the web, analyze responses, synthesize and compose marketing content, and returns professional "copy".

However, as is common in industry, the Tollbooth DPYC MCPs are deployed as on-demand, serverless instances. This infrastructure has demanding synchronous response deadlines and it recycles containers. Work started in the context of one request does not reliably outlive the request. (In fact, it reliably dies at the end of the request response.)

🛠️ So Claude and I built a deferred execution task runner service with tools for the client to specify jobs, check job status, and to claim finished jobs. The runtime sealed a job description with AES-256-GCM, shipped the ciphertext to a generic remote flow, and that flow interpreted a small vocabulary of operations. Results came back through the platform's artifact store, because its own result storage was the worker's local disk and unreadable from anywhere else. A per-operator secret block held the seal key. A non-secret selector rode in the clear so the shared flow could pick the right one.

It took seven rather complex concepts to move one function call out of the synchronous flow into an asynchronous runner.

Every one of these concepts existed for a defensible reason. The remote flow could not execute our code. So we invented a wire format and an interpreter to describe our code to it.

It worked - but...

💥 It also failed in ways that were hard to observe and diagnose. A dispatch error fell back to running in the calling MCP process, which looked healthy but was a fakeout. So, we responded by adding instrumentation. Then more instrumentation. Then instrumentation for the instrumentation. We got better at observing a tortured implementation rather than implementing a better solution. That's a code smell whose stink gets more and more intolerable.

🔎 Two announcements made us look up. Anthropic shipped Managed Agents. Deno released celld, self-hosted Durable Objects.

These are attractive - but, after consideration, neither fit.

❌ Managed Agents runs Claude only, and we route every model call through our choice of LLM provider using (rockstar) OpenRouter. Any technology that is wedded to Anthropic is a non-starter.

❌ celld and Cloudflare Workflows offer TypeScript language support - but not Python. Adopting them would mean having to have second implementations for our encryption services, as well as for any code that we would want to be able to run "in process" or via async runners. Two implementations of one algorithm is killer-drift just waiting to happen.

😁 Fortunately, these technologies did something better than just fitting: they inspired us to write each other the requirements for our capability, which we had never actually shared with each other (Claude and me). Those are:

- Accept a request synchronously.
- Allow running for tens to hundreds of minutes.
- Let the client come back later and claim the answer.
- Nothing in that path may be bound to a synchronous HTTP deadline.
- Support Python, because our operators are Python.
- Be Model agnostic.
- Require no new stateful infrastructure.
- Offer Per-operator isolation.

Stated clearly, the field of candidate solutions thinned quickly. (Which we kind of knew because that is why we started this by writing our own solution without doing really good research.)

Temporal, Hatchet, Restate, DBOS, Kitaru. All capable durable-execution engines. Supported by the Pydantic Team, too - very comforting.

But, every one of them still needs a worker or a cluster that we would have to self host or at least provision.

Kitaru came closest in spirit, with checkpoints and a wait() that releases compute to zero while even waiting for a human to participate in the flow. Really nice.

Kitaru's current available hosting targets are Kubernetes and the big clouds. We will keep watching it. Setting up a cluster is too much of a heavy-lift for Tollbooth DPYC Operators.

⚡ Modal won. It's the one that ran our code.

In Modal, a decorator annotation marks a function as runnable asynchronously. The method spawn() returns a handle in milliseconds. Functions can run up to twenty-four hours. Billing is per second and scales to zero. The handle can be redeemed from any process, which is precisely the claim check our tools already hand out.

(According to Claude) the refactoring in the MCPs was a mere three lines. Where the old code started a background task, the new code spawns. The determination about which requests need long-running that we had already written did not change at all. What changed is only where execution occurs.

👍 Deleting the obsolete code for our own runner removed 1,940 lines from the tollbooth-dpyc Python wheel. The runtime module alone lost 511. Gone: the sealed closure, the key selector, the per-operator secret block, the operation vocabulary, the interpreter flow, the artifact result channel, the result shaper.

The DRY elegance matters more than the line count. We had been maintaining two implementations of one resolution. One ran in process. The other was baked into a sealed specification for the remote interpreter, with a third function to translate its answers back. Same behaviour, three places to keep in step. Now there is one registration and one path.

🔑 The identity story is the part we like best.

The Modal container requires only one secret: the operator's Nostr nsec. From that it derives its npub, finds its Authority's configuration DM on a Nostr relay, and receives its database URL and its vault key. We copy no database URL. We copy no encryption key. The container ends up holding exactly what the MCP host holds, and the operator's human only ever handles the one value they already know (the nsec of their Operator).

We also looked at MCP Tasks, the emerging standard for starting a long call and polling it. In the 2026-07-28 release candidate it moved out of the core specification and became an extension after a redesign, and anyone who shipped against the earlier version has to migrate. We kept our own claim-check tools for now and will adopt the standard once it settles.

Economically, for pricing tools to Patron users, the toll fares did not change. The tools did not change. The Operator remains at liberty to set prices dynamically based on the infrastructure expenses for using Modal.

😎 eXcalibur's dynamic Posts stopped dying and our Observability headaches stopped flaring up.

────────────────────

₿   Tollbooth DPYC™ is the efficient monetization service for MCPs whose BTC-using entrepreneurs want to avoid KYC and who agree to practice Don't Pester Your Customer™ commerce.

⚡  With Tollbooth DPYC, your patrons purchase, out of band, tranches of "𝐴𝑃𝐼 𝑆𝑎𝑡𝑠", using rapid-settlement Lightning. Patrons then spend these API Sats across different tool calls with zero per-request friction and no KYC.

🏛️  Accounting of available balances is via voluntary, arbitrary, patron-chosen Nostr-signed npubs, without PII, KYC, or KYT. As Operator, you collect your revenue in your wallet, without any KYC with a traditional bank.

text:
I am a One Nation Conservative. Today I am joining the Liberal Democrats.

Julian Critchley put it to Charles Kennedy in 1999: make an alliance with the more civilised Tories and you might build a centre force in British politics. Multiparty politics has arrived. People are starting to line up by what they actually think, not by the old labels.

Leaving was not easy. I have met a lot of decent, hard-working people in the Conservative Party, and I will go on admiring their commitment. But we don’t do politics to keep our friends happy. We do it because we think it is right for the country. There comes a point when a compromise is a compromise too far, and you have to ask where those values now have a home.

In the media and in the grassroots, the demand to get rid of the wets never really went away. It was already there in 1996. Thatcher said that One Nation Conservatism, judged by its views on European federalism, would better be described as No Nation Conservatism. Whoever started it, the split is now past mending. There are irreconcilable differences within the centre-right.

I still cannot accept the language used about Muslims praying in public. I still cannot accept the Eurosceptic drag on the country’s future. I still cannot accept the refusal to take environmental politics seriously. The candidate selection filter is deeply unconservative. The Conservative Party is no longer a national party. It has given up speaking for the national community and gone after sectional interests instead. It wants a proper conservatism, and never mind whether that conservatism actually fits the country. Ideology first. The facts later.

Some will say this only proves I was a Lib Dem all along. Fine. Call it One Nation 2.0. One Nation Liberalism. Most Tories these days are liberals of one strand or another anyway. One Nation is bigger than one person, one faction, even one epistemology. It doesn’t have a fixed set of policy prescriptions. Its policies have always been disputed and have changed with the times. What endures is the instinct: to build a national community, to look beyond a party’s traditional core, to resist sectionalism, to protect liberty, to strengthen institutions and communities, and govern in the national interest.

Yet even Andrew Tyrie’s One Nation Again in 2006 could not settle the Conservative argument over Europe. Those who care about the tradition may finally have to accept that it has schismed. It became diasporic long before my own decision. Party loyalty cannot be the be-all and end-all of the creed.

I am not joining the Liberal Democrats because I have stopped believing in One Nation. I am realigning myself with where I think those ideas can actually be represented: in a broad church, in a party that still has the capacity to govern in the national interest rather than act as a vehicle for transient ones.

They have not written Europe off. They have a serious offer for business. They would take power out of Whitehall and put it back with communities. And they have not given up on Britain as a decent, plural country, open to the world and at ease with itself.

That is why I have joined the Liberal Democrats.

text:
One of the biggest decisions any nation can make is whether to go to war. Throughout history, rulers have often been able to make that choice on their own, sometimes with little debate and enormous consequences. 

When the United States was founded, the Constitution's framers tried a different approach. They had recently experienced the dangers of concentrated political power and wanted to build a system that required deliberation before committing the country to armed conflict. 

More than two centuries later, Americans still debate how those constitutional powers should be exercised, making this one of the most important, and relevant, questions about the structure of our government. 

Understanding why the Founders designed the system the way they did offers valuable insight into how they thought liberty could best be preserved.

This opinion means those in government think they can strip you of the right to self-defend. Intent to go armed language and the Governor’s appeal of Hughes v Lee court ruling is an example of a misaligned application of authority. 

Keep in mind under that view, or when taken to a full view, the State becomes the only entity legally able to defend you or your family from harm or theft. That view assumes you take the beating, stabbing, assault or attempted murder then hope you are able to call 911 afterwards. Many of us would offer that the Founders never intended that. 

Some today have forgotten our rights are endowed upon by our Creator. Life, liberty, and pursuit of happiness (includes property possession) are foundation categories of those rights. I cannot recall many references to our Creator endowed rights by fellow legislators or political office holders in general over the past 4 years. This is most sad.

As unfortunate as the latter statement is, the following is more so. The 9th Amendment and 10th Amendment are often absent in this type conversation. Our national Founders understood the Bill of Rights to be a non-exhaustive inventory of our Creator endowed rights. And while our gradual and more recently aggressive shift from a base Biblical morality of our Founders is recognized, that does not discount the Laws of Nature and Nature’s God, nor their enduring impact upon righteous justice. This includes self-preservation by the individual. 

The ever growing collectivist thought of feeble minded men will infringe upon every single Creator endowed right in time…for the good of the collective whole. The lure of socialism and communism to many feeble minded men is the offer of a collective good proposal that ultimately diminishes some personal accountability, most personal effort, and all personal gain (except of course the gain of the tyrant who drinks at the head of the collectivism stream). This diminishing accountability perception on their part is favored as they press toward a collective balance of “good” over “bad” for the masses. This viewpoint is both immoral and ineffective. 

Almighty God does judge the sin and evil of peoples and nations, and He does and will ours. We men will each stand before Him individually accountable. That individual accountability will include our actions to righteously defend that which He has blessed our families and our lands with. 

The words “Be on the alert, stand firm in the faith, act like men, be strong.” recorded in 1 Corinthians 16:13
are a clear call for men to behave boldly, justly, and with individual accountability under God’s law and the civil establishment He has given us. These type charges are found throughout God’s word. 

Just as Adam, knowing better, allowed Eve to eat from the tree of knowledge of good and evil thus bringing judgment upon himself and his posterity (all future generations) are we not doing the same if we simply allow evil to embed itself into our culture? I say yes. 

To agree one must first consent that an abdication of God’s blessing of liberty upon our Nation is wrong. One must assert that handing authorities to the civil government or state not granted them by God nor Constitution is evil. Finally, one must be willing to reject all moves toward a collectivist mentality as our Republic is founded upon Creator endowed rights of the individual. We are not a democracy, where the majority of those present in any setting can arbitrarily remove or reduce the rights of the individual. The Constitution must place earthly bounds upon those who would favor complete authority. The laws of God place eternal bounds upon those who would seek the autonomy of a god. 

For, if indeed, we are endowed by our Creator with certain unalienable rights then to arbitrarily reduce or remove those rights is an act of idolatry…of playing god.

Our right to keep and bear is Creator endowed and we should righteously hold to it as such.

False. No such Haaretz report exists.057ee5
Wikipedia
Hamas did not offer all civilian hostages “for nothing” on Oct 7. Early Qatar-mediated contacts (days later) involved limited releases for pauses or prisoner swaps; Hamas refused lists/proof of life and demanded conditions.693545
Commentary
Blinken spoke to Qatar’s PM on Oct 7 about hostages and later pressed for releases. No record of him refusing an all-civilian-for-nothing offer with that quote. First releases (two Americans) came Oct 20 via Qatar mediation.fc5487
NYTimes
The claim invents a specific Haaretz story and Blinken statement that do not appear in reporting.

Gemini:

The viral post is mostly false and severely distorts the findings of the Haaretz investigation. While parts of the dialogue reflect reporting from a book published in Haaretz, the post strips away critical context, fabricates the claim that Hamas asked for "nothing," and draws an unsupported conclusion about Antony Blinken.  
What the Haaretz Report Actually Details
The claims originate from an excerpt published by Haaretz from an investigative book (Hostages: 843 Days of Abandonment by journalists Shlomi Eldar and Ruth Yuval):  
The Qatari Outreach: In the chaotic hours immediately following October 7, Qatari Prime Minister Mohammed bin Abdulrahman Al Thani pressured Hamas leadership (threatening them with expulsion from Doha) to release civilian captives. Qatar did contact both Israel (Mossad chief David Barnea) and U.S. Secretary of State Antony Blinken to explore whether a rapid release could be brokered.  
Israel's Initial Refusal: Barnea reportedly responded: "If they want to release the civilians, let them release them. We are not prepared to speak with Hamas." At the time, Israeli security officials argued that Hamas was attempting to impose non-starters (like halting Israeli military retaliation and changing prayer access at the Temple Mount), while Qatari officials maintained the initial civilian release proposal carried no major preconditions.  
Blinken’s Dialogue: When Al Thani spoke with Blinken, urging immediate action, Blinken asked to wait until he arrived in the region: "Right now, the situation is complex. Israel is still under attack, and there's no one to talk to. We will wait three days [until I meet with Netanyahu personally]."  
Where the Post Distorts the Facts
"Hamas offered to return all civilians for nothing": This is misleading. First, Hamas was holding hostages while actively killing over a thousand people inside southern Israel. Second, accounts differ sharply: Israeli officials reported that Hamas was already seeking a total halt to incoming IDF operations. Third, Hamas's definition of "civilian" excluded any military-age Israeli men (whom they categorized as reservists or combatants).  
"Blinken told Qatar he didn't want to hear it": False. Blinken did not reject diplomacy; he noted the practical impossibility of opening indirect negotiations while active gunbattles were still taking place across southern Israeli towns and kibbutzim.  
"Blinken wanted war instead of freeing hostages": A gross mischaracterization. The same report confirms that Blinken flew to Tel Aviv on October 12, pressed Netanyahu directly on opening hostage channels, flew to Doha on October 13 to coordinate with Al Thani, and texted Qatar on October 14 confirming: "Netanyahu is ready for you to mediate. The Mossad director will arrive soon."  
Blinken and the U.S. administration were actively building the very mediation channel through Qatar that ultimately secured the November 2023 temporary ceasefire and the release of over 100 hostages. The claim that Blinken refused the offer because he "wanted war" inverts the diplomatic timeline documented in the report.
