text:
A few of the risk numbers conflict across sources. I’ll pull the official BLS outlook so the advice isn’t built on marketing sites.The short version: your job is not disappearing the way office jobs are. A line cook in a real restaurant is one of the least AI-exposed occupations in the economy. Fast-food fry stations are a different story. The people who get hurt will be the ones who stay one-station, one-menu, and treat every new screen like an enemy. The people who come out ahead will be the ones who get more versatile, more senior, and harder to replace than a robot that only fries.
What you should actually know
The official numbers do not match the panic.
The Bureau of Labor Statistics projects overall cook employment to keep growing. Restaurant cooks specifically are projected to grow much faster than average — O*NET/BLS data shows restaurant cook employment rising from about 1.46 million in 2024 to about 1.68 million in 2034, with roughly 250,000 openings a year. Most of those openings exist because people quit, not because robots ate the jobs.
Fast-food cooks are the exception: BLS projects that category to shrink about 13% over the decade. That is the segment robots actually touch.
AI is not cooking your tickets. What is spreading first is not a robot chef. It is:
* Voice AI and kiosks at the drive-thru / counter
* Inventory, waste tracking, and scheduling software
* Kitchen display systems that time tickets
* Automated fryers and a few high-volume assembly lines (Flippy-style fry robots, Sweetgreen-style bowl lines, stir-fry robots in some Asian chains)
Those tools change how a kitchen runs. They do not, in most restaurants, remove the person who can sauté, grill, taste, recover a broken sauce, and fire eight tickets at once when the printer explodes.
Physical cooking is hard to automate cheaply. A robot that fries the same three items all day can pencil out in a high-volume chain. A robot that handles a changing menu, variable product quality, 86s, specials, allergies, a dead burner, and a Saturday night crush still does not make economic sense for most independent and full-service kitchens. Cost, space, maintenance, and flexibility are the real barriers — not “AI isn’t smart enough yet.”
Owners want fewer hires, not a kitchen with zero humans. Labor is expensive and unreliable. Operators are using AI to schedule tighter and get more output per person. That can mean a smaller crew on some shifts. It does not automatically mean “line cooks are obsolete.” It means the remaining humans have to be better.
Your coworkers looking at each other like it’s a death match are reading the wrong story. The industry still has chronic turnover and a shortage of people who can actually cook. The competition that matters is not “who survives AI.” It is who becomes the person a chef cannot afford to lose.
What to prepare for
Expect the kitchen to get more digital around you, not empty of people.
1. More screens, fewer clipboards. Inventory apps, waste cameras, smart ovens, ticket timing. Someone on the line will have to work with that, not pretend it isn’t there.
2. Standardized stations get automated first. Fry, portion, assemble-the-same-bowl, drop-the-same-nuggets. If your whole identity is one repetitive station in a high-volume chain, that is the vulnerable seat.
3. Prep may shrink in some places. Commissaries, pre-cut product, and ghost-kitchen production already eat some knife work. Factory-style food production is more automatable than a restaurant line.
4. The job splits. Low end: fewer people babysitting machines. High end / independent / hotel / catering / chef-driven: humans still run the food. The middle is where you need a plan.
5. Labor models get tighter. Not “no cooks.” “We will try to run Saturday with one less body if the tools let us.” That rewards cooks who can cover two stations and train the new kid.
6. Asia is moving faster than the US on cooking robots for standardized dishes. That matters for chains copying those models. It matters less for a neighborhood restaurant with a real menu.
How you come out the other side
Do not try to beat a robot at being a robot. Beat it at being a cook.
1. Get off the most replaceable station
If you only fry, only grill the same three proteins, or only assemble, expand now. Learn sauté, sauces, butchery, pastry basics, garde manger, or a cuisine that is not fully standardized. Specialty skills — butchery, fermentation, pastry, serious plant-based cooking, regional cuisines — are much harder to automate than “drop basket, pull basket.”
2. Become the person who can run the line
Lead cook / sous is the durable path. Chefs and head cooks have higher pay and much more resilience because the job is judgment, taste, timing, people, and recovery — not just execution. Median pay for chefs/head cooks is already in the low $60ks; line cook medians sit in the mid-$30ks. That gap is the actual ladder.
Take extra responsibility before anyone offers it: open/close, order product, write the prep list, train the new hire, own food cost on your station.
3. Learn the tools instead of resenting them
You do not need to become a programmer. You do need to be the cook who can:
* Use the inventory / ordering system without calling the manager
* Read a KDS and not fall behind
* Understand food cost and waste numbers
* Use a phone or laptop to scale a recipe, check a yield, or draft a special
There is already a small emerging role of “the person who makes the kitchen tech actually work.” That person does not get cut first.
4. Stack credentials that travel
Cheap, useful, portable:
* ServSafe Manager (not just food handler)
* Allergen certification
* ACF Certified Fundamentals Cook if you want a paper trail
* Community-college or short courses in butchery, baking, or a cuisine you don’t know
Formal culinary school is optional at 36. Targeted skills plus a reputation for not being a problem are worth more than a $40k diploma.
5. Choose your employer type on purpose
Safer / more human for longer:
* Independent restaurants with real menus
* Hotels, clubs, catering, banquet
* Hospitals / institutions / corporate dining (less glamorous, more stable)
* Chef-owned places where taste still sells the room
More exposed:
* High-volume QSR fry/assembly
* Concepts built around one machine-friendly product
* Places already talking about “labor-light” as the whole business model
You can work QSR while you skill up. Just don’t build your whole future on the station a $5k/month arm can run.
6. Build a second floor under your life
AI is not the only way a cook ends up broke. Injuries, a bad owner, a closed restaurant, and burnout do it every year.
Practical insulation:
* Live below what a good week of shifts pays
* Keep a real emergency fund even if it is ugly and slow
* Maintain a skill you can sell outside one restaurant: catering, private dinners, meal prep, butchery, teaching a class, pop-ups
* Stay in shape and protect your hands, back, and knees. A robot doesn’t need ACL surgery. You might.
7. Stop treating the crew like a hunger games
The coworker energy you’re seeing — “someone’s going to win and it might as well be me” — is how kitchens eat themselves. The cook who trains people, stays calm on a 300-cover night, and makes the chef’s life easier is the one who gets hours when the schedule shrinks. The cook who hoards station tricks and roots for other people to fail is easy to replace with the next body or the next gadget.
The honest end state
In ten years there will still be line cooks. There will be fewer people doing the dumbest, hottest, most repetitive tasks in chains. There will be more pressure to produce with a leaner crew. There will be more software in the walk-in.
What will not exist is a cheap general-purpose robot that can taste, adapt, lead a station, and care whether the food is good.
You come out the other end by becoming expensive in the human ways: more stations, better palate, better judgment, some comfort with the new tools, and a path toward lead/sous/chef or a specialty that customers still pay a person for. The cooks who only offer “I can execute this one ticket the same way every time” are the ones competing with a machine. Don’t be that cook.

The creation of the Jewish State was legal in every iteration. Only legal illiterates and Kangaroo courts disagree. 

What are the legal claims of the Arabs? And why did they reject Peace and offers of Arab sovereignty more than 5 times. Is it because they have a pathological and theological hatred of Jews? 

Here are the legal facts (not that you care) 

•International law is treaty‑ and custom‑based, not a global constitution. States are bound mainly by what they sign (treaties) and by customary rules that crystallize from state practice plus opinio juris (belief of legal obligation).

•Critical date is 1948, not 1967. The legal status turns on Israel’s declaration of independence and the customary rule uti possidetis juris, under which a new state inherits the administrative borders of the predecessor entity (here, Mandatory Palestine).

•Mandate borders include Judea & Samaria and East Jerusalem. On this view, those areas became part of Israel’s sovereign territory in 1948; Jordan’s 1948–1967 control was an unlawful occupation, not sovereignty.

•Therefore, 1967 was not conquest of foreign sovereign territory. Israel’s entry into the West Bank and East Jerusalem is framed as recovering territory already within its sovereign title, so the label “belligerent occupation” is legally misplaced.

•Geneva Convention IV’s occupation regime does not fully apply. Because there was no prior legitimate sovereign, the territory is “disputed,” not “occupied” in the strict sense, and the Fourth Geneva Convention’s settlement bar (Art. 49(6)) is inapplicable or at least contested.

•Oslo created Palestinian autonomy, not sovereignty. Areas A/B are administered by the Palestinian Authority under Oslo; Area C remains under Israeli administration. This arrangement, negates “one rule for Jews, another for Arabs” apartheid claims as a matter of legal structure.

Statehood, self‑determination, and Palestine

•No state of Palestine under Montevideo criteria. The Montevideo Convention criteria (permanent population, defined territory, government, capacity to enter relations) and neither Hamas/Gaza nor the PA meet them.

•Self‑determination ≠ automatic right to a state. While peoples have a right to self‑determination, international law does not grant every national group an enforceable right to sovereign statehood, especially where it would compromise an existing state’s territorial integrity.

•UNGA Res. 181 (partition) was non‑binding. The 1947 partition plan as a recommendation that was never implemented (rejected by Arab leaders and followed by war), thus not a source of binding borders.

Jewish/Israeli claim: Sovereign title derives from the League of Nations Mandate for Palestine (1922), which implemented the San Remo Resolution (1920) and incorporated the Balfour Declaration (1917) to establish a “Jewish National Home” in the whole of Mandatory Palestine.

Jewish/Israeli claim: Though initially a British policy statement, it became binding international law when incorporated verbatim into San Remo and the Mandate, creating a legal obligation to facilitate the Jewish national home

Jewish/Israeli claim: UNGA Res. 181(II) recommended a Jewish state; Israel’s 1948 Declaration of Independence and subsequent widespread recognition (and UN membership in 1949) cemented sovereign statehood.

Jewish/Israeli claim: The West Bank (Judea & Samaria) and Gaza were not under a prior legitimate sovereign (Jordan’s annexation was unrecognized); thus they are “disputed” and Israel’s presence is not classic belligerent occupation; some argue historical/legal title extends there under the Mandate.

Jewish/Israeli claim: Emphasizes Res. 242’s “secure and recognized boundaries” and the absence of a prior legitimate sovereign; argues later resolutions are non‑binding General Assembly measures.

text:
I built this with AI. That matters for what follows, so I'm saying it up front.

The AI wrote the maths, and then it wrote a table for my site that said a 90% collapse in market cap would cost a holder 8%. A 97% collapse, 9%.

I couldn't make that sit right. Not because I checked the algebra — I didn't. Because if a mechanism existed where the market could fall ninety percent and you lost single digits, that isn't a clever contract. That's a free lunch, and free lunches don't survive contact with economics. Someone would have found it, and there'd be a Nobel in it, and the textbooks would need rewriting. So either the world is wrong or the table is. I kept saying this. The answer kept being that the table was fine.

Tonight I made it go back and compute. I was right.

The table wasn't lying, it was measuring the wrong thing. On this curve a 97% fall in market cap is 96.8% of supply being burned out of existence and only a 7.8% fall in price. Market cap here is mostly a headcount of tokens, not a price. Quote the drop in market cap and you sound protected. You aren't.

The real rule is plain: the most the curve can take from you equals the share of the 21,000,000 ceiling already minted when you buy. Buy at 8% minted, it can take 8%. Buy at 95%, it can take 95%. The same number caps the upside. No setting of that dial is generous one way and free the other.

A second line had to go too — the one saying the price you paid is a floor. It isn't. Someone who bought before you holds more tokens for the same money, so if they burn first the curve drops below your entry. Two people deposit 100 NVDA each: if the later one exits first, both recover 99.2, just the fee. If the earlier one exits first, they take 118.6 and the later one is left 79.8.

So let me put the mechanism plainly. Nothing here produces revenue. The curve creates no value. If you exit above what you paid, the difference came from someone who bought after you. Minus fees, it is a redistribution with a published rulebook.

The curve mechanism came from sato. I took the shape openly — same 21,000,000 asymptote, same exponential form, same 500-unit scale — and wrote my own implementation, because an ERC-20 reserve and a chain without usable block randomness meant a copy wouldn't have run anyway.

What I did not know until tonight is that sato went through this exact reckoning first. In May 2026 community developers found a state mismatch inside its hook — users minting against one curve position and burning against a lower one. sato published a second whitepaper, switched its interface from buy and sell to mint and burn, and redefined the curve as an issuance system with a final buyback pool rather than a fully collateralised redemption system. Its market cap fell from near forty million dollars to around fourteen.

I found that out an hour ago, looking it up while checking my own numbers. So I inherited the mechanism without inheriting the lesson, and arrived at the same correction by refusing to believe a table. The difference is only timing, and timing is the entire difference: sato had to say this with people's money already inside. I get to say it with nobody's.

There's a Spanish film, The Platform. A vertical prison, a slab of food lowered floor by floor. The top eats first. What reaches the bottom is what the floors above left. Nobody is stealing. The mechanism is simply gravity plus sequence.

I told the AI this is that. It agreed, and then it gave me the one distinction that actually holds: in the film your floor is assigned by lottery and reshuffled every month. Here you pick your own floor, and you can read the number before you commit.

That's a real difference. It is not absolution. Someone standing on a low floor still gets scraps, and knowing the floor number in advance doesn't put food on it. What it changes is who is responsible for the choice.

So the whole offer, with nothing else attached:

The terms are published. That fraction is on chain, before you commit, identical for everyone.

Nobody can change them. No owner, no pause, no upgrade. Constructor arguments. Not movable by anyone, me included.

Nobody can take the reserve. There is no withdrawal function. The only way anything leaves is someone burning along the same curve they minted on.

Legible terms and unchangeable rules do not make this safe. They make it honest. Those are different words and I'm not going to blur them.

Where I stand: two wallets hold satohood and both are mine. Test buys, five to ten dollars each. The entire reserve is under forty dollars. Nobody outside my own wallets has ever bought this. 0.19% of volume goes to the fee address written into the constructor — that's me. sato takes nothing. Unaudited. It may go nowhere.

One coincidence, since it happened on the same chain in the same week. $MEME paired itself with tokenized AMC — a company whose shareholders were diluted from roughly 500 million shares to something near 2.4 billion equivalent across 2021 to 2024. I picked NVDA, which didn't do that. Two tokens on the same chain, one reserved in the most famous dilution story of the last decade and one reserved in its opposite. Neither of us planned that as commentary. It just landed that way.

They're the better-executed launch, and I'd say so with money on the table. Deep pair, 1,600 traders, a gag that actually worked. What I have is a mechanism and no one in it. Those are different problems and mine is the harder one to fix.

I started this because I was angry at ruggers. Mint authority left open, LP unlocked, deployer sitting on a supply block — I wanted to show the format was fixable. I did fix that part. What I didn't fix, and what I now think no contract can fix, is that being early is worth more than being late. I removed the ways to cheat. I couldn't remove the ways to lose.

I'd rather publish this now than after someone's money is in it.

text:
The Sovereign Illusion: Why Late-Stage Capitalist Systems Are Stranded at the Threshold of Reality

There is a moment in macroeconomic history when a civilization’s primary output ceases to be goods, services, or innovation, and becomes something entirely different: the production of compensatory structures to hide its own systemic wounds.

When an economic or corporate configuration can no longer stand on its own terms, it does not immediately collapse. Instead, it enters a state of suspended animation. It constructs a global apparatus—a matrix of skyrocketing public debt, perpetual asset-price interventions, protectionist tariffs, and institutional bailouts—designed specifically to prevent underlying contradictions from becoming visible.
This is the phenomenon of the scaffolded organism. Like a mortally wounded animal held upright by a labyrinth of wooden props, the system appears to be standing. 
But a highly provocative question must now be leveled at our global institutions: What is actually standing—the living, productive capacity of society, or the dead weight of the scaffolding holding it up?

The Geopolitical Theater: Suppressing the Information of Reality

The current global economic tension—particularly between the United States and the ascending industrial ecosystems of Asia—is not merely a trade war. It is an epistemological war. It is a desperate struggle to reject the uncomfortable information that reality is delivering.

For decades, Western capital optimization operated on a convenient formula of geographic extraction: shift complex manufacturing and engineering ecosystems eastward to maximize short-term corporate margins. It was an ideology built on a weaponized, half-extracted reading of Adam Smith. 
The West retained Smith’s emphasis on self-interest and competition but completely discarded his foundational premise: that individual initiative must operate within a deeply felt, socially embedded moral universe.

When you remove the moral psychology from the market, the proposition "freedom allows an order to emerge" degenerates into the dangerous delusion: "whatever makes money must be the correct order".

Today, that one-sided focus has produced an irreversible macroeconomic migration. The nations once cast as low-cost subcontractors are now producing advanced electric vehicles, battery technologies, and smartphones that render Western legacy flagships uncompetitive dinosaurs. 

In response, the established hegemony does not transform; it adds more beams to the scaffolding. It enacts aggressive protectionist barriers, permanent tariffs, and national security exclusions.
But we must look past the political theater and ask the harder question: Is this protection buying time for genuine transformation, or is it merely protecting an obsolete cost structure from the information reality is trying to give it? 
When a system chooses to make its citizens pay inflated prices for inferior products just to keep an obsolete industrial architecture from failing, it is no longer practicing strategy. It is cheating reality to preserve a ghost.

The Core Inversion: Rescuing Functions, Not Institutions

This structural blindness reached its peak during the financial interventionism of 2008 and the systemic bailouts that followed. The ruling elite argued that letting failing financial conglomerates or automotive giants collapse would destroy the world. They intentionally confused the living, vital function with the historical container carrying it.

A society absolutely needs banking—it needs payments, payroll processing, credit creation, and the secure circulation of value. But society does not need every existing legacy bank, nor does it owe an eternal existence to incompetent executive structures, speculative asset claims, or concentrated financial ownership.

The system committed a profound error by rescuing the institution to save the function. The truly radical, hard-hitting alternative would have been to execute an precise separation: rescue the depositors, protect the workers' livelihoods, keep the viable factories running—but let the toxic ownership claims, the speculative gains, and the failed organizational structures collapse completely.

By propping up the dead forms, the West ensured that its institutions became primarily occupied with suppressing economic reality rather than adapting to it. A crisis should never be romanticized, but it possesses a peculiar, sacred utility: it is an act of revelation. It tears away the scaffolding and forces us to look at what can actually stand on its own feet.

Beyond Individuality: The Tapestry of Conscious Interdependence

The path forward is not a retreat into the suffocating, blind collectivism of the twentieth century, which abstracts human beings into lifeless statistical units. 

The historical sequence of human evolution moves through three distinct phases: 

Dependence → Individuality → Conscious Interdependence.

The emancipation of the individual from inherited tribes, castes, and predetermined social roles was a magnificent civilizational achievement. But individualism was never meant to be the endpoint. 
It was merely the necessary training ground to produce autonomous human beings who could then choose to form a conscious whole.

True economic health requires the development of associative organs—spaces where individual initiative is balanced by social perception and conscious coordination. 
The anonymous market mechanism only knows that Person A bought from Person B for a specific price; it remains completely blind to the human beings, the exploited labor, the depleted soil, or the long-term geopolitical dependencies hidden behind that transaction.

An associative economic approach transforms abstract curves into humanly perceptible realities. It brings needs, capacities, and consequences into direct, conscious encounter, turning the blind "Invisible Hand" into an awake, visible coordinate of human awareness.

The Sovereign Blueprint: 4 Lessons for Daily and Professional Life

You do not have to wait for global macroeconomics to reform to apply these insights. 
The breakdown of the global scaffolding offers a clear, uncompromising framework for individual leadership, professional strategy, and personal resilience:

1. Audit Your Personal Scaffolding
Look closely at your career, your business model, or your personal finances. How much of your current success is standing on its own organic merits, and how much is being artificially propped up by temporary, unsustainable scaffolding (unbacked debt, toxic relationships, legacy prestige, or avoiding difficult adjustments)?

The Action: Stop adding beams to a failing internal structure. Face the uncomfortable information your reality is trying to give you, and let unviable projects or outdated skill sets fail cleanly so you can rebuild on solid ground.

2. Differentiate the Function From the Container
When facing a professional crisis or organizational restructuring, do not waste energy trying to save a legacy form just because it is familiar. Strip away the ego and ask: What is the core, indispensable function that must be preserved here?

The Action: If a business structure, a specific job role, or an administrative process is no longer working, let the container dissolve. Aggressively protect and salvage the raw human talent, the foundational knowledge, and the core relationships—the living assets—and build a entirely new form around them.

3. Stop Outsourcing Your Perception to "Prices"
In professional settings, it is easy to succumb to the delusion that if a transaction is profitable on paper, it is automatically correct. 
Cheap shortcuts, outsourced labor with unmonitored conditions, or burning out your team for quarterly margins are the corporate equivalent of an extracted breakfast table. The immediate price tag is concealing a massive, compounding liability.

The Action: Build a personal "sensory organ" for your choices. Actively investigate the long-term human, ecological, and strategic costs of your professional decisions. True sustainability means optimizing for the whole ecosystem, not just the isolated transaction.

4. Practice "Association After Individuality"
Do not fall into the trap of hyper-isolated individualism or passive compliance. True power in the modern workplace belongs to the autonomous professional who possesses the maturity to consciously collaborate.

The Action: Shift your networking and collaboration away from transactional manipulation. Create authentic associations where you actively seek to perceive the genuine capacities, unused resources, and real needs of those around you. Move your team from blind competition into a conscious tapestry of mutual realization.

An order does not die because its metrics contract or its legacy structures fracture. It begins to die when maintaining its rigid conception of reality becomes more important than perceiving reality itself. Step off the scaffolding, strip away the theater, and look directly at what is alive. Start there. And build from that.

[Critique of the Use of Power for Personal Interests Amid National Tragedy, and Condemnation of the French Government’s Complacency]

On July 12, 2026, a tragic incident occurred when a sailor from the Republic of Korea Navy went missing while carrying out a patrol mission near the Northern Limit Line (NLL) in the East Sea, before being found dead the following day. The security situation was sufficiently urgent that South Korean authorities sought North Korea’s cooperation in the search operation.

Yet serious and specific evidence has emerged raising questions about whether Lee Jae-myung, the so-called commander-in-chief of the South Korean armed forces, was enjoying a round of golf with his son while a Navy sailor was missing during a critical security situation.

These are not vague or abstract suspicions. A VIP security motorcade under extensive police traffic control was reportedly captured on the route to Taereung Country Club that day, while four tee times on the club’s Hwarang Course were left vacant during a 35-minute period between 11:40 AM and 12:22 PM. The same time period had been fully booked the previous day. The Presidential Security Service, meanwhile, declined to confirm the schedule or security arrangements concerning the individual under protection.

This episode also echoes earlier reports that Lee visited a military golf course the day after the collapse of the Seosemun Elevated Road last May—a tragedy that claimed three lives. Taken together, these circumstances raise grave questions about Lee Jae-myung’s moral sensitivity to his public duties and his fitness to exercise the responsibilities of commander-in-chief.

Faced with these concrete and specific circumstances, the Office of the President continues to take refuge behind “state secrecy” rather than provide the public with a clear and transparent account.

If Lee Jae-myung chose personal leisure after being informed that a serviceman was missing during a national security incident, such conduct would represent a profound failure of the public ethics and moral responsibility required of a commander-in-chief. If he was not informed at all, that would raise an equally serious question about the functioning of South Korea’s national security command structure.

Either scenario demands a direct and transparent explanation to the South Korean people.

Furthermore, the attitude of the French government, which offers Lee Jae-myung a diplomatic platform as lavish as a state visit despite these serious and unresolved questions surrounding his exercise of public responsibility, deserves severe condemnation.

President Emmanuel Macron and the French authorities present themselves as champions of freedom, human rights, and democratic values. Granting the highest diplomatic honors and political legitimacy to a leader facing such grave questions of responsibility risks endorsing a political charade while disregarding the tragic reality endured by the South Korean people.

We express our deep bitterness at this irresponsible conduct by the French government. Diplomatic courtesy must not become a diplomatic carte blanche when serious questions concerning national security, military lives, public accountability, and the moral responsibility of a head of state remain unanswered.

📌 Documented Sources and Facts

Source 1: https://t.co/CYUEFFpO3o

Background of the Suspicion: On July 12, the day a Navy sailor went missing in waters near the NLL, suspicions were raised that President Lee Jae-myung had played golf at Taereung Country Club (CC).

CCTV Footage: On that same day, a motorcade of VIP security vehicles, escorted under extensive police traffic control and including three motorcycle officers, was reportedly captured on the route leading to Taereung CC.

Vacant Tee Times: On the Hwarang Course at Taereung CC, four tee times were vacant during a 35-minute period between 11:40 AM and 12:22 PM, leaving an unusually open window without groups immediately ahead or behind. The same time period had been fully booked the previous day.

Position of the Presidential Security Service: The Security Service stated that it could not confirm the schedule or security arrangements concerning the individual under protection, citing laws and regulations governing presidential security.

Source 2: https://t.co/uCe2pqVUwR

A crew member of a Navy frigate who went missing on July 12 in waters near the Northern Limit Line (NLL) in the East Sea was found dead the following day.

The Navy announced that at around 5:58 AM on July 13, it discovered and recovered the body of the sailor, who had disappeared from a vessel on patrol duty, approximately 52 km east of Geojin-eup, Goseong County, Gangwon Province.

The Navy and Coast Guard had conducted joint search operations involving around ten vessels and several aircraft.

Source 3: https://t.co/Kn5h3bAs6f

The People Power Party (PPP) raised suspicions that President Lee Jae-myung had played golf on July 12, the day the Navy sailor went missing, and demanded the “full disclosure of all relevant records.”

Jang Dong-hyeok, leader of the PPP, wrote on social media: “Suspicions have been raised that the president was leisurely playing golf while a sailor breathed his last in the freezing waters of the East Sea,” adding, “How devastating must the grief of the bereaved family be?”

Jang stated: “The suspicions are very specific. The sailor’s disappearance was confirmed early in the morning of the 12th. The president reportedly began playing golf at around 11:00 AM,” adding that “many people, including security personnel, reportedly spotted the presidential motorcade.”

He continued: “If this turns out to be true, we can no longer recognize Lee Jae-myung as the commander-in-chief of the armed forces of the Republic of Korea. Publish, with minute-by-minute accuracy, all relevant documents, including reports received after the sailor’s disappearance, access logs for Taereung CC, and CCTV footage.”

Shin Dong-wook, a member of the PPP Supreme Council, also stated on social media: “At the very moment the missing sailor was found dead, suspicions that the president was playing golf at Taereung were spreading online,” calling on the Office of the President to provide a clear explanation.

Representative Na Kyung-won emphasized on social media: “If the reported suspicions are well-founded, this is a grave national security failure that, under a conservative administration, would have led the Democratic Party to immediately push for a parliamentary investigation, a special counsel probe, and an impeachment motion,” adding that “President Lee must directly explain to the people the truth behind these golf allegations.”

Representative Yoo Sang-bum also stated: “If President Lee swung his golf club while having been informed of the disappearance, that would disqualify him from serving as commander-in-chief; if he did not even receive a report, it would amount to blatant incompetence in national security,” demanding an immediate and transparent explanation.

text:
THE WAR THAT LASTED THIRTY-EIGHT MINUTES.

HOW A MORNING'S GUNFIRE IN ZANZIBAR HARBOUR ENDED AN EMPIRE OF SLAVES.

BG: The great events of history are not always the long ones. Some wars ran for thirty years, and some for a hundred, and a few have left almost no mark on the world beyond a line in a schoolbook. One of the shortest wars ever fought lasted less time than a church service, and yet it closed a trade in human beings that had run through the same harbour for a thousand years. It was fought on the morning of 27 August 1896, in the roadstead off Zanzibar, and it was over before the tea had cooled.

Zanzibar deserves a moment of explanation, because its importance is easy to forget. It was a small island of cloves and coral off the coast of East Africa, ruled by an Arab sultan whose ancestors had come from Oman. Its wealth did not lie in the cloves. It lay in the caravans that came down from the interior, from the Great Lakes and beyond, bringing ivory and bringing men, women and children in chains. Zanzibar was the marketplace, the counting house and the port of dispatch. From its beaches the slaving dhows sailed north to Arabia and the Persian Gulf, and for centuries no European power had the reach, or the interest, to stop them.

Britain acquired both. Having abolished the slave trade within its own empire early in the nineteenth century, it spent the next several generations trying, with the Royal Navy as its instrument, to abolish it everywhere else. This was not pure altruism, and it was not pure calculation either. It was the unusual mixture of moral conviction and naval power that characterised the Victorian age, and the mixture is worth noticing, because history rarely offers an instance of a great power spending money and ships for decades on a cause that brought it no obvious profit. The sultans of Zanzibar were pressed, treaty by treaty, to close their slave markets and to permit British warships to search their dhows. The last sultan, Hamad bin Thuwaini, had signed such undertakings. He was, in the language of the day, a friend of Britain.

On 25 August 1896 he died, suddenly and conveniently for some. Within hours his cousin, Khalid bin Barghash, walked into the palace with an armed following and proclaimed himself sultan. He had, by the reckoning of the British consul, about 2,800 armed men, a palace full of slaves, and a firm belief that the British would not fire on him. The consul, Basil Cave, took a different view. Whether Khalid was a good man or a bad one was hardly the question. The question was whether a man who had seized power by force, and who owed nothing to the treaties his cousin had signed, could be trusted to keep them. Cave thought not, and London agreed.

Five warships lay in the harbour, and their names have the ring of a different century: St George, Philomel, Racoon, Thrush and Sparrow. An ultimatum was sent to the palace. Khalid was to haul down his flag and stand aside by nine o'clock on the morning of the 27th. He replied, in effect, that he did not think the British were serious. This was an error of judgement of the kind that ambitious men have made throughout history, but few have been corrected so promptly.

At nine o'clock the flag was still flying over the palace. At two minutes past nine the ships opened fire. The palace replied with bronze cannon that were two hundred years old, and with the guns of the sultan's single vessel, an armed yacht called the Glasgow, which engaged a British cruiser and was sunk for her trouble. She went down in water so shallow that her masts stayed above the surface, where they remained for years as a kind of monument. Then came an episode that tells us something about the men involved. British sailors lowered their boats and rowed into the smoke to rescue the crew of the ship they had just sunk. Every one of them was pulled from the water alive.

By twenty minutes to ten the palace flag had come down. Khalid had already left for the German consulate, where he was given shelter and, in due course, passage to the mainland. The bombardment had lasted thirty-eight minutes. By the afternoon a new sultan, Hamoud bin Mohammed, had been installed, and the British terms were plain and few. Slavery in Zanzibar was to end. Within a year the decree abolishing it was signed, and the largest slave market on the eastern coast of Africa, which had outlived Rome and outlived the Portuguese and outlived the Omani empire that founded it, was closed by a decision made under the guns of five ships on a hot August morning.

It is tempting to draw a large lesson from a small war, and the temptation should be resisted, but not entirely. Historians are fond of the long view, and the long view here is instructive. The Indian Ocean slave trade was old when the Atlantic trade began, and it continued after the Atlantic trade was suppressed. It ended not because the world grew gentler, nor because the traders repented, but because one nation had decided that it should end and possessed the means to make the decision stick. That is an uncomfortable truth for those who prefer their history to be a story of moral progress arriving on its own, and it is equally uncomfortable for those who prefer to remember the British Empire only for its sins, of which there were many. The empire that took so much from so many places also, on this particular morning, in this particular harbour, took away the chains.

The thirty-eight minutes at Zanzibar are remembered today, when they are remembered at all, as a curiosity, a piece of trivia for the quiz night. They deserve better. The people freed by that decree did not measure the war by its length. They measured it by what came after, and by that measure it was one of the more consequential mornings of the nineteenth century.

Press Conference Will Kick off Orange County District Attorney’s First E-Bike and E-Moto Buy Back Event Sunday, September 13 at Angel Stadium

Full Media Advisory: https://t.co/AnG8aibKJW

Santa Ana – A 20-year-old man who spent three months on life support after suffering a life-altering traumatic brain injury while riding an E-Bike in Huntington Beach will be the first participant at the Orange County District Attorney’s Office Buy Back Safety: E-Bike and E-Moto Buy Back Program on Sunday, September 13, 2026, surrendering the E-Bike he was riding when he was critically injured to send a strong message of the increasingly dangerous and deadly consequences of improperly riding E-Bikes and E-Motos.

Jesse Hayes and his mother, Kasey, have become ardent safety advocates in the wake of Jesse’s October 2024 crash and will speak at a press conference along with Orange County District Attorney Todd Spitzer, members of the Orange County E-Bike Injury Prevention Collaborative, the California Office of Traffic Safety, first responders, trauma surgeons, county supervisors, and educators in a statewide effort to reduce E-Bike and E-Moto injuries and save lives.

“After our 18-year-old son survived a tragic E-Bike accident that left him with a severe traumatic brain injury, our family committed to advocating for rider safety and new legislation,” said Kasey Hayes. “We are taking part in this event to raise vital awareness about E-Bike dangers and to help protect other families from going through this devastating experience.”

The Orange County District Attorney’s Office is hosting the first E-Bike and E-Moto Buy Back Program on Sunday, September 13, 2026, from 10 a.m. to 1 p.m. at Angel Stadium, offering up to $1,000 in gift cards and tickets to a Los Angeles Angels baseball game in exchange for E-Bikes, pocket bikes, E-Scooters, mopeds, and E-Motos in an effort to reduce injuries and deaths. E-Bikes and E-Motos have become the number one reason Orange County children are admitted to the emergency room, with injuries increasing 430% in just the last four years across Southern California.

Orange County District Attorney’s Office
E-Bike and E-Moto Buy Back Program
Sunday, September 13, 2026
PRESS CONFERENCE – 9:15 a.m. to 10 a.m.
BUY BACK PROGRAM - 10 a.m. to 1 p.m.
Angel Stadium
2000 E. Gene Autry Way, Anaheim, CA 92806
(Enter off Orangewood Avenue at Bus Gate next to the George Apartment Homes)

BUY BACK SAFETY PRESS CONFERENCE SPEAKERS

Orange County District Attorney Todd Spitzer
Kasey Hayes and her son Jesse Hayes, who was critically injured while riding an E-Bike in Huntington Beach and continues to live with a severe traumatic brain injury.
Orange County Board of Supervisors Vice Chair Katrina Foley

Dr. Almaas Shaikh – OC Health Care Agency Deputy Health Officer, Interim EMS Medical Director, trauma surgeon, and Chair of the Orange County E-Bike Injury Prevention Collaborative
California Office of Traffic Safety Director Stephanie Dougherty
Chief Brandon Shipwash, commander of the California Highway Patrol’s Border Division
Orange County Department of Education Superintendent Dr. Stefan Bean
Dennis Kuhl, the Chairman of the Los Angeles Angels and President of the Angels Baseball Foundation

MEMBERS OF THE MEDIA ARE ASKED TO RSVP TO: MEDIA@OCDISTRICTATTORNEY.GOV FOR PARKING PASS AND DIRECTIONS

Patterned after law enforcement gun buyback programs, the Orange County District Attorney’s Office’s BUY BACK SAFETY: E-Bike and E-Moto Buy Back Program will offer gift cards from Target, Walmart, Dick’s Sporting Goods, and Best Buy in exchange for E-Bikes, pocket bikes, E-Scooters, and E-Motos ranging from $200 to $1,000 depending on the classification of the vehicle as determined by law enforcement on site. Store bought pocket bikes as well as homemade miniature bikes equipped with electric or gas-powered motors will also be accepted. The District Attorney’s Office is utilizing federal asset forfeiture monies which are funds seized from criminal enterprises to pay for the gift cards. Orange County Board of Supervisors Vice Chair Katrina Foley has also contributed $5,000 in discretionary funding to buy gift cards for the buy back event.

“These vehicles are not child’s play, and the consequences are incredibly dangerous and increasingly deadly,” said Orange County District Attorney Todd Spitzer. “This event is sparking conversations about E-Bike and E-Moto safety like never before, and those conversations will hopefully lead to increased rider responsibility, education, and accountability. I’m proud of the efforts we have made collectively as a community, from first responders to medical professionals to educators, community advocates, parents, and prosecutors to address this issue from all different angles with a singular goal: to reduce injuries and save lives.”

“High powered E-Bikes and E-Motos can cause catastrophic injuries in seconds, especially when children ride vehicles built for speeds they cannot safely handle,” said Orange County Board of Supervisors Katrina Foley. “I led the County of Orange’s efforts to strengthen E-Bike safety rules, expanded enforcement resources, and supported stronger state laws. This buy back event gives parents a practical way to get dangerous vehicles out of their homes before another preventable crash causes a life-changing injury or death.”

Orange County District Attorney’s Office
E-Bike and E-Moto Buy Back Program Trade in Values
Pocket bikes/Homemade miniature bikes - $200 in gift cards
Class 1 E-Bike/E-Scooter/Moped - $300 in gift cards
Class 2 E-Bike - $400 in gift cards
Class 3 E-Bike - $600 in gift cards
E-Moto - $1,000 in gift cards

The first 75 people to turn in their E-Bike, E-Moto, pocket bike, or E-Scooter will also receive two tickets to a Los Angeles Angels baseball game, generously donated by the Angels. In addition to the buyback packages, the September 13 event will also feature free giveaways and E-Bike safety information from local law enforcement, fire departments, healthcare, and community partners.

Gift card quantities are limited and will be available on a first-come, first-served basis. E-vehicles can be surrendered anonymously. Working and non-working vehicles will be accepted, and no questions will be asked.

Among the agencies participating in the Buy Back Safety: E-Bike and E-Moto Buy Back Program are the police departments of Anaheim, Brea, California State University, Fullerton (CSUF), Cypress, Fullerton, Fountain Valley, Garden Grove, Huntington Beach, Irvine, La Habra, Laguna Beach, La Palma, Los Alamitos, Orange, Placentia, Seal Beach, and Westminster, along with the California Highway Patrol, the California Office of Traffic Safety, Anaheim Fire & Rescue, and the Orange County Fire Authority. Providence Mission Hospital, Riverside University Health System, Rady Children’s Health, Orange County Global Medical Center, UCI, the Automobile Club of Southern California, Memorial Care, and OC Health Care Agency are also participating.

In May 2026, Orange County District Attorney Todd Spitzer announced the creation of a new E-Bike/E-Moto unit – RIDE SAFELY (Smart Accountability for E-Bikes and E-Motos and Law Enforcement for Youth) to review all potential criminal charges against juveniles and adults, including parents who knowingly allow their children to illegally ride E-Motos and E-Bikes. The unit is part of the District Attorney’s multi-pronged approach to reducing E-Bike and E-Moto injuries and saving lives along with increased education, prosecution of riders and their parents, pursuing additional legislation, and holding manufacturers and retailers accountable.

Since January, the Orange County District Attorney’s Office has filed child endangerment charges against four parents for allowing their children to illegally ride E-Motos, including filing involuntary manslaughter charges against a mother after her 14-year-old son hit and killed an 81-year-old Vietnam veteran in Lake Forest after she had been repeatedly warned that the E-Moto he was riding was illegal and that she could be held criminally liable. She faces a maximum sentence of seven years and eight months in state prison if convicted.

The Orange County District Attorney’s Office has also filed felony charges against a Yorba Linda father whose 12-year-old son was critically injured after he ran a red light and was hit by a car while riding an E-Moto which had been modified to go up to 60 miles per hour, after the boy and his father had been warned about the dangers of children riding E-Moto illegally. He faces a maximum sentence of six years in state prison if convicted on all counts.

Last month, District Attorney Spitzer issued formal warning letters to more than 80 Orange County retailers reiterating their legal duties in connection with selling E-Bike and E-Motos and the potential criminal and civil penalties they could face if they fail to fulfill those duties. California strictly prohibits the sale of products or devices that can modify the speed capability of an electric bicycle so that it no longer meets the definition of an electric bicycle.  Retailers will be subject to periodic inspections by Orange County District Attorney investigators to ensure they are following the law.

More than 100 deaths have been attributed to E-Bikes and E-Motos in the United States, including a 15-year-old boy who was riding on the back of an E-Motos in La Habra, a 13-year-old boy who was killed while riding an E-Moto in Garden Grove, and a 21-year-old who died five days after crashing an E-Bike in Huntington Beach. Children between the ages of 11 and 14 account for 61.7% of E-Moto crashes even though children under the age of 16 are legally prohibited from riding E-Moto, according to the California Statewide Integrated Traffic Record System (SWITRS).

“E-bikes offer a different experience than the traditional bikes many of us learned to ride on,” California Office of Traffic Safety (OTS) Director Stephanie Dougherty said. “They are faster, heavier, and, like learning to drive, require training and practice to operate safely. With the continued surge in popularity of E-Bikes as a convenient and sustainable mobility option, we encourage drivers and riders to make safety part of their everyday travel routine.”

To help riders better understand how to operate E-Bikes safely and responsibly, the California Highway Patrol developed a free online e-bike safety and training program available to riders of all ages and skill levels. The program provides practical information on E-Bike laws, rules of the road, safety equipment, roadway hazards, and safe-riding practices.

“Education is one of our most powerful tools for preventing crashes before they happen,” said CHP Chief Brandon Shipwash. “As E-Bikes become an increasingly popular way to travel, we want riders, especially young riders, to understand the rules, recognize the risks, and develop safe habits every time they ride. Through education, community outreach, and enforcement, the CHP is working to make California’s roads safer for everyone.”

California law distinguishes between E-Bikes and E-Motos based on three main features: the power limit of its motor, its maximum speed limit, and whether it is equipped with operable pedals. Electric bicycles with Class1 or Class 2 designations do not have rider age or licensing restrictions; E-Bikes with Class 3 designations require riders to be aged 16 or older.

To help the public understand the different rules for E-Bike use, the OTS has launched a new “Know Your Bike, Know the Rules” statewide social media campaign. Messages will run through Sept. 20 that emphasize the differences between E-Bikes and E-Motos, the E-Bike classes and helmet requirements, and tips for drivers and riders on safe road interactions. Visit the Go Safely, California website to download the social media toolkit.

Generally, an electric bike that does not qualify as Class 1, 2 or 3, will be classified as an electric motorcycle. That means either that the bike has an electric motor that exceeds 750 watts of power or can reach speeds higher than 20-mph on motor power alone. Additionally, if the bike is not equipped with fully operable pedals, or if it has been modified to reach speeds higher than 20-mph or to attain power higher than 750 watts, the bike cannot be designated an electric bike and instead would be considered an E-Moto.

E-Motos must be registered with the California Department of Motor Vehicles (DMV) as an off-highway use vehicle (OHV), have current insurance, and can only be ridden off public highways by a rider over the age of 16 with a valid motorcycle license and a DOT-approved helmet. Riders who do not fit the legally required criteria can be cited and have their vehicle impounded at a cost in excess of $2,600 a month.

“Between the work we’ve done in Huntington Beach and the training I’ve been involved with across California, one thing is clear: if we want kids to be safer on E-Bikes, we have to give them the right skills, make sure parents understand what they’re buying, and hold riders accountable when they make dangerous choices,” said Huntington Beach Police Sgt. Mike Thomas.

State leaders have developed an e-bike guide with an inventory of best practices and resources from local agencies, such as school-based trainings, policies, safety pledges, and other educational materials. To learn more, visit https://t.co/KTl0dZMFNB. The CHP has also developed a ready reference guide for law enforcement officers and issued an Information Bulletin for Allied Agencies with applicable California Vehicle Code definitions and requirements.

To help keep all road users safe, local, and state leaders offer the following tips for drivers and riders:

Drivers
• Follow the posted speed limit.
• Slow down at intersections as E-Bikes can move      faster than traditional bikes and enter your blind spot quickly.
• When possible, change lanes to allow a minimum of three feet when passing bicyclists.

E-Bike Riders
• Ride in the same direction as traffic.
• Stop at stop signs and signals. The same rules of the      road for vehicles apply to E-Bikes.
• Always wear a properly fitted bicycle helmet,      regardless of your age or the type of bike you're riding.
• Get familiar with the different E-Bike classes, top      speed and motor assist features, and rules for E-Bike use. Some counties, cities, and local authorities may have specific ordinances and/or resolutions.

For a summary of updated E-Bike laws and ordinances in Orange County, visit the Orange County Transportation Authority (OCTA) website.

One year after the shooting death of Charlie Kirk, the need for healing remains great for many of the people who witnessed it.

I spoke with Brady Clegg of Tangible Therapy, who has met with dozens of students who were there that day. He is part of a broader coalition of mental health providers who offered free counseling to students on campus, ultimately serving about 1,000 people.

The FBI also offered counseling following the shooting, with hundreds requesting help.
The Utah Office for Victims of Crime says at least 500 witnesses initially sought compensation for services, including mental health counseling. So far, 173 people have formally applied for those benefits.
For many who witnessed the shooting, processing what they saw — and the emotions that can resurface around the one-year anniversary — remains an ongoing journey.

Clegg talks about why anniversaries of traumatic events can be difficult, what people may experience and how they can take care of themselves and those around them as they continue to heal.

text:
Emergency department triage requires rapid, accurate decisions to prioritize patients using the Emergency Severity Index (ESI), which ranges from level 1 (most urgent) to level 5 (least urgent). 

Traditional human-led triage suffers from heavy workloads, fatigue, and inconsistency, while single AI models often struggle with complex medical scenarios and nuanced boundaries between urgency levels.

To address these challenges, researchers from Virginia Tech and Children's National Hospital introduced TRIAGEAGENT, a novel multi-agent AI framework designed for clinical triage.

Instead of relying on a single model, TRIAGEAGENT simulates a team of specialized AI "doctors" who collaborate through a structured five-stage workflow:

Document Allocation: Patient clinical notes are assigned to the AI doctor team.

Group-Based Analysis: One group uses a coarse-to-fine approach (Doctor A determines high vs. low urgency, then Doctor B narrows it to an exact level), while a third agent (Doctor C) performs a direct classification.

Confidence Summarization: A Summarizer Agent aggregates predictions, rationales, confidence scores, and relevant guidelines retrieved directly from the official ESI Handbook v4 using Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG).

Collaborative Discussion: Agents review the summary and engage in multi-round debate, updating their opinions if a peer offers stronger reasoning or a higher confidence score.

Consensus Agreement: The team reaches a final consensus, outputting the ESI level, medical justification, and an overall confidence score.

To optimize efficiency, the framework uses an early-stopping mechanism inspired by Byzantine consensus theory. When agents consistently reach a high-confidence agreement, the debate ends early, maintaining an average processing speed of just 1.3 to 1.5 seconds per patient case.

Key Performance Numbers:
Overall Accuracy: Evaluated on the total error (discordance) rate across test cases, TRIAGEAGENT powered by GPT-4 achieved a total error rate of 18.98%.

Outperforming Human Experts: Human expert clinicians evaluated on the same test set achieved a total error rate of 31.43%, meaning TRIAGEAGENT reduced triage errors significantly compared to human baselines.

Gain Over Single-Agent AI: Standard single-agent Chain-of-Thought prompting with GPT-4 resulted in a 37.40% error rate; TRIAGEAGENT reduced error rates by up to 18.42% with GPT-4 and 10.84% with GPT-3.5.

Outperforming Multi-Agent Baselines: TRIAGEAGENT outperformed existing medical multi-agent systems like MedAgent by 9.02% and Exchange-of-Thought by 6.25% using GPT-3.5.

In addition to the framework, the authors released the first publicly available benchmark dataset for clinical triage, featuring 218 training cases and 3 test sets of 72 cases each, paired with official ESI handbook ground-truth labels and human expert performance metrics.

text:
On January 18, 2026, about 39 anti-ICE protesters interrupted a Sunday service at Cities Church in St. Paul, Minnesota (Twin Cities area). They chanted slogans such as “ICE out” after learning that one of the church’s pastors, David Easterwood, also served as acting director of the local ICE field office. The disruption ended the service early.

Federal outcome: The U.S. Department of Justice charged 39 people with conspiracy to deprive others of religious freedom and related FACE Act violations (interfering with worship). Those charged include activist Nekima Levy Armstrong, former CNN anchor Don Lemon, journalist Georgia Fort, and others. All have pleaded not guilty. The cases remain pending in federal court in St. Paul. In July 2026 prosecutors offered most defendants plea deals that would reduce the charges from felonies to misdemeanors (with possible community service, fines, or restitution); none appear to have accepted. Defense attorneys filed motions to dismiss in August 2026.

State outcome: In June 2026 the St. Paul City Attorney’s Office declined to file any Minnesota state charges, stating the evidence did not meet the legal standard for prosecution.

No convictions or final resolutions of the federal cases have been reported as of early September 2026.

text:
September 9, 1913: No Hostility Toward Blease, Says Slaton 

Reading Time: 16 minutes, [2630 words]

The Atlanta Journal,

Tuesday, 9th September 1913,

PAGE 1, COLUMN 6.

Friendly Relations Between Georgia and South Carolina Must Be Maintained

Utterances attributed in the newspapers to Governor Blease to the effect that he had cut off relations with Georgia because Governor Slaton declined to grant his requisition for Julian J. Zachry, the young Augusta attorney, and because former governors had declined to grant requisitions for Thomas E. Felder, the Atlanta attorney, brought forth a statement from Governor Slaton Tuesday morning.

So long as I am governor of Georgia, said Governor Slaton, the requisitions of Governor Blease will be g careful and courteous considering the requisitions of other states. His requisitions are made in the name of South Carolina and the dignity of Georgia demands that they receive proper consideration.

I do not propose to pursue any retaliatory policy toward Governor Blease, and whenever he declines my requisitions, I shall assume that after proper investigation he has, in the line of his duty exercised his best discretion which the constitution of his state empowers and requires him to do.

It would be nothing short of disastrous if through misunderstandings or disagreements there should come an interruption in the cordial and reciprocal relations between Georgia and South Carolina to the end that the criminals of one state might a haven and asylum in the other. This condition of affairs would be most lamentable.

PAGE 1, COLUMN 7

CONLEY IS INDICTED ON TWO COUNTS BY FULTON GRAND JURY

One Bill Charges a Felony in That Knowing Frank Murdered Mary Phagan, He Harbored and Concealed Him

FRANK'S ATTORNEY WILL CITE WILL MEYERS CASE

Decision in This Famous Case Sure to Figure at Hearing For New Trial-Jurors Charged With Bias

Two true bills, one charging Jim Conley with a misdemeanor in concealing knowledge of the murder of Mary Phagan, and the other charging him with felony in being accessory to the murder after the deed, were turned Tuesday morning by the grand jury. The bills were returned after a brief deliberation only, the Conley case being the last taken up by the jury prior to adjournment.

The felony bill says that Conley, Knowing that Leo M. Frank unlawfully and maliciously, with malice aforethought, killed and murdered one Mary Phagan, did conceal the body of Mary Phagan and did receive, harbor and conceal the said Leo M. Frank, and concealed the knowledge of the crime from the officers of the law.

The misdemeanor bill, drawn under another section of the code, charges that Conley, Knowing that Leo M. Frank had unlawfully and with malice aforethought killed and murdered one Mary Phagan, did conceal said knowledge from the magistrate and did harbor and assist and protect Leo M. Frank.

Two bills were drawn because of a technical question as to the exact meaning of the word conceal in the felony bill, the solicitor intending to secure indictment under the felony charge if not on the misdemeanor charge.

The indictment of Leo M. Frank, showing the record of his conviction, was placed before the jury to show that the principal in the crime had been convicted.

Bond in the misdemeanor case was assessed at $1,000 and in the felony case at $4,000; and if Conley can arrange for a $5,000 bond he will be released.

Assistant Solicitor Stephens says that in all probability Conley will be tried on the felony charge instead of the misdemeanor charge; but could not estimate just when the trial would be held.

The maximum sentence in the misdemeanor charge is twelve months on the county gang, or six months in jail, or a fine or all three in the discretion of the judge.

The maximum penalty for the felony is three years' imprisonment.

Attack on Frank Jurors Regarded as Certain

That at least one and perhaps more of the jurors who tried and convicted Leo M. Frank on a charge of a murdering Mary Phagan were biased before they entered the jury box and had previously expressed an opinion that the young factory superintendent was guilty and should be hanged, will be one of the principal contentions for a new trial are made before Judge L. S. Roan on October 4.

Attorneys who represented the accused man in the famous trial are still unceasingly at work on the case and are directing their efforts toward unearthing facts upon which to base an appeal for a new trial.

The eligibility of a travelling salesman who voted for a conviction to serve on the jury is now under fire. Attorney Stiles Hopkins, associated with Attorney Luther Z. Rosser's office, left Atlanta a few days ago for Greensboro, Ga., with the intention of securing affidavits from persons who are said to have overheard remarks made by a salesman who later was a juror. Whether or not he procured the sworn statements is not known. A special dispatch to The Journal from its Greensboro correspondent contained the information that Attorney Hopkins was in that city Monday.

A rumor was afloat in Greensboro to the effect that Mr. Hopkins had three affidavits already in his possession.

(Continued on Page 4, Col. 1.)

PAGE 4, COLUMN 1

CONLEY IS INDICTED ON TWO COUNTS BY FULTON GRAND JURY (Continued From Page 1.)

This could not be affirmed either in the former town or Atlanta.

The rumor that the defense is endeavoring to prove bias on several jurors has been current in Atlanta for several days. Last Saturday night special investigators attached to Attorney Rosser's office interviewed in a local hotel a travelling salesman who is said to have heard of remarks made by one of the jurors. News of the juror's supposed remarks had come to him second-hand, however, and no affidavit was taken from him.

The attack of the defense upon the jury is regarded as vital. On several occasions in the legal history of the south judgements of lower courts have been reversed because it had been shown that jurors who voted for a conviction had previously expressed an opinion that the defendant was guilty.

MEYERS CASE TO FIGURE.

A striking example of this is contained in the opinion of the supreme court of Georgia reversing the judgement of the lower court in the first trial of Will Meyers. This is one of the state's most note criminal cases.

Paragraph No. 2 of this decision deals with this point:

Upon the trial of a criminal case, the mind of every person chosen as a juror should at the time of his selection, with respect to the person and the particular matter under investigation, be, as between the state and the accused, in a position of perfect neutrality and though upon the voir dire they each do qualify as being thus impartial, a verdict of guilty may, nevertheless, be impeached by satisfactory proof that a single juror entered upon the discharge of his duties with a fixed and determined purpose, formed in advance of hearing the evidence, to convict the accused.

The decision continues, saying that the mere reading of newspapers or ephemeral impressions or opinions formed by other means is not necessarily inconsistent with such a state of neutrality as would permit the acceptance of the juror.

Paragraph No. 4 of the Meyer decision deals with a point that is likely to arise if the defense attacks the eligibility of the Frank jurors:

The probative effect of affidavits submitted pro and con upon a motion to set aside a verdict upon the ground prejudice of a juror is ordinarily a matter for the trial court, and where there is upon such an issue a conflict of the evidence, this court will not usually control the discretion of the judge who tried the case if he sustain the verdict, even though, as against the affidavit of a single witness showing prejudice, nothing he offered in reply except that the juror upon voir dire qualified; yet where two witnesses depose with direct circumstantiality to statements and conduct of a person afterwards selected as a juror, made and occurring before the trial, which evidenced a deliberate purpose upon his part to convict the defendant in the event he should be chosen a juror, and no effort is made to discredit such affidavits, even by a contrary statement of the juror as to the facts stated herein or otherwise (he being at the time accessible), the testimony of such witnesses shall be accepted as true, and if supported by evidence that the facts to which they depose were unknown to the accused or his counsel until after the verdict, a new trial should be awarded.

CONFLICT IS LIKELY.

Indications are that the defense will make an attack upon the Frank jury similar to the one made upon the convicting body in the Meyers case. And there is certain to be a conflict of evidence inasmuch as Solicitor Dorsey till has a corps of aides gathering evidence to frustrate the effort of Attorneys Rosser and Reuben R. Arnold to secure a new trial.

If affidavits are presented declaring that one or more of the Frank jurors expressed bias and prejudice before the trial the prosecution is certain to attack these documents and attempt to impeach them. The merits of the attack upon the decision of the trial jury and of Solicitor Dorsey to discredit such an attack will be placed before Judge Roan upon whom will fall the responsibility of determining their legal weight.

In passing upon the question of jury bias in the Meyers case the decision of the supreme court reads:

This defendant was convicted and is now under sentence of death, and upon the verdict of a jury one member of which he complains was not legally competent to try him. He alleges that before the juror entered upon the trial of the case, his individual judgement was concluded by what he had heard against the prisoner, and that this juror entered upon the trial of this case corruptly, with a deliberate purpose to bring about his execution. In support of this ground of the motion, he submitted the testimony of witnesses, two of whom deposed that upon one occasion soon after the commission of the homicide, the person afterwards chosen as a juror stated in their presence that the accused ought to be hung and pointed out a tree upon which the execution should take place. He submitted the testimony of two other witnesses who deposed that, some time after the homicide occurred and after the apprehension of this defendant, this juror stated in their presence with much earnestness and vehemence, that if he were chosen as a juror to try the accused he would sit upon a jury fifty years to break his neck. This juror in response to these several affidavits filed an answer to the first one above referred to only.

After other discussion of this phase of Meyers' motion the supreme court reversed the decision of the lower court and gave Meyers a new trial. He was again convicted, but made his escape from jail before the date set for his execution.

OVER FIFTY GROUNDS.

Attorney Luther Z. Rosser is devoting all of his time to preparing his argument for a new trial before Judge Roan on October 4. His chief associate, Reuben R. Arnold, is still out of the city and the work of compiling the exhaustive motion has made it necessary for Mr. Rosser to put aside virtually all other legal business.

There will be between fifty and one hundred grounds named in the motion for a new trial, it is reliably stated.

Every bit of the evidence is being gone over for flaws and nothing that shows favorably for Frank is being neglected.

The atmosphere of the court room and the alleged apparent hospitality of the crowd will be another important contention of Attorneys Rosser and Arnold. They will claim that the jury was, in a measure, cowed and influenced by the cheering that, on several occasions marked Solicitor Dorsey's efforts to convict the factory superintendent.

ANOTHER MEYER'S PARALLEL.

In the Meyers case is found another striking similarity with this feature. The contention that the defendant in the former case did not get a fair trial on account of the handling of the jury was claimed. Regarding this, the decision reads:

While every person accused of crime is entitled to a public trial. It is not necessary to its legality that a great multitude should be in attendance, and the bar or court room to become so crowded as to impede the progress of the trial rendering it difficult for the jurors to enter or leave the box, or by preventing the free movement of counsel and witnesses; moreover, the jury should not be in such close and constant contact with the audience as that remarks of bystanders as to the guilt or innocence of the accused, or other indications of public feeling for or against him, may reach their ears or come under their observation. The bar at least should at all times be kept sufficiently open and clear for the prompt and orderly dispatch of the business of the court.

PAGE 3, COLUMN 3

MAYOR MUST PAY FOR BEING DICTOGRAPHED

Attorney Rules That Mayor Must Pay for City Dictograph Bill Which Caught him

Mayor Woodward is legally obliged to pay the cost of the installation of the dictograph which was used by the city detective department to overhear conversations between Colonel T. B. Felder, A. S. Colyar, Stenographer Febuary, the mayor himself and others, according to an official opinion of City Attorney J. L. Mayson received by Chief of Police Beavers Tuesday morning.

Mayor Woodward several days ago refused to put his O. K. to the claim, which was presented against the city for this purpose. Also he refused to recognize bills for the rent of the two rooms in Williams House No. 2, the scene of the famous dictograph episode and for expenses sustained by the detective department in getting evidence against blind tigers. The amounts asked in the latter request embodied amounts paid stool pigeons.

City Attorney Mayson's opinion to Chief Beavers was brief. It set forth simply that the claims were entirely legal and that he could find no city ordinance to sustain the non-payment of the bills. He advised Chief Beavers to bring again the bills before council and thus get them before the mayor once more.

The opinion was rendered at the request of Chief Beavers.

PAGE 4, COLUMN 3

PLENNIE MINOR WILL GIVE BIG BARBECUE

Fish Fry Also Will Be Feature of Entertainment on September 13

Plennie Minor, special deputy in the criminal court, has sent out invitations to a big barbecue that will be held September 13 at Germania park.

Deputy Minor will have automobiles at the court house to convey his friends to the park, and the machines will have the corner of Pryor and Mitchell streets promptly at 12:30 o'clock.

A fish fry will also be a feature of the entertainment.

PAGE 5, COLUMN 6

JUDGE ROAN INDORSED FOR FULTON JUDGESHIP

Atlanta Lawyers Urge Governor Slaton to Appoint Well-Known Jurist to Office

A number of Atlanta lawyers, headed by Attorney Eugene R. Black, appeared before Governor Slaton Monday afternoon and urged him to appoint Judge L. S. Roan to the fourth superior court judgeship of the Atlanta circuit, which was created by the last general assembly.

Mr. Black declared to Governor Slaton that many members of the Atlanta Bar association who had signed the petition for the appointment of an Atlanta lawyer had based their action on the theory that Judge Roan was not an Atlanta lawyer. It was pointed out that Judge Roan has been a resident of Atlanta for about a year and that for many years he has, under a special act of the legislature, presided over the criminal division of the Fulton county superior court.

Governor Slaton expressed the hope that the Atlanta Bar association would be able to get together on the appointment, as he desired by all means to have a unanimity of action on the part of the association behind such an appointment.

It’s About Growth, Not a Checklist

Our goal is to let these scriptures transform our perspective and our priorities. If you missed a few days or are just joining us for the first time—don’t worry! Just jump right in with us today. Today’s Reading

In Isaiah 7–8, King Ahaz faces the looming threat of invasion, prompting the prophet Isaiah to deliver a call for steadfast faith rather than fear. God offers a sign to the house of David: a virgin shall conceive and bear a son whose name will be Immanuel—"God with us." As political alliances falter, Isaiah warns the people not to fear what the world fears, but to honor the Lord of hosts as holy, trusting Him as both a sanctuary for the faithful and a stone of stumbling to those who reject His word. Turning to the New Testament, John 7 brings Jesus to Jerusalem during the Feast of Booths amid mounting tension and divided public opinion. On the great day of the feast, Jesus stands and proclaims that anyone who thirsts should come to Him and drink, promising that rivers of living water will flow from the hearts of those who believe in Him, speaking of the Spirit yet to come. text:
Every digital forensics firm in Texas runs the same software.

Cellebrite, Magnet, Axiom. The license doesn't care who's holding it. Push the button, get a report.

That is not what you are hiring.

You are hiring the person who has to sit in the chair and explain, under cross, why the extraction was sound, why the hash matches, why the timeline holds, and why nothing between the seizure and the exhibit changed the file.

That question got harder this year.

In February, New York's highest court reversed the admission of home security video in a 4-3 decision. Nobody proved the video was fake. The proponent simply could not prove it was real. No one who installed or operated the cameras testified. Roughly two and a half years of chain of custody was unaccounted for. Clips were offered instead of the original recording, with no explanation of what was cut. The agent vouching for it had no training in detecting tampering and had never examined the file for it.

In March, the Sixth Circuit sanctioned attorneys $15,000 each for fabricated citations. The sanction made the headlines. The consequence didn't. Judges now start from the possibility that something in a filing is fabricated, and that suspicion moves from the brief to the exhibits.

"My client sent it to me" stopped being an answer.

So the question to ask any forensics vendor, including us, is not which tools they own. It is:
How many times have you been qualified as an expert? When were you last cross-examined, and by whom? Has a report of yours ever been excluded? Can you produce the original file, not the export?

Extraction is a button. Admissibility is a discipline.

Black Dog Forensics. Retrieve the Truth.
