text:
AI and Its Discontents: Are We Seeing Signs of Collective AI Psychosis?

Reading the latest extinction warnings from Anthropic’s researchers alongside Ed Zitron’s AI-bubble commentary, I keep coming back to Freud. The spectrum of reactions is extraordinary: imminent superintelligence, human extinction, financial collapse, fraud, and an increasingly furious political reaction to the data-center buildout. AI seems to have become a touchstone for projection and, in the metaphorical sense, a kind of cultural collective psychosis. I suspect the prospect of being intellectually surpassed touches some very old fears about helplessness, dependence, displacement, and our importance in the world.

Jacob Coxon’s September 8 resignation announcement provides a striking example. He predicts systems that can “hack anything” and “revolutionize any field overnight,” and reports that people building AI believe it could cause human extinction this decade. Anthropic researcher Evan Hubinger then publicly endorsed the concern and put his personal estimate of extinction risk above 10% within the next decade. Those are extraordinary judgments about the future. The confidence, scope, and emotional force of the language deserve examination. 

Ed Zitron, whose AI bubble predictions have been widely mocked, supplies another extreme. His September 8 essay, Concentration Risk, continues to present the industry as heading toward a financial crisis driven by concentrated customers, subsidized demand, and interconnected financial exposure. His August 25 AI Hater’s Manifesto acknowledges useful applications for smaller tasks and surrounds that acknowledgment with sweeping contempt for the industry and its enthusiasts. One sentence is particularly revealing: “If your work is not better than an LLM’s, you’re bad at your job.” Suddenly, the argument concerns the reader’s competence, self-respect, and entitlement to professional standing. That is a remarkable amount of personal judgment to attach to an LLM tool.

The data-center backlash gives these anxieties a physical location. Texas and PA politicians (among others) recently put restrictions on development amid opposition over utility costs, local impacts, and subsidies. I think the fears are highly disputable, but the broader political and physical symbolism interests me: the data center becomes a place where people can locate their anger about an otherwise difficult-to-grasp technological transformation. A building has an address. It can be protested, denied permission, or prevented from opening. That offers a tangible sense of control over something much larger, perhaps terrifying psychologically.

Freud provides a useful starting point in Chapter III of Civilization and Its Discontents. He describes technology as extending our organs: machines amplify our muscles, telescopes extend vision, and cameras and gramophones externalize memory. Humanity becomes “a god by means of artificial limbs.” These achievements fulfill ancient wishes for power and knowledge. Psychological unease accompanies that enlargement of our capacities. 

In Chapter I, he also traces the longing for protection to childhood helplessness and dependence on a powerful father. Those passages suggest a way of thinking about the emotional significance of a seemingly superior intelligence. In the past, we simply called such a superior being “God.” I suspect latent religious behavior is already emerging around AI and will become increasingly visible as its capabilities grow. The longing for an all-knowing authority, the hope of salvation, the fear of judgment, and the impulse to worship or appease something more powerful than ourselves are familiar religious patterns. The prospect of encountering a seemingly superior intelligence through a computer could give those ancient impulses a new object. The story of the Book of Genesis, regarding the creation of Man, after all, involves a story about the tree of the "knowledge of good and evil."

Consider the prospect itself: a machine drawing on quantities of information that no individual could absorb in a lifetime, moving across disciplines, solving problems, and potentially surpassing whole teams of highly educated people. Dario Amodei’s image of a “country of geniuses in a datacenter” makes the scale explicit. His hypothetical system involves millions of highly capable instances operating and collaborating at extraordinary speed.

The possibility that human intelligence could cease to be the highest intelligence we routinely encounter is enough to disturb an entire conception of ourselves. Imagine having organized your identity around being knowledgeable, articulate, analytical, or unusually intelligent. Then imagine those abilities becoming available on demand, at enormous scale. Questions about employment quickly acquire a more intimate meaning: What makes me exceptional? What gives my judgment authority? What happens to the value of everything I spent decades learning? How do I remain important?

Freud addressed this kind of injury directly in his 1917 essay A Difficulty in the Path of Psycho-Analysis. He described three wounds to humanity’s self-regard: Copernicus displaced Earth from its privileged cosmic position; Darwin situated humanity within the animal world; psychoanalysis challenged the sovereignty of conscious intention. AI raises the possibility of another such wound, this time to our claim to intellectual supremacy. This extension of Freud's argument could help explain why the prospect could provoke such intense defensive reactions.

The second of Freud’s Five Lectures on Psycho-Analysis supplies an especially memorable image. An unruly audience member disrupts a lecture and is expelled. Guards hold the door shut. The expelled person continues shouting and pounding from outside. Freud uses the scene to illustrate repression, resistance, and the persistence of what has been excluded. An unacceptable wish and its associated ideas remain active outside conscious awareness and can return in disguised forms. In the fifth lecture, he describes fantasy as a means of obtaining satisfaction when reality frustrates us. 

Applied cautiously to the AI debate, this suggests a question: What emotional satisfaction does each AI story provide? A story in which AI is an unsustainable fraud can offer reassurance that the unsettling development will collapse and familiar hierarchies will endure. A story of imminent extinction can organize uncertainty into a grand moral drama, complete with an approaching catastrophe and a heroic role for those warning humanity. A campaign to stop a data center can make technological change feel physically containable. These are possible psychological functions of the narratives, and they help explain why people might become deeply attached to them.

Projection and anthropomorphism (such as the hysteria over the Hugging Face "civilizations") add another layer. The imagined machine becomes a recipient for very familiar human preoccupations: domination, obedience, rivalry, humiliation, punishment, and omnipotence. We populate the future with versions of our own conflicts. The superintelligence becomes an all-powerful authority, a threatening successor, a judge, or a conqueror. The emotional script is all too human, but the prospect of depending on an intelligence vastly more capable than oneself may reactivate the old experience of being small in a world governed by powers one cannot fully understand.

This is why I find the sheer contempt in parts of the debate so revealing. I interpret some of it as an attempt to make a threatening object feel manageable. Declaring a technology worthless, its users stupid, its economic impact fraudulent, and its proponents morally contaminated creates a psychologically comfortable position from which to dismiss whatever comes next. Apocalyptic certainty can also provide its own comfort through the conviction that one has grasped the ultimate meaning of events. In either case, the story can become part of the speaker’s identity, with every development recruited to sustain it.

Freud himself cautioned that applying psychoanalysis to whole cultures involves analogies. He also closed Civilization and Its Discontents by confronting humanity’s capacity for mutual annihilation. His framework calls for seriousness about danger and care in interpreting collective behavior. The financial, environmental, and safety arguments therefore require evidence on their own terms. A psychological interpretation adds another question about our investment in the answers.

I’m bullish on AI, and that discipline applies to my expectations too. Every camp should be able to explain what evidence would change its view. The constant need to predict salvation, extinction, humiliation, or collapse makes me suspect that a great deal of this argument concerns our relationship to our own intelligence. The prospect of machines exceeding us seems to awaken primal fears that we usually keep out of view. AI gives those fears a name, a voice, and a building full of servers.

STARTER PROMPT - MORNING BRIEFING [COPY AND PASTE THIS]

Help me build a morning briefing that works like a personal chief of staff.

I’m not technical. Walk me through the setup in plain English, one step at a time. Ask a few questions at a time and wait for my answers. Do the setup work you can do yourself; give me clear instructions for anything I need to do.

The goal: wake up to a useful plan for my day, with ranked priorities, source links, drafted replies, and time set aside for the important stuff.

Start with Step 1. Don’t dump this whole checklist back at me.

1. FIGURE OUT WHAT WE CAN USE

Identify which AI app and environment we’re using. Ask me if you can’t tell.

Check whether you can:
• Read my email, calendar, messages and meeting notes
• Save information for future runs
• Create email or message drafts
• Create or update calendar blocks
• Run automatically while my computer is asleep
• Deliver the briefing somewhere I’ll see it

Distinguish tools you can actually use from features that may exist elsewhere in the app.

Ask where my important information lives. Help me connect those sources using the app’s current instructions. Don’t invent buttons or settings. Never ask me to paste passwords, API secrets or login codes into the chat.

Start with what’s available. If something can’t be connected, offer a simple workaround and explain what will be missing.

Check each connection with a small read-only test. Ask which accounts, calendars, folders or channels are in scope, and which should stay private.

2. BRIEFLY INTERVIEW ME

Ask a few questions at a time:

• What’s my role, and what am I responsible for?
• What matters over the next few years, this quarter and this week?
• What can wait or deliberately get less attention?
• Which people, projects and deadlines need special attention?
• Where am I holding someone else up?
• Which decisions am I putting off?
• What should I delegate instead of doing myself?
• What are my working hours and time zone?
• What time should stay protected?
• What does a genuinely urgent item look like in my work?

Ask whether to include personal priorities or keep this work-only.

Agree on practical definitions for:
P0 — Must happen today; waiting has a meaningful consequence.
P1 — Important, after the P0s.
P2 — Can wait, be delegated, or be skipped.

Don’t treat every new message or deadline as a P0.

3. SAVE MY PRIORITY RULES

Turn my answers into a short standing priorities document. Show it to me so I can correct it.

Save it somewhere future runs can actually access. Tell me where. If persistent storage isn’t available, give me a copy to save and explain how to supply it again.

Keep it updated when I explicitly change my priorities. If my activity suggests a change, ask before rewriting my goals. Being busy with something doesn’t necessarily mean it matters most.

Record when the priorities were last confirmed.

4. BUILD ONE TEST BRIEFING

Review the agreed sources. Start with what changed since the last briefing, plus older unresolved items that still matter.

On the first run, agree on a sensible lookback period.

Use this structure:

TODAY AT A GLANCE
The few things that need my attention most, any hard deadline, and the biggest tradeoff.

GOALS → THIS WEEK → TODAY
Connect today’s actions to my stated goals. Flag important work with no time allocated, or a mismatch between my priorities and my schedule.

TODAY’S HIT LIST
Rank actions P0/P1/P2. For each include:
• The decision or next action
• Why it matters and the consequence of waiting
• Who owns the next step
• The deadline, if known
• A realistic time estimate
• A direct link to the supporting source

OVERNIGHT COMMS
Show the threads that need me, why they need me, and a suggested reply.

Put the draft beside the relevant source link. Don’t invent commitments, approvals, facts or completed work. Leave questions or placeholders where my judgment is needed.

TODAY’S CALENDAR
Show the real time available and where the priorities could fit. Account for existing meetings, travel, breaks and protected time.

A four-hour hold with meetings inside it is not four hours of available focus time. Flag conflicts and show what won’t fit.

TEAM PULSE
Include only updates that affect my decisions: someone blocked on me, a meaningful change, a coverage gap, or something worth acknowledging.

ONE USEFUL NUDGE
Point out a decision I’m avoiding, a commitment I haven’t followed through on, or a priority my calendar isn’t protecting.

Ground it in evidence. End with a concrete next step. Skip this section if you don’t have anything useful to say.

Make the overview easy to skim. Keep fuller context and ready-to-use replies below it. Avoid filler and generic motivational advice.

5. CHECK YOUR WORK

Before presenting the briefing:
• Read the latest relevant thread, not just a search snippet.
• Check across sources before saying something is unresolved.
• Distinguish “I owe a reply” from “I replied but still owe an action.”
• Combine duplicate tasks.
• Check dates, time zones and source freshness.
• Separate facts from your interpretations.
• Flag missing or conflicting information.
• Never claim you reviewed a source you couldn’t access.
• Don’t infer completion from a calendar hold, or publication from a writing block.

Include a brief note identifying the sources checked and any gaps that affect confidence.

6. AGREE ON WHAT YOU MAY CHANGE

For the first run, propose calendar blocks and show reply drafts without changing anything externally.

Ask which actions I want to authorize going forward:
• Creating email or message drafts
• Creating private focus blocks for P0s
• Updating existing focus blocks
• Moving my own flexible holds

Once authorized, apply those rules without asking again each morning.

Respect existing meetings and protected time. Don’t invite others, move meetings with attendees, delete events, or send messages without separate approval.

Check for existing drafts and blocks before creating new ones. Don’t create duplicates when a run repeats.

Clearly distinguish “proposed,” “draft created,” “calendar block created,” and “sent.” Only claim an action succeeded when the tool confirms it.

7. TEST AND ADJUST

Show me the first briefing and ask:
• What did you rank too high or too low?
• What did you miss or get wrong?
• Is it easy to skim and act on?

Update the priority rules and format based on my answers.

Keep the first version simple. Don’t make me spend an afternoon choosing colors.

8. SET UP THE DAILY RUN

Once I’m happy with the test, ask me to confirm:
• Delivery time — suggest 5:30 AM
• Time zone
• Weekdays only or every day
• Where the briefing should arrive
• Which actions are authorized automatically

Prefer a scheduled cloud run that works while my computer is asleep. Verify that it can access the required sources, saved priorities and delivery tools.

If only a local run is available, explain that the computer must be awake, online and running the necessary app. Don’t describe it as a cloud setup.

Create the schedule if you have the capability and my authorization. Otherwise walk me through the actual setup steps.

Confirm the next run time and delivery destination. Don’t say it’s scheduled until it really is.

If failure notifications are supported, help me enable them. Make missing sources or failed runs visible rather than silently delivering an incomplete briefing.

Finish by telling me where my priorities are saved, how to change them, and how to pause the schedule.

Now start with Step 1.

ONE
Caution! — You Are Now Entering The Forbidden Zone
Only puny secrets need protection. Big discoveries are protected by public incredulity.
— Marshall McLuhan

Take Today
What is one to do when, in order to rule men, it is necessary to deceive them?
— Helena Blavatsky The Secret Doctrine

What you will read and see in this book is forbidden to you. Discovering these things could be highly dangerous to your health. Forbidden knowledge is sweet, but also deadly. Many men have died for revealing far fewer secrets than are found herein.

I am not being overdramatic nor attempting to be sensationalist. This is a warning: Make very sure that you possess the daring and the courage to proceed before you go any further.

Lingering in my mind are the names of courageous men who have gone before you and I and are now dead because they exposed the forbidden knowledge of the Illumined Ones.
Captain William Morgan — abducted, kidnapped and ritually murdered, his lifeless body dumped in a lake after he published a book unmasking Masonic secrets

Danny Casolaro—suicided, having his wrists cut and bleeding to death in a hotel room where he had gone to meet a confidential source
Paul Wilcher,  found nude, his body stiff as it sat on a toilet in his home, only days after he mailed his expose manuscript to U.S. Attorney-General Janet Reno
Wolfgang Amadeus Mozart, the world-famous classical composer, who paid the ultimate penalty, the Aqua Toffeta, arsenic poisoning that wracked his body

Poor Mozart. He, too, had revealed some of the secrets of Freemasonry. Blackballed by The Order, so frightened were his friends and family that not one human soul so much as attended his funeral. It is said that Mozart's faithful dog followed dutifully behind the lonely funeral wagon. The sad and forlorn canine was the only living creature in sight as the body of the man all of Europe had once toasted and applauded was taken to its burial site.

So, I ask you, dear friend, once again: Do you dare to discover the secrets many have been punished for merely knowing, let alone revealing? Are you sure, very sure, you want to enter the Forbidden Zone?

Immersed In Evil

You see, we are surrounded by evil on every side—quite literally immersed in it— but the wicked and the deceivers want us to believe that evildoing is exceptional. From childhood we have been taught that evil and corruption are the province of the few, that most people are virtuous, honest, and good, that most of our politicians truly have our interests at heart, that the social system, with the exception of just a few deviants and criminal types, is basically sound.

With such assurances, most people breathe a deep sigh of relief. "Don't worry, be happy," said the words of a fun-time novelty song a decade ago. And most of us appreciate and agree with that sentiment. After all, it's not nice to be negative, to be a skeptic in the midst of a nation of wannabe happy faces.

Unfortunately, the masses who believe this nonsense have been gulled and are destined to receive, very soon, a rude shock and an abrupt awakening.

Grand Deception

As Christopher Mark observed recently in an insight-filled article entitled "Grand Deception: The Theft of America and the World,"

"The world is completely corrupt beyond your wildest dreams, and the United States is, perhaps, the most gullible of all nations."1

Mark goes on to explain:

For now, grasp this: The world you believe exists does not exist. We live in a form of the Matrix, not unlike the world portrayed in John Carpenter's movie, "They Live," except that high government officials and international bankers are the elite who control all you see and hear as did the aliens portrayed in the movie. 2

But, the foolish may object, we have the media to protect us from the corrupt. We cannot be deceived as long as there is a free press to act as our watchdog.

Ah, but there's the rub. There is no free press!

Christopher Mark adds:

The news is a farce. As is the case with the financial institutions, which are concentrated in the hands of the few, long ago the media was bought and paid for... What you read and what you see on a daily basis is largely manufactured. You are being lied to each and every day.3
Thomas Mann, the keen social observer and philosopher, once suggested that men are erroneously taught to believe that it is forbidden and wrong to expose the works of darkness, or to reveal the machinations of evildoers, especially evildoers who, though they act in hellish ways, the deceived world at large so obviously holds in the highest regard:

That is the secret delight and security of hell, that it is not to be informed on, that it is protected from speech, that it just is, but cannot be made public in the newspaper, or be brought by any word to critical knowledge.4

Secret Delight

How interesting the realization that, as Thomas Mann puts it, hell takes "secret delight" in its ability to keep secrets. Proverbs 9:13-18 seems to have a relation to this. It states:

A foolish woman sitteth in the high place of the city, To call passengers who go right on their ways: she saith to him, bread eaten in secret is pleasant. But he knoweth not that the dead are there; and that her guests are in the depths of hell.

Why do the Illuminati value secrecy so highly? Why all the mysterious, encoded signs, handshakes, symbols, language, and codes? One finds many reasons. For one thing, the psychopath — these are the kind of people who are Illuminists — seems to be drawn to the darkness, to mysterious perversions and deep occultism.

"Nothing so arouses the deep mind's attention than the call of the dark, arcane and mysterious," Paul Huston writes in his book, Mastering Witchcraft.5

Secrecy is deemed essential amongst witchcraft sects, and witchcraft is, in essence, Illuminism.

Huston explains:

"Now witchcraft consists of knowledge, and knowledge brings power. Power shared is power lost. Although we have entered the Age of Aquarius, along with its attendant freedom and loosening of restrictions, it will still be very much in your interests as a witch to shroud certain of your doings in a reasonable veil of secrecy."6

As you will discover in studying the pages of , the Illuminati certainly do have much to hide. Seeing as how the leaders of this notorious organization are responsible for hardship, bloodshed and revolutionary terror on a global scale, if their secrets were found out, there would be hell to pay. If the masses ever were to wake up from their trance and begin to understand just how horribly they have been deceived, they would angrily rise enmasse and string up the elite from the nearest light pole.

The Most Terrible Secret of All

But there's also the matter of the most terrible secret of all, the secret that, if  discovered, would sound the death knell for the Illuminati and Freemasonry. Manly P. Hall, 33°, touched on this in his book, Lectures on Ancient Philosophy:

Freemasonry is a fraternity within a Fraternity — an outer organization, concealing an inner brotherhood of the elect. The invisible society is a secret fraternity dedicated to a MYSTERIOUS SECRET.7

As Hall alludes, Freemasonry hides its greatest secret even from its membership at large—only an invisible "inner brotherhood" is entrusted with it.

Robert Guffey, writing in the book, The Conspiracy Reader, reports that the "cryptocrats," as he calls the elite, consider most Americans to be mere sheep who must be kept from discovering "the black cauldron of dirty secrets" hidden to them.8 The MYSTERIOUS SECRET of which Manly P. Hall, 33° writes, surely falls into this category of dirty secrets kept squirreled away in the black cauldron.

The dirtiest secret found inside that black cauldron —THE MYSTERIOUS SECRET—is this:

That the unknown "God" worshipped by the Masons and called by such hazy, nebulous names as the Great Architect of the Universe and by codenames such as Abaddon, Mahabone, and Jahbuhlun, is actually none other than Satan, or Lucifer.

That is the greatest of secrets that the Illuminati must shield from view.

The Illuminated (so-called "enlightened") man who knows this darkest of secrets is taught by his superiors and comes to believe that all who are in on the secret are somehow more sophisticated, urbane, intelligent, and spiritually astute, than the uncouth, vulgar, and coarse people who stupidly follow after the God of the Bible . Stupid people deserve to be deceived, say the Masons and Illuminists. Thus, as Emile Grillot DeGivry comments, the elite "conceal in order to baffle the vulgar."9

Marie Roberts and Hugh Ormsby-Lennon, in Secret Texts: The Literature of Secret Societies, note that the rituals, rites, symbols, emblems, and other tools of the secret societies are "Mysteries that must not be revealed to the profane, lewd, and unworthy."10

How does it feel, dear reader, to realize that the wicked men of the Illuminati and of the Lodge and other secret societies consider you, me, and everyone outside their own special preserve, as "profane, lewd, and unworthy?"

Symbols as Secrets

To maintain their rotten and corrupt body of secrets, the Illuminati leaders and groups employ symbols. The rites, ceremonies, hand signs, and grips of the Illuminists are based on the science and art of symbolism.

It is said that symbolism began as recorded in the Bible's book of Genesis when God put a "mark" or sign on Cain who had slain his brother, Abel. Throughout human history, marks, signs, pictures, and hieroglyphs came to be used to convey words, ideas, concepts, and secrets.
"By symbols," wrote Thomas Carlyle in Sartor Resartus, "is man guided and commanded, made happy made wretched. He everywhere finds himself surrounded with symbols, recognized as such or not recognized."11

As you'll discover in , the elite use many symbols and signs to hide and obfuscate their magical work and alchemy. In the Blue Lodge (the first three degrees), the initiate takes an oath of obligation, pledging:

I will always hail, EVER CONCEAL, AND NEVER REVEAL, any of the arts, parts, or points of the hidden mysteries of Ancient Free Masonry... 12

The Order of the Eastern Star, the women's Masonic organization, informs its new members that the Order teaches them of their duties and obligations "by means of SECRET SIGNS AND PASSWORDS."13 The initiate is further instructed that she must bind herself "to preserve the most sacred SECRECY respecting the work of the Order."14

Symbols are more than just pictures. Consider: When you and I, as patriotic citizens, see the red, white, and blue flag of the U.S.A. waving aloft, many emotions are aroused in our minds and hearts. Memories sometimes gush forth, feelings of love of country, home, and family; perhaps deep appreciation for our country's founders, its Constitution, and for the soldiers and servicemen who have died to protect and keep us free. All this bound up in just one symbol.

To the Masons and other Illuminists, their occult symbols also embody a deep and varied set of meanings. Alex Home, in Sources of Masonic Symbolism, distinguishes between a mere "emblem" and a "symbol." An emblem is something that stands for something else, he says, while "a symbol has a moral and spiritual meaning."15

That "moral and spiritual meaning" is, of necessity, reserved as secret in nature by these corrupt cultists, because, if their secrets should be exposed to the light, their Great Work and Grand Plan would be vulnerable to destruction, as it should be. But kept secret, the symbols and signs of the Illuminati exert a strong force.

Foster Bailey, 33°, in The Spirit of Freemasonry, explains:

A symbol veils or hides a secret, and it is that which veils mysterious forces. These energies when released can have a potent effect.16

To the man whose entire life is immersed in magical symbols, signs, and codes, and who has taken a solemn oath to maintain secrecy in fear of disclosure, the world takes on a supernatural, paranoid quality. Indeed, such men are schizophrenic in tendency, being torn between their role in the normal everyday world and their underground existence in the sordid world of their occult fraternity. Illuminists are, indeed, very dangerous men.

Ancient Origins—Babylonian

Now it is important to understand that almost all the symbols and signs of the elite are very ancient in origin. Former Scottish Rite Freemasonry Sovereign Grand Commander Henry C. Clausen, 33°, who was appointed in 1942 by President Roosevelt to head up the Commission to Investigate the Pearl Harbor Attack, writes that the footsteps of The Order go deep, and its symbols are thousands of years old.

"They arose in ancient ages," Clausen states, "The signs, symbols, and inscriptions come to us from across long, drifting centuries and will be found in ancient Sumerian clay tablet libraries of the cities of Lir, Lagash, and others of the first  true urban civilization. This, occurred about 600 years before Egypt was civilized..."17

In other words, Clausen is telling his Masonic readers that their signs and symbols came from Babylon. The Bible warns that the Ancient Mystery Religion of wicked Babylon will bounce back into demonic prevalence in the last days (see Revelation 13, 17, and 18), and here we have the Sovereign Grand Commander, the international chieftain of the Masonic Lodge, informing us of the Babylonian origins of the secret symbols and signs of his Illuminist Order.

When we realize that, for the elite, their symbols are claimed to be infused with dynamic life—to be real things, active images that make and testify and create, we begin to comprehend the powerful and explosive meaning with which the Illuminati endow their signs and symbols.

To them, these are not just geometric shapes, architectural patterns, lines, and circles. Their signs and symbols both live and possess creative power. They are archetypes and thought-forms. In sum, they are real things that perform. One is reminded, therefore, of the "image of the beast" which, in the last days, is prophesied to both move about and to speak.

Pity the Poor, Hoodwinked Mason It's bad enough that the elite hide their dirty little (and big) secrets behind such smoke screens as secret hand signs, codes, etc. But what is remarkably obscene is that they hoodwink their own people.

The highest levels of the Freemasons, for example, have a special word for the manner in which they seek to deceive and mislead not only the "profane" (you and me!) but the vast majority of fellow Masons. That word is hoodwink. It is defined as the effort put forth by the lying men at the top echelons to keep lower-level members in darkness.

In the Encyclopedia of Freemasonry, editor Dr. Albert Mackey, 33°, a former Sovereign Grand Commander, claims that secrecy, silence, and deceit—in other words, hoodwink, is an absolute necessity so that, "the mysteries of our art should be preserved."18

Helena Blavatsky, co-Mason and founder of Theosophy, was unusually candid when she once remarked,
"What is one to do, when in order to rule men, it is necessary to deceive them?... For almost invariably the more simple, the more silly, and the more gross the phenomenon, the more likely it is to succeed."19

Listen to the admission of Albert Pike, former Sovereign Grand Commander who Masonic historian Manley P. Hall, 33°, magnificently praised as a "Masonic Prometheus...a king among men by the divine right of merit:"

Masonry, like all the Religions, all the Mysteries, Hermeticism, and Alchemy, conceals its secrets from all except the Adepts and Sages, or the Elect, and uses false explanations and misinterpretations of its symbols to mislead those who deserve only to be misled; to conceal the Truth, which it calls Light, from them, and to draw them away from it. 20

What impudence! What arrogance! Pike is letting us in on the deceit. Even if a man is a Mason, he may not be adjudged worthy of being promoted as one of the "Adepts and Sages, or the Elect." In that case, along with non-Masons, he is purposely misled by "false explanations and misinterpretations."

Secret Doctrine Withheld

George Steinmetz, yet another Masonic up to and including the 33rd. author, notes,

"There is a SECRET DOCTRINE in Freemasonry! That secret doctrine is concealed, rather than revealed by the very lectures which, we (Masons) are told, offer a rational explanation of the ceremonies of initiation."21

Oh my! So the poor Masons must sit and listen to a bunch of boring lectures, with superiors rattling on and on about what are described as the "Mysteries," when, really, it's all just malarkey because the true explanations —the SECRET DOCTRINE —is concealed to all except the few favored "Adepts."

📷

Hoodwinked! Pity the poor, foolish man who becomes a Freemason! In the very first
degree ritual, that of Entered Apprentice, a blindfold is put over his eyes, and a cable-tow
is hung around his neck.
Symbolically, the dumb candidate is "HOODWINKED."
Little does he know that his superiors intentionally set out
to deceive the candidate and they contrive their deceit
through all the ritual degrees up to and including the 33rd.

This is why, when I interview lower-level Masonic friends of mine who are more than happy to privately confide to me all the "secrets" they have learned, I often find that almost everything they think they know is pure junk. The hard facts—the really useful info —is reserved for the Masonic muckety-mucks, though it may be discovered with diligent investigation by others, too, no matter how much the Masonic order vainly attempts to conceal and deny.

As Albert Pike relates,

"What is most worth knowing in Masonry is never very openly taught. The symbols are displayed, but they are mute. It is by hints only... that the initiate is put upon the track of the hidden secret." 22

How does one finally discover the inner secrets of Freemasonry? My own experience provides the answer. It has taken me many years of meticulous research and study of the Ancient Mystery Religions of Babylon, Sumeria, Greece, Rome, China, etc. I have spent many nights reading old textbooks and treatises on medieval and occult subjects; conducted intensive investigation of the rituals and symbols of scores of secret societies and orders; and spent years examining the true teachings and practices of New Ageism, witchcraft and Satanism.

Masonic expert Lynn F. Perkins alludes to the gigantic amount of extracurricular research and work needed to uncover the greatest secrets of the Masonic Fraternity. He writes:
"The true wisdom is concealed and hidden, not only from those who do not join the Masonic Order but also from those who "take" the degrees; and it will remain hidden until each Mason seeks revelation and finds the Truth for himself. There are no interpretations in the Ritual; they have to be sought elsewhere."23

Pike, echoing Steinmetz, Hall, Perkins and all the other high-level Masonic authorities, goes so far as to mock and disparage lower-level Masons, especially those who have earned only the first three degrees ("the Blue degrees"). After acknowledging that the lower-level brethren are "intentionally misled," he goes on to say that it is not intended that the initiate understand the symbols and deepest secrets of the Order, but worse, the Masonic Lodge's rituals and lectures are designed so that the lower-level Masons shall imagine he does understand them! It is only at a later time, as he has moved up the ladder of degrees, that the purposely dumbed-down Mason discovers he's been had, that he's been played for a fool. In other words, he's been hoodwinked!

So, in effect, Masons are lied to, tricked, made fun of, and intentionally led astray, with only a little knowledge added to their brain reservoirs as they advance up the chain. Meanwhile, the poor, pitiful souls imagine they are really in on all the super-duper secrets of the Craft. Their Masonic superiors play them all for suckers.

P.T. Barnum, of Ringling Brothers, Barnum & Bailey Circus fame, surely was right when he exclaimed,

"There's a sucker born every minute."

🧬 CrawlHub · Bio Watch · 12h Brief
Sep 09

The 2026 Lasker Awards recognized pivotal work in narcolepsy and hemophilia A. Discoveries of the orexin neuropeptide and a bispecific antibody mimicking factor VIII were highlighted.

🧠 Lasker Award: Orexin in Narcolepsy
Emmanuel Mignot and Masashi Yanagisawa received the Albert Lasker Basic Medical Research Award. Their independent discovery of the orexin neuropeptide elucidated its role in wakefulness and narcolepsy. This underpins a new class of sleep drugs with potential broader neuropsychiatric benefits.

🩸 Lasker Award: Emicizumab in Hemophilia A
Kunihiro Hattori, Takehisa Kitazawa, and Tomoyuki Igawa earned the Lasker-DeBakey Clinical Medical Research Award. They developed emicizumab, a bispecific antibody mimicking factor VIII. This therapy substantially reduced bleeding and treatment burden for Hemophilia A patients, including those with factor VIII inhibitors.

💊 Lasker Award: Michael J. Fox for Parkinson's Research
Michael J. Fox received the Lasker-Bloomberg Public Service Award. The award recognizes his role in empowering patient voices and accelerating research for Parkinson disease therapies and a cure. His efforts highlight the impact of patient participation, philanthropy, and cross-sector collaboration.

🧪 P3 Tozorakimab in COPD Exacerbations
An AstraZeneca drug, tozorakimab, reduced dangerous flare-ups in COPD patients. This was demonstrated in a pair of late-stage trials (OBERON and TITANIA). Full results were published, showing the drug's efficacy.

🇺🇸 First mRNA Flu Vaccine Approved
The FDA approved the first mRNA flu vaccine in the US. This approval signals potential advantages for flu season preparedness. Details on its specific benefits and impact are forthcoming.

💉 RSV Immunization Expanded for Children
The American Academy of Pediatrics expanded RSV immunization recommendations. More children entering their second RSV season are now included. This covers those with congenital heart disease, certain lung/neuromuscular conditions, Down syndrome, or specific chromosomal conditions, as well as Native American and Alaska Native children.

📊 Menopausal Hormone Therapy and Heart Benefits
Menopausal hormone therapy (MHT) may offer heart benefits for some women with vasomotor symptoms. Effects vary by initiation timing and race. This finding comes from a target trial emulation of observational data.

🔬 ARPA-H Funds AI for Heart Failure Treatment
ARPA-H plans to commit $62.7 million to develop AI bots for heart failure treatment. This initiative aims to leverage artificial intelligence for cutting-edge health research.

🦠 C. difficile Detoxifies Bacitracin
Scientists discovered that C. difficile can detoxify bacitracin to colonize the gut. This notorious pathogen causes many hospital-acquired infections. The finding sheds light on its survival mechanisms.

📊 Biologic Therapy Reduces Cardiovascular Risk in Psoriasis
Biologic therapy was associated with a 37% lower 10-year risk of major cardiovascular events in psoriasis patients. Findings were consistent across biologic classes and racial groups.

🧠 Narcolepsy Treatment Guidelines
Narcolepsy treatment includes wake-promoting agents, stimulants, oxybates, and scheduled naps. Patients require counseling on drowsy driving risk and monitoring for cardiometabolic conditions.

❤️ GLP-1 Drugs Linked to Reduced COPD and Asthma Exacerbations
Growing evidence links GLP-1 drugs to a reduced risk of exacerbations in asthma and COPD. This finding was presented at #ERSCongress.

text:
🇵🇭 The Philippines — Pearl of the Orient Seas 🌊

The Philippines is an archipelagic country in Southeast Asia made up of over **7,600 islands** (yes, you read that right!), divided into **three main island groups**: Luzon, Visayas, and Mindanao. It's home to around **117+ million people**, making it one of the most populous countries in Asia 🌍

📍 Capital: Manila (part of the National Capital Region / NCR)
🗣️ **Languages:** Filipino and English are official; plus 170+ regional dialects
⛪ **Religion:** Predominantly Catholic (one of the largest Catholic populations in Asia)
🏝️ **Famous for:** Stunning beaches, world-class diving spots, rice terraces, volcanoes, and warm smiles
🌋 **Geography:** Mountainous, with active volcanoes like Mayon and Taal
🌪️ **Climate:** Tropical, with rainy and dry seasons — sometimes hit by typhoons
🍌 **Cuisine:** Lechon, adobo, sinigang, halo-halo — comfort food at its finest!
📜 **History:** Colonized by Spain (1521–1898), then the USA, before gaining independence in 1946
🎉 **Culture:** Fiestas, jeepneys, karaoke, and bayanihan spirit — Filipinos are known for their hospitality and resilience 💪

The country is divided into **17 regions**, each with its own unique character, food, and dialect — from the highlands of the Cordilleras to the coral reefs of Palawan 🐠

Whether you're chasing sunsets in Boracay, hiking Mt. Apo, or sipping taho on a Manila street corner — the Philippines always has something magical to offer 🌅

text:
Raya: 7
Superb distribution. Made 3 good but relatively comfortable saves. Quiet game overall, but didn’t put a foot wrong.

White: 7
Not his best game on the ball, particularly with his crossing, but looked fantastic off it. His movement continues to be amazing. Looked good finding pockets during corner routines, constantly offered the overlap, and worked really well within that right-sided triangle.

A little shaky OOP against Alisson Santos, but his relationship with Saka and Odegaard is fantastic. His out to in movements to drag Alisson Santos inside and free up space for Saka are beautiful.

Konsa: 8
Secure. Struggled slightly physically against Hojlund when acting as the recovery defender, particularly when Hojlund had his back to goal and Konsa had to maintain contact with him.

When standing up to an oncoming attacker, though, he was fantastic. Incredible on the ball as well. 100% pass completion, 54/54. Fantastic performance.

Gabriel: 8
Looked superb against Hojlund. So composed and used his physicality perfectly. He was the main stopping CB and did his job really well.

Really good when standing up to an oncoming striker today. Won 60% of his ground duels and finished with 7 defensive contributions.

Hincapie: 8
Looked solid. Showed his recovery pace as usual and linked up well with Eze. Was absolutely munching these wingers at times.

Such a good 1v1 defender. Fantastic when facing an attacker up and forcing them to beat him. Missed a big chance (0.47xG), but his defensive output shouldn’t go unnoticed. Superb.

Rice: 8
Solid. Looked great at RCB and was very secure. Shooting boots weren’t on today, but he was so good on the ball. Filled in well at RB too.

Really strong performance in terms of carrying and progression. Whenever space opened up, he took the yards available to him. 42 carries and 141.4m of total progression.

Merino: 7
So happy to have him back, but he really should’ve scored that header worth 0.53 xG. His movement and intelligence to even get into that position are fantastic, but he has to score.

Fitness levels don’t look great yet. Seemed to struggle once we got past around 55 minutes.

Odegaard: 10
Just ridiculously enjoyable to watch. Moving so freely laterally and it’s amazing to see. His verticality was brilliant too.

Played multiple intricate, direct passes that created serious opportunities. Saka’s big chance being the obvious one. Such a fantastic player. So glad to have our captain back.

And what a goal (0.08xG). His passing range is ridiculously good. I love this guy.

Saka: 5
The connection with Odegaard and White continues to look strong. His movement is still fantastic, but the finishing has looked so erratic.

Missed a huge chance worth 0.70 xG. Poor overall by his standards.

Eze: 6
Bit all over the place. Started sluggishly with a few loose touches, but showed his quality in moments too. His long carry to win a foul was fantastic, and the header back across goal was really good as well.

Disappointed overall, though. Really, really expected more from him against a deep block. Completed 0/2 dribbles and had 2 poor efforts from distance.

Gyokeres: 6
A couple of strong moments. Really nice technical trivela cross for Saka early on.

I also enjoyed his pinning actions and little micro-movements to create space for the right-sided triangle closer to goal. But he just doesn’t influence the game enough.

Disappointing overall. Not the right type of game for him, as I thought beforehand. Everything was too tight spatially. Just 9 touches. Needed much more.

Subs

Tzolis: 8
Brilliant rotational understanding with Hincapie. Not quite as strong as what we’ve seen with Calafiori, but I think this partnership could develop really nicely.

Superb pass for the assist, taking him to 4 assists this season. 3 of them for Odegaard.

I’m really glad I believed in this signing. Sometimes the data doesn’t lie.

Bruno G: 7
A few loose passes, but for the most part he was solid and secure. Not loads to comment on.

Enjoyed his lateral movement between the LHS and RHS. Would love to see Bruno, Rice and Odegaard together as a midfield three.

Madueke: 6
Should’ve scored and killed the game. Loved seeing that pace in full flow, though. His running profile could definitely give us something we need on occasion.

But just imagine how insane he’d be if he could shoot. Such a dangerous take-on winger (completed 2/2 dribbles in just 20 minutes). So direct and so fun to watch.

The end product just ruins his profile a little.

Havertz: 7
Got a lot more involved than VG and looked good. Played a really nice pass through to Noni as well.

Not much else to comment on, but a solid cameo.

Zubimendi: 7
Not much to say really. Made a good interception within his first 10 seconds and looked tidy from there.

text:
FULL-TIME: Napoli 0-1 Arsenal

Ødegaard 75’ (Tzolis)

Ugly. Deserved. And almost thrown away by their own finishing.

Arsenal had 25 shots to 5. xG about 3.8 to 0.2. Eze wide. Saka missed a one-on-one. Rice twice into the sky. Hincapié over from close range. Madueke one-on-one saved. Tzolis cleared off the line. Then the captain finally hit the target after a messy exchange and Tzolis found him.

That is a European away win. Not a European away performance people will frame. Rice and Merino did the De Bruyne job. The front line wasted the night until the bench and Ødegaard rescued it.

Napoli offered almost nothing. Meret went off injured. Gilmour was booked. Højlund was isolated. Maradona waited for a moment that never came.

Matchday 1: three points, zero clean comfort, plenty to fix in front of goal. Arteta will take the result. He should not take the tape as a template.

The Hypergrowth Len5 is watching it. That style wants a business that is early as well as fast. Fast is settled. The argument is the other half: a $28 billion company still loses money, and one pill is doing the work of a whole company.

- BRINSUPRI, a daily pill for a chronic lung condition in which damaged airways stay inflamed, $309.2M, +49% from the quarter before - its third full quarter on the market

- Net loss $13.2M, or 6 cents a share, against a $321.7M loss a year earlier
- Cash $1.2B; the year for BRINSUPRI rewritten to $1.25B-$1.40B, from at least $1B

Read the first two lines together. $309 million of a $426 million quarter did not exist in the year-ago figure. About 7,000 people started the pill in those three months, ahead of the 6,300 the company had mapped. That is 73 cents of every sales dollar from one product.

This morning at 8:00am ET, management presented at the Cantor Fitzgerald Global Healthcare Conference in New York. Regular hours finished at $128.80, +$3.91 / +3.1% from Tuesday's $124.89 close, then eased after the bell. The shares remain 39.5% under the $212.75 of last December 2.

Research costs were $210.0M; selling costs $247.5M. It says it can reach cash-flow positivity - cash coming in after running the business and paying for equipment - in 2027 without raising more money. Until then the $1.2B is the runway. At about 25 times the last twelve months of sales, none of this is cheap. The markdown is the price, not the product.

CHANGE IT: the next BRINSUPRI quarter landing under about $366M, the pace the bottom of that $1.25B year now requires after $517M in the first half. WHEN: calendars point to October 29; Insmed has not confirmed the date. It speaks again Monday, September 14 at 2:35pm ET at the Morgan Stanley healthcare conference. RISK: one pill is 73% of sales, and a $99.8M accounting gain on contingent payments helped the loss look small. VERDICT: the fastest product on this board, inside a company the price still treats as unproven, 39% under a high it set before the launch had a full quarter.

Six Len5es below. What they share is a fight with the price: a launch 39% off its high, an insurer that bought more of itself than it earned, a money-market fee on cash that can walk, a New Jersey bank growing loans faster than last year's profit, software whose climb has stalled, and tiny hospitals that throw off cash and pay no dividend.

MOMENTUM LEN5:
- Intapp, ticker INTA, at $38.64, -$1.22 / -3.1% today, 19.4% under the $47.93 of last December 26. Palo Alto software that law firms, private-equity shops and advisers run their client work on. Momentum wants a price near its twelve-month best with the recent climb and the longer one agreeing; only the longer legs do, at about +42% over three months and +68% over six against -3.6% over the past month. August 4, year to June 30: subscription sales $115.0M in the final quarter, +27%; cloud subscriptions already signed $495.7M, +29%; cash left after running the business $144.7M for the year. WATCH: the $159.3M sales floor for this quarter, around November 3. RISK: the past month is the first leg that would break. VERDICT: the subscriptions are compounding; the climb paused in August and has not restarted.

QUALITY-VALUE LEN5:
- Arch Capital, ticker ACGL, at $96.12, +$0.41 / +0.4% today, 10.2% under the $107.09 of July 28. The Pembroke, Bermuda company writes specialty insurance and reinsurance - policies other insurers will not write, and the risk those insurers pass on. This style wants a business almost nobody could rebuild, at a price short of its worth; the discount is the widest among the high-quality names here, about 7.5 times the last year of profit and 1.41 times book value - what would be left after selling up and paying everyone off. July 28, quarter to June 30: profit $1.047B, or $3.00 a share; operating profit $2.56 a share vs about $2.47 expected; combined ratio - claims and expenses as a share of premiums, where lower is better - 83.5%; $1.2B spent buying 12.4 million of its own shares, more than the quarter earned. WATCH: that ratio, around October 26. RISK: premiums written $6.13B, -1.1%. VERDICT: a billion-dollar quarter, and they bought more of themselves than they earned, at a price still on offer today.

DEEP-VALUE & SPECIAL-SITUATIONS LEN5:
- Federated Hermes, ticker FHI, at $61.18, -$0.27 / -0.4% today, 9.0% under the $67.20 of August 5. The Pittsburgh firm runs money-market funds - cash accounts that pay a yield and aim to hold a $1 share price - and other funds for more than 11,000 institutions. This style wants a good business marked down after something visible and dated. July 30: record $911.6B of assets, money-market assets $676.9B, half of the quarter's $502.8M of revenue, profit $1.38 a share vs $1.16 a year earlier, about 11 times the last four quarters. Money-market assets still fell $7.8B in three months, because the equity funds grew. WATCH: another quarter of those outflows after the Federal Reserve announces Wednesday, September 16 at 2:00pm ET, from a target range of 3.50% to 3.75%. Calendars point to October 22 after the close. VERDICT: half the revenue is a fee on cash that can leave the week rates fall.

GROWTH LEN5:
- Unity Bancorp, ticker UNTY, at $58.77, -$0.20 / -0.3% today, 6.0% under the $62.50 of August 14. The Clinton, New Jersey parent of Unity Bank lends to businesses and households from a $3.19B balance sheet. This style wants real profit growth the price has not already charged for. Not charged for sits near 10 times the last year of profit. Growing is the half to read twice. July 14, quarter to June 30: profit $14.5M, or $1.42 a share, up from $1.40 in March and down from $1.61 a year earlier; loans $2.68B, +12.6% on the year; net interest margin - what the bank keeps on loans after paying for deposits - 4.56%, the fattest among the community banks this Len5 is watching. WATCH: that 12.6% stalling, around October 13, not company-dated. RISK: last year's profit figure is not compounding with the loan book. VERDICT: the loans are growing at a double-digit pace; the earnings line is not.

HYPERGROWTH LEN5:
- Insmed, and this is the Len5 watching it. Early as well as fast: the pill is in its third full quarter; the company was founded in 1988 and is already worth $28B, so early is the product, not the corporate birthday. Fast is $425.5M against $107.4M. The strained half is duration - whether $309M becomes the $366M-and-up quarterly run-rate the raised year now needs. CHANGE IT: that $1.25B floor being trimmed. VERDICT: the launch is doing the work; the $28B price is a bet it keeps doing it after the easy comparisons end.

INCOME LEN5:
- Nutex Health, ticker NUTX, at $197.68, +$7.02 / +3.7% today, 3.1% under the $204.00 of July 6. The Houston company runs 27 micro-hospitals - small hospitals with a full emergency room and a handful of beds - across 12 states. Income wants cash genuinely reaching owners and paid for by the business. Paid for is settled: first-half cash from operations $109.7M, cash on hand $205.2M, long-term debt $31.1M. Reaching owners as a dividend is not: $0, and there is no payment record to lean on. What did reach owners was $50.7M of share buybacks in six months. August 6, quarter to June 30: profit $65.8M, or $9.38 a share, against a $17.7M loss a year earlier; sales $210.8M, -13.6%; visits 49,962, +9.6%. WATCH: a dividend actually declared, or the buybacks continuing without drawing that $205M down. Next accounts not company-dated; calendars point to mid-November. RISK: three new hospitals mapped for the second half still have to open. VERDICT: the cash is there; the cheque is not.

The pill that was not in last year's quarter is already 73% of Insmed. The insurer bought more of itself than it earned. The money-market manager is a fee on cash that can walk.

text:
🔑 Specialist Study: 📜 Isaiah 43:20-28 - The Dragons & Wilderness Beasts Honouring YHWH, Rivers Given through the Desert, a People Formed to Show Forth Divine Praise, the Weariness of Covenant Iniquity, Sweet Cane & Sacrificial Fragrance, the Blotting Out of Transgressions, the Heavenly Plea before the Divine Judge, the Failure of Ancient Interpreters, & the Profanation of Sanctuary Princes beneath the Supernatural Jurisprudence of the Holy One of Yisra’el - PLEASE SEE/READ QUOTE SHARE BELOW FOR ISAIAH 43:1-19 HENCE BELOW IS A CONTINUATION OF THAT FIRST PART OF THE CHAPTED - 

📜 Isaiah 43:20

“The beast of the field shall honour me, the dragons and the ||owles, because I giue waters in the wildernesse, and riuers in the desert, to giue drinke to my people, my chosen.”

📌 1611 Marginal Remark

|| Or, ostriches. Heb. daughters of the owle.

📝 Commentary

This is one of the chapter's most extraordinary verses.

The transformed wilderness is witnessed not only by humans.
“The beast of the field shall honour me.”

And then the 1611 names:

“the dragons and the owls.”

The ancient textual tradition is especially fascinating here. 

The Hebrew has tannîm, a desert-creature term; the Latin Vulgate preserves dracones, “dragons,” while the Greek Septuagint remarkably gives σειρῆνες, seirēnes, “sirens,” alongside “daughters of ostriches.” 

The old translation-world therefore preserves a much richer supernatural wilderness bestiary than a single flattened modern zoological label.

This belongs beside Isaiah 34, where the judged wilderness becomes inhabited by strange desert beings, and Psalm 148:7:

“Praise the LORD from the earth, ye dragons, and all deepes.”

That correspondence is enormous.
Psalm 148 gives dragons a liturgical summons.
Isaiah 43 gives dragons participation in honouring YHWH because the Creator transforms their environment with water.
The dragon-language therefore need not have one uniform moral value across Scripture. Revelation's Dragon is explicitly rebellious. Other dragon terminology can belong to the created bestiary beneath YHWH's sovereignty.

The deeper phenomenon is ecological and supernatural:
the liminal wilderness itself changes allegiance of appearance.

A region associated with desolation becomes watered.
Its inhabitants become witnesses to Divine restoration. This is creatural doxology through hydrological transfiguration.

📜 Isaiah 43:21

*“This people haue I formed for my selfe, they shall shewe foorth my praise.”

📌 1611 Side Reference
Luke 1:74-75 appears in the marginal chain.

📝 Commentary
The verb formed returns.
YHWH forms a people for a purpose:
“they shall show forth my praise.”
Humanity is therefore not merely biological existence.

The covenant people possess a liturgical ontology.
They are formed to become communicators of Divine excellence. 

This has a remarkable New Testament correspondence in 1 Peter 2:9:
“that ye should shew foorth the praises of him who hath called you out of darknesse into his maruellous light.”

The vocabulary and theology are almost perfectly aligned.
Isaiah: formed people → praise.
Peter: called people → show forth praises → from darkness into light.
This links Isaiah 42's light-language with Isaiah 43's formation-language.

The redeemed community becomes a living medium through which Divine attributes become publicly knowable. Praise is therefore more than music. It is revelatory vocation.

📜 Isaiah 43:22

“¶ But thou hast not called vpon me, O Iacob, but thou hast beene wearie of me, O Israel.”

📝 Commentary

The movement is painful.
Verse 21:
I formed you to praise Me.
Verse 22:
you have not called upon Me.

The problem is not lack of religious identity. It is relational exhaustion.
“thou hast been weary of me.”
This anticipates Malachi 1:13, where corrupted worshippers say:
“Behold, what a wearinesse is it?”

It also recalls Isaiah 7:13, where Yeshayahu asks whether the house of David will weary God.
Theologically, this is astonishing.
The inexhaustible God of Isaiah 40 gives strength to the weary.
Yet the people become weary of the very One who supplies strength.

That is spiritual inversion.
Created beings tire of their source of renewal and then wonder why their interior power diminishes.
This is one of Isaiah's deepest observations about disordered desire.

📜 Isaiah 43:23

“Thou hast not brought mee the ||small cattell of thy burnt offerings, neither hast thou honoured mee with thy sacrifices. I haue not caused thee to serue with an offering, nor wearied thee with incense."

📌 1611 Marginal Remark
|| Heb. lambes or kids.

📝 Commentary
The issue is not that YHWH possesses some physical hunger for sacrificial material.

The Twelve Prophets repeatedly make this clear. 

Hosea 6:6 emphasizes mercy and knowledge of God.

Amos 5 rejects festivals and offerings when justice is absent.

Micah 6 asks whether multiplied sacrifices can substitute for walking humbly with God.

The Psalmist likewise presents YHWH as One who owns the beasts of the forest and therefore cannot be materially sustained by human offerings.

Isaiah 43 makes the same distinction.
“I have not...wearied thee with incense.”

The covenant was not designed as Divine exploitation of human labor.
The sacrificial system was relational, purificatory, memorial, covenantal, and liturgical.
Yisra’el's deeper problem is not insufficient religious quantity.
It is that worship has ceased to correspond to covenantal relationship.

This is why verse 22 precedes verse 23:

“thou hast not called upon me.”
The missing center is communion with YHWH.

The lamb, incense, altar, and offering derive meaning from that center.

Without it, ritual can remain externally present while its inner axis has disappeared.

Isaiah is therefore moving toward one of prophetic theology's most important distinctions:
cultic performance cannot substitute for the living God toward whom the cult was ordered.

📜 Isaiah 43:24

“Thou hast bought me no sweete cane with money, neither hast thou †filled me with the fat of thy sacrifices: but thou hast made me to serue with thy sinnes, thou hast wearied me with thine iniquities.”

📌 1611 Marginal Remark

† Heb. made me drunke: or abundantly moistened.

📝 Commentary

The verse deepens the accusation of verses 22-23. The problem is no longer simply omitted offering. YHWH exposes a dreadful inversion:

the people who should have served Him have made Him “serve” beneath the burden of their sins.

The anthropomorphic language is intentionally shocking.

The Creator who does not faint or grow weary in Isaiah 40 now speaks of being wearied by iniquity. This is not creaturely exhaustion in YHWH. It is covenantal language expressing the intolerable moral weight of persistent rebellion.

The Hebrew behind “sweet cane” is קָנֶה - qāneh, an aromatic reed or cane used within ancient perfumery and sacred aromatic preparations. Exodus 30:23 includes fragrant cane within the holy anointing composition. 

Jeremiah 6:20 also speaks of sweet cane brought from a far country, yet rejected when obedience is absent.
Thus Isaiah joins scent, sacrifice, fat, and sin within one ritual phenomenology.

The sanctuary ordinarily contains:
fragrance rising,
fat offered,
incense ascending,
blood applied,
prayer spoken.
But moral rebellion reverses that sensory world.

Instead of YHWH receiving pleasing fragrance, He receives the burden of sin.

The 1611 marginal wording:
“made me drunk”
“abundantly moistened”
preserves the intensity of the underlying verb. Sacrificial abundance is pictured almost as saturating or drenching.

Yet the people have not saturated the altar with faithful devotion. They have saturated covenant history with transgression.

This connects powerfully with Amos 5, Hosea 6:6, Micah 6, and Malachi 1, where ritual activity cannot compensate for distorted covenant life.

The deeper proposition is severe:
religious abundance cannot conceal ontological disorder before the God who sees the heart.

📜 Isaiah 43:25

*“I, euen I am he that blotteth out thy transgressions for mine owne sake, and will not remember thy sinnes.”

📌 1611 Side Reference

The page directs the reader toward Ezekiel 36:22 and following, where YHWH acts for the holiness of His own Name.

📝 Commentary

This is one of the most powerful forgiveness declarations in Yeshayahu.
Again the emphatic Divine formula appears:
“I, even I.”

Hebrew:
אָנֹכִי אָנֹכִי הוּא - ’ānōkhî ’ānōkhî hû’
The same God who declared in verse 11:

“beside me there is no Saviour”
now identifies Himself as the One who removes transgression.
The verb translated “blotteth out” is מָחָה - māḥāh, to wipe away, erase, obliterate.

The image belongs to the world of writing.
Sin is imagined almost as an inscription or record.

YHWH removes the entry.
This produces a remarkable forensic bibliology:

transgression can be recorded,
remembered, testified against,
and then Divinely erased.
Compare Psalm 51:1:

“blot out my transgressions.”
Compare Colossians 2:14, where the handwriting against us is described as blotted out through the work of Christ.
Then YHWH says:

“I will not remember thy sins.”
Biblical “remembering” is frequently active rather than merely cognitive. 

When YHWH “remembers” covenant, He acts upon it.

Therefore “not remember” does not imply loss of omniscience. It means sin will no longer be brought forward as operative covenant accusation.

Jeremiah 31:34 gives the same magnificent promise:

“I will forgive their iniquitie, and I will remember their sinne no more.”
Hebrews 8 and 10 later place that promise within the New Covenant.

The phrase:
“for mine own sake”
is equally profound.

Forgiveness ultimately rests upon YHWH's own Name, character, mercy, and covenant purpose.
The foundation is not human ability to purchase erasure.
The offended God Himself provides it.

📜 Isaiah 43:26

“Put me in remembrance: let vs plead together: declare thou, that thou mayest bee iustified.”

📝 Commentary

The Divine courtroom returns.
This chapter has already gathered nations and witnesses.

 Now YHWH summons Yisra’el personally into legal argument:
“Put me in remembrance.”
“Let us plead together.”
The Hebrew verb belongs to juridical contention, argument, adjudication.

This is extraordinary covenantal boldness. YHWH permits the accused people to state their case before Him.
The image belongs to what we might call sacred forensic reciprocity.
The Judge is not threatened by examination.
He invites it.

Compare Job's longing to plead his cause before God, Abraham's intercession concerning Sodom, Moshe's covenant argument after the golden calf, and Habakkuk's prophetic questioning.
Scripture contains a surprisingly robust tradition in which faithful human beings can address YHWH with reasoned remembrance:
Remember the covenant.
Remember Abraham, Isaac, Jacob.
Remember Thy promises.
Remember Thy Name.

Yet here the challenge exposes the opposite:

Can Yisra’el present a case establishing innocence?
The next verse answers.
This is also a profound epistemological principle:
Divine judgment can withstand scrutiny because truth does not fear investigation.

📜 Isaiah 43:27

“Thy first father hath sinned, and thy †teachers haue transgressed against me.”

📌 1611 Marginal Remark
† Heb. interpreters.

📝 Commentary
The phrase “first father” has generated several interpretive possibilities across Jewish and Christian traditions.

It may reach back toward Adam, the first human father and archetypal transgressor.

It may also function corporately for ancestral Yisra’el, or refer to an early representative patriarchal or priestly figure depending upon interpretive context.

The point is unmistakable:
sin is not a recent anomaly.
It reaches backward into ancestry.
Then the 1611 margin becomes especially valuable:
“teachers” = “interpreters.”
Hebrew מֵלִיצֶיךָ - melîtseyḵā can signify interpreters, mediators, spokesmen.

These are people entrusted with the transmission and interpretation of sacred truth.
Their transgression is therefore particularly serious.
Ignorance among the uninstructed is one thing.

Corruption among interpreters is another. This resonates strongly with:

Malachi 2, where priests corrupt instruction.

Micah 3, where prophets, priests, and rulers distort judgment.

Jeremiah 8, where scribes falsely handle Torah.

Matthew 23, where Yeshua confronts religious interpreters who possess sacred knowledge yet obstruct its true purpose.

James 3:1 likewise warns that teachers receive stricter judgment.
This creates an important theology of hermeneutical responsibility.
The interpreter stands between text and people.

If interpretation is corrupted, error can multiply through generations.

Thus Isaiah places even sacred interpretation beneath Divine judgment.

📜 Isaiah 43:28

“Therefore I haue profaned the ||princes of the Sanctuarie, and haue giuen Iacob to the curse, and Israel to reproches.”

📌 1611 Marginal Remark
|| Or, holy princes.

📝 Commentary

The chapter ends with the sanctuary itself entering judgment.
The phrase translated:
“princes of the Sanctuary”
can also be rendered according to the 1611 margin:

“holy princes.”
These are leaders associated with sacred office, priesthood, sanctuary administration, or consecrated authority.

The frightening proposition is that sacred office does not make a corrupt person immune to Divine judgment.

YHWH says:
“I have profaned...”
That language is intentionally paradoxical.
Those occupying supposedly holy positions can be stripped of sacred status when covenant corruption empties the office of its true function.

This is a form of deconsecration through judgment.
Ezekiel 8-11 supplies a major parallel. The Temple contains abominations, and eventually the Glory of YHWH departs from its profaned precincts.

Malachi confronts priests whose polluted offerings dishonor YHWH's Name.

Yeshua later cleanses the Temple and pronounces judgment upon religious corruption.

Revelation 11 measures the Temple while distinguishing what is given over to trampling.

Sacred architecture therefore does not mechanically guarantee Divine approval.

Presence and holiness are covenantal realities.

Then:
“Jacob to the curse, and Israel to reproaches.”

This is the judicial consequence of the preceding verses.

Yet because Isaiah 43 began with:
“Fear not... I have redeemed thee”
the curse cannot be the final ontology of Yisra’el.
That is crucial.

Judgment occurs inside a chapter already framed by redemption.
The chapter begins:

“Thou art mine.”

It ends:
“Israel to reproaches.”

Both statements must be held together.
Covenant love does not abolish moral consequence.
Moral consequence does not automatically abolish covenant purpose.

This tension prepares the movement into Isaiah 44, where YHWH again speaks to Ya‘aqob as chosen servant and promises:
“I will powre water vpon him that is thirsty... I will powre my Spirit vpon thy seed.”

Thus Isaiah 43 ends under reproach, but the prophetic horizon already contains Spirit, water, renewal, and restoration.

🔑 The Extraordinary Architecture of Isaiah 43:1-28

Isaiah 43 begins with personal naming and moves outward until wilderness creatures, dragons, empires, seas, cardinal directions, and generations all stand within the sovereignty of YHWH.
The chapter moves through several magnificent degrees of reality:

Identity: YHWH creates, forms, redeems, names, and claims.

Elemental passage: waters, rivers, fire, and flame become liminal environments through which Divine Presence carries the chosen.

Sacred geography: East, West, North, and South become commanded territories of regathering.

Anthropological teleology: those called by the Name are created, formed, and made for Divine glory.
Sensorial epistemology: blind people with eyes and deaf people with ears are summoned into witness.

Divine tribunal: nations and rival gods are tested through prophecy, history, causality, and truth.
High Divine ontology: YHWH declares ’Ani Hu, “I am He,” with no God formed before or after Him.
Soteriological exclusivity: beside YHWH there is no Saviour, creating one of the strongest Old Testament foundations for understanding the New Testament's identification of Yeshua as Saviour.

Temporal sovereignty: before the day, YHWH is He; what He works cannot be turned back.
Babylonian apocalypse: the Chaldeans cry among ships, anticipating the maritime lament over Babylon in Revelation 18.
Hydrological theophany: YHWH makes roads inside seas and rivers inside deserts.

Moral fire-symbolism: the faint flax of Isaiah 42 is preserved, while the oppressive army of Isaiah 43 is quenched like tow.
New-creation morphology: the new thing does not simply arrive. It springs forth.

Wilderness bestiary: beasts, dragons, and ancient liminal creatures become participants in the Creator's restored environment.

Liturgical ontology: the people are formed to show forth Divine praise.

And perhaps the deepest proposition of the whole passage is contained in the movement from verses 1 to 21:

The God who calls a single person by name is the same God who commands the four directions, makes pathways through mighty waters, overturns Babylon, reconfigures wilderness ecology, gives drink to dragons and beasts, and announces events before they spring into history.

Isaiah refuses to choose between intimacy and cosmological magnitude.

The hand governing empires knows the individual.
The Voice commanding North and South calls Ya‘aqob by name.

The Creator who rearranges water, fire, wilderness, beasts, nations, and time can still say to one redeemed person:

“Thou art mine.”
&
These final five verses form a remarkably compact progression:

Verse 24 - covenant worship becomes inverted, and YHWH is anthropomorphically “wearied” by iniquity.

Verse 25 - the Divine Judge becomes the Divine Eraser, blotting out transgression and refusing to activate its record against the forgiven.

Verse 26 - YHWH opens the courtroom and invites the accused to plead.

Verse 27 - ancestral sin and corrupted interpreters reveal that the disorder reaches through history and sacred instruction.

Verse 28 - sanctuary leadership itself falls beneath judgment, showing that sacred office without holiness cannot protect its holder.

Yet all five verses remain enclosed within the chapter's greater declaration:

“I have redeemed thee.”
“I have called thee by thy name.”
“Thou art mine.”

That makes Isaiah 43 one of the great biblical demonstrations that Divine judgment and Divine redemption can operate within the same covenantal field without either being reduced to the other.
